qa_results.bill_summary: The Maryland Fallen Heroes Tuition Benefits Act exempts spouses and financially dependent children of State or local public safety employees killed in the line of duty from paying out-of-state or out-of-county tuition at Maryland public higher education institutions. It also restructures the Edward T. and Mary A. Conroy Memorial Scholarship and Jean B. Cryor Memorial Scholarship programs by capping total award allocations to the amount available in the State budget rather than funding all verified eligible applicants, directing the Maryland Higher Education Commission to allocate funds using a new formula, and giving funding priority to scholarship renewals over new applicants.
qa_results.stakeholders: Spouses and financially dependent children of deceased Maryland State or local public safety employees, students eligible for the Conroy and Cryor memorial scholarships, and Maryland public and private postsecondary institutions (including community colleges and private career schools).
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures potentially decrease significantly beginning in FY 2027 due to eliminating an open-ended entitlement requirement and capping scholarship awards to funds appropriated in the State budget (for context, awards totaled $9.5 million in FY 2025, while the FY 2027 budget appropriated $7.0 million). Consequently, higher education and community college revenues and expenditures for scholarship awards decrease. The nonresident tuition exemption is expected to impact very few individuals and will have no material fiscal effect on higher education or community college tuition revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is the primary regulatory and implementing agency for the bill. It is tasked with adopting regulations for the tuition exemption, establishing the allocation formula for the Conroy and Cryor scholarship programs, developing implementation guidelines, and allocating funds to postsecondary institutions.
Identical to MHEC, the Commission is designated as the primary entity responsible for adopting regulations, establishing the scholarship allocation formula, and administering the scholarship funds.

USM institutions are directly impacted as they must grant the out-of-state tuition exemption to qualifying spouses and dependent children and will award Conroy and Cryor scholarships subject to MHEC's new formula and state budget allocations.

As an independent public university, Morgan State must implement the out-of-state tuition exemption for eligible dependents and award scholarship funds based on allocations from MHEC under the revised program guidelines.

As a public institution of higher education, St. Mary's College is directly required to provide the out-of-state tuition exemption to qualifying individuals and administer scholarship allocations received under the modified Conroy and Cryor scholarship formulas.
Under the statute reenacted in the bill, the State Treasurer is designated to hold the Edward T. Conroy and Jean B. Cryor Scholarship Fund and receive deposited gifts or grants.
Under the statute reenacted in the bill, the Comptroller is responsible for accounting for the Edward T. Conroy and Jean B. Cryor Scholarship Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) to collect student-level data from public higher education institutions on students' parental status and submit annual summary reports to legislative committees. It requires public institutions of higher education (excluding the University of Maryland Global Campus) to include parental status questions on demographic forms, expands the requirement to adopt and post a plan for pregnant and parenting students to community colleges, and includes parental status (while excluding pregnancy status) in the student data that can be shared with the Maryland Longitudinal Data System.
qa_results.stakeholders: Pregnant and parenting students enrolled at Maryland public institutions of higher education and community colleges, as well as the institutions themselves.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $51,857 ($51,900 rounded) in FY 2027 for MHEC to hire a part-time Staff Specialist II for protocol development, institutional technical assistance, and reporting. Higher education expenditures for public four-year colleges and Baltimore City Community College may increase minimally for data collection. Potential increases in participation in government assistance programs (such as Medicaid and MCHP) may increase expenditures and federal matching revenues. Local community colleges will incur minimal costs to collect and report data, while policies can be implemented with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is the primary implementing agency responsible for developing survey questions in consultation with institutions, collecting student-level parental status data, adopting regulations, and submitting an annual summary report to the General Assembly.

Duplicate listing for MHEC; the Commission is the primary agency tasked with developing data collection questions, collecting parental status data from public institutions, adopting implementing regulations, and reporting annually.
The bill alters statutory definitions governing student data collected and maintained by the MLDS Center, specifically adding parental status and excluding pregnancy status.

Constituent institutions of USM are required to incorporate parental status questions into demographic data collection forms, report the data to MHEC, and maintain and post Title IX-compliant plans for pregnant and parenting students.

As a public senior higher education institution, Morgan State University must collect and report parental status data to MHEC and adopt, maintain, and publish a support plan for pregnant and parenting students.

As a public senior higher education institution, St. Mary's College of Maryland must collect and report parental status data to MHEC and post an updated support plan for pregnant and parenting students.

The fiscal note indicates that required institutional referrals to the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and MCHP could increase program participation and state/federal expenditures administered by MDH.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists to issue limited licenses to practice music therapy under the supervision of a fully licensed music therapist while an applicant completes full licensure requirements.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals seeking full licensure as music therapists, supervising licensed music therapists, and clients receiving music therapy services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: The board can implement and issue limited licenses using existing budgeted resources. License and renewal fees are not anticipated to meaningfully impact special fund revenues. Local effect: None.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists, which is a regulatory health occupations board housed within the Maryland Department of Health, by authorizing it to issue and renew limited licenses for the practice of music therapy.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Sheriff of Anne Arundel County to appoint up to three majors who will serve at the Sheriff's pleasure at a salary established by the Anne Arundel County Council.
qa_results.stakeholders: Anne Arundel County Sheriff's Office, prospective and appointed majors, and Anne Arundel County taxpayers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected. Anne Arundel County expenditures may increase by up to $822,300 in FY 2027 and by at least $730,000 annually thereafter if the Sheriff appoints three new majors and expands overall staff, covering salaries, benefits, vehicles, uniforms, and equipment. Local revenues are not affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) to update the standard bullying, harassment, or intimidation reporting form to record motivating personal characteristics. It also requires local school boards to report incidents motivated by personal characteristics to the State Board of Education under specified conditions, make disaggregated incident data available upon request while protecting student privacy, and requires MSDE to adopt relevant standards by July 1, 2027.
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland public school students, parents and guardians, school staff, and local school boards
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland State Department of Education can update reporting forms, policies, and guidance with existing resources, and local school boards can collect and provide the required data using existing resources. There is no effect on revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is the primary implementing agency under the bill. MSDE is required to update the standard bullying, harassment, or intimidation reporting form to include motivating personal characteristics, establish standards for reporting group characteristics by July 1, 2027, receive annual data from local school boards, and compile an annual summary report for legislative committees.

As an independent unit within the Maryland State Department of Education tasked with school safety coordination, resources, and the statewide anonymous reporting system, the Center's mission and programs intersect with state policies, guidance, and reporting on student bullying, harassment, and intimidation.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill modifies and expands the criteria for determining the proper county venue for administrative or judicial probate regarding estates of decedents not domiciled in the United States. It also establishes that, for Maryland inheritance tax purposes, the taxable situs of intangible personal property is the domicile of the decedent, and repeals a related reciprocal inheritance tax exemption for personal property of nonresident decedents.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Registers of Wills and Orphans' Courts
qa_results.stakeholders: Personal representatives, executors, beneficiaries, heirs, and petitioners handling estates of decedents who were not domiciled in Maryland or the United States.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may decrease beginning in FY 2027 to the extent that intangible personal property of nonresident decedents is no longer subject to Maryland inheritance tax; however, any revenue reduction is anticipated to be minimal. State expenditures are unaffected, and there is no direct impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Register of Wills is the primary agency responsible for overseeing administrative probate of estates, serving as clerk to the Orphans' Court, and calculating and collecting the Maryland inheritance tax, all of which are directly altered by the bill's provisions regarding probate venue and the taxable situs of intangible property.

The Administrative Office of the Courts provides administrative and legal support to the judicial branch, including the Orphans' Courts and Circuit Courts that handle judicial probate proceedings and determinations of proper venue under the revised statutory criteria.

The Comptroller serves as the state's chief tax collector and fiscal officer; inheritance tax collections administered by the registers of wills ultimately affect state general fund revenues monitored and managed by the Comptroller.

qa_results.bill_summary: Reestablishes a related event promoter's permit in Baltimore City, authorizing the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to issue permits to third-party promoters and participating license holders to hold social events related to the Central Intercollegiate Athletic Association (CIAA) Basketball Tournament. It specifies permit requirements, application procedures, fees, and penalties for violations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City
qa_results.stakeholders: Related event promoters, Baltimore City alcoholic beverages license holders, State caterer's license holders, and attendees of CIAA Basketball Tournament events.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Baltimore City revenues may increase minimally from FY 2026 through FY 2029 due to a $50 application fee, permit fees of $500 or $1,500 depending on venue capacity, and potential fines of $1,000 to $3,000 for violations. Local monitoring and enforcement can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill concerns alcoholic beverages regulation and penalties affecting holders of State caterer's licenses. The Comptroller's office is charged with state revenue collection and oversight related to the alcohol industry.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 30 expands the Department of State Police's regulations on police-initiated towing beyond commercial vehicles to include all motor vehicles, specifically establishing approved rate caps for light-duty towing and recovery services at no more than 80% of medium-duty rates. It also alters the scope of the Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution for Police-Initiated Towing and Recovery to include light-duty towing recommendations and examination of certain out-of-state vehicle insurance and debris cleanup matters.
qa_results.stakeholders: Motor vehicle owners and drivers subject to police-initiated towing, authorized towing businesses and operators, the trucking industry, and motor vehicle insurers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of State Police can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances and operations are not materially affected. The bill may have a meaningful impact on small business tow companies and small businesses that are the subject of police-initiated towing.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the Department of State Police, requiring the department to establish approved rates for light-duty towing and recovery, maintain the tow list, handle complaint adjudication, and provide staff support to the Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution.

The Insurance Commissioner appoints a representative to serve on the Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution, which is specifically tasked by the bill with examining and reporting on insurance matters related to out-of-state insured vehicles and cargo cleanup costs.
A representative of the Maryland Transportation Authority Police is a designated member of the Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution for Police-Initiated Towing and Recovery.
The Administrator of the State Highway Administration appoints a representative to serve on the Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution for Police-Initiated Towing and Recovery.
The Secretary of Transportation appoints the Maryland Transportation Authority Police representative to the Committee, and the department oversees the modal administrations involved.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The legislation modifies the name, statutory responsibilities, and reporting scope of the Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution for Police-Initiated Towing and Recovery.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes county and municipal governing bodies to adopt ordinances regulating trees of heaven and other listed invasive trees, including prohibiting their sale, planting, or uncontained growth on private property. It also permits local governments to establish civil fines, enforce damage mitigation, and create bounty or native tree replacement programs to incentivize the removal of invasive trees.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governing bodies of Maryland counties and municipalities
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland property owners, plant dealers and nurseries, landscaping businesses, and county and municipal governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected. Local government impact is indeterminate and authorizing in nature: expenditures may increase if a local government establishes bounty or native tree replacement programs, while revenues may increase to the extent civil fines are imposed and collected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill defines 'listed invasive tree' by direct statutory reference to the Maryland Prohibited Invasive Plant List established and posted by the Department of Agriculture, linking local regulatory authority and enforcement to the department's invasive species determinations.

The bill statutorily establishes that any local bounty or native tree replacement program must follow the identification standards and eradication methodologies published by the University of Maryland Agriculture Extension, an institution within the University System of Maryland.

The Department of Natural Resources conserves Maryland's forest and natural resources and served as an information source on the legislation, although the bill does not impose direct operational or fiscal obligations on the agency.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands licensing provisions for affiliated insurance producer–mortgage loan originators (AIP-MLOs) by permitting individuals who originate mortgage loans made by an approved mortgage lender, rather than solely a financial institution, to be licensed as an AIP-MLO. It establishes approval criteria for mortgage lenders sponsoring AIP-MLOs and updates statutory terminology from 'employer' to 'sponsor'.
qa_results.responsible_party: Commissioner of Financial Regulation (Office of Financial Regulation, Maryland Department of Labor)
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed insurance producers, mortgage loan originators, mortgage lenders, financial institutions, and mortgage borrowers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues may increase minimally beginning in FY 2027 from the $700 AIP-MLO licensing fee and related amendment fees; however, few applications are anticipated. The Office of Financial Regulation can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. There is no material impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of Financial Regulation (OFR) is a unit of the Maryland Department of Labor. The bill directly alters licensing and regulatory requirements for affiliated insurance producer–mortgage loan originators and requires the Commissioner of Financial Regulation to review and approve sponsoring financial institutions and mortgage lenders.

The bill concerns licensing requirements for affiliated insurance producer–mortgage loan originators, who are required to be licensed insurance producers in good standing under the Insurance Article regulated by the Maryland Insurance Administration.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill allows registered massage practitioners to continue practicing in non-healthcare settings beyond October 31, 2026, rather than phasing out their registrations. It modifies licensure qualifications for graduates of out-of-state massage therapy programs, allowing them to make up missing contact hours through continuing education or verified practice experience. Additionally, the bill requires criminal history records checks to reactivate inactive licenses or registrations, repeals hearing requirements for imposing a $100 fine for failing to report name or address changes, and establishes that lapsed registrations unrenewed after five years can only be reinstated by satisfying new licensure standards.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners
qa_results.stakeholders: Registered massage practitioners, licensed massage therapists, out-of-state applicants for massage therapy licensure, and massage therapy businesses.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected by the bill, and there is no local government fiscal impact. Small businesses and registered massage practitioners experience a potential meaningful benefit by being permitted to continue operating without having to incur the costs and time required to obtain a full license.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners is a health occupations licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill directly alters the Board's licensing and registration standards, out-of-state education requirements, reinstatement policies, and administrative penalty processes.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Civic Excellence Program, authorizing local school systems to participate to recognize public high school students for civic readiness and engagement. The State Board of Education must adopt regulations by the 2027–2028 school year setting criteria to award a Seal of Civic Excellence—including a capstone project through an extracurricular civic service activity—which is recognized via a cord, medal, or diploma insignia.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Education and the Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Public high school students, participating local school systems, public high schools, and school staff supervising extracurricular activities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Education can adopt regulations and establish criteria using existing resources, resulting in no state fiscal impact. For local school systems, participation is optional; however, systems that choose to participate may experience discretionary increases in local expenditures for staff, recognition materials (e.g., cords, medals, diploma insignia), and related operational costs. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 57 establishes the Maryland Civic Excellence Program within the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE). It requires the State Board of Education to adopt regulations setting the criteria and requirements for awarding the Seal of Civic Excellence and tasks MSDE with administering the program and receiving annual implementation reports from participating local school systems.

qa_results.bill_summary: Clarifies that communications between an attorney and a client acting as a fiduciary are protected by attorney-client privilege, even if fiduciary funds are used to pay for the legal services, and specifies that a fiduciary relationship with a beneficiary does not waive that privilege.
qa_results.stakeholders: Fiduciaries (including trustees, personal representatives, and agents under powers of attorney), attorneys providing counsel to fiduciaries, and trust or estate beneficiaries.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local government finances. The effect on small businesses is anticipated to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts evidentiary rules and attorney-client privilege standards applied in Maryland courts during judicial proceedings involving fiduciaries, trusts, and estates.
The bill clarifies fiduciary and attorney-client privilege rules directly affecting personal representatives, executors, and estates administered through the Register of Wills and the Orphans' Court.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill authorizes a Maryland nonstock corporation to convert to a cooperative limited equity housing corporation (CLEHC) upon acquiring a residential rental facility, establishing procedures, voting requirements, and filings for such conversions. It requires CLEHCs to provide notices, an offer of membership to existing eligible tenants, and moving expense reimbursements to displaced low-income households, while restricting equity appreciation and sales primarily to low- and moderate-income households. Additionally, it authorizes the Department of Housing and Community Development to adopt regulations, set requirements, and establish a grant program to support CLEHCs, and prohibits local governments from imposing discriminatory restrictions on CLEHC conversions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Tenants and residents of residential rental facilities undergoing conversion, low- and moderate-income households, senior citizens, disabled individuals, nonstock housing corporations, and local governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Department of Housing and Community Development may increase beginning as early as fiscal 2027 if DHCD elects to establish a grant program to promote CLEHCs and hires additional staff for program oversight; however, specific dollar estimates are unavailable. The State Department of Assessments and Taxation can handle implementation using existing resources, with potential minimal increases in corporate filing fee revenues. Local government finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) to establish additional rights and requirements for cooperative limited equity housing corporations (CLEHCs) and their members, adopt implementing regulations, and establish a grant program to support nonstock corporations in establishing CLEHCs, which carries potential fiscal impacts for agency staffing and grant expenditures.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a five-year initial validity period and five-year renewal periods for handgun permits issued to retired law enforcement officers who retired in good standing from Maryland state, county, or municipal law enforcement agencies.
qa_results.stakeholders: Retired law enforcement officers in Maryland who retired in good standing from a state, county, or municipal agency.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $170,000 in FY 2027 only for one-time computer programming changes to the Department of State Police's automated permit system. Revenues are not affected because retired officers are already exempt from permit fees. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Police (under the Secretary of State Police) is responsible for administering, processing, and issuing Maryland handgun permits. The agency is directly responsible for implementing the bill's changes to the expiration and renewal schedule for retired law enforcement officers, requiring an estimated $170,000 in general fund expenditures in FY 2027 for computer system reprogramming.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill increases the membership of the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission from 19 to 21 members by adding representatives from the American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees (AFSCME) Local 3, Council 434, and the Citizens Advisory Council for Gifted and Talented Education. It also updates the chamber of commerce representative to the Greater Baltimore Chamber of Commerce and establishes staggered term expirations for commission members.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Members and appointing organizations of the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission, candidates for the Baltimore County Board of Education, and Baltimore County Public Schools students, staff, and community members.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact. Adding members to the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission does not materially affect Baltimore County finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor appoints eight members to the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission in consultation with the County Executive, and the bill staggers the term expiration dates for these specific gubernatorial appointees. Furthermore, the Governor appoints members to the Baltimore County Board of Education based on recommendations submitted by this Commission.

The Office of Appointments vets and manages gubernatorial appointments to state and local boards and commissions, including the eight district members appointed by the Governor to the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission as well as the Governor's appointments to the Baltimore County Board of Education.

Towson University, a member institution of the University System of Maryland, is statutorily designated to appoint a member to the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission, and the bill establishes the termination date for the term of Towson University's appointee.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission is a statutory advisory and nominating body established under state law whose membership and appointment term schedule are altered by this bill.

The Maryland State Department of Education oversees public education policy and standards across Maryland's 24 school districts, which includes the governance framework and appointment process for the Baltimore County Board of Education.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires county superintendents of schools to establish a fee-free remote advance enrollment process for dependent children of active service members relocating to Maryland on official military orders. It also requires the registration process to accommodate children with individualized education programs (IEPs) or 504 plans to ensure educational services without undue delay, permits enrolled students to finish the school year even if residency changes, and directs the Secretary of Veterans and Military Families to publish and maintain related enrollment and support information.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Veterans and Military Families and local county boards of education/superintendents
qa_results.stakeholders: Active service members, their dependent children (including children with disabilities) relocating to Maryland, and local public school systems
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect governmental operations or finances. The Department of Veterans and Military Families and local school systems can implement the requirements using existing budgeted resources, and there is no effect on revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Secretary of Veterans and Military Families, in consultation with specified entities, to publish and maintain information regarding advance enrollment procedures, the Purple Star Schools Program, the Interstate Compact on Educational Opportunity for Military Children, and available support services for military families.

The bill amends the Education Article to govern public school advance enrollment procedures, remote registration, and timely provision of education for students with disabilities (IEP/504 plans) across local school systems, as well as referencing the Purple Star Schools Program administered by MSDE.

The bill specifically requires the Secretary of Veterans and Military Families to consult with the Office of Military and Federal Affairs and the Maryland Military Installation Council, both housed within the Department of Commerce, when compiling and publishing enrollment guidance.

The bill incorporates provisions of and requires consultation with the Military Family Education Liaison designated under the Interstate Compact on Educational Opportunity for Military Children, in which Maryland participates via interstate compact.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 103 prohibits consumer contracts from including provisions that waive, limit, impair, or disclaim certain remedies authorized by federal or State law, including statutory damages, punitive damages, declaratory relief, or injunctive relief, or that shorten the statute of limitations to bring an action. Violations are classified as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices subject to enforcement under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland consumers entering into consumer contracts and businesses or service providers offering consumer contracts for goods and services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal and Policy Note, the bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations, and the impact on small businesses is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes that violations of consumer contract waiver prohibitions are unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under Title 13 of the Commercial Law Article. The Office of the Attorney General, through its Consumer Protection Division, is the primary agency responsible for enforcing State consumer protection laws and prosecuting deceptive trade practices.

The bill specifies how Maryland courts must handle illegal consumer contract provisions (prohibiting courts from giving effect to void waiver clauses while enforcing the remainder of contracts) and authorizes civil actions in court for declaratory and injunctive relief.
The bill addresses statutory exemptions from consumer contract restrictions for services regulated by the Maryland Public Service Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Intelligent Speed Assistance (ISA) System Pilot Program under the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA). The program requires drivers facing license suspension or revocation due to excessive speeding, reckless driving, or speed contest point accumulations to participate for one year by installing an aftermarket ISA device that actively prevents their vehicle from exceeding posted speed limits.
qa_results.stakeholders: Drivers facing license suspension or revocation for excessive speeding, reckless driving, or speed contests; ISA system manufacturers and certified service providers; and the traveling public.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues are projected to increase by up to $61,020 annually from FY 2028 through FY 2031 from participant fees and restricted license transactions (based on an estimated 678 participants per year). The MVA expects to implement the program primarily with existing resources, though an external consultant costing approximately $100,000 per year may be required during the program development phase. District Court operations are not materially impacted, and there is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is the primary implementing agency tasked with establishing and operating the Intelligent Speed Assistance System Pilot Program, certifying service providers, issuing restrictive licenses, monitoring compliance, setting fees, adopting regulations, and submitting an implementation report.

As the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT oversees the agency and the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), which will receive fee revenues generated by the pilot program. The bill also authorizes program data to be shared with the Department.

The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the operations of the Judicial Branch, and the bill directly requires the District Court to update its traffic fine schedule to include separate entries for specified reckless driving violations.
The bill requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to submit a comprehensive evaluation report on the pilot program's implementation and participation metrics to the Governor by December 30, 2030.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Volunteer Services Program within the Division of Correction to facilitate access for volunteers, including formerly incarcerated individuals and organizations led by formerly incarcerated individuals, to State correctional facilities to help incarcerated individuals prepare for release.
qa_results.responsible_party: Division of Correction within the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals preparing for release, formerly incarcerated individuals, and volunteer organizations providing reentry and release preparation services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services can implement the program using existing resources. The bill is not expected to materially affect State finances, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 108 directly establishes the Volunteer Services Program within the Division of Correction, an agency of DPSCS, requiring the department to establish a registration protocol, manage volunteer access and schedules, and maintain public records.
The bill explicitly mandates that the Division of Correction submit its volunteer registration protocol to the Office of the Attorney General for review and approval.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to transmit monthly information to the State Board of Elections regarding individuals released from State correctional facilities, and directs the State Board of Elections to automatically restore the voter registration of eligible individuals who were registered to vote prior to incarceration and reside in the State.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Elections and Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals released from incarceration at State correctional facilities who were previously registered Maryland voters, as well as local boards of elections
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not expected to be materially affected. Local government expenditures increase collectively by $400,000 in FY 2027 only to cover one-time development costs billed by the State Board of Elections for necessary modifications to the statewide voter registration system. Local and state revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates DPSCS to jointly develop and implement procedures and an electronic transmission process with the State Board of Elections by January 1, 2028, and to transmit monthly data regarding individuals released from State correctional facilities to facilitate the automatic restoration of their voter registration.

The bill mandates the State Board of Elections to jointly develop and implement the electronic transmission process with DPSCS, receive monthly release lists, identify previously registered voters residing in Maryland, and promptly restore their voter registration to active status.

qa_results.bill_summary: Excludes certain agents providing payroll processing services on behalf of a payor from the definition of 'money transmitter' under the Maryland Money Transmission Act, exempting them from associated licensing requirements if specific conditions are met.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor, Office of Financial Regulation
qa_results.stakeholders: Payroll processing service providers, employers/payors, employees/payees, and the Office of Financial Regulation
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues for the Maryland Department of Labor (Nondepository Special Fund administered by the Office of Financial Regulation) decrease by $6,000 annually beginning in FY 2027 due to lost licensing fees from entities that will no longer require a money transmitter license. Expenditures are not affected, and local governments experience no fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the definition of 'money transmitter' under the Maryland Money Transmission Act, which is administered and enforced by the Office of Financial Regulation within the Maryland Department of Labor. As a result, certain payroll processors are exempt from licensing, resulting in an estimated reduction of $6,000 annually in special fund licensing fee revenue for the department beginning in FY 2027.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill allows certain Class B and Class D alcoholic beverages license holders in Baltimore County to obtain a permit to sell mixed drinks or cocktails in sealed containers for off-premises consumption along with prepared food until 11:00 p.m., provided that the Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners adopts regulations authorizing such sales. The board is prohibited from charging an additional fee for this authorization but may limit the quantity sold per transaction.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Class B and Class D alcoholic beverage license holders (restaurants and bars) in Baltimore County, restaurant and bar patrons, and the Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Baltimore County finances and operations are not expected to be materially affected, as the Board of License Commissioners is prohibited from charging license holders an additional fee. Small business restaurants and bars in Baltimore County are likely to experience increased revenues from off-premises sales.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for regulating the state's alcohol industry and collecting applicable excise and sales taxes on alcoholic beverages. While HB 121 is local legislation implemented by the Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners, it directly governs the conditions for selling alcoholic beverages for off-premises consumption, which falls under the Comptroller's broader regulatory and tax administration scope for alcohol.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force to Study Deed Fraud to examine incidents of deed fraud in Maryland, analyze demographic and economic impacts on victims, review methods used by perpetrators and practices in other states, and recommend detection tools and intergovernmental strategies for prevention. The task force must report its findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by July 1, 2028.
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland real property owners, victims of deed fraud, land title insurance representatives, notaries public, prosecutors, and the judiciary.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances: The Department of Legislative Services can staff the task force with existing budgeted resources. Any expense reimbursements for task force members are assumed to be minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected. Local finances: The bill has no effect on local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 130 establishes the Task Force to Study Deed Fraud as a temporary body charged with studying deed fraud patterns, impact on victims, and state countermeasures, and reporting findings to the General Assembly.
The Secretary of Housing and Community Development (or the Secretary's designee) is designated as a mandatory member of the Task Force to Study Deed Fraud.
The Governor is required to appoint two members of the Task Force (representing the land title insurance industry and notary publics) and designate the chair of the Task Force.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointees to the newly established task force.
The bill requires a representative of the Judiciary, designated by the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Maryland, to serve on the Task Force to Study Deed Fraud.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the governing body of a political subdivision, including Baltimore City, to designate noncontiguous blighted areas as development districts under the Tax Increment Financing Act to facilitate redevelopment through tax increment financing.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governing bodies of Maryland political subdivisions (counties and municipalities, including Baltimore City)
qa_results.stakeholders: Local governments, property owners and residents in designated noncontiguous blighted areas, and small businesses and construction contractors operating in or near those districts
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected. Local government revenues and expenditures may increase beginning as early as FY 2027 from TIF bond issuances, debt service, development-related spending, and eventual property tax growth; specific dollar estimates are unavailable. There is no fiscal impact on Baltimore City because its charter already permits noncontiguous TIF districts.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's principal economic development agency, the Department of Commerce monitors and coordinates economic development tools and programs across Maryland, including the statutory frameworks under the Economic Development Article that govern development districts.

MEDCO finances and supports economic development projects throughout Maryland, and under current law, local revenues generated through tax increment financing (TIF) districts may be pledged to debt issued by MEDCO in certain circumstances.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes collective bargaining rights and establishes a separate collective bargaining unit for eligible graduate assistants, including teaching, administrative, or research assistants, fellows, and postdoctoral interns, at the University of Maryland, College Park and the University of Maryland, Baltimore County.
qa_results.stakeholders: Graduate assistants, fellows, postdoctoral interns, and administrative leadership at the University of Maryland, College Park and the University of Maryland, Baltimore County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2029, expenditures for UMCP and UMBC increase minimally to reimburse the Public Employee Relations Board (PERB) for collective bargaining expenses, and PERB reimbursable revenues and expenditures increase minimally. UMCP and UMBC may incur additional minimal administrative and collective bargaining costs, as well as potential increases in salary and fringe benefit expenditures subject to negotiations. Local finances are unaffected. Specific dollar figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: PERB is the primary regulatory body responsible for administering collective bargaining, conducting union certification elections, and adjudicating disputes or unfair labor practice charges for the newly established graduate assistant bargaining units.

USM is directly impacted as the employer of the graduate assistants at UMCP and UMBC who are granted collective bargaining rights, resulting in administrative, operational, and potential compensation and benefit expenditures.

DBM is the principal fiscal and personnel agency for the State, which shares in the cost of salary and fringe benefit adjustments for State-supported employees resulting from collective bargaining agreements.

Morgan State University is explicitly referenced in the statutory sections governing higher education collective bargaining units amended by the bill, although the definition of eligible graduate assistants is currently limited to UMCP and UMBC.

St. Mary's College of Maryland is explicitly referenced in the statutory provisions governing public higher education bargaining units amended by the bill, though the specific graduate assistant provisions currently apply only to UMCP and UMBC.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires residential rental high-rise buildings undergoing substantial renovations to install automatic fire sprinklers and specific life safety equipment starting October 1, 2026. It also mandates that the State Fire Prevention Commission establish a licensing and regulatory program for fire alarm system technicians and companies, and directs the State Fire Marshal to establish minimum training, certification, and qualification standards for assistant and special assistant State fire marshals.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Fire Prevention Commission and the Office of the State Fire Marshal (within the Department of State Police)
qa_results.stakeholders: Tenants and owners of residential rental high-rise buildings, fire alarm system technicians and companies, fire sprinkler contractors, and local government fire officials and assistant State fire marshals.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $311,100 in FY 2027 for 3 new staff positions, IT system upgrades, and NFPA certifications, with ongoing annual expenditures ranging from $231,400 to $264,500 through FY 2031. General fund revenues will increase beginning in FY 2027 or FY 2028 from license fee collections, though the exact amount is indeterminate. Local government expenditures will increase to cover additional training and certification costs for assistant State fire marshals.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the State Fire Marshal and the State Fire Prevention Commission are units within the Department of State Police. The agency is directly responsible for implementing the bill, including establishing minimum standards for assistant fire marshals, promulgating regulations to license and regulate fire alarm system technicians and companies, hiring administrative personnel, and upgrading licensing IT systems.

The bill mandates automatic sprinkler system installations and other life safety upgrades during substantial renovations of residential high-rise buildings, which may impact capital project planning and costs for university-owned high-rise student housing facilities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the governing body of a county, municipal corporation, or Baltimore City to establish an optional property tax credit for real property converted from a retail service station to a residential use, an eligible retail use, or a mixed residential and retail use, primarily intended to defray costs associated with removing underground storage tanks and remediating contamination.
qa_results.responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City and the governing bodies of Maryland counties and municipal corporations
qa_results.stakeholders: Property owners and small businesses converting retail service stations, local governments, and communities undergoing commercial redevelopment
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Local property tax revenues may decrease beginning in fiscal 2027 to the extent that local governments grant the credit. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the revenue reduction depends on local adoption, local tax rates, the number of converted stations, and the assessed value of eligible properties. Local expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly conditions eligibility for the local property tax credit on underground storage tanks being permanently closed in accordance with regulations of the Department of the Environment (MDE), aligning with MDE's regulatory authority over underground storage tanks and site remediation.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 168 authorizes county boards of education to consider the provision of educator workforce housing as a school purpose, allowing them to use or retain school property for affordable housing reserved for teachers and non-administrative school employees. The bill also expands the Housing Innovation Fund, the Housing Innovation Pilot Program, and the Neighborhood and Community Assistance Program to include municipal corporations and county boards of education as eligible recipients, and prioritizes funding for projects that incorporate educator workforce housing.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Public school teachers and non-administrative school staff, county boards of education, municipal corporations, local housing authorities, and affordable housing developers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Housing and Community Development can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources, resulting in no effect on State revenues. At the local level, local school boards and municipal corporations become eligible for State funding assistance to support educator workforce housing development, but the bill does not otherwise materially affect local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary state agency responsible for administering the Housing Innovation Fund, the Housing Innovation Pilot Program, and the Neighborhood and Community Assistance Program, all of which are amended by the bill to support and prioritize educator workforce housing projects.

The bill amends the Education Article to allow county boards of education to consider educator workforce housing as a valid 'school purpose' when acquiring, maintaining, or disposing of school property, an area overseen with the approval of the State Superintendent of Schools.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes sole owners and certain co-owners of marine vessels, as well as co-owners of motor vehicles holding title as joint tenants with right of survivorship or tenants by the entirety, to designate a transfer-on-death (TOD) beneficiary on the certificate of title. Upon the death of the sole owner or last surviving co-owner, ownership passes directly to the surviving designated beneficiary outside of estate administration.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources and the Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Sole owners and co-owners of marine vessels, co-owners of motor vehicles, designated beneficiaries, and registers of wills handling estate administration.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues may increase beginning in FY 2027 from title application fees; illustratively, Department of Natural Resources State Boat Act Fund revenues could increase by $269,540 and Transportation Trust Fund revenues could increase by $1,000,000 in FY 2027. State general fund revenues may decrease minimally beginning in FY 2027 due to lower probate fees and potential inheritance tax losses as vehicles and vessels bypass probate estates. State expenditures and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the Department of Natural Resources to administer transfer-on-death beneficiary designations for marine vessels, process new certificates of title upon the death of owners, collect associated fees, and adopt implementing regulations.

The bill directly expands the Motor Vehicle Administration's transfer-on-death beneficiary designation program to include co-owners of motor vehicles holding title as joint tenants with right of survivorship or tenants by the entirety.

As the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT oversees the Transportation Trust Fund, which will receive increased revenue from application and titling fees resulting from the new transfer-on-death designations for co-owned vehicles.

The bill allows vessels and co-owned motor vehicles to pass directly to beneficiaries outside of estate administration, reducing the property subject to probate and potentially decreasing probate fees and inheritance taxes collected by the Registers of Wills.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the nonrefundable State income tax credit for venison donation by increasing or removing the limit on the total credit amount an individual may claim annually for expenses incurred butchering and processing antlerless deer donated to qualified charitable organizations.
qa_results.stakeholders: Hunters who donate deer meat, charitable venison donation organizations, food banks/programs serving low-income individuals, and the Maryland Comptroller's Office.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by an estimated $125,000 annually in FY 2027 through FY 2029 due to increased tax credit claims. The Comptroller's Office can administer the change using existing budgeted resources. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the state's tax collector and directly administers the individual income tax system, including the venison donation income tax credit. The bill also explicitly requires participating venison donation programs to submit annual reports directly to the Comptroller detailing donor information and the number of deer donated.

The Department of Natural Resources manages wildlife populations and regulates deer hunting in Maryland. The tax credit is tied to the harvest of antlerless deer compliant with state hunting laws and regulations, which directly impacts deer herd management objectives.

qa_results.bill_summary: Modifies procedures governing the nomination, appointment, and voting of presidential electors and alternates in Maryland. Requires electors to pledge to vote for their party's or candidate's nominees, designates the State Administrator of Elections to preside over the electors' meeting, establishes procedures to replace absent or faithless electors who violate their pledge, and sets guidelines for preparing and transmitting certificates of ascertainment and vote.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections (specifically the State Administrator of Elections) and the Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: Presidential electors, alternate presidential electors, political parties, unaffiliated presidential candidates, and Maryland voters
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State or local fiscal impact. The bill can be implemented using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill assigns extensive administrative duties to the State Board of Elections and the State Administrator of Elections, including receiving elector nominations and pledges, presiding and serving as secretary at the meeting of presidential electors, verifying ballots, enforcing pledges, handling vacancies, and preparing and transmitting certificates of vote and ascertainment.

The bill imposes specific statutory requirements on the Governor to certify presidential electors in the State's Certificate of Ascertainment in compliance with federal law, and to sign and deliver amended Certificates of Ascertainment if substitute electors are appointed.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a person to file a petition for expungement of an eligible criminal offense if a remaining charge was disposed of by the court with a "no finding" designation or included in a case designated as terminated without finding.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts)
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals seeking expungement of criminal records for cases or charges disposed of with a "no finding" designation or terminated without finding.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $11,740 in FY 2027 only for the Judiciary to revise expungement-related brochures, forms, and instructional videos. Beyond potential operational workload impacts on the Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, the bill does not materially affect State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands criminal record expungement eligibility, directly impacting the courts. The Administrative Office of the Courts incurs direct fiscal costs in FY 2027 to update expungement brochures, forms, and instructional videos, and faces operational impacts relating to case management system tracking and processing of court petitions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS houses the Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS), which is responsible for processing and executing court-ordered criminal record expungements across state databases.
As the primary state law enforcement agency and a custodian of arrest and police records, the Maryland State Police is required to expunge applicable police records upon receipt of court orders.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits retail merchants from refusing cash payments, requiring credit or debit card usage, or charging higher prices for cash payments during in-person retail transactions under $300 for essential consumer goods between 6:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m., subject to certain exceptions. Violations constitute unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices enforceable through civil penalties following compliance notices.
qa_results.responsible_party: Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Retail merchants and small business owners selling essential consumer goods, as well as consumers purchasing essential goods with cash.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances and operations are not materially impacted. The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division can enforce the bill's provisions using existing resources, and penalty revenues are not expected to have a material financial effect. Small businesses operating cashless retail establishments may experience meaningful operational costs to comply.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates violations of the cash payment requirements as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, directly tasking the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General with administering compliance notices and enforcing civil penalty provisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters Maryland State procurement laws and procedures by requiring procurement units to provide contract award debriefings to unsuccessful offerors upon request prior to contract approval. It establishes an exemption from conflict-of-interest prohibitions for individuals who provide information during solicitation development that does not confer an unfair competitive advantage. Additionally, it mandates contract clauses allowing contractors to request equitable adjustments for cost or time increases resulting from changes in State law, updates change order requirements, extends certain contract claim provisions to non-construction contracts, and modifies timelines and procedures for resolving bid protests and contract claims.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of State Procurement within the Department of General Services
qa_results.stakeholders: State procurement agencies, government contractors, subcontractors, and prospective bidders and offerors (including unsuccessful offerors).
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Implementation of the bill can be absorbed using existing agency resources, and State revenues are not affected. Modifications to procurement ethics exemptions may lead to an increase in bid protests, potentially delaying contract execution and resulting in project cost overruns; however, a reliable fiscal estimate cannot be determined. Local finances and operations are not materially impacted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DGS is the state's central procurement agency, and the bill directly tasks its Office of State Procurement with establishing guidelines and procedures for debriefings of contract awards, including request deadlines.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSBCA adjudicates bid protests and contract disputes for the State. The bill directly alters the procedures, timelines, deemed denials, and final action determinations for appeals of protests and contract claims before the Board.
The bill explicitly mandates that procurement officers seek the advice of the Office of the Attorney General on any legal issues raised in bid protests and contract claims.

BPW approves significant state contracts and expenditures. The bill stipulates that debriefings of recommended contract awards must occur before the award is presented for approval to the unit head or the Board of Public Works.

MDOT manages extensive state infrastructure and construction procurements, which are heavily impacted by the bill's changes to change orders, equitable adjustment clauses for changes in law, and revised contract claim timelines and procedures.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of the Environment to create, publish, and maintain a residential real property flood risk disclosure statement form, and requires sellers of residential real property with four or fewer units to provide this completed disclosure statement and any available FEMA elevation certificate to prospective buyers prior to entering into a sales contract, subject to certain exceptions.
qa_results.stakeholders: Buyers and sellers of residential real property with four or fewer single-family units, and real estate professionals in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are not affected, and the Maryland Department of the Environment can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. Local government operations and finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Department of the Environment develop, publish, and maintain the real property flood risk disclosure statement form by June 1, 2027, for use in residential property sales.
The Department of Labor regulates and licenses real estate brokers and agents who facilitate residential real estate transactions and must ensure compliance with statutory contract disclosures.

The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division oversees enforcement regarding statutory consumer disclosure requirements and deceptive trade practices in residential property transactions.
The Judiciary may adjudicate contract disputes or civil actions arising from residential real property sales and noncompliance with flood risk disclosure requirements.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the governing body of Baltimore County to grant a 100% property tax credit against the county property tax imposed on real property owned by the Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34 located at 730 Wampler Road in Middle River, Maryland.
qa_results.stakeholders: Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34 and Baltimore County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Baltimore County property tax revenues may decrease by approximately $9,600 annually beginning in fiscal year 2027 if the optional property tax credit is enacted by county law. Baltimore County expenditures are unaffected.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill establishes the crime of benefits exploitation, prohibiting a person from knowingly recruiting, harboring, transporting, or obtaining an individual through deception, coercion, exploitation, or isolation to appropriate that individual's government benefits. It also prohibits knowingly benefiting from, aiding, abetting, or conspiring in such exploitation, and sets graduated misdemeanor and felony criminal penalties based on the total value of benefits involved.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts) and Maryland Law Enforcement/State Courts
qa_results.stakeholders: Recipients of government assistance programs (including seniors, disabled individuals, and low-income adults receiving benefits such as SNAP, TANF, SSI/SSDI, Medicare, and Medicaid) and individuals prosecuted under benefits exploitation offenses.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $1,600 ($1,573) in FY 2027 only for the Judiciary to complete one-time computer programming changes. Other State operational and financial impacts, including caseloads for the Office of the Public Defender and correctional facilities, are expected to be absorbed with existing resources. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new criminal offense for benefits exploitation with graduated misdemeanor and felony penalties. The fiscal note identifies an expenditure of $1,600 in FY 2027 for the Judiciary to make necessary computer programming changes to implement the new charge codes and court tracking.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new criminal penalties ranging up to 20 years of imprisonment, requiring legal representation from the Office of the Public Defender for indigent individuals charged under the statute.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes new misdemeanor and felony penalties that include terms of imprisonment ranging up to 20 years, potentially affecting inmate population and community supervision caseloads managed by DPSCS.

The Office of the Attorney General investigates and prosecutes financial crimes and fraud involving vulnerable adults and Medicaid benefits, and represents the State in criminal appeals arising from convictions under this new statute.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the annual reporting deadline, from November 30 to October 1, for the Office of the Attorney General to report on the activities of the Environmental and Natural Resources Crimes Unit and specifies that the report must cover activities from the previous fiscal year.
qa_results.stakeholders: Office of the Attorney General, Maryland Department of the Environment, Department of Natural Resources, Governor, and the General Assembly
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State operations or finances, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the reporting deadline and reporting period for the Office of the Attorney General's Environmental and Natural Resources Crimes Unit, changing the submission date to October 1 and specifying coverage of the previous fiscal year.

The bill affects the annual report that documents actions taken by the Department of the Environment in response to findings and recommendations of the Environmental and Natural Resources Crimes Unit, aligning the date with MDE's own annual enforcement reporting.

The report required by the bill must include any actions taken by the Department of Natural Resources in response to the findings and recommendations of the Environmental and Natural Resources Crimes Unit.
The Governor is a statutory recipient of the annual report prepared by the Office of the Attorney General regarding the Environmental and Natural Resources Crimes Unit.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes owners, operators, managers, or local housing authorities to install individual water submeters in apartment buildings and mobile home parks. It regulates billing by limiting charges to actual water and sewer provider costs allocated proportionally to usage, caps administrative billing fees at $1 per unit per month, establishes standards for faulty meters, sets recordkeeping and lease disclosure requirements, and creates a complaint resolution process for occupants.
qa_results.stakeholders: Tenants and occupants of apartment houses and mobile home parks, owners, operators, and property managers, local housing authorities, and water service providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State requirements can be handled with existing budgeted resources, and revenues are not materially affected. The bill is not anticipated to materially affect local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds provisions to Title 9 of the Environment Article and designates the Department of the Environment as the primary regulatory agency responsible for adopting regulations and standards for the accuracy, testing, and recordkeeping of individual water submeters.

The bill requires local housing authorities to obtain approval from the Department of Housing and Community Development before installing individual submeters, and requires the Department of the Environment to consult with DHCD when developing submeter regulations and standards.

The Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General is designated to receive and handle complaints filed by occupants against apartment or mobile home park owners, operators, or managers where local commissions or agencies lack jurisdiction.
Approval from the Board of Public Works (or an equivalent local authority) is required for local housing authorities to install individual submeters for apartment houses or dwelling units.

The bill establishes a private right of action for tenants regarding water submeter billing violations and sets lease and billing requirements under the Real Property Article, which may impact civil court proceedings.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill extends the termination date and statutory authority of the Maryland Horse Industry Board by 10 years, from July 1, 2026, to July 1, 2036, under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Horse Industry Board (within the Maryland Department of Agriculture)
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial horse stables, equine industry businesses, horse owners, and equine feed sellers in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues and expenditures are maintained from FY 2027 through FY 2036 rather than terminating. The FY 2027 introduced budget includes $435,471 in special funds and $12,298 in federal funds for board operations. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Horse Industry Board (MHIB) is housed within the Maryland Department of Agriculture. This departmental bill extends the board's termination date under the Program Evaluation Act by 10 years, ensuring the continuation of its licensing, inspection, and promotional duties as well as its special fund operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill extends the statutory sunset authorization of the Maryland Horse Industry Board, an executive state board, through July 1, 2036.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Disabilities (MDOD) to oversee and administer affordable and accessible housing programs. It also authorizes MDOD to establish one or more affiliated non-state foundations to solicit and accept private or public funds, establish partnerships, and support programs related to assistive technology, disability employment advancement, and accessible housing.
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals with disabilities in Maryland who utilize or need accessible and affordable housing, assistive technology, and employment support services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State administrative requirements can likely be absorbed with existing budgeted resources. If an affiliated foundation is established and contributes funds, MDOD special fund revenues and expenditures may increase by an indeterminate amount. General fund expenditures may increase by an indeterminate, though likely minimal, amount annually for MDOD to hire an independent certified public accountant to audit each affiliated foundation if not absorbable. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly applies to the Department of Disabilities, requiring it to oversee affordable and accessible housing programs and authorizing it to establish affiliated foundations, establish operating policies, and arrange annual independent audits.

The State Ethics Commission is tasked with reviewing and approving conflict of interest policies for department personnel serving with affiliated foundations, reviewing notifications of joint service, and receiving required annual reports.
The Office of the Attorney General is required to review policies governing the relationship between the department and any affiliated foundation for form and legal sufficiency.
The Governor receives an annual reporting submission from the Department of Disabilities regarding affiliated foundation personnel and policy implementation.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 227 expands the duties that the Treasurer of the Maryland Environmental Service (MES) may delegate to the Deputy Treasurer, increases the maximum contract threshold for MES small procurements from $25,000 to $50,000, and modernizes public notice requirements for establishing or adjusting service district charges.
qa_results.stakeholders: Ratepayers, residents, and property owners in Maryland Environmental Service districts, contractors and vendors providing goods or services to MES, and MES administrative personnel.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no material impact on MES finances or local government finances. MES may experience administrative efficiencies by using the small procurement process for purchases up to $50,000.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the internal governance, procurement authority, and operational requirements of the Maryland Environmental Service (MES). Specifically, it expands the delegable authorities of the MES Treasurer to the Deputy Treasurer, raises MES's small procurement threshold from $25,000 to $50,000, and modernizes public notice requirements for rate changes in its service districts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits slaughtering or causing the slaughter of a racehorse in Maryland for commercial purposes, including human or animal consumption, as well as purchasing, selling, transporting, importing, or transferring a racehorse with the knowledge that it will be slaughtered for such purposes. Violators face criminal misdemeanor fines and potential imprisonment, fines are deposited into the racing Special Fund, and the Maryland Racing Commission and the Maryland Department of Agriculture are authorized to revoke or suspend licenses of violators.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Racing Commission (Maryland Racing Commission) and the Maryland Department of Agriculture
qa_results.stakeholders: Racehorse owners, breeders, trainers, equine transporters, racing industry licensees, and commercial livestock processors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues to the horse racing Special Fund may increase beginning in FY 2027 from fines collected from violations of the bill, but the exact impact cannot be reliably estimated.
