The bill also adjusts civil penalties for violations to a maximum of $250 for a first offense and up to $1,000 for subsequent offenses.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police (Secretary of State Police)
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed firearms dealers in Maryland and the Department of State Police.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operational requirements can be handled using existing budgeted resources. Adjustments to civil penalties are not anticipated to materially affect State revenues, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 284 is a departmental bill requested by the Department of State Police. It mandates that licensed firearms dealers notify the Secretary of State Police within 24 hours of a burglary, theft, or compromise of required security features, and authorizes the Secretary to enforce compliance and impose civil penalties and licensing sanctions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires any individual who violates a driver's license alcohol restriction to participate in the Ignition Interlock System Program as a condition of modifying a suspension or revocation of their license or obtaining a restricted license, expanding the requirement beyond individuals under age 21.
qa_results.stakeholders: Drivers, particularly those age 21 and older, who violate an alcohol restriction on their driver's license and seek a restricted license or modified suspension
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State finances or operations, though it may decrease hearing requests before the Office of Administrative Hearings. Local government finances and operations are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 286 is a departmental bill requested by MDOT that amends the Transportation Article governing driver's licensing, alcohol restrictions, and the Ignition Interlock System Program.

MVA is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the Ignition Interlock System Program, managing alcohol-restricted driver's licenses, and issuing restricted licenses or suspensions.

By enabling drivers age 21 and older who violate alcohol restrictions to enroll directly into the Ignition Interlock System Program without an ALJ hearing, the bill directly impacts OAH by reducing its hearing caseload.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the State Superintendent of Schools, rather than the Governor, to declare a prolonged state of emergency that prevents regular, in-person attendance at a public school for at least 14 consecutive school days due to natural disasters, civil disasters, public health emergencies, or specific security threats. This declaration allows local school systems to transition affected schools or the entire system to virtual instruction under an approved virtual education plan.
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland public school students, teachers, staff, and local school systems
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact. State officials and local school systems can declare, implement, and terminate a prolonged state of emergency using existing resources and existing virtual education plans without requiring new programs, staffing, or changes to state or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This departmental bill directly affects MSDE by transferring the authority to declare a prolonged state of emergency for public school closures from the Governor to the State Superintendent of Schools, enabling local school systems to implement virtual education plans.

The bill shifts the authority to declare a prolonged state of emergency for school closures from the Governor to the State Superintendent of Schools, but mandates that the State Superintendent consult with the Governor prior to issuing any declaration.

The State Superintendent is authorized to consult with MDH when declaring a prolonged state of emergency, and the bill explicitly preserves the independent statutory authority and responsibilities of the Secretary of Health during public health emergencies.
MDEM is specifically designated in statute as one of the agencies the State Superintendent may consult when determining whether to declare a prolonged state of emergency for public schools.

The Maryland State Police is specifically identified as an agency the State Superintendent may consult when considering a prolonged state of emergency declaration, particularly in cases involving security threats or civil disasters.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Central Collection Unit to certify debts owed to the State to video lottery operators to intercept casino prize payouts requiring IRS Form W-2G, clarifies certification processes for child support and restitution arrearages, establishes notice and appeal procedures for debtors, and defines the priority order in which intercepted funds are applied.
qa_results.responsible_party: Central Collection Unit (within the Department of Budget and Management) and the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: Casino patrons who win reportable video lottery prizes and owe delinquent child support, restitution, or State debts; video lottery facility operators; and State agencies and community colleges owed delinquent funds.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2027, State revenues across all funds are estimated to increase by at least $3.0 million annually from video lottery prize intercepts credited to referring agencies. Special fund revenues to the Central Collection Fund increase by at least $510,000 annually via CCU's 17% administrative fee. Affected State agencies can implement the bill using existing resources. Local community college revenues may also increase to the extent delinquent accounts referred to CCU are collected through intercepted prizes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was requested by the Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency (SLGCA). It regulates video lottery operators, establishes the order of prize interception requests honored by SLGCA and operators, and authorizes the Director of SLGCA to jointly adopt implementing regulations with the Secretary of Budget and Management.

The Central Collection Unit (CCU), a unit of DBM, is authorized to certify debts owed to the State and restitution arrearages to video lottery operators for prize interception. The bill also authorizes the Secretary of DBM to jointly adopt regulations, and DBM's Central Collection Fund will receive an estimated $510,000 annually in administrative fees from intercepted prizes.

The Child Support Administration (CSA), housed within the Department of Human Services, is authorized to certify unpaid child support debts of more than $150 directly to video lottery operators for prize payouts interception.

The bill establishes an administrative appeal process under the Administrative Procedure Act for debtors disputing intercepted video lottery prizes, which will be heard by Administrative Law Judges at the Office of Administrative Hearings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Governing Board of the Maryland Longitudinal Data System (MLDS) Center to share individual-level student and workforce data with one third-party data center at a time to facilitate multistate research and reporting on student outcomes, subject to strict data privacy, de-identification, and FedRAMP certification requirements. It also mandates annual compliance reviews, requires regular reporting to the General Assembly, and repeals existing authority to share student information with the U.S. Census Bureau.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center Governing Board
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland public and higher education students, Maryland workforce participants, education researchers, policymakers, and participating multistate data platforms.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are not affected. The MLDS Center can execute the data sharing agreements and compile the required legislative reports using existing budgeted resources, supported in part by previously secured grant funding. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 293 is a departmental bill requested by and directly governing the Maryland Longitudinal Data System (MLDS) Center. The bill authorizes the MLDS Center Governing Board to enter into data sharing agreements and provide individual-level student and workforce data to a third-party data center for multistate reporting, repeals the Center's authority to send data to the U.S. Census Bureau, and mandates reporting requirements to the General Assembly.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the MDiplomaWorks Pathway within the Maryland Department of Labor as an alternative method for eligible adult residents who have withdrawn from school to earn a high school diploma by demonstrating academic and career competencies, including industry-recognized credentials, foundational academic skills, career and technical education coursework, and on-the-job learning experience.
qa_results.stakeholders: Adult Maryland residents who do not hold a high school diploma and have withdrawn from compulsory schooling, as well as small businesses and employers seeking skilled workers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Labor can implement and publicize the MDiplomaWorks Pathway using existing resources, and the Maryland State Department of Education can collaborate within existing resources. State revenues and State education aid are not affected because participants are not enrolled in public school systems. Local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was introduced as departmental legislation by the Maryland Department of Labor. It tasks the department with establishing, approving components of, and adopting regulations for the new MDiplomaWorks pathway, as well as publicizing information about the pathway in 2027 and 2028.

The Maryland State Board of Education is required to jointly adopt regulations with the Secretary of Labor to award high school diplomas through the MDiplomaWorks pathway, and MSDE collaborates on its development.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts contracts entered into by the Office of International Trade in the Department of Commerce related to international business activities from state-level prohibitions on certain contract clauses (such as indemnification, binding arbitration, and out-of-state venue provisions).
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of International Trade within the Maryland Department of Commerce
qa_results.stakeholders: The Maryland Department of Commerce Office of International Trade, international vendors, and entities contracting with Maryland for international trade and business development activities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact as it codifies existing practice to allow the Office of International Trade to continue standard international contracting operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 300 is a departmental bill requested by the Department of Commerce. It directly impacts the department by exempting contracts entered into by its Office of International Trade from certain statutory prohibitions on state contract provisions.

The Department of General Services serves as the state's central procurement authority overseeing state contracting standards under the State Finance and Procurement Article and was consulted as an information source on this legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Provides for operational command and control of Maryland Military Department personnel during State active duty, placing members under the command of the Adjutant General or a designated National Guard officer regardless of whether the Adjutant General or designee is serving in State active duty or in a federal status in which the Governor is Commander in Chief.
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the Maryland Military Department, including the Maryland National Guard, Maryland Defense Force, and State operations personnel called to State active duty.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill codifies existing operational practice within the Maryland Military Department to clarify chain-of-command authority during emergency responses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the head of the Maryland Military Department, the Adjutant General is directly granted statutory operational command and control over all members of the department during State active duty, regardless of whether the Adjutant General is in State active duty or in a federal status where the Governor is Commander in Chief.

The bill explicitly governs the operational command and control structure of National Guard personnel during State active duty mobilizations and authorizes designated National Guard officers to exercise operational command and control.

The Governor serves as Commander-in-Chief of the state militia, holds the authority to order units into State active duty, and retains supreme command when military leadership operates under dual-status federal authorities.

The statute amended by this bill provides that ranking militia officers placed into State active duty under this command structure may, under exigent circumstances and by order of the Governor, direct and coordinate operations with the Department of State Police.

qa_results.bill_summary: Enacts the Jack Fitzgerald Price Transparency Act, prohibiting motor vehicle manufacturers, distributors, and factory branches from taking adverse action against a vehicle dealer for disclosing on the dealer's website that an advertised vehicle price is the manufacturer's minimum allowable advertised price and that the dealer may offer a lower price, provided the dealer does not violate laws regarding deceptive advertising or public protection.
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed motor vehicle dealers, vehicle manufacturers, distributors, factory branches, and prospective motor vehicle buyers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration regulates and licenses motor vehicle manufacturers, distributors, factory branches, and dealers under Title 15 of the Maryland Transportation Article, which is amended by this bill.

As the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, the Department of Transportation oversees the administration and enforcement of Maryland vehicle laws governing vehicle dealers and manufacturers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Maryland business entities, including corporations, limited liability companies, limited liability partnerships, and limited partnerships, to use an address supplied by a commercial mail receiving agency under a valid agreement conforming to U.S. Postal Service regulations as their designated principal office.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland business entities (corporations, LLCs, LLPs, and LPs) seeking alternative principal office locations, and commercial mail receiving agencies offering address and mailbox services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues increase minimally in FY 2027 from existing business entities paying the $25 filing fee (and optional expedited fees) to update their principal office addresses with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). The bill does not materially impact SDAT operations or finances, and there is no local government fiscal impact.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires local school systems to identify and address accessibility issues for individuals with disabilities as part of regular school safety evaluations. Additionally, local school systems must include in their annual safety reports to the Maryland Center for School Safety (MCSS) any instances where a facility became inaccessible for a student with a disability in a way that could impede evacuation or emergency response, while establishing confidentiality protections for such reports.
qa_results.responsible_party: Local school systems and the Maryland Center for School Safety (MCSS)
qa_results.stakeholders: Public school students with disabilities, local school systems, public school staff, and emergency responders.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not materially affected. The Maryland Center for School Safety can implement the bill's provisions using existing budgeted resources, and local school systems are expected to absorb the additional evaluation and reporting requirements without requiring additional funding. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Center for School Safety (MCSS) is the primary state entity responsible for receiving and reviewing the required safety evaluations, emergency plans, and annual reports detailing instances where school facilities became inaccessible for students with disabilities.
The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees the state's public school systems and emergency planning guidelines, and MCSS is housed as an independent unit within the department.

Under the statute amended by the bill, designated school safety coordinators must coordinate with the Interagency Commission on School Construction's facility assessment process when identifying facility issues impacting safety and accessibility.

The Department of Disabilities coordinates state policies regarding accessibility and accommodations for individuals with disabilities in public facilities, aligning with the subject matter of the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill prohibits residential landlords who evaluate financial information from refusing to rent to prospective tenants receiving income-based housing subsidies based on income, credit score, lack of credit score, or adverse credit history from periods when they did not have a subsidy. Such refusals are established as discriminatory housing practices subject to enforcement by the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights. Additionally, landlords owning six or more residential rental units must offer tenants the option to have positive rental payment history reported to at least one consumer reporting agency.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Commission on Civil Rights and the Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential rental property owners and landlords (especially those owning six or more units), residential tenants, prospective tenants receiving income-based housing vouchers or subsidies, and consumer reporting agencies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights and the Department of Housing and Community Development can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. The bill does not significantly impact court workloads or the Office of Administrative Hearings, and does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates violations of the new prohibitions on refusing to rent to individuals using income-based housing subsidies as discriminatory housing practices, making them subject to enforcement and investigation by the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights.

The bill mandates that the Secretary of Housing and Community Development adopt regulations specifying the form and requirements for the mandatory offer of positive rental payment history reporting provided to tenants.
The Judiciary could see civil actions or appeals arising from alleged discriminatory housing practices under the bill, though the workload impact is anticipated to be minimal.
The Office of Administrative Hearings conducts administrative hearings for contested discriminatory housing practice cases referred by the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill permanently repeals the June 30, 2026 sunset date on provisions authorizing county boards of education to transport certain public school students using vehicles other than standard Type I or Type II yellow school buses when standard buses cannot reasonably be provided. It also requires the Maryland State Department of Education, in consultation with county boards of education and the Motor Vehicle Administration, to review regulations regarding alternative student transportation vehicles and drivers and report recommendations to the General Assembly by January 1, 2027.
qa_results.stakeholders: Public school students (including students with disabilities, homeless youth, foster care children, preschool-age students, and dual enrollment students), county boards of education/local school systems, transportation contractors, and alternative vehicle drivers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operational requirements for the study and reporting can be handled within existing budgeted resources by the Maryland State Department of Education and the Motor Vehicle Administration. Local school system expenditures for student transportation may decrease or avoid potential cost increases beyond FY 2026 by maintaining flexibility to use alternative vehicles instead of acquiring or operating standard Type I and Type II school buses; specific dollar amounts are indeterminate.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary agency tasked with reviewing regulations regarding alternative student transportation vehicles and drivers, consulting with stakeholders, and submitting a report to legislative committees by January 1, 2027.
The bill explicitly requires MSDE to consult with the MVA to review minimum safety standards and regulations for alternative student transportation vehicles and drivers.
MDOT is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, which is statutorily mandated to participate in the required regulatory review.
The bill mandates that MSDE examine the PSC's regulations for transportation network operators to determine whether student transportation rules can be aligned with PSC standards.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the governing body of Anne Arundel County to enact a local property tax credit for real property located within a designated Rural Legacy Area whose owner has sold development rights under the Rural Legacy Program.
qa_results.stakeholders: Anne Arundel County property owners who have sold development rights under the Rural Legacy Program and the Anne Arundel County government.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Anne Arundel County property tax revenues are estimated to decrease by approximately $27,800 to $27,825 annually beginning in fiscal year 2027, to the extent the county implements the optional credit for the 21 currently eligible properties (with additional decreases if more easements are acquired). County expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a local property tax credit for properties within a Rural Legacy Area where development rights have been sold under the Rural Legacy Program, which is a state conservation program administered under Title 5, Subtitle 9A of the Natural Resources Article by the Department of Natural Resources.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the deadline from July 1, 2026, to January 15, 2027, for the Maryland Department of the Environment to submit a comprehensive study and report on the synthetic turf industry, existing synthetic turf fields, and synthetic turf disposal practices in the State.
qa_results.stakeholders: Synthetic turf manufacturers, retailers, and industry representatives; synthetic turf users including local governments, county public school systems, higher education institutions, and professional sports organizations; and local environmental and community groups.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Extending the deadline for the Maryland Department of the Environment to complete and submit the synthetic turf study and report does not materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly applies to the Department of the Environment (MDE), extending the deadline from July 1, 2026, to January 15, 2027, for the department to conduct a study and submit a report regarding the synthetic turf industry, existing fields, and disposal methods to the General Assembly.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the composition of the 15-member Maryland Health Care Commission by reducing the number of members without a connection to health care providers or payors from nine to eight and requiring one member to be a hospital administrator. It also reduces from five to four the minimum number of members required to be residents of different counties with a population of 300,000 or more.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor of Maryland and the Maryland Health Care Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the Maryland Health Care Commission, hospital administrators, health care providers, and Maryland health care consumers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact, as modifying the membership requirements of the commission does not affect governmental revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 322 directly alters the statutory composition of the Maryland Health Care Commission by adding a hospital administrator and modifying consumer and geographic representation requirements for its 15 members.

The Maryland Health Care Commission is an independent regulatory commission housed within the Maryland Department of Health, making changes to the Commission's governing structure relevant to the Department.
The Governor is responsible for appointing members to the Commission and must adhere to the bill's updated membership criteria and county population representation quotas.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and managing appointments to state boards and commissions, and will need to apply the revised membership qualifications when filling vacancies on the Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the composition of the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board by removing a seat for a certified nonpublic school classroom teacher nominated by the Association of Independent Schools and adding a seat nominated by the Maryland Association of Nonpublic Special Education Facilities (MANSEF), resulting in two MANSEF representatives: one licensed special education teacher currently providing classroom instruction and one administrator or supervisory staff member.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor of Maryland and the Maryland State Board of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board, the Maryland Association of Nonpublic Special Education Facilities, the Association of Independent Schools, and nonpublic special education teachers and administrators.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal or operational impact. Revenues and expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the membership composition of the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board (PSTEB), which governs educator certification and standards, includes the State Superintendent of Schools, and is staffed by the Maryland State Department of Education/State Board of Education.

The Governor is statutorily responsible for appointing the members of the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board with the advice and consent of the Senate, subject to the revised composition requirements.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting, managing, and processing nominations and appointments to state boards and commissions, including the modified seats on the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board is a state regulatory and advisory board within the executive branch whose statutory membership requirements are altered by this bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Center for School Safety to develop and administer an anonymous reporting system for school and student safety concerns, provide operational guidelines and staff training, and mandates participation by local school systems by July 1, 2027, unless they operate a substantially similar system. The bill also shields reporting system records from public disclosure under the Maryland Public Information Act.
qa_results.stakeholders: Public school students, teachers, school personnel, parents, local school systems, and the public
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state or local fiscal impact because the bill codifies existing practice; the Maryland Center for School Safety already operates the anonymous Safe Schools Maryland reporting system and local school systems already comply with its requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Center for School Safety (MCSS) to develop and administer a statewide anonymous reporting system for school safety concerns, develop operational guidelines and procedures, and provide training sessions to school personnel.

The Maryland Center for School Safety is established as an independent unit within the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), which oversees Maryland's public education system and the local school systems required to participate in the reporting system.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the membership of the Board of Community College Trustees for Baltimore County by reducing the total number of members from 15 to 11, consisting of two at-large members and one member from each of Baltimore County's nine councilmanic districts, while outlining the transition and staggering of trustee terms.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor of Maryland and the Board of Community College Trustees for Baltimore County
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the Board of Community College Trustees for Baltimore County, Baltimore County residents, and the Community College of Baltimore County community
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no State fiscal impact. Locally, it results in a minimal decrease in reimbursement expenditures for Board of Community College trustee members beginning in FY 2027 due to the smaller board size. Local revenues are unaffected, and specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the composition of the Board of Community College Trustees for Baltimore County, whose members are appointed by the Governor with the advice and consent of the Senate.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments to state and local boards and commissions, which includes the Board of Community College Trustees for Baltimore County.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires applicants for appointment as bicounty commissioners in Prince George's County, as well as the chief administrative officer of the county, to submit financial disclosure statements to the Prince George's County Office of Ethics and Accountability. The Office of Ethics and Accountability is tasked with retaining the statements for the duration of a commissioner's term, returning statements to unappointed applicants, notifying the State Ethics Commission to delete electronic filings of unappointed applicants, and managing public examination and copying of the statements.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prince George's County Office of Ethics and Accountability and the State Ethics Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants for appointment and commissioners of bicounty commissions (such as the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission and Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission) from Prince George's County, and members of the public examining disclosure statements.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact because it applies solely to bicounty commissions. In addition, it does not materially affect local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the administration of financial disclosure statements for bicounty commissioners and applicants, which are filed electronically with the State Ethics Commission. It specifies that upon notification from the Prince George's County Office of Ethics and Accountability or Montgomery County, the State Ethics Commission must delete statements of unappointed applicants, and outlines procedures for statement maintenance and public inspection.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands criminal prohibitions on sexual activity by law enforcement officers to prohibit an officer assigned as a school resource officer from engaging in sexual contact, vaginal intercourse, or a sexual act with a student enrolled in that school. Violations are classified as a misdemeanor punishable by up to three years imprisonment and/or a maximum fine of $3,000.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary, local State's Attorneys, and State and local law enforcement agencies
qa_results.stakeholders: School resource officers, law enforcement officers assigned to schools, and enrolled students at schools with assigned resource officers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. Potential fine revenues and incarceration expenditures are not expected to have a material financial effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly references Section 7-1501 of the Education Article, which defines school resource officers and falls under the statutory purview of the Maryland Center for School Safety, the state entity responsible for statewide school safety standards, training, and coordination of school safety personnel.

The Maryland State Department of Education oversees the state's public school system, where school resource officers are placed via memorandums of understanding, and the bill establishes criminal protections for enrolled students.
The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the judicial branch, which will process and adjudicate any new criminal misdemeanor charges and trials arising under the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent defendants charged with criminal offenses, including the misdemeanor offenses established by this bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department is responsible for correctional facilities and community supervision, which could house or supervise individuals convicted under the misdemeanor penalty of up to 3 years imprisonment.

As the state's primary law enforcement agency, its sworn personnel and allied agency coordinators are subject to the statutory conduct prohibitions established for law enforcement officers serving in school resource officer capacities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the number of voting members on the Maryland Legal Services Corporation Board of Directors from 9 to 12, requiring 7 members to be admitted Maryland lawyers and 5 to be nonlawyers, and increases the number of votes required to remove a voting member from 7 to 9.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Legal Services Corporation and the Governor of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Members and prospective members of the Maryland Legal Services Corporation Board of Directors, Maryland attorneys, and organizations and low-income individuals served by MLSC legal aid programs.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact. Altering the composition of the board does not affect State operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the Board of Directors of the Maryland Legal Services Corporation from 9 to 12 members, all of whom are appointed by the Governor with the advice and consent of the Senate.

The Office of Appointments is responsible for recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointees for state boards and commissions, and will handle the additional board seats created by this legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands and alters the jurisdiction of the Department of General Services and the Maryland Capitol Police, extending their authority to enforce criminal, parking, and motor vehicle laws statewide as well as within 2,000 feet of State-owned or State-leased buildings and grounds, subject to specific notice requirements to local and state law enforcement agencies and an agreement before operating in Baltimore City.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of General Services (Maryland Capitol Police)
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Capitol Police officers, state employees, public officials, local law enforcement agencies, and individuals on or near State-owned or State-leased properties.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Altering and expanding the jurisdiction of the Department of General Services and the Maryland Capitol Police is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters and expands the statutory jurisdiction and law enforcement authority of the Maryland Capitol Police, which is an operational unit within the Department of General Services.

The bill requires the Maryland Capitol Police to provide advance notice to the Secretary of State Police before conducting statewide investigations or enforcement actions, as well as post-enforcement notification to local barracks commanders where the State Police provides general law enforcement.

The bill explicitly mandates notification to the Chief of Police of the Maryland Transit Administration Police Force when statewide enforcement or investigations are exercised by Maryland Capitol Police as applicable.

The bill specifically requires notification to the Superintendent of the Maryland Department of Natural Resources Police when Maryland Capitol Police officers exercise statewide enforcement powers as applicable.

The bill requires notification to the Chief of Police of the Maryland Department of Health Secured Transport and Investigation Unit following the exercise of certain statewide investigative or enforcement powers.
The bill maintains the Board of Public Works' authority to designate public improvements or grounds over which the Department of General Services holds jurisdiction and police authority.
As the parent department of the Maryland Transit Administration, MDOT is impacted through coordination and required notification to its transit police force.

qa_results.bill_summary: Enters Maryland into the School Psychologist Interstate Licensure Compact, establishing a pathway for licensed school psychologists to obtain equivalent multistate licenses to provide psychological services across member states, while establishing the School Psychologist Interstate Licensure Compact Commission to govern and administer the compact.
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed school psychologists, active military members and their spouses practicing school psychology, and public and nonpublic school students and educational systems.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Maryland State Department of Education increase by $30,000 in FY 2027 for one-time IT modifications to the licensure system and by $7,000 in FY 2027 and annually thereafter for compact participation fees. A potential minimal increase in fee revenues may occur from licensing fees and criminal background checks. There is no direct local fiscal impact, though it may facilitate recruitment of school psychologists by local school systems.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary licensing authority in Maryland for school psychologists. The department will implement the compact, serve on the compact commission, upgrade its educator licensure portal, investigate complaints, and pay annual compact participation fees.
The bill officially enters Maryland into the School Psychologist Interstate Licensure Compact and establishes membership in the multistate School Psychologist Interstate Licensure Compact Commission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The compact requires applicants to undergo criminal background checks, which are administered and processed with fee collection by the Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository (CJIS-CR) within DPSCS.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the educational qualifications for a forestry license by requiring applicants to have graduated from a four-year forestry curriculum approved by the State Board of Foresters and accredited by the Society of American Foresters or an equivalent entity, or to have education (such as a comparable graduate or international degree) determined by the board to be substantially equivalent.
qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants seeking a Maryland forestry license, licensed foresters, and individuals with forestry degrees, including international or comparable graduate degree holders.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Foresters can implement the bill with existing resources, resulting in no material effect on State revenues and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Foresters is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing. The bill alters the statutory educational qualifications and accreditation standards required for an applicant to obtain a forestry license issued by the Board.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires recipients of funding from the Strategic Demolition Fund or the Baltimore Vacants Reinvestment Initiative for single-family homeownership projects to provide information on HUD-approved housing counseling services to prospective residents before executing a purchase contract. The bill also establishes an ongoing annual state appropriation beginning in fiscal year 2028 for community development organizations to partner with HUD-approved housing counseling agencies.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Prospective home purchasers/residents of state-funded single-family housing projects, community development organizations, and HUD-approved housing counseling agencies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in fiscal 2028, state general fund expenditures increase by $90,000 annually due to a mandated appropriation for community development organizations partnering with approved housing counseling agencies. The Department of Housing and Community Development can administer the funds with existing resources. State revenues are unaffected, and local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary implementing agency. The bill places conditions on recipients of DHCD's Strategic Demolition Fund and Baltimore Vacants Reinvestment Initiative funding to provide housing counseling information, and DHCD will administer and disburse the mandated $90,000 annual appropriation to community development organizations beginning in FY 2028.

DBM is responsible for state budget development and fiscal planning, which includes incorporating the bill's statutory mandated appropriation of $90,000 annually starting in FY 2028 into the executive budget.

The bill mandates that the Governor appropriate $90,000 in the annual state budget in FY 2028 and each fiscal year thereafter for community development organizations to partner with housing counseling agencies.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 347 establishes that certain public safety employees—including paid firefighters, firefighting instructors, rescue squad members, advanced life support unit members, and sworn members of the Office of the State Fire Marshal—who suffer from hypertension are presumed to have an occupational disease suffered in the line of duty and to be disabled for workers' compensation purposes. To qualify, the individual must be diagnosed with hypertension, have been prescribed medication for at least 90 consecutive days, have completed at least two years of cumulative service, and be currently employed in a covered position at the time of the claim.
qa_results.stakeholders: Paid firefighters, firefighting instructors, rescue squad members, advanced life support unit members, sworn members of the Office of the State Fire Marshal, and state and local public safety employers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government expenditures may increase minimally beginning in fiscal year 2027 due to the expansion of occupational disease presumptions for hypertension. Expenditures for Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company may also increase minimally to cover additional workers' compensation payments, offset potentially by higher premiums. State and local revenues are not affected, and specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 347 directly amends the Maryland Workers' Compensation Law by establishing a new presumption of occupational disease and disablement for hypertension. The bill explicitly directs the Commission to define 'authorized provider' by regulation and will govern the claims adjudicated by the Commission.

Operating as Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company, the entity acts as the third-party administrator handling workers' compensation claims for State of Maryland employees and insures local entities. The fiscal note specifically evaluates Chesapeake's claims history and potential increase in expenditures and premiums resulting from the expanded presumption.

The Office of the State Fire Marshal is a unit within the Department of State Police, and its sworn members are expressly included among the public safety personnel covered by the expanded occupational disease presumption.

The bill explicitly provides that, except as otherwise specified in a collective bargaining agreement, an individual qualifying for compensation under this provision may not be eligible to receive disability retirement benefits for the same condition, directly impacting disability benefit administration by the Agency.

MDOT employs covered fire and rescue personnel (such as airport rescue and firefighting personnel through the Maryland Aviation Administration at BWI Airport) and was consulted for the fiscal analysis of the bill.

The MAA operates Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport and employs career airport firefighters and emergency response personnel who are covered under the bill's provisions for airport authorities.
The Subsequent Injury Fund reviews and investigates workers' compensation claims involving pre-existing conditions and was an information source for the legislation's fiscal and policy note.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the expiration date of an alcoholic beverages racetrack license for premises in the 5200 block of Park Heights Avenue (Pimlico Race Course) in Baltimore City through July 1, 2029, in order to permit the completion of renovations as well as an ownership transfer and license renewal.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Pimlico Race Course operators/owners, event attendees, and Baltimore City alcoholic beverage regulators
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact. Baltimore City local government expenditures and revenues are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcoholic beverages industry and oversees state alcohol laws and taxation, although local licensing enforcement is handled by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners.
The bill directly applies to the racetrack license at the Pimlico Race Course premises located in the 5200 block of Park Heights Avenue during its ongoing renovations and transfer of ownership.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 351 creates a civil cause of action allowing an aggrieved party or the Office of the Attorney General to sue a judicial/covered officer who, under color of law, deprives an individual of rights, privileges, or immunities secured under law. It also permits the Attorney General, State Prosecutors, or State's Attorneys to direct law enforcement agencies to gather and retain identifying digital data regarding an officer accused of misconduct, accessible to plaintiffs only via court order.
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals alleging constitutional violations by officers, covered/judicial officers authorized to enforce federal law, state and local law enforcement agencies, and litigation attorneys.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to affect State liability or materially impact local finances. General fund revenues may increase indeterminately if the Office of the Attorney General is awarded damages, reasonable fees, or court costs in actions filed under the bill. The Office of the Attorney General can handle any workload with existing resources, and potential staff needs for the State Treasurer's Office are deemed speculative.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes the Office of the Attorney General to initiate civil actions for damages, declaratory, and injunctive relief against judicial officers for constitutional rights deprivations, as well as to direct law enforcement agencies to collect and retain identifying digital data upon receiving misconduct complaints.

The bill explicitly authorizes a State Prosecutor, upon receipt of a complaint of judicial officer misconduct, to direct appropriate state or local law enforcement agencies to gather and securely retain identifying digital data.

The bill creates a new civil cause of action for deprivation of constitutional rights under the Courts Article and requires a court order to obtain identifying digital data, directly impacting judicial administration and caseloads.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police may be directed by prosecutors or the Attorney General to gather and securely retain specialized identifying digital data (such as cell tower, location, license plate, and facial recognition data) regarding targeted officers.

The State Treasurer's Office administers the Maryland Tort Claims Act and the State Insurance Trust Fund. The fiscal note highlights the office's concerns regarding potential claims volume, liability, and the possible need for additional claims adjusters.

The Department operates the Natural Resources Police, a state law enforcement agency that could fall under directives to gather and retain digital evidence, and was consulted as an information source for the bill's fiscal note.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 357 requires municipalities that maintain a website to prominently display information regarding upcoming regular and special elections, including election dates and offices to be voted on. It also requires municipalities to report the date and offices for their next regular municipal election when submitting election results to the State Board of Elections, and mandates that the State Board of Elections display these upcoming elections and list municipalities that have not yet reported on its website.
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland municipalities and municipal voters and residents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the Maryland State Board of Elections to receive reports on upcoming municipal election dates and offices from municipalities, and to prominently display on its website a list of reported upcoming elections as well as a list of municipalities that have not yet reported.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts sales made at in-person elementary or secondary school book fairs from the Maryland sales and use tax, including book fairs held in partnership with third-party vendors, provided the net proceeds are used solely for the educational benefit of the school or its students.
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland elementary and secondary schools, students, teachers, parent-teacher organizations (PTAs/PTOs), and third-party book fair vendors.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues decrease by an indeterminate amount beginning in FY 2027, estimated at approximately $150,000 annually based on certain assumptions regarding book fair frequency and sales volume. State expenditures and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the state's principal tax collector responsible for administering and collecting sales and use taxes. This bill creates a specific sales and use tax exemption for in-person school book fairs, impacting state sales tax revenues and requiring the agency to implement the exemption guidelines.

The Maryland State Department of Education oversees elementary and secondary education in the state. The bill directly impacts fundraising activities, schools, and affiliated parent-teacher organizations operating book fairs on school grounds.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the eligibility criteria for a local option property tax credit on urban agricultural property by removing acreage limits and the requirement that the property be within a priority funding area, defining it instead as real property not assessed as agricultural land. It expands qualifying urban agricultural purposes to include indoor/outdoor crop production, value-added products, beekeeping, livestock, composting, controlled-environment farming, pollinator habitats, and agritourism, while requiring local jurisdictions to provide at least one year's advance notice and opportunity for comment before terminating the credit.
qa_results.responsible_party: The governing bodies of Maryland counties and municipal corporations, including the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City
qa_results.stakeholders: Urban farmers, agricultural property owners, small agricultural businesses, and local county and municipal governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: County and municipal property tax revenues may decrease by a minimal amount beginning in fiscal 2027 to the extent local governments grant the credit and the expanded criteria allow additional properties to qualify. Local expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 359 expands the statutory definitions and scope of urban agricultural purposes and activities—including beekeeping, livestock, hydroponics, agritourism, and value-added agricultural production—which align with the Department of Agriculture's mission to support and promote agricultural viability and farming initiatives across Maryland.
The bill repeals the requirement that eligible urban agricultural property be located within a Priority Funding Area (PFA), a land-use designation overseen and mapped by the Department of Planning.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Maryland counties to establish a local grant program for residents who qualify for the State child tax credit, specifically targeting low-income taxpayers with qualified dependent children under age 6 or under age 17 with disabilities. Counties must reimburse the Comptroller for reasonable expenses incurred in sharing information necessary to administer the program.
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income Maryland taxpayers with eligible dependent young children or children with disabilities, as well as county governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not directly affected, as participating counties must reimburse the Comptroller for any reasonable implementation expenses. Local expenditures may increase beginning as early as FY 2027 depending on whether and to what extent individual counties choose to enact local child grant programs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires counties that provide the local child grant to reimburse the Comptroller for reasonable expenses incurred in providing the county with the necessary taxpayer information to implement the grant.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill defines the terms "interment" and "interment location" for State veterans' cemeteries and requires the Department of Veterans and Military Families to provide an outer burial receptacle or columbarium niche and marker at no cost (instead of a grave liner) for eligible veterans, spouses, or dependents. It also updates terminology across Maryland law regarding burial and interment.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Veterans and Military Families
qa_results.stakeholders: Eligible military veterans, qualified reserve members, their eligible spouses and dependents, veterans service organizations, and funeral and crematory operators.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the Department of Veterans and Military Families (DVMF) operations regarding State veterans' cemeteries, requiring DVMF to provide outer burial receptacles or columbarium niches and markers at no cost and receive unclaimed remains of veterans and eligible dependents.

The bill amends Title 5 of the Business Regulation Article, which governs cemetery oversight and regulation administered by the Department of Labor, modifying definitions and procedures for handling unclaimed veteran remains.

The bill amends Title 7 of the Health Occupations Article concerning funeral establishments, crematories, and morticians regulated under boards within the Department of Health, updating requirements for handling and reporting unclaimed veteran remains.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to DVMF and the regulatory boards involved, and enforces civil penalty actions under the veterans benefits services provisions amended in the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires hospitals with emergency departments to screen, stabilize, or appropriately transfer pregnant patients presenting with emergency pregnancy-related medical conditions. It mandates that hospitals permit the termination of a pregnancy when medically necessary to stabilize the patient, protects health care providers and employees from adverse retaliatory actions, and establishes civil penalties for negligent violations.
qa_results.stakeholders: Pregnant patients presenting with emergency conditions, hospitals with emergency departments, treating healthcare practitioners, and hospital employees
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill generally codifies existing practice and can be implemented by the Maryland Department of Health with existing budgeted resources. State general fund revenues and local revenues may increase minimally from civil penalties imposed on hospitals for violations in cases heard in the District Court and circuit courts, respectively.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary regulatory and enforcement agency for the bill. It is directly responsible for adjudicating potential violations by hospitals, imposing civil penalties of up to $50,000, and coordinating fine assessments or refunds with federal EMTALA enforcement actions.

The Maryland Judiciary is affected as civil penalty cases resulting from violations of the bill may be heard in the District Court and Circuit Courts, resulting in potential court filings and minimal general fund revenues.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS regulates and coordinates the statewide emergency medical services system and emergency hospital patient transfers, both of which are central components of the emergency stabilization and transfer procedures governed by the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires the State Acupuncture Board to make proof of license renewal available to licensees rather than issuing paper renewal certificates. It also prohibits employing an unlicensed individual to practice acupuncture or aiding and abetting the unauthorized practice of acupuncture, establishing criminal and civil penalties for violations, and updates the name of the relevant accrediting body for acupuncture programs.
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed acupuncturists, individuals and businesses employing acupuncture practitioners, and consumers of acupuncture services in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, any changes in the State Acupuncture Board's workload can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. Although civil fines (up to $10,000) and criminal fines are remitted to the State General Fund, the penalty provisions do not have a material impact on State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Acupuncture Board is an occupational licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill directly alters the board's administrative licensing renewal procedures and authorizes it to assess civil penalties for the unlawful employment or aiding and abetting of unlicensed acupuncturists.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands the scope and authorized duties of physician assistants (PAs), certified nurse-midwives, and licensed certified midwives to achieve parity with other health care practitioners in various statutory areas. Key provisions authorize PAs to sign certificates of competency for guardianship petitions, participate in voluntary mental health admissions, petition for emergency evaluations, prescribe and dispense emergency epinephrine, certify individuals for the Attendant Care Program, and sign State employee sick leave certificates. Additionally, health maintenance organizations (HMOs) must allow members the opportunity to select PAs or midwives as primary care providers, a PA is added to the Statewide Advisory Commission on Immunizations, and the Maryland Health Care Commission is required to study emergency department lengths of stay for involuntary admission evaluations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and Maryland Health Care Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Physician assistants, certified nurse-midwives, licensed certified midwives, HMO enrollees, pregnant incarcerated individuals, individuals undergoing mental health evaluation or guardianship proceedings, and health care facilities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the Maryland Health Care Commission can carry out the required data review and reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local government fiscal impact. The bill may have a meaningful positive operational effect on small business health care practices employing physician assistants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Health Care Commission to review emergency department length-of-stay data for involuntary admissions, evaluate hospital overnight shifts staffed with physician assistants, and submit a report with findings and recommendations by November 1, 2026.

The bill makes extensive changes across the Health - General Article affecting programs within MDH, including emergency evaluation fee payments, the Emergency and Allergy Treatment Program, HMO quality-of-care regulations, and the Statewide Advisory Commission on Immunizations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Correctional Services Article to expand the categories of health care practitioners who may authorize the admission of a pregnant incarcerated individual to a correctional infirmary.

The bill amends provisions governing the Attendant Care Program, allowing physician assistants to certify that an individual is at risk of nursing facility placement to qualify for attendant care services.

The bill amends the State Personnel and Pensions Article by permitting State employees taking five or more consecutive days of sick leave to submit certificates of illness or disability signed by a physician assistant.
The bill alters judicial procedures in guardianship cases by permitting certificates of competency signed by a physician assistant to accompany petitions for guardianship of a disabled person.
The bill amends the Human Services Article regarding certification requirements under the Attendant Care Program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds a physician assistant member from the Maryland Academy of Physician Assistants to the Statewide Advisory Commission on Immunizations.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill clarifies that applicants for optometrist licensure or reinstatement must pass all sections of each part of an examination, and requires the State Board of Examiners in Optometry to set passing scores accordingly. It also limits the duration an optometrist can remain on inactive status to no more than six consecutive years, and repeals provisions requiring the Board to directly administer examinations and collect a reexamination fee.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Examiners in Optometry
qa_results.stakeholders: Optometrists and applicants seeking optometry licensure or license reinstatement in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not substantively change board activities or operations. State Board of Examiners in Optometry special fund expenditures and revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Examiners in Optometry is a health occupations licensing board housed under the Maryland Department of Health (MDH). The bill directly modifies statutory requirements governing the Board's examination requirements, reexamination fees, and inactive status durations for optometrists.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes supervisory employees of the Baltimore County Public Library to form, join, and participate in collective bargaining, and establishes up to two separate collective bargaining units for library staff: one for supervisory employees and one for nonsupervisory employees.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore County Public Library Board of Library Trustees
qa_results.stakeholders: Supervisory employees and staff of the Baltimore County Public Library, employee bargaining organizations, and Baltimore County government.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Baltimore County Public Library expenditures may increase minimally to hire outside mediators or due to potential wage and benefit increases resulting from collective bargaining agreements; payroll deductions for dues and service fees can be handled with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Library Agency provides coordination, funding, and oversight support for Maryland's 24 public library systems, including the Baltimore County Public Library system affected by this collective bargaining legislation.

The Public Employee Relations Board administers and standardizes collective bargaining across Maryland public sector entities and was consulted regarding the creation and restructuring of these public library bargaining units.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires certain health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations that provide coverage for cancer chemotherapy to also provide coverage for scalp cooling systems used to preserve hair during chemotherapy treatment.
qa_results.stakeholders: Cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy, health insurance carriers, and state and local government employee health plans.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Maryland Insurance Administration special fund revenues increase minimally in FY 2027 from $125 rate and form filing fees. State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program expenditures increase by an indeterminate but likely nominal amount, estimated between $11,600 and $302,800 beginning in FY 2027. Local government expenditures may increase for those offering fully insured health plans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIA is the primary regulatory agency responsible for overseeing health insurance carriers, approving policy form and rate filings reflecting the new coverage requirement, handling consumer complaints, and collecting associated filing fees.

DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which generally covers mandated health insurance benefits and will incur an increase in health expenditures to cover scalp cooling systems.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill repeals the requirement that an entity hold a concentrated animal feeding operation (CAFO) discharge permit from the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) prior to starting construction on a new CAFO, as well as the ban on issuing a permit to violators of that requirement. Additionally, when the general discharge permit for animal feeding operations (AFOs) is administratively extended, MDE may authorize construction to begin on a new AFO through an approval process requiring proof of compliance with the extended permit and other applicable laws.
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners and operators of animal feeding operations (AFOs) and concentrated animal feeding operations (CAFOs) seeking to construct new facilities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State finances or operations, and it has no local fiscal impact. It may provide a positive operational impact to small business AFOs by enabling new construction to begin while an updated general discharge permit is developed.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the Environment Article and authorizes the Department of the Environment (MDE) to establish an approval process allowing construction on animal feeding operations when a general discharge permit is administratively extended.

The bill directly affects agricultural operations and animal feeding operations (AFOs/CAFOs) in Maryland, which fall under the scope of the agricultural community and practices supported and regulated in coordination with the Department of Agriculture.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill removes the age cap (previously under 16) for children in residential child care programs who receive educational support, applying requirements to all children in care who are at least five years old. It requires program operators to keep children enrolled in their previous school unless determined not in their best interest, mandates specific educational and homework supports, and specifies required curriculum topics for training programs for certified residential child and youth care practitioners.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Human Services and the State Board for the Certification of Residential Child Care Program Professionals
qa_results.stakeholders: Children aged five and older placed in residential child care facilities, operators of residential child care programs, and certified residential child and youth care practitioners.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $25,000 in FY 2027 for the Department of Human Services to conduct staff training, update regulations, and modify provider contracts; future compliance monitoring will require an indeterminate but minimal amount. The Maryland Department of Health, Department of Juvenile Services, and the certification board can implement the bill with existing resources. There is no effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHS licenses residential child care programs and oversees local departments of social services, which are tasked by the bill with determining whether remaining in an existing school is in a child's best interest. DHS also incurs a fiscal impact of $25,000 in FY 2027 to update regulations, complete staff training, and modify provider contracts.

MDH licenses residential child care programs and houses the State Board for the Certification of Residential Child Care Program Professionals, which is responsible for establishing the updated training and curriculum requirements for residential child and youth care practitioners mandated by the bill.

DJS licenses residential child care programs subject to the bill's new educational support standards and practitioner requirements, and must monitor its contracted and licensed facilities for compliance.

The bill amends the Education Article concerning school enrollment continuity, homework support, and coordination between residential child care programs and local school systems regarding Individualized Education Programs (IEPs) and Behavioral Intervention Plans (BIPs).

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the reporting deadline and termination date for a workgroup convened by the State Retirement Agency to study member service transfers between State and local retirement and pension systems, setting a new reporting deadline of October 1, 2026, and terminating the workgroup on June 30, 2027.
qa_results.stakeholders: Members and retirees of Maryland State and local retirement and pension systems who transfer service credit between systems
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Extending the reporting and termination dates of the workgroup has no State or local fiscal impact, as it does not affect governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the State Retirement Agency with convening and staffing the workgroup, extending its reporting deadline and statutory termination date to allow additional time to study service transfers between State and local retirement systems.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill extends the operational timeline and final reporting date of the stakeholder workgroup convened to study transfer of service between State and local pension systems.
The State Retirement Agency is required by the bill to submit the final findings and legislative recommendations of the workgroup to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters statutory terminology related to State parks that preserve and interpret the history of underrepresented populations by removing the word "historical" from general references, and specifically renaming "Freedman's State Historical Park" and "Port of Deposit State Historical Park" to "Freedman's State Park" and "Port Deposit State Park," respectively, while maintaining their underlying historical purpose.
qa_results.stakeholders: Visitors to Maryland State parks, local communities and advisory bodies in Montgomery and Cecil counties, and the Department of Natural Resources.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no direct effect on State or local finances because signage and publications have not yet been produced for Freedman’s State Historical Park or Port of Deposit State Historical Park.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Natural Resources Article governing the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) and its administration of the State park system, updating statutory terminology from 'State historical parks' to 'State parks' and formally changing the names of Freedman's State Park and Port Deposit State Park.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits the governing documents of condominiums and homeowners associations from prohibiting or unreasonably restricting the governing body from installing or authorizing electric vehicle recharging equipment in common or limited common use parking spaces. The bill subjects such installations to the entity's ordinary budget process for comparable renovations, requires consideration of community parking needs, and allows governing bodies to grant up to three-year renewable licenses for necessary common elements.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
qa_results.stakeholders: Condominium and homeowners association governing bodies, unit and lot owners, and electric vehicle owners residing in common ownership communities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division oversees common ownership community issues and mediates disputes involving homeowners and condominium associations, making the legal changes to association governing documents relevant to their consumer protection activities.
The Maryland Energy Administration promotes clean energy policies and electric vehicle infrastructure adoption statewide, and contributed policy input to the bill's analysis.

The Judiciary and state courts may adjudicate civil disputes or litigation arising between unit/lot owners and condominium or HOA governing boards regarding covenant enforcement and equipment installation.

The Office of the Secretary of State handles the registration and statutory oversight of residential condominiums in Maryland, which are directly affected by the bill's provisions on governing documents and bylaws.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts Class B (on-sale) beer and wine licenses and Class B (on-sale) beer, wine, and liquor licenses from the general prohibition in Prince George's County against issuing multiple alcoholic beverages licenses to the same person or premises.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Restaurant, hotel, and hospitality business owners in Prince George's County seeking multiple on-sale alcoholic beverages licenses, as well as local licensing authorities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Prince George's County revenues will increase depending on the number of additional licenses issued, generating $365 annually for each new Class B (on-sale) beer and wine license and $2,305 annually for each new Class B (on-sale) beer, wine, and liquor license. Any additional local enforcement activity can be absorbed using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters local alcoholic beverage licensing restrictions in Prince George's County.
