While retail licensing is administered locally by the Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, the Comptroller regulates the state's alcohol industry and oversees state alcohol taxation and enforcement.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the Maryland–Ireland Trade Commission from September 30, 2026, to September 30, 2028, and alters its membership by reducing General Assembly representation from four members to two and adding two members from the private sector.
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland businesses engaged in international trade, members of the Irish-American community, higher education institutions, and commission members.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Commerce can continue to support the commission using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are unaffected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland-Ireland Trade Commission is established within the Department of Commerce, which provides operational support to the Commission, and the Secretary of Commerce serves as a statutory member.
The Secretary of State or the Secretary's designee serves as a statutory member of the Maryland-Ireland Trade Commission.

The Governor appoints several members of the Commission with the advice and consent of the Senate, may remove members for cause, and receives annual reports of findings and recommendations from the Commission.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for state boards and commissions, which applies to the altered membership requiring the appointment of two additional private sector members.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the membership composition, reporting requirements, and termination date of the Maryland-Ireland Trade Commission, an executive advisory commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands Maryland's Expedited Partner Therapy program by adding bacterial vaginosis to the conditions eligible for partner antibiotic treatment without a prior physical assessment, and authorizes licensed certified midwives to prescribe or dispense expedited partner therapy.
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals diagnosed with bacterial vaginosis, their sexual partners, licensed certified midwives, and other authorized health care practitioners.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can update regulations and provider materials using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 422 alters Maryland's Expedited Partner Therapy (EPT) statute under the Health - General Article by adding bacterial vaginosis and authorizing licensed certified midwives to provide partner therapy. The Secretary of Health is tasked with adopting regulations to implement these requirements, and the Maryland Department of Health must update its EPT regulations and provider educational materials.

qa_results.bill_summary: Beginning in the 2026–2027 school year, requires the Prince George's County Board of Education to have public high schools provide drink spiking detection products, as well as fentanyl drug detection strips (for schools reporting an incident requiring overdose-reversing medication), to students at no cost, conditioned upon the schools receiving these products at no cost. It also mandates that county public high schools submit an annual report to Maryland's Office of Overdose Response regarding the volume of products distributed.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prince George's County Board of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Prince George's County public high school students, school staff, and public high schools
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not impacted; Maryland's Office of Overdose Response can handle reporting requirements with existing budgeted resources, and revenues are unaffected. Local school system expenditures may increase minimally if automatic dispensers are purchased and installed; however, schools are only required to provide the detection products if obtained at no cost through donations, grants, or existing programs like the Overdose Response Program or local Opioid Restitution Fund awards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Education Article to require Prince George's County public high schools to distribute drug detection strips and drink spiking detection products. The requirement is conditioned on naloxone incident reports previously submitted by schools to the Maryland State Department of Education under existing education law.

The bill mandates annual reporting on product distribution to Maryland's Office of Overdose Response (MOOR), which coordinates with the Department of Health. Furthermore, MDH administers the Overdose Response Program (ORP), which provides fentanyl detection strips at no cost to authorized entities such as schools.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a party to a guardianship of the property of an alleged disabled person to request a stay of specified civil actions or proceedings—such as eviction, foreclosure, or sheriff's sales—in the court presiding over the action. The stay may last up to 90 days unless extended for good cause, must be automatically lifted upon the appointment of a guardian or denial of the petition, and establishes service of process requirements on the guardian.
qa_results.stakeholders: Alleged disabled persons facing civil or property actions, appointed guardians and parties to guardianship proceedings, and creditors or landlords initiating civil actions (e.g., evictions, foreclosures).
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Legislative Services advises the bill can be implemented with existing resources and that state revenues will not be materially affected, although the Judiciary estimated a one-time programming cost of $142,238. There is no local government fiscal impact. Small business plaintiffs may experience delays or lost revenues due to stayed proceedings.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts court operations and judicial case management across Maryland's District and Circuit courts by establishing statutory procedures for requesting, administering, and lifting stays in civil actions (such as eviction proceedings, foreclosures, and sheriff's sales) upon the filing of a petition for guardianship of an alleged disabled person's property.

The Register of Wills serves as the clerk to the Orphans' Court and maintains records and dockets concerning estate and protective proceedings under the Estates and Trusts Article, making the agency a consulted stakeholder regarding procedures for guardianship petitions.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill extends the Task Force on Responsible Use of Natural Psychedelic Substances by one year to terminate on December 31, 2027, adds a representative from a historically Black college or university to its membership, and requires an updated report of findings and recommendations by October 31, 2026.
qa_results.stakeholders: Patients, healthcare practitioners, researchers, historically Black colleges and universities, individuals with criminal records or incarceration for nonviolent natural psychedelic offenses, and the Maryland Cannabis Administration.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Cannabis Administration can continue staffing the task force with existing budgeted resources. Expense reimbursements for task force members are minimal and absorbable within existing resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Cannabis Administration is the primary agency responsible for providing operational and staff support for the Task Force, and the Director serves as a statutory member.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly extends the termination date, reporting timeline, and membership composition of an active executive task force.
The Secretary of Health (or designee) is a designated statutory member of the Task Force, which studies health benefits, risks, and medical use of natural psychedelic substances.
The Secretary of Disabilities (or designee) serves as a statutory member on the Task Force examining access and treatment options.
The Secretary of the department (formerly Veterans Affairs) or a designee serves as a statutory member of the Task Force.
USM is specifically identified as an eligible appointing body for research representation on the Task Force and includes multiple historically Black colleges and universities in the state.
As Maryland's independent public historically Black university, Morgan State University is eligible to represent HBCUs under the newly added seat on the Task Force.
The Governor appoints the members (including the new HBCU representative), designates the chair, and receives the Task Force's updated report.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the On-Farm Organics Diversion and Recycling Grant Program within the Maryland Department of Agriculture, in consultation with the Maryland Department of the Environment, to award annual grants supporting on-farm organics recycling, compost use, food waste prevention, and food rescue projects.
qa_results.stakeholders: Farmers, urban agricultural producers, soil conservation districts, institutions of higher education, nonprofit organizations, participating businesses, and local communities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $250,000 in FY 2028 due to a mandated annual appropriation of $250,000, which MDA will use for administrative start-up costs. Beginning in FY 2029, expenditures increase to approximately $371,500 annually (growing to $380,300 by FY 2031), reflecting the $250,000 mandated appropriation for grant awards plus ongoing administrative and personnel costs. Local soil conservation districts and higher education institutions may see increased revenues and expenditures if awarded grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDA is the primary administering agency responsible for establishing, managing, and reporting on the On-Farm Organics Diversion and Recycling Grant Program, as well as applying for federal or alternative funding.
MDE is required to consult with MDA on the administration of the grant program, identifying and applying for funding, and prioritizing grant awards.
The bill mandates that the Governor include an annual appropriation of $250,000 for the grant program in the state budget bill beginning in FY 2028.
DBM oversees the state budget execution and development, which must incorporate the $250,000 statutory annual mandated appropriation starting in FY 2028.
State institutions of higher education within USM are explicitly eligible entities to apply for and receive grant funding under the program.
As a public institution of higher education, Morgan State University is an eligible entity to apply for and receive grants under the program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires family child care providers who are members of a military reserve component to designate a substitute provider during absences for required training and active service, allowing the substitute to provide child care for up to 45 working days in any 12-month period.
qa_results.stakeholders: Family child care providers who are members of a military reserve component, substitute child care providers, and children and families enrolled in family child care homes.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland State Department of Education can implement the bill's requirements using existing resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) regulates and licenses family child care homes and providers in the state. MSDE is responsible for implementing the allowance of up to 45 working days for substitute providers when a provider is absent for reserve training or active service.

The agency advocates for and assists military service members, reservists, and their families. The bill directly supports reserve component members who operate family child care businesses during active service and required training periods.

As the head of the Maryland Military Department overseeing National Guard personnel, this bill supports Guard and reserve members balancing military training and active duty requirements with their civilian child care businesses.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing to the Office of the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing, and renames the Maryland Advisory Council on Deaf and Hard of Hearing accordingly. It also expands the membership of the advisory council to include the Secretary of Disabilities or their designee.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor's Office of the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing
qa_results.stakeholders: Deaf, deafblind, and hard of hearing Maryland residents, the Maryland Department of Disabilities, and state and local agencies providing services to these populations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operational costs to update the names of the office and council can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources, and existing print materials must be exhausted before new ones are printed. The Maryland Department of Disabilities can participate on the council with existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 439 directly renames the agency to the Office of the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing and updates its governing statutory provisions, advisory council, and references across Maryland Code.
The bill explicitly expands the membership of the renamed Maryland Advisory Council on the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing to include the Secretary of Disabilities or a designee.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill renames the Maryland Advisory Council on Deaf and Hard of Hearing to the Maryland Advisory Council on the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing and alters its statutory composition.
The Office of the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing is an entity established within the Office of the Governor, and the Governor appoints the members of its advisory council.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires nursing homes, assisted living programs, nurse midwives, and licensed certified midwives in Maryland to provide written notification to residents, prospective residents, or patients if they do not carry professional liability insurance or if coverage has lapsed without renewal, and mandates posting notices in conspicuous locations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Board of Nursing
qa_results.stakeholders: Nursing homes, assisted living facilities, nurse midwives, licensed certified midwives, and their residents, patients, and prospective residents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government finances and operations are not directly affected by the bill. The change is technical in nature, and the impact on small businesses is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) regulates health care facilities, including nursing homes and assisted living programs, and houses health occupations licensing boards such as the State Board of Nursing, which licenses and regulates nurse midwives and certified midwives affected by the disclosure requirements.
The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates medical professional liability insurance and insurers within the state and was consulted regarding the bill's insurance disclosure mandates.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office resolves medical malpractice claims in Maryland and tracks issues concerning health care provider professional liability coverage.

The Department of Aging advocates for older adults and individuals residing in nursing homes and assisted living programs, where residents and prospective residents will receive mandatory notifications regarding liability coverage.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a Class B-SEC (small event center) beer, wine, and liquor license in Prince George's County, allowing qualified venues with a capacity between 75 and 110 people to sell alcoholic beverages for on-premises event consumption. It sets minimum capital investment requirements, limits the issuance to no more than 24 total licenses annually and 3 per legislative district, and establishes an annual license fee of $3,500.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Small event center venue owners and operators in Prince George's County, event patrons, and local licensing authorities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Prince George’s County license fee revenues are estimated to increase by approximately $10,500 annually beginning in FY 2027, assuming three businesses apply for the $3,500 annual license. County expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the alcohol industry and administers excise and sales taxes in the state. While the Class B-SEC license is administered locally by the Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners with no direct state fiscal effect, the bill falls under the general scope of alcoholic beverage regulation and commerce in Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits the State, local governments, county sheriffs, and their agencies, officers, or agents from entering into immigration enforcement agreements (such as federal 287(g) agreements) authorizing the enforcement of civil immigration law, and requires immediate termination of any existing agreements upon enactment.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State agencies, units of local government, and county sheriffs
qa_results.stakeholders: Immigrants residing in or detained in Maryland, county sheriffs' offices and local correctional facilities (specifically those with active 287(g) agreements), local law enforcement officers, and federal immigration authorities (ICE/DHS)
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state law enforcement agency, Maryland State Police officers and divisions are directly prohibited under the bill from entering into immigration enforcement agreements (such as 287(g) task force agreements) with the federal government.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS operates state correctional facilities and detention operations, and the bill explicitly prohibits state agencies, correctional staff, or agents from entering into or maintaining civil immigration enforcement agreements or partnerships with federal authorities.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal guidance and counsel to state agencies and law enforcement on interacting with federal law enforcement and advises on the termination and legality of intergovernmental agreements.
The Governor's Office oversees executive branch agencies and departments that are subject to the prohibition against entering into or maintaining immigration enforcement agreements.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and certain health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to provide coverage for orthoses, orthosis components, repairs, and replacements, including those deemed medically necessary for daily living, essential job activities, or physical activities to maximize whole-body health and limb function. It also clarifies coverage requirements for prostheses and requires insurers and Medicaid managed care organizations to submit a compliance report by June 30, 2032.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Medicaid enrollees and commercially insured individuals requiring orthotic or prosthetic devices, healthcare providers and orthotic suppliers, health insurance carriers, and Medicaid managed care organizations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration will increase minimally in FY 2027 from $125 rate and form filing fees, with any administrative workload managed using existing resources. There is no impact on the Medicaid program because the bill codifies coverage already established in January 2026, and impact on the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program is negligible. Local government expenditures for fully insured employee health benefit plans may increase slightly if premiums rise, with no effect on local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which is administered by the Maryland Department of Health, to provide coverage for orthoses. Additionally, MDH must jointly prescribe reporting forms with the Maryland Insurance Administration and submit a joint compliance report by December 31, 2032.

The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates health insurers and HMOs subject to the mandated coverage for orthoses and prostheses. MIA will review rate and policy form filings, receive carrier compliance filings, and collaborate with the Maryland Department of Health to submit a joint report by December 31, 2032.

DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which was reviewed for potential fiscal impact from the coverage mandate (determined to have a negligible impact as coverage is already substantially provided).

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill establishes the Dementia Services and Brain Health Program within the Maryland Department of Health to lead the State's public health efforts related to brain health and dementia. The program assumes and expands upon duties formerly assigned to the Director of Dementia Services and Brain Health, including supporting the Virginia I. Jones Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias Council and promoting dementia-capable care. Additionally, the bill requires the department, in partnership with the Department of Aging and other stakeholders, to establish, promote, and annually update a provider resource toolkit for dementia care by October 1, 2027.
qa_results.stakeholders: Health care providers, individuals with or at risk for Alzheimer's disease and related dementias, and their caregivers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $77,700 in FY 2027, rising to $90,600 in FY 2028 and $103,500 by FY 2031 to hire one program administrator to manage stakeholder coordination and develop and maintain the provider toolkit. The Maryland Department of Aging can participate using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 446 establishes the Dementia Services and Brain Health Program within the Maryland Department of Health, requires MDH to hire staff, oversee the State Plan, develop and maintain an annual provider resource toolkit for dementia care, and promote dementia-capable care practices across health care models.

The bill explicitly requires the Department of Aging to assist the Dementia Services and Brain Health Program in providing staff support to the Council and to partner with MDH in establishing and maintaining the dementia care provider resource toolkit.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory duties of the Virginia I. Jones Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias Council, requiring it to examine provider readiness and capacity to deliver dementia care and collaborate on the provider resource toolkit.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 451 permanently establishes the Maryland Zero Emission Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Council (ZEEVIC) by repealing its termination date. The bill alters the council's membership, refines its duties to focus on addressing barriers and recommending policies for electric vehicle charging infrastructure integration, and institutes an ongoing annual reporting requirement due by December 1 each year.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Zero Emission Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Council (staffed by the Maryland Department of Transportation, with assistance from the Maryland Energy Administration and the Maryland Public Service Commission)
qa_results.stakeholders: Electric and fuel cell zero-emission vehicle drivers, fleet vehicle operators, electric utilities, EV and charging equipment manufacturers, multidwelling unit residents, automotive recyclers, and local governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are not affected. Reporting, council operations, and staffing requirements can continue to be absorbed using existing resources by the Maryland Department of Transportation, the Maryland Energy Administration, and the Public Service Commission. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Transportation is the primary agency responsible for the Maryland Zero Emission Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Council (ZEEVIC), with the Secretary serving on the Council and MDOT tasked with providing ongoing staff support.
The Director of the Maryland Energy Administration is a designated statutory member of the Council, and MEA is statutorily required to assist MDOT with staffing and supporting Council operations.
The Executive Director of the PSC's Technical Staff is a member of the Council, and the PSC is explicitly mandated by statute to assist MDOT in providing staff support to the Council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: ZEEVIC is an executive branch advisory body whose statutory duties, membership, reporting structure, and permanent continuation via sunset repeal are directly modified by this bill.
The bill explicitly adds the Secretary of Agriculture, or the Secretary's designee, as a new statutory member of the Council.
The People's Counsel, or the People's Counsel's designee, serves as a statutory member of the Council to represent utility consumer interests regarding EV infrastructure.
The Governor designates the chair or co-chairs of the Council, appoints numerous stakeholder members, and receives the Council's annual reports.
The Secretary of Commerce, or the Secretary's designee, serves as an ex officio member of the Council.
The Secretary of General Services, or the Secretary's designee, is an ex officio member of the Council, which addresses state fleet vehicle electrification and building charging solutions.
The Secretary of Planning, or the Secretary's designee, serves as an ex officio member of the Council.
The Secretary of the Environment, or the Secretary's designee, serves as an ex officio member of the Council.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and processing the appointment of the multiple non-governmental stakeholder members to the Council.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners from taking disciplinary actions—such as suspending or revoking a license, censuring, reprimanding, or placing on probation—against a veterinarian or veterinary practitioner solely for discussing or recommending cannabis or cannabidiol (CBD) products for an animal's potential therapeutic effect or health supplementation.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners
qa_results.stakeholders: Veterinarians, veterinary practitioners, veterinary clinics/practices, and animal owners.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations, nor does it materially affect small businesses, as the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners has not taken formal disciplinary actions that would be prohibited under the bill.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners is a regulatory board housed within the Maryland Department of Agriculture. The bill directly amends the Agriculture Article to restrict the Board's authority regarding disciplinary actions against licensed veterinarians discussing or recommending cannabis or CBD products for animals.

The bill references statutory definitions of cannabis under the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article and touches on therapeutic recommendations of cannabis products; while it does not alter the administration's direct regulatory functions or have a fiscal impact, it relates tangentially to the state's broader cannabis policy framework.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill establishes a gift basket permit in Howard County for businesses primarily engaged in the sale and delivery of flowers or gift baskets, authorizing them to sell and deliver baskets containing beer, wine, or liquor to legal-age consumers. The permit costs $100 annually, excludes chain stores and supermarkets, and requires that alcohol be purchased from local retail licensees and not exceed 10% of the holder's total annual gross sales.
qa_results.responsible_party: Howard County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Florists and gift basket businesses in Howard County, and consumers of legal drinking age in the county.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is no State fiscal impact. Local revenues for Howard County increase by $100 annually for each permit issued. Based on an illustrative estimate of 15 potential florist applicants, Howard County revenues are projected to increase by approximately $1,500 annually. Monitoring and enforcement activities are expected to be handled within existing county resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor is the state's chief executive responsible for signing House Bill 456 into law. The office oversees the executive branch and the enforcement of state laws, including those modified by this legislation in the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article.

As the state's principal financial officer and regulator of the alcohol industry, the Comptroller is responsible for broad oversight of alcohol-related laws and tax collection. This bill establishes a new permit type for the sale and delivery of alcohol, which falls within the industry regulated by this agency.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the chief legal representative for the state. It is relevant to this bill as it provides legal counsel to the Governor and General Assembly on the constitutional and statutory implications of creating new permit types and amending the state's alcoholic beverages laws.

The bill amends existing law regarding the proximity of alcohol-licensed establishments to public school buildings. As the state agency overseeing public education and local school systems, the Department of Education is relevant to legislative changes that affect the zoning and licensing of businesses near school facilities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires institutions of higher education in Maryland that provide on-campus housing to provide menstrual hygiene products, such as tampons and sanitary napkins, free of charge in all student health centers by August 1, 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: Institutions of higher education that provide on-campus housing (including University System of Maryland institutions, Morgan State University, and St. Mary's College of Maryland)
qa_results.stakeholders: Students attending Maryland institutions of higher education that offer on-campus housing, and public and private degree-granting colleges and universities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State higher education expenditures increase, likely minimally, beginning in FY 2029 (with potential minor initial costs earlier) for public four-year institutions with on-campus housing to supply products and potential dispensers in student health centers. Local community college expenditures increase minimally for colleges providing on-campus housing (Allegany College of Maryland and Garrett College). State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Constituent institutions of the University System of Maryland that provide on-campus housing are directly mandated to provide free menstrual hygiene products in all student health centers, incurring minimal operating and supply costs.
As a public four-year institution offering on-campus housing, Morgan State University is directly required to supply free menstrual hygiene products in its student health center by August 1, 2028.

As a residential public honors college offering on-campus housing, St. Mary's College of Maryland is directly subject to the mandate to provide free menstrual hygiene products in its student health center.

The bill amends Title 11 of the Education Article, which falls under the regulatory and policy oversight of the Maryland Higher Education Commission regarding postsecondary degree-granting institutions in Maryland.
As the coordinating board for the state's postsecondary institutions, the commission oversees policies governing degree-granting institutions affected by the provisions of this legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Rural Readiness Program administered by the Rural Maryland Council to assist rural communities with economic development capacity, grant applications, and revenue-generating projects. The bill also establishes the Rural Maryland Capacity Building Fund to provide competitive grants of up to $50,000 to eligible rural entities that complete the program.
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonprofits, local governments, State-recognized tribes, higher education institutions, regional planning agencies, economic or workforce development organizations, and residents in Maryland's 18 rural counties.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $100,000 annually beginning in FY 2027 to capitalize the Rural Maryland Capacity Building Fund, with special fund revenues and expenditures increasing correspondingly as grants are awarded. The Rural Maryland Council can administer the program using existing budgeted resources. Local governments in rural communities may benefit from technical assistance and competitive grants of up to $50,000 per project, subject to matching funds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 461 establishes the Rural Readiness Program and the Rural Maryland Capacity Building Fund, both of which are directly administered by the Rural Maryland Council. The Council is responsible for setting criteria, developing toolkits, certifying program completion, and reporting annually on grants.

The Rural Maryland Council is administratively and budgetarily housed within the Maryland Department of Agriculture, making the department relevant to the administrative and operational oversight of the council's new programs and funds.
The bill establishes the Rural Maryland Capacity Building Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund and explicitly tasks the State Treasurer with holding and investing the moneys of the fund.
The bill explicitly assigns the Comptroller the statutory responsibility to account for the newly created Rural Maryland Capacity Building Fund.
The Council is required to submit an annual report on the grant awards, recipients, and purposes of the Rural Maryland Capacity Building Fund to the Governor by October 1 each year.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill prohibits the Maryland Parole Commission (MPC) from permanently denying parole and establishes mandatory schedules for subsequent parole hearings following a denial. It mandates that MPC provide relevant documents to incarcerated individuals and their representatives before hearings, shortens deadlines for hearing examiner reports, extends appeal windows, requires MPC to record parole hearings and provide those recordings free of charge to incarcerated individuals, and expands MPC's annual reporting requirements disaggregated by race. In addition, it prohibits counties from being named or designated as parties in administrative proceedings concerning compensation for erroneously convicted individuals.
qa_results.stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals eligible for parole, their legal representatives, crime victims, erroneously convicted individuals, and county governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $346,843 in FY 2027, rising to $456,000 by FY 2031, reflecting the cost of hiring four office secretaries to handle redaction, document distribution, and data reporting, as well as operational costs to provide recordings free of charge. General fund revenues may decrease indeterminately due to foregone $30 fees previously charged for audio recordings. Local government finances are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Parole Commission is housed within the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services. The bill places extensive new requirements on parole hearings, records retention, disclosure timelines, mandatory subsequent hearings, and annual reporting, resulting in a direct general fund fiscal impact of over $346,000 annually.

Administrative law judges at the Office of Administrative Hearings hear and decide petitions for compensation and benefits for erroneously convicted individuals under § 10-501, which this bill alters regarding eligible parties.
The Attorney General represents the State in administrative proceedings involving claims by erroneously convicted individuals, where county participation is explicitly prohibited by the bill.

The Board of Public Works is the state entity named as a party caption and responsible for paying monetary compensation to erroneously convicted individuals based on ALJ orders under the amended statute.

The Maryland Parole Commission is statutorily required to submit its comprehensive annual report to the Governor, which this bill expands to include specific parole denial, grant, and revocation data disaggregated by race.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Digital Asset and Blockchain Technology Task Force to study and make recommendations regarding the expansion, regulation, and risks and benefits of blockchain technology and cryptocurrency in Maryland. The task force is required to submit a report of its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by October 1, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of Financial Regulation within the Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Cryptocurrency and blockchain businesses, the financial services industry, state and local government agencies, and Maryland consumers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by $49,400 in FY 2027 and $53,500 in FY 2028 for the Maryland Department of Labor's Office of Financial Regulation to hire one full-time contractual administrative specialist to staff the task force. Task force member travel reimbursements are assumed to be minimal and absorbable within existing resources. The bill has no effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Secretary of Labor as a member of the Task Force and mandates that the Office of Financial Regulation within the Maryland Department of Labor provide staff support, resulting in a direct fiscal impact for contractual staffing.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally establishes a new temporary body, the Digital Asset and Blockchain Technology Task Force, to study issues surrounding blockchain technology and cryptocurrency and report recommendations.

The Secretary of Information Technology (or designee) is designated as a member of the Task Force, which is tasked with studying the technology, risks, benefits, and use of blockchain in State and local government.
The Comptroller (or designee) is designated as a member of the Task Force, which will examine the financial impacts and revenue implications of cryptocurrency and digital assets on the State.
The State Treasurer (or designee) is designated as a member of the Task Force to examine digital assets, cryptocurrency, and blockchain technology in Maryland.
The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) serves on the Task Force, which explores the economic impact, benefits, and regulation of blockchain and cryptocurrency for private businesses in Maryland.
The Securities Commissioner, who heads the Securities Division within the Office of the Attorney General, is designated as a member of the Task Force to examine digital assets and state regulations.
The Governor is responsible for appointing five members to the Task Force and will receive the Task Force's final report and recommendations by October 1, 2027.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and processing candidates for the five gubernatorial appointments to the Task Force.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill extends the Maryland theatrical production tax credit for an additional five years through tax year 2031 and caps the aggregate amount of unissued tax credits that may be carried forward and issued in subsequent fiscal years at $20 million.
qa_results.stakeholders: Qualified theatrical production entities (producers of for-profit national touring or pre-Broadway live stage productions), Maryland theatrical venues and facilities, and the State's arts and entertainment workforce.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues are projected to decrease by approximately $500,000 annually from FY 2028 through FY 2032 due to personal income tax credits. If credits are claimed against the corporate income tax, Higher Education Investment Fund and Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues and TTF expenditures will also decrease. Local highway user revenues will decrease to the extent credits are claimed against the corporate income tax, while local expenditures remain unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Commerce is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the theatrical production tax credit, evaluating applications, issuing tax credit certificates, and managing the aggregate and carryforward caps.

The Comptroller of Maryland administers the State income tax system and is responsible for processing tax returns claiming the theatrical production credit, including issuing refunds for credit amounts that exceed tax liability.

The Department of Transportation may experience a minor indirect fiscal impact, as Transportation Trust Fund revenues and subsequent local highway user revenue expenditures decrease to the extent credits are claimed against the corporate income tax.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Clear Before You Drive Act prohibits a person from operating or towing a vehicle without making reasonable efforts to remove dangerous accumulations of snow and ice from exposed surfaces such as roofs, windshields, hoods, and trailers. The offense is enforced as a secondary action unless the failure to clear snow and ice contributes to an accident resulting in property damage, serious bodily injury, or death, and establishes tiered fine structures for noncommercial and commercial vehicles.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of State Police and local law enforcement agencies
qa_results.stakeholders: Drivers and operators of commercial and noncommercial motor vehicles, vehicle towing operators, law enforcement officers, and other motorists and pedestrians.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may experience a potential minimal increase from traffic fines collected in District Court. Enforcement can be handled using existing resources, and the bill is not anticipated to materially impact local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Maryland Vehicle Law within the Transportation Article, establishing new operating requirements and safety standards for noncommercial and commercial vehicles operating on Maryland roadways.

As the primary state law enforcement agency responsible for enforcing motor vehicle and traffic safety laws on Maryland highways, the Maryland State Police is responsible for enforcing the bill's provisions and issuing citations for violations.
The District Court within the Judicial Branch processes traffic citations, establishes prepayment penalties, and collects fine revenues generated by violations of the new vehicle law.
As the MDOT administration regulating vehicle operations and maintaining driver records, the MVA is impacted by updates to Maryland vehicle laws, driver education, and commercial vehicle compliance.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands Maryland's existing state income tax subtraction modification of up to $250 for unreimbursed classroom supplies to include full-time prekindergarten teachers employed in eligible publicly funded prekindergarten programs.
qa_results.stakeholders: Full-time prekindergarten classroom teachers, lead teachers, and consulting teachers in publicly funded prekindergarten programs at eligible public and private providers in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in fiscal 2027, State general fund revenues are estimated to decrease by approximately $80,000 annually, while local income tax revenues are estimated to decrease by about $50,000 annually. The Comptroller's Office can administer the tax modification using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the state's tax collection agency and is directly responsible for administering personal income tax forms, regulations, and subtraction modifications, including processing the expanded classroom supply subtraction modification for eligible prekindergarten teachers.

The Maryland State Department of Education oversees early childhood education programs and eligible public and private prekindergarten providers referenced in § 7-1A-01 of the Education Article, which defines eligibility for teachers under the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires transportation network companies (TNCs) to establish, maintain, and publish a written plain-language deactivation policy and an internal appeals process for drivers facing permanent account deactivation. It restricts TNCs from deactivating drivers for reasons outside their policy, establishes standards and timelines for relying on passenger complaints and providing written notice of deactivation, outlines an appeals review procedure, and permits deactivated drivers to withdraw previously accrued earnings except under specified circumstances.
qa_results.stakeholders: Transportation network companies (such as Uber and Lyft), rideshare operators and drivers, and rideshare passengers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances or operations, resulting in no state or local fiscal impact. Transportation network drivers operating as small businesses may experience a meaningful operational benefit from the newly established deactivation protections and appeal procedures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission (PSC) is the primary regulatory body overseeing transportation network companies (TNCs) and operators under Title 10 of the Public Utilities Article, which this bill amends to establish statutory standards and requirements for driver deactivation policies and internal appeals.

The bill mandates that a TNC's deactivation policy be enforceable as a term of contract between the TNC and the operator, which may lead to contract disputes or civil litigation in the Maryland court system.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the gross income contribution thresholds that trigger mandatory financial audits and reviews for charitable organizations registering in Maryland, raising the threshold for an independent audit from $750,000 to $1,000,000 and for an independent review from $300,000 to $400,000.
qa_results.stakeholders: Charitable organizations soliciting or receiving charitable contributions in Maryland and independent certified public accountants.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State costs to update online filing systems and implement the bill are minimal and can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of State is the primary regulatory agency responsible for registering and overseeing charitable organizations in Maryland. The bill directly alters statutory financial audit and review reporting thresholds submitted to the Secretary of State with charitable registration statements.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 485 renames the State Board of Examiners of Landscape Architects to the State Board of Professional Landscape Architects and replaces the term 'licensed landscape architect' with 'professional landscape architect'. The bill updates board member qualification standards, alters examination administration and educational accreditation requirements, creates an emeritus status license for qualifying individuals, and removes a permit exemption for businesses performing landscape architectural services for themselves or affiliates.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Professional Landscape Architects (Maryland Department of Labor)
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed and professional landscape architects, retired landscape architects seeking emeritus status, landscape architecture applicants, landscape architectural businesses, and local code officials.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not materially affected as the State Board of Professional Landscape Architects can implement the bill with existing resources. State revenues are likely not materially affected by the creation of the emeritus license fee, elimination of board-collected examination fees, or permit adjustments. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Professional Landscape Architects is an occupational and professional licensing unit housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. The bill directly alters the board's name, membership qualifications, licensing requirements, examination processes, fee structures, and regulatory powers.

The bill alters the statutory qualifications and experience requirements for professional landscape architect members appointed by the Governor to the State Board of Professional Landscape Architects, impacting candidate vetting and appointment processes.

The Governor is responsible for appointing members to the State Board of Professional Landscape Architects, and the bill amends the required professional experience qualifications for those executive appointments.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO) to adopt regulations establishing a process for considering remedies, including divestment, when an invested business no longer qualifies as a qualified business. Additionally, it authorizes TEDCO, upon review and approval by its investment committee, to either divest from an equity investment within 15 years or pursue another remedy in TEDCO's best interest, rather than mandating divestment.
qa_results.stakeholders: Businesses and startups receiving investments or equity funding from TEDCO, venture and private equity firms partnering with TEDCO, and TEDCO's investment committee.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not anticipated to be materially affected, though financial investment returns to TEDCO may potentially increase. There is no local government fiscal impact, and the impact on small businesses is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs TEDCO's investment committee responsibilities, requiring the Corporation to adopt regulations establishing a process for considering remedies (such as divestment) when an investment no longer meets the definition of a qualified business, and giving TEDCO discretion rather than a mandate regarding divestment after 15 years.

As the state's primary economic development agency, the Department of Commerce collaborates closely with TEDCO on state business development and investment strategies, although the bill does not impose direct administrative requirements on Commerce.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits law enforcement agencies from requesting verbal acknowledgements from victims of sexually assaultive behavior that would waive agency obligations, define or limit the scope of an investigation or prosecution, or restrict the victim's private right of action.
qa_results.responsible_party: State and local law enforcement agencies
qa_results.stakeholders: Victims of sexually assaultive behavior and law enforcement officers and agencies in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state law enforcement agency, MSP investigators interact directly with victims of sexually assaultive behavior and must adhere to the prohibition against requesting verbal acknowledgments that waive obligations, investigations, prosecutions, or private rights of action.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS houses the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC), which is statutorily tasked under this section with recommending the practices and standards law enforcement must follow when a victim requests to limit or suspend an investigation.
The bill enforces provisions allowing an affected victim to file an action for injunctive or declaratory relief in Maryland courts if a law enforcement agency violates the statute.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes minimum adequate security standards for courtroom security at all courthouse facilities in Maryland, requiring entities responsible for courthouse security to use best efforts to maintain specified staffing levels phased in on July 1, 2027, and July 1, 2029, and requiring court security officers to meet the qualifications of a special police officer.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and local entities responsible for courthouse security (including county sheriffs' offices)
qa_results.stakeholders: Judges, court personnel, litigants, criminal defendants, visitors to state and local courthouses, and local law enforcement agencies/sheriffs' offices
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $5.6 million in FY 2027 to provide grants to local jurisdictions to enhance circuit court security, with no impact on state revenues; the Judiciary can comply with standards in state-run courts using existing resources. Local government expenditures increase beginning in FY 2027—substantially in several jurisdictions—to hire an estimated 206 additional court security officers, partially offset in FY 2027 by local grant revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts (Judiciary) is directly responsible for administering and staffing security in the Supreme Court of Maryland, the Appellate Court of Maryland, and the District Court of Maryland. The AOC also staffed the Task Force to Ensure the Safety of Judicial Facilities that recommended these standards and is responsible for administering state grant funds provided to local jurisdictions for courtroom security.

The bill requires court security officers to meet the qualifications of a special police officer as defined under § 3–301 of the Public Safety Article, a program and set of statutory standards administered and vetted through the Department of State Police.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the number of District Court associate judges in District 11 appointed from Washington County from two to three, expanding the total number of associate judges in District 11 from five to six.
qa_results.stakeholders: Litigants, attorneys, and residents in Washington County and District 11, as well as District Court staff and judges.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $423,500 in FY 2027 (annualizing to $571,800 by FY 2031) to fund one new District Court judge, one courtroom clerk, two contractual bailiffs, and associated operating expenses. Funding is included in the FY 2027 budget. State revenues and local government operations and finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 493 establishes an additional District Court judgeship in District 11 (Washington County) along with associated courtroom clerk and bailiff positions, which directly impacts the court system operations and budget supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and recommending candidates for judicial vacancies and newly created judgeships.
The Governor is constitutionally responsible for appointing judges to fill newly established District Court seats.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 497 alters the duration and scheduling requirements for domestic protective orders by establishing that a temporary protective order is effective for up to 14 days after issuance (rather than 7 days after service) and requiring that the final protective order hearing be held no later than 14 days after issuance (rather than 7 days after service).
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts and District and Circuit Courts)
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals filing for or responding to protective orders (victims of alleged abuse and respondents), court personnel, and process servers or law enforcement officers serving orders.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies judicial timelines for domestic violence proceedings, establishing that temporary protective orders are effective for up to 14 days after issuance (rather than 7 days after service) and requiring final protective order hearings to be held within 14 days after issuance. The Administrative Office of the Courts must adjust court scheduling practices, case management systems, and court forms accordingly.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters Certificate of Need (CON) requirements for intermediate care facilities providing substance use disorder treatment services. It repeals a previous blanket CON exemption for bed capacity changes at residential or intensive substance-related disorder intermediate care facilities, establishing instead that a CON is not required to establish, operate, or alter bed capacity for facilities offering medically managed residential substance use disorder treatment services (ASAM Level 3.7) if 45 days' advance written notice is provided and the Maryland Health Care Commission finds the action complies with the State Health Plan, promotes efficient care, and serves the public interest.
qa_results.stakeholders: Intermediate care facilities offering substance use disorder treatment services (specifically ASAM Level 3.7 medically managed residential treatment programs) and individuals seeking substance use disorder treatment.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not significantly impacted; any additional workload for the Maryland Health Care Commission to review notices and make determinations can be handled using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHCC is the primary entity responsible for administering the Certificate of Need (CON) program in Maryland. The bill directly alters CON requirements and exemptions for intermediate care facilities offering substance use disorder treatment services, requiring facilities to submit notices of intent to MHCC and requiring MHCC to make formal findings under the State Health Plan.

MDH is the cabinet department overseeing health care facilities and behavioral health services in Maryland. The intermediate care facilities subject to the bill's provisions must be licensed by the Secretary of Health, and MHCC is an independent regulatory agency operating within MDH.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the State sales and use tax exemption for sales of precious metal bullion or coins priced over $1,000 by repealing the requirement that the transaction must occur at the Baltimore Convention Center.
qa_results.stakeholders: Buyers, sellers, and dealers of precious metal bullion and coins in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State General Fund revenues decrease by $2.5 million in FY 2027 and $2.8 million in FY 2031. Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund (BMFF) revenues decrease by $0.3 million in FY 2027 and $0.4 million in FY 2031. State expenditures and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the State's principal tax collector and administrator of the sales and use tax, the Comptroller of Maryland is directly responsible for implementing the expanded sales and use tax exemption on precious metal bullion and coins, updating tax guidance, and managing the resulting reduction in sales tax collections.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 501 establishes a separate statutory offense for sexual offenses committed by a person in a position of authority and creates new felony penalties for violations involving a victim under the age of 13 or repeat offenders. It also designates these felony violations as predicate crimes for sexual solicitation of a minor and requires individuals convicted of the newly established felony offenses to register as Tier III sex offenders.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Minors participating in school or youth programs, persons in positions of authority (such as teachers, coaches, school counselors, and program leaders), criminal defendants, and law enforcement agencies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances, though it may shift an unknown number of cases from District Court to circuit courts and could result in longer terms of incarceration.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is responsible for the incarceration and community supervision of justice-involved individuals, as well as maintaining elements of sex offender registry compliance. The bill alters penalties, creates new felony offenses for individuals in a position of authority, and mandates Tier III sex offender registration for specified convictions.

AOC oversees the judicial branch operations. By creating felony penalties for subsequent offenses and offenses involving children under age 13, the bill shifts prosecution of certain cases from the District Court to the Circuit Courts and alters court sentencing requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD provides legal defense for indigent defendants in criminal cases. The creation of new felony offenses with significantly longer maximum terms of incarceration directly affects the caseload and defense requirements for qualifying clients.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes full-time sworn deputy sheriffs (at the rank of lieutenant or below) and court security officers in the Baltimore City Sheriff's Office to collectively bargain over compensation, including salary, wages, and merit step increases, directly with the Sheriff (or designee) and Baltimore City.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City Sheriff's Office and Baltimore City
qa_results.stakeholders: Full-time sworn law enforcement officers at or below the rank of lieutenant and court security officers in the Baltimore City Sheriff's Office, as well as Baltimore City government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected. Baltimore City expenditures may increase if negotiated agreements lead to higher personnel costs, though any potential increase cannot be reliably estimated in advance. Baltimore City revenues are not affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill increases the minimum annual salaries for the chair, members, and part-time inspectors of the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners and entitles them, as well as the deputy chief inspector, to receive any cost-of-living increases provided to nonrepresented county employees.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Members, deputy chief inspector, and part-time inspectors of the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners, as well as Anne Arundel County taxpayers and local government.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact. Anne Arundel County expenditures increase by at least $33,716 annually starting in fiscal year 2027 to cover base salary increases for the board chair, two members, and 18 part-time inspectors. Expenditures are estimated to increase further in subsequent years (e.g., $34,390 in FY 2028 and $36,495 in FY 2031) assuming a 2% annual cost-of-living adjustment. Local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor is responsible for appointing the members and designating the chair of the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners. While this bill increases compensation and provides cost-of-living increases funded entirely by Anne Arundel County with no state fiscal impact, it directly affects gubernatorial appointee positions.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and recommending appointees for boards and commissions across Maryland, including the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners. The bill modifies the compensation terms for these appointed positions, though it imposes no new operational requirements on the office.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames and alters the authorized activities and requirements for alcoholic beverages entertainment permits in Anne Arundel County, reclassifying music permits as background entertainment permits, entertainment permits as general entertainment permits, and dancing permits as full entertainment permits. It also establishes a 100-foot setback requirement from residentially zoned property for outdoor entertainment under general and full entertainment permits.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license holders and entertainment venues in Anne Arundel County, their patrons, and residents living near licensed establishments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. The bill is not expected to materially affect Anne Arundel County finances or operations, with permit fees remaining unchanged.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article regarding entertainment permits for alcoholic beverages license holders in Anne Arundel County. While the permits are issued and administered locally by the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, the bill pertains to the broader regulation of the alcoholic beverage industry, which falls under the regulatory scope of the Comptroller of Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the fee structure for Class C per diem alcoholic beverages licenses in Anne Arundel County based on estimated event attendance. For events with fewer than 500 attendees, the license fees remain $25 per day for beer or beer and wine, and $50 per day for beer, wine, and liquor. For events with an estimated attendance of 500 or more, the daily fees of $25 or $50 are charged per point of sale location serving alcohol at the event.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Clubs, organizations, and applicants holding events serving alcohol under Class C per diem licenses in Anne Arundel County, particularly those hosting large events of 500 or more individuals.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is no State fiscal effect. Anne Arundel County revenues are estimated to increase by up to $7,000 annually beginning in fiscal year 2027 due to increased fees charged per point of sale location for events with an estimated attendance of 500 or more individuals. County expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for state-level regulation of the alcohol industry. While this bill specifically alters local Class C per diem license fees administered by the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal effect, it pertains to the broader subject area of alcoholic beverage licensing and regulation.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Joanne C. Benson Maryland Phone-Free Schools Act requires each county board of education to develop and implement a policy by the 2027-2028 school year prohibiting student use of personal electronic communication devices and social media platforms during the academic school day, with certain exceptions for disabilities, documented health issues, instructional use, language translation, or caregiving needs. It also establishes tiered discipline guidelines prohibiting suspension or expulsion solely for device violations, and mandates reporting by local boards and the Maryland State Department of Education.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) and local county boards of education
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland public school students, parents, teachers, school administrators, and local school boards (excluding the Maryland School for the Blind and the Maryland School for the Deaf)
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local revenues are unaffected. MSDE can fulfill regulatory, data collection, and reporting duties using existing budgeted resources. Local school boards can develop, implement, store devices under, and report on the policies using existing resources and infrastructure, with any additional reporting or administrative costs expected to be minimal and absorbable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates MSDE as the primary regulatory and oversight authority, requiring the department to adopt implementing regulations, collect and publish local school system device policies, and receive annual implementation impact reports.
The bill explicitly mentions the Maryland School for the Deaf to exempt it from the requirement to implement the electronic communication device prohibition policy.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 529 is a code revision measure that revises, restates, and recodifies laws governing the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and the Maryland Children's Health Program. It makes technical and stylistic updates, corrects cross-references, modernizes behavioral health terminology (such as updating 'substance abuse' to 'substance use disorder'), and reorganizes sections without making substantive changes to the law.
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Medical Assistance Program and Maryland Children's Health Program recipients, managed care organizations, contracted health care providers, and state behavioral health and Medicaid administrators.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state or local fiscal impact. The Fiscal and Policy Note indicates that the bill's provisions are intended solely as nonsubstantive statutory revisions, restatements, and recodifications.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill revises, restates, and recodifies the core statutory provisions governing the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which is administered directly by the Maryland Department of Health and its Behavioral Health Administration.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill recodifies the statutory provisions establishing the Maryland Medicaid Advisory Committee, detailing its composition, operational duties, and advisory responsibilities.
The Executive Director of the Maryland Health Care Commission serves as an ex officio member of the Maryland Medicaid Advisory Committee, and commission data is reviewed by the committee.
The bill recodifies provisions conditioning Medicaid hospital reimbursement rates on the submission of patient discharge data to the Health Services Cost Review Commission.
The Secretary of Human Services serves ex officio on the Maryland Medicaid Advisory Committee, and Medicaid enrollment coordinates directly with SNAP and foster care programs administered by DHS.
The Maryland Insurance Commissioner must be consulted by the Secretary of Health regarding the actuarial adjustment of capitation payments to managed care organizations.
The bill recodifies requirements that MDH consult with the State Department of Education to define school-based clinics participating in Medicaid managed care reimbursement.
The bill maintains statutory provisions for managed care organizations to appeal penalties imposed by MDH to the Office of Administrative Hearings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires governmental units that employ firefighters to calculate overtime pay based on hours worked in excess of 168 hours in a 28-day work period. It also requires counties and municipalities to provide specific payroll information to employed firefighters and authorizes a grievance process with potential damages if a local government fails to provide the required payroll information or wages due.
qa_results.stakeholders: Firefighters employed by governmental units across Maryland, as well as county and municipal governments that employ them.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected, as existing State-employed firefighters at BWI Airport generally do not exceed 168 hours in a 28-day period and the Maryland Department of Labor and Office of Administrative Hearings can handle enforcement with existing resources. Local government expenditures are expected to increase beginning in FY 2029, potentially by millions of dollars in certain jurisdictions (such as Frederick, Howard, and Montgomery counties), due to paying additional overtime, hiring extra personnel to avoid overtime thresholds, or paying grievance damages.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor oversees and enforces the state's Wage and Hour Law and Wage Payment and Collection Law, and is responsible for investigating complaints regarding overtime pay and wage payments.

The Maryland Aviation Administration directly employs 99 state firefighters at Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport whose overtime wage calculations are subject to the bill's requirements.

The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent department of the Maryland Aviation Administration and manages the Transportation Trust Fund, which funds the state firefighters affected by the overtime provisions.

The Office of Administrative Hearings adjudicates contested wage payment cases referred by the Department of Labor as well as state employee grievances, and will need to train its administrative law judges on the substantive requirements of the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Natural Resources to report annually on the agricultural land transfer tax proceeds distributed to the Mel Noland Woodland Incentives and Fellowship Fund from woodland property transfers, including any uncertainties regarding the amounts distributed and steps needed to resolve them.
qa_results.stakeholders: Department of Natural Resources, the Maryland General Assembly, private woodland owners, and participants in the Woodland Incentives and Mel Noland Fellowship programs
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Department of Natural Resources can implement the reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 533 directly impacts DNR as the administering agency of the Mel Noland Woodland Incentives and Fellowship Fund, requiring DNR to expand its annual report to include proceeds distributed from the agricultural land transfer tax on entirely woodland parcels and report any uncertainties regarding those distributions.

The Comptroller of Maryland receives agricultural land transfer tax remittances and oversees distributions to state funds, making the agency relevant to determining the proceeds distributed to the Fund and addressing any reporting uncertainties identified by DNR.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the maximum annual revenue cap for a business to qualify as a cottage food business from $50,000 to $100,000.
qa_results.stakeholders: Cottage food business owners, home-based food producers, consumers, and retail food stores.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Maryland Department of Health increase by $52,434 in FY 2027 to hire one part-time registered sanitarian to process additional cottage food business requests, rising to $67,700 by FY 2031. There is also a potential minimal decrease in general fund revenues beginning in FY 2027 if businesses choose to operate as cottage food businesses instead of paying licensing fees for commercial food manufacturing. Local health departments can handle any increase in complaint investigations or inspections with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health regulates cottage food businesses under the Health - General Article, issues unique identification numbers, reviews labeling and training certifications, and anticipates an increase in administrative and inspection workload requiring additional personnel.
The Department of Agriculture promotes local agricultural products and oversees food quality and farmers' markets where cottage food products are commonly marketed and sold directly to consumers.
