qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland State Department of Education to make available a synchronous or asynchronous professional development course on educator well-being and flourishing to all school personnel and administrators by July 1, 2027, provided it can be offered at no cost or at a cost comparable to similar courses.
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland public school teachers, administrators, and other school personnel
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures are not materially affected, as the Maryland State Department of Education can offer an existing qualifying course using existing resources, and the bill only requires course provision if done at no cost or comparable cost. State revenues are not affected. Local school system finances are not affected because local systems are not required to develop, provide, or mandate completion of the course.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 546 directly mandates that the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) make available a professional development course on educator well-being and flourishing for all school personnel and administrators by July 1, 2027.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires the Secretary of Agriculture to submit an annual report to the Governor and the General Assembly recommending additional equipment that should qualify for the State income tax subtraction modification for enhanced agricultural management equipment. It also establishes a refundable State income tax credit of up to $1,000 for parents of a stillborn child, subject to income phaseouts based on federal adjusted gross income, beginning in taxable year 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture and Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Parents of stillborn children, agricultural producers and equipment owners, and the Maryland Department of Agriculture.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal and Policy Note, the Maryland Department of Agriculture's reporting requirement can be implemented with existing budgeted resources. While the attached Fiscal Note indicates no effect on revenues, the enrolled version of the bill subsequently added a refundable income tax credit of up to $1,000 per stillborn child beginning in tax year 2027, which will result in an indeterminate decrease in State general fund revenues; specific overall dollar estimates for the credit are unavailable in the provided note.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the state's tax administration agency responsible for administering the individual and corporate income tax, including the enhanced agricultural management equipment subtraction modification and the newly established refundable tax credit for parents of a stillborn child.

The bill directly mandates that the Secretary of Agriculture report annually to the Governor and the General Assembly regarding additional types of equipment recommended to qualify as enhanced agricultural management equipment for the tax subtraction modification.

The bill requires the Secretary of Agriculture to submit an annual report to the Governor detailing recommended equipment eligible for the enhanced agricultural management equipment subtraction modification.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Maryland Housing Certainty Act establishes that housing development project applications must be evaluated solely under the local laws and regulations in effect when a complete application is submitted. It grants proponents of approved housing projects vested development rights for at least five years, requires local authorities and M-NCPPC to make completeness determinations within 30 days, and prohibits local governments from collecting residential development impact fees and excise taxes until construction is completed and occupancy requirements are met (or up to 30 days prior to final inspection).
qa_results.responsible_party: Local regulatory authorities and the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission (M-NCPPC)
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential real estate developers, home builders, housing construction businesses, and local county and municipal planning and zoning authorities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State finances. Local government finances are affected by delaying the collection of development impact fees and excise taxes until project completion, which may require local jurisdictions to issue additional debt or defer capital projects. Additionally, local government expenditures may increase in some jurisdictions to hire personnel or upgrade systems to meet the 30-day application completeness review requirement and manage tracking of vested rights.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Planning provides policy guidance, data analysis, and technical assistance to local governments on comprehensive planning, zoning, and land use regulation. The fiscal note specifically notes that MDP may provide guidance and technical assistance to local jurisdictions to manage the implementation of these land use and vesting changes.

As the state's principal agency for housing policy, community development, and housing supply initiatives, the department is directly invested in statutory changes that affect housing construction predictability, permitting timelines, and local development impact fees on residential real estate projects.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Commission on the House of Reformation and Instruction for Colored Children within the Office of the Attorney General to investigate the facility's history, operations, and resident deaths. The commission is charged with locating and documenting unmarked graves, conducting forensic and genealogical analysis to identify deceased children, engaging descendants and communities, and recommending memorials, reburial protocols, reparative measures, and systemic juvenile justice reforms.
qa_results.stakeholders: Descendants and families of youth who died or resided at the institution, former residents and justice-involved youth, African American communities, and historical researchers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $1,050,000 in FY 2027, reflecting budgeted funds for the Boys' Village of Maryland Cemetery project redirected to support the commission's work, with potential additional indeterminate expenditures in FY 2028 and FY 2029. The Office of the Attorney General can handle commission staffing within existing resources. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 552 designates the Attorney General as the Chair of the newly created Commission on the House of Reformation and Instruction for Colored Children. The Office of the Attorney General is responsible for staffing the Commission, administering its funds and appropriations, appointing six public members, procuring contracts and services, and issuing subpoenas on behalf of the Commission.

The Secretary of Juvenile Services serves as a member of the Commission. The House of Reformation and Instruction for Colored Children is the historical predecessor of DJS's Cheltenham Youth Detention Center, where the cemetery is located, and DJS holds relevant historical and juvenile records. Additionally, existing FY 2027 funding for the cemetery project was allocated within DJS's budget.

The Director of the Maryland Historical Trust (a unit within the Department of Planning) is designated as a Commission member. Furthermore, the Commission must consult with the Maryland Historical Trust regarding methods and safety for archaeological surveys, excavations, and disinterments.

The State Archivist serves as an ex officio member of the Commission, and the Commission will examine historical records maintained by the State Archives concerning the facility, its residents, and resident deaths.

The Commission must consult with the Maryland Department of Health regarding protocols and safety for disinterment and forensic analysis of human remains, and the investigation will review historical health and vital records.
The Chief Archaeologist of MDOT State Highway Administration (or their designee) is explicitly designated as a statutory member of the Commission to provide archaeological expertise.

The State Superintendent of Schools serves as a member of the Commission. Additionally, the Commission is tasked with developing recommendations to incorporate the history of the institution into the State's educational curriculum.

The Secretary of General Services (or their designee) is designated as a member of the Commission, which is tasked with cemetery preservation, restoration, and recommending a permanent state memorial.
The Secretary of Human Services (or their designee) is designated as a member of the Commission examining child welfare, institutional conditions, and state custody history.
The Secretary of Veterans and Military Families is designated as a Commission member, and the agency has collaborated with DJS on cemetery conservation planning.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally establishes a new temporary executive commission (operating for four years through June 30, 2030) charged with investigating, researching, and reporting recommendations.

The Executive Director of the Gibson-Banks Center for Race and Law at the University of Maryland Francis King Carey School of Law (a USM institution) serves on the Commission, and USM institutions may be engaged for contracted research and forensic analysis.
The Commission is required to submit both its initial progress report (due December 31, 2027) and final report with recommendations for systemic reform (due December 31, 2029) to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to maintain and publish a user-friendly, searchable database of active elevator inspection certificates on the Maryland Department of Labor's website, allowing users to search active certificates by street address, city, and county.
qa_results.responsible_party: Commissioner of Labor and Industry within the Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Elevator owners and operators, building managers, and members of the general public seeking elevator safety and certification information.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State requirements can likely be handled using existing budgeted resources. However, if the Maryland Department of Labor's current monthly spreadsheet does not satisfy the statutory requirement for a user-friendly searchable database, one-time general fund expenditures may increase by up to $75,000 to implement an online database module. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Commissioner of Labor and Industry, housed within the Maryland Department of Labor, to create and maintain a user-friendly, searchable database of active elevator inspection certificates on the department's website, searchable by address, city, and county.

qa_results.bill_summary: Updates statutory references to reflect the renaming of certain General Assembly committees, including renaming the House Health and Government Operations Committee to the House Health Committee and updating the Senate Committee on Education, Energy, and the Environment. It also alters the membership of the Legislative Policy Committee by adding the chair of the House Government, Labor, and Elections Committee and reducing the number of other appointed Delegates from four to three.
qa_results.stakeholders: Members and committees of the Maryland General Assembly, as well as State agencies submitting mandated reports and notices to legislative committees.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is technical in nature and has no effect on State or local governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Updates statutory reporting and notice requirements for the Department of Health to reflect the renaming of the House Health and Government Operations Committee to the House Health Committee.
Conforms statutory references to the House Health Committee for required submissions of proposed regulations and alternative contracting plans by the Exchange.

Updates the committee names (House Health Committee and Senate Finance Committee) that receive notices and recommendations from the Commissioner of Labor and Industry regarding federal Bloodborne Pathogen Standards.

Updates the committee chair titles (Senate Committee on Education, Energy, and the Environment and House Government, Labor, and Elections Committee) authorized to request the State Archivist to evaluate and make recommendations on official State designations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a binding predetermination review process enabling individuals to request specified Maryland departments to determine whether their criminal history disqualifies them from obtaining an occupational license or certificate before formally applying, permits a review fee up to $100 with waivers for low-income applicants, removes the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services from the definition of department under these provisions, and exempts mortgage loan originators.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor, Maryland Department of Agriculture, Maryland Department of Health, Department of Human Services, and Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals with criminal convictions seeking occupational or professional licenses or certificates in Maryland, and state licensing boards and regulatory departments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by $50,800 in FY 2027 ($30,814 for the Maryland Department of Labor to hire a part-time contractual employee and $20,000 for the Maryland Department of Agriculture for IT updates), $22,500 in FY 2028, and $23,500 in FY 2029 until the act terminates on June 30, 2029. Special fund revenues from review fees (up to $100, waivable) and subsequent licensing applications are indeterminate but expected to be minimal overall. Local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MD Labor is one of the primary departments required to implement the predetermination review process for its occupational licensing boards. It incurs a direct fiscal impact of $30,814 in FY 2027 (and ongoing costs through FY 2029) to hire a contractual staff member to manage predeterminations, and is required to submit an implementation report by October 1, 2028.

MDA is explicitly designated as a department subject to the predetermination review requirements and must report on implementation by October 1, 2028. The State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners within MDA incurs a $20,000 special fund expenditure in FY 2027 for IT programming to accommodate predetermination applications and fee collection.

MDH oversees numerous health occupational licensing boards that must establish the predetermination review process for applicants with criminal histories. MDH is also required to submit a report on implementation and costs to the General Assembly by October 1, 2028.

MDE is designated as one of the covered departments that must administer the criminal history predetermination review process for occupational licenses and certificates it issues, and it must report on implementation to the General Assembly by October 1, 2028.

DHS is explicitly included as one of the covered departments required to conduct predetermination reviews regarding criminal history for occupational licenses/certifications under its purview and submit an implementation report by October 1, 2028.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly removes DPSCS from the definition of 'department' under § 1-209 of the Criminal Procedure Article, exempting the department from the occupational licensing restrictions and predetermination review requirements.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill renames the Prince George’s County Wine Festival license to the wine festival license, removes the annual restriction allowing only one license per year to permit multiple licenses, and repeals the prohibition against holding a wine festival in the 24th legislative district.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Holders of retail alcoholic beverage licenses, Class 3 wineries, Class 4 limited wineries, event organizers, and residents and businesses in Prince George's County (including the 24th legislative district).
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal effect and does not materially affect Prince George's County operations or finances. Prince George's County anticipates issuing up to three additional wine festival licenses each year at the current license fee of $75, resulting in a minimal annual revenue increase of up to $225.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller regulates the alcohol industry and collects state alcohol taxes. While this legislation specifically affects the Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners and has no state fiscal impact, it relates to alcoholic beverages licensing and involves state-licensed Class 3 and Class 4 wineries.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill reestablishes mandated funding for the Maryland Child Care Credential Program by requiring the Governor to appropriate $5,687,000 annually in the State budget for fiscal years 2028 through 2030.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education (Office of Child Care)
qa_results.stakeholders: Child care staff, child care administrators, child care providers and small businesses, and the children and families they serve.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $5,687,000 annually in FY 2028, FY 2029, and FY 2030 to fulfill the statutory funding mandate for the Maryland Child Care Credential Program. There is no fiscal impact in FY 2027, no effect on state revenues, and no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), through its Division of Early Childhood/Office of Child Care, administers the Maryland Child Care Credential Program, which provides credentials, achievement bonuses, training vouchers, and reimbursements to child care providers funded by the bill.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for formulating the state budget and must incorporate the bill's statutory mandated appropriation of $5,687,000 in general funds annually for fiscal years 2028 through 2030.
The bill statutorily directs the Governor to include a specific mandated appropriation of $5,687,000 for the program in the annual executive budget bills for fiscal years 2028 through 2030.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 563 repeals the felony offense of intentionally harming, permanently disabling, or killing an animal owned or used by a law enforcement unit, replacing it with misdemeanor offenses specifically prohibiting intentionally harassing, interfering with, injuring, or killing an 'emergency response animal' (such as police dogs, police horses, or search and rescue dogs). It establishes graduated misdemeanor penalties depending on the severity of the act or whether it occurred during the commission of another crime, and recognizes defenses including necessity and reasonable actions taken to prevent physical harm from unlawful police use of force.
qa_results.responsible_party: The Maryland Judiciary, the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, and State and local law enforcement units
qa_results.stakeholders: Emergency response animal handlers, law enforcement officers, search and rescue personnel, emergency response animals (police and search/rescue dogs and horses), and individuals charged with interfering with or harming such animals
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances. Reclassifying the offenses from a felony to misdemeanors may shift some cases from the circuit courts to the District Court, but any resulting changes in incarceration or fine revenues are expected to be negligible given the historically low number of convictions for harming law enforcement animals.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state law enforcement agency, MSP regularly trains and deploys police work animals (such as K-9 units) protected under this statute, and its officers are responsible for enforcing criminal prohibitions against harassing, injuring, or killing emergency response animals.

The bill alters criminal penalties and shifts certain offenses regarding law enforcement animals from felonies to misdemeanors, affecting caseload distribution between the District Court and Circuit Courts across the state judicial system.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is responsible for the detention, incarceration, and community supervision of individuals sentenced under the criminal penalties established or modified by this bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent defendants charged with the criminal misdemeanors established by the bill, which carry potential sentences of incarceration ranging up to 5 years.

DNR oversees the Natural Resources Police, which employs trained law enforcement K-9 units and participates in search and rescue efforts covered under the bill's definition of emergency response animals.
MDEM coordinates state-level disaster response and emergency efforts, which include state-directed search and rescue operations that utilize search and rescue dogs protected by this legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Pet Cremation and Burial Services Consumer Protection Act establishes consumer protection, disclosure, and operational requirements for providers offering pet cremation services. It requires businesses to provide clear written descriptions of cremation options (such as private, individual-partitioned, and communal), issue certificates of verification upon returning pet cremains, meet standards for holding facilities, maintain records for at least five years, and establishes civil and criminal penalties for violations, classifying noncompliance as an unfair, deceptive, or abusive trade practice.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors and the Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Pet owners, crematories, registered cemeterians and cemetery operators, morticians and funeral directors, veterinarians, and pet shops.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State impacts are assumed to be absorbable within existing budgeted resources, with no material effect on State revenues. The Office of the Attorney General estimated needing approximately $300,000 annually for an assistant Attorney General and an investigator, but the Department of Legislative Services determined existing resources are sufficient. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill places regulatory requirements and oversight on crematory licensees under the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors, which is a licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health.

The bill establishes consumer protection and recordkeeping requirements for registered cemeterians, cemetery operators, and permit holders under Title 5 of the Business Regulation Article, which is administered and enforced by the Office of Cemetery Oversight within the Maryland Department of Labor.

The bill classifies violations as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is enforced by the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General, and authorizes regulatory bodies to refer violations directly to the Attorney General for civil enforcement.

The bill explicitly mandates that crematory licensees, registrants, and permit holders distribute written descriptions of their pet cremation services directly to the Maryland Department of Agriculture.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the County Commissioners of Queen Anne's County to use revenue collected from development impact fees to pay for capital costs associated with replacing public school facilities.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Commissioners of Queen Anne's County
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents, public school students and staff, and property developers in Queen Anne's County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Effect: None. Local Effect: None. The bill does not change the amount of development impact fees imposed or collected by Queen Anne's County; it only expands the authorized uses of existing fee revenues to cover capital costs related to replacing public school facilities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes Queen Anne's County to use development impact fee revenues to finance the capital costs of replacing public school facilities. The IAC oversees and coordinates public school construction and capital funding across Maryland school districts, making this local school facility funding expansion relevant to its work.

Under Maryland law, local jurisdictions that collect and spend development impact fees must report their collection, expenditure, and authorizing local laws to the Maryland Department of Planning. Any local implementation or amendment resulting from this authorization will fall under MDP's reporting and land use data tracking oversight.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the definition of 'nonprofit housing corporation' and extends exemptions from State and local real property taxes and special assessments to certain real property owned directly or indirectly through subsidiaries of nonprofit housing corporations providing affordable housing, excluding properties in Baltimore City and certain projects that received prior local government funding.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonprofit housing corporations, subsidiary housing entities, low- and moderate-income renters, and local governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local property tax revenues decrease by an indeterminate amount beginning in FY 2027, depending on the number of nonprofit housing corporations and eligible affordable housing properties qualifying for the exemption. State and local expenditures are not directly affected, though local governments may negotiate payments in lieu of taxes (PILOTs).

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Housing and Community Development Article regarding the definition and tax-exempt status of nonprofit housing corporations and their subsidiaries developing and operating affordable housing (including properties under the federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credit program administered by DHCD).

PTAAB hears appeals regarding disputes over real property valuations and tax exemptions, which may be affected by the altered and expanded exemption standards for nonprofit housing corporation properties.

The Comptroller serves as the State's chief tax collector and financial officer and tracks changes to State tax revenues, including the State property tax revenue decreases resulting from expanded exemptions.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill prohibits actions related to residential housing that have a discriminatory effect regardless of intent, codifying a disparate impact standard under State fair housing laws. It creates an exception where an action without discriminatory intent is necessary to achieve substantial, legitimate, and nondiscriminatory interests that could not be achieved by less discriminatory means, and authorizes the Department of Housing and Community Development to adopt regulations regarding the requirement to affirmatively further fair housing.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development and the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights
qa_results.stakeholders: Housing providers, landlords, real estate professionals, local housing authorities, and Maryland residents, particularly members of protected classes seeking residential housing.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. Any effect on small businesses, such as residential landlords, is expected to be minimal as the bill primarily codifies existing federal disparate impact standards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights is the primary enforcement agency for the State's fair housing laws. The bill directly impacts the Commission by defining discriminatory effect and prohibiting housing acts that have a discriminatory effect regardless of intent under Title 20 of the State Government Article.

The bill directly amends the Housing and Community Development Article to authorize the Department of Housing and Community Development to adopt regulations regarding its statutory duties to affirmatively further fair housing.

The bill references statutory sections governing the Attorney General's authority to investigate, prosecute, and remediate civil rights violations, which include discriminatory housing practices under Title 20.
Administrative Law Judges from the Office of Administrative Hearings conduct hearings and issue orders for contested housing discrimination charges initiated by the Commission on Civil Rights.
The bill affects provisions governing private rights of action in State courts for alleged discriminatory housing practices, including available relief, punitive damages, and attorney's fees.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires county boards of education to update their student attendance policies to allow excused or discretionary absences for public school students participating in civic engagement activities, such as testifying before legislative bodies, meeting with lawmakers, advocating on policy issues, and participating in the Maryland General Assembly Page Program.
qa_results.responsible_party: County boards of education (local school systems) and the Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland public school students, parents and guardians, public school teachers and administrators, and local school systems.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state or local fiscal impact. Local school systems can implement policy updates and track civic engagement absences using existing operational resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 575 amends the Education Article concerning public school attendance policies for civic engagement and explicitly authorizes the Department of Education, alongside local county boards, to deem additional activities as eligible civic engagement.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill updates Maryland's endangered and threatened species laws and the Irreplaceable Natural Areas Program. It defines 'harm' and 'foreseeable future,' requires determinations on listing species to be made without regard to economic impacts, establishes standards and petition procedures for delisting species, authorizes the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) to designate and manage essential habitats, requires periodic reviews of species lists and program regulations, and directs DNR to adopt regulations authorizing the taking of black vultures if federal protections are removed.
qa_results.stakeholders: Property owners, developers, small businesses engaged in land use or infrastructure, agricultural producers dealing with black vultures, conservationists, and the general public.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures for the Department of Natural Resources may increase beginning in FY 2027 to handle regulatory updates, permit reviews, and enforcement; however, costs cannot be reliably estimated. Other State agencies and local governments may experience increased capital project expenditures to comply with strengthened protections. State revenues are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary implementing and regulatory agency for the bill, tasked with establishing regulations, reviewing and delisting endangered and threatened species, designating essential habitats, updating Irreplaceable Natural Areas Program rules, and regulating the taking of wildlife such as migratory birds and black vultures.

The bill explicitly mandates statutory consultation with the Secretary of Agriculture regarding conservation programs for nongame, endangered, or threatened wildlife and plants, and addresses wildlife management impacting agriculture such as depredation permits for black vultures.

MDOT manages extensive state transportation infrastructure and capital development projects that must comply with strengthened essential habitat designations and regulations against habitat degradation and taking of protected species.

As the primary manager of state-owned facilities and capital construction projects, DGS's building and land operations may be impacted by requirements to avoid harming designated essential habitats or endangered species.

USM undertakes large-scale capital construction and land management across its campuses and was identified in the fiscal note as potentially impacted by compliance with strengthened fish, wildlife, and habitat protections.

The statute specifically references the Governor's duty to review programs administered under executive authority to utilize them in furtherance of the conservation of endangered and threatened species.

qa_results.bill_summary: Updates the Prince George's County alcoholic beverages law to require the Board of License Commissioners to send notice of the issuance of a Class C per diem beer, wine, and liquor license to the director of the Department of Permitting, Inspections, and Enforcement, rather than the former Department of Environmental Resources.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Prince George's County Department of Permitting, Inspections, and Enforcement, the Board of License Commissioners, and applicants or holders of Class C per diem alcoholic beverage licenses in Prince George's County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected, and the bill does not materially affect Prince George's County operations or finances.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a county board of library trustees to provide for the selection of a student member, establishing the student member's qualifications, one-year term of office, and voting rights on policy matters (and other nonpolicy matters if authorized by board policy or bylaws).
qa_results.stakeholders: High school students (juniors and seniors in public, nonpublic, or home instruction programs) and county boards of library trustees.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no State fiscal impact and does not materially affect local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Library Agency provides leadership, funding, and coordination for Maryland's 24 public library systems. This bill alters the governance framework of county boards of library trustees by authorizing and establishing criteria for a student member.
The bill establishes qualifications for student members based on high school enrollment and standing, which relates to MSDE's oversight of public secondary education students.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Workgroup on Transportation Contract Approval Authority to study the existing procurement approval authority structure and statutory exemptions from Board of Public Works oversight for capital expenditures by the Maryland Department of Transportation and the Maryland Transportation Authority concerning State roads, bridges, and highways, and requires a report of findings and recommendations by December 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation and the Board of Public Works
qa_results.stakeholders: State transportation procurement officials, transportation engineering and construction contractors, Disadvantaged Business Enterprises and Minority Business Enterprises (DBEs/MBEs), and labor organizations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state or local fiscal impact. Staffing requirements for the workgroup can be handled by the Maryland Department of Transportation and the Board of Public Works using existing resources, and any travel reimbursements for workgroup members are minimal and absorbable. Revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly studies the contract and procurement approval authority of MDOT and the Maryland Transportation Authority. The Secretary of Transportation is a designated member of the workgroup, and MDOT is tasked with jointly staffing the workgroup.

The bill centers on examining the Board of Public Works' approval and oversight authority over transportation capital expenditures, and BPW is required to jointly provide staff support for the workgroup.
The study and report specifically examine the procurement and approval authority structure for capital expenditures by MDTA in connection with State roads, bridges, or highways.
The workgroup is specifically tasked with evaluating whether to expand delegated procurement authority to contracts and change orders supporting MTA fixed guideway systems, facilities, and vehicles.
The Comptroller, or the Comptroller's designee, is statutorily designated as a member of the Workgroup on Transportation Contract Approval Authority.
The State Treasurer, or the State Treasurer's designee, is statutorily designated as a member of the Workgroup on Transportation Contract Approval Authority.

The Governor is responsible for designating the chair of the workgroup, appointing four workgroup members representing specific industry and labor stakeholders, and receiving the workgroup's final report.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a temporary study body, the Workgroup on Transportation Contract Approval Authority, tasked with evaluating state procurement procedures and submitting findings and recommendations.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for the four gubernatorial appointments to the workgroup.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames the Howard County Agricultural Land Preservation Fund to the Howard County Agricultural Preservation and Innovation Fund and broadens the authorized uses of transfer tax proceeds distributed to the fund to include programs, services, and initiatives that enhance the commercial viability or environmental sustainability of agriculture in Howard County.
qa_results.stakeholders: Howard County farmers, agricultural businesses, and county residents involved in or benefiting from agricultural preservation and sustainability initiatives.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact. It does not alter transfer tax rates, funding sources, or the overall revenue allocated to the fund; it only alters the fund's name and broadens the allowable uses of the funds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill broadens the allowable uses of Howard County's agricultural preservation fund to include programs that enhance the commercial viability and environmental sustainability of agriculture. While this pertains strictly to Howard County local transfer tax proceeds with no state fiscal impact, it relates tangentially to the Department of Agriculture's mission regarding agricultural viability and land preservation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits a person in Wicomico County from standing in a roadway, shoulder, median divider, or intersection determined by the county or a local municipality (in consultation with the State Highway Administration) to be inherently dangerous. Police officers may only issue citations if approved traffic warning signs have been properly installed.
qa_results.stakeholders: Pedestrians, drivers, and law enforcement officers in Wicomico County and its municipalities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances, as the State Highway Administration can implement consultation and approval requirements with existing resources. Wicomico County and local municipal operations and finances are also not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the State Highway Administration with consulting on whether State roadways in Wicomico County are inherently dangerous, providing standards for warning signs under its traffic control manual, and approving the installation of signage on State highways.

The Department of Transportation is the parent department of the State Highway Administration, which is directly responsible for regulatory oversight, consultation, and approval of signage on State highways under the bill.

As the primary law enforcement agency patrolling State highways in Maryland, State Police troopers enforcing traffic safety in Wicomico County are subject to the bill's restrictions on issuing citations for pedestrian standing violations.
The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the District Court system, which processes and adjudicates citations issued for traffic and pedestrian violations under the Transportation Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill prohibits unauthorized computer access and related acts committed with the intent to interrupt or impair the functioning of critical infrastructure or a public safety answering point (PSAP), punishable as a felony with up to 5 years imprisonment and a fine up to $25,000. It also creates a new felony offense for committing such acts that actually deny access to an authorized user or interrupt or impair critical infrastructure or a PSAP, punishable by up to 10 years imprisonment and a fine up to $50,000.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services and the Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Operators and users of critical infrastructure (including public utilities, healthcare, and transportation), 9-1-1 public safety answering points (PSAPs), Maryland residents relying on emergency and essential services, and individuals accused of computer-related offenses.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new felony offense and expands existing criminal provisions concerning computer-related interference with critical infrastructure and public safety answering points, which directly impacts state court caseloads and judicial administration.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The legislation establishes new felony penalties and expands existing criminal liability for cyber interference with critical infrastructure, impacting caseloads and legal defense representation provided to indigent defendants.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new 10-year felony and expands existing felony provisions, affecting the department's correctional facilities, inmate population intake, and community supervision caseloads.
MDEM oversees the Maryland 9-1-1 Board, which governs and supports local Public Safety Answering Points (PSAPs), a primary subject of the bill's criminal protections against cyber interference.

As the primary state law enforcement agency with criminal investigation responsibilities, MSP investigates cybercrimes, computer tampering offenses, and physical threats targeting critical infrastructure.
DoIT manages the state's IT network and leads cybersecurity posture for state virtual and physical infrastructure assets covered under the bill's critical infrastructure definition.
GOHS advises on statewide strategies for disaster prevention, emergency response, and the security and protection of Maryland's critical infrastructure assets.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands eligibility for the State income tax credit for physician preceptors in health care workforce shortage areas by allowing preceptorship programs authorized by accredited out-of-state medical schools. It also reduces the required clinical training hours per rotation from 100 to 90 hours and caps the cumulative amount of unused credit certificates that may be carried forward to subsequent years at $100,000.
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed physicians serving as uncompensated preceptors, medical students and postgraduate trainees in accredited medical programs (including out-of-state programs), and residents in Maryland areas with health care workforce shortages.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may decrease beginning in FY 2027 if the bill increases utilization of the tax credit. The credit program is capped at $100,000 annually, with up to $100,000 in unused credits eligible to carry forward from prior years, but the exact revenue decrease cannot be reliably estimated. State expenditures are unaffected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health directly administers the physician preceptors tax credit, reviewing applications, issuing tax credit certificates, tracking carryforwards, reporting annually to the Comptroller and General Assembly, and adopting regulations.

As the state's principal tax collector, the Comptroller administers the state income tax against which this credit is claimed and receives annual reports from MDH regarding issued credit certificates.
The Board is statutorily required to consult with the Maryland Department of Health to identify geographic areas with health care workforce shortages and to adopt program regulations.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill updates the Maryland Uniform Simultaneous Death Act to conform with the 1993 Uniform Law Commission model act. Under the bill, an individual must be shown by clear and convincing evidence to have survived another individual or specified event by at least 120 hours to be legally deemed a survivor for purposes of property devolution, rights to elective shares/allowances, or governing instruments. The bill also specifies exceptions, evidentiary standards for determining time of death, and liability protections for third-party payors who distribute assets in good faith.
qa_results.responsible_party: The Maryland Judiciary, including the Orphans' Courts and the Registers of Wills
qa_results.stakeholders: Heirs, estate beneficiaries, joint property owners, estate executors and administrators, trustees, insurers, and other third-party payors managing property distributions upon death.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances, and small businesses are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Register of Wills is responsible for the administrative probate of decedents' estates and serves as clerk to the Orphans' Court. The bill directly modifies rules governing the devolution of property and inheritance by establishing a 120-hour survival requirement and setting procedures for disputed property held or deposited in probate proceedings.

The bill amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article to establish evidentiary procedures and standards for determining an individual's death or survival, and authorizes third-party payors to deposit disputed funds or property directly with the courts having jurisdiction over probate proceedings.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill modifies the Community Choice Aggregation Pilot Program in Montgomery County by adjusting its start date to the earlier of when the county provides notice or April 1, 2026, extending the program's duration from seven to nine years, and pushing back interim and final reporting deadlines for the Public Service Commission to the seventh year and December 31, 2035, respectively.
qa_results.stakeholders: Montgomery County government, residential and small commercial electric customers in Montgomery County, and local electric distribution companies (BGE, Pepco, and Potomac Edison).
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations can implement the bill's changes with existing budgeted resources through the Public Service Commission and the Office of People's Counsel, with no effect on state revenues. Montgomery County finances and local small businesses are not anticipated to be significantly affected within the five-year fiscal note period, though the broader pilot program may lower utility rates for participating residents and small businesses over time.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary regulatory agency overseeing the Community Choice Aggregation Pilot Program, reviewing aggregation plans, conducting the concluding cost-benefit study, and submitting required interim and final reports.

The Office of the People's Counsel represents residential utility consumers in proceedings and matters before the PSC related to the pilot program and is noted in the fiscal analysis as monitoring and implementing changes with existing resources.
The Governor's Office is a statutory recipient of the final study and report on the pilot program's findings and effectiveness submitted by the Public Service Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill increases the required bond amount for the Treasurer and Deputy Treasurer of the St. Mary's County Metropolitan Commission (MetCom) from $25,000 to $250,000, makes MetCom's studies and plans for new facilities discretionary rather than mandatory in areas not planned for service, and increases maximum criminal and civil fines and administrative enforcement remedies for violations of water, sewer, and commission regulations.
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents, property owners, and water and sewer utility customers in St. Mary's County, individuals who violate MetCom regulations, and MetCom executive officers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected. St. Mary's County and MetCom revenues may increase beginning in FY 2027 to the extent higher fines and penalties are imposed for misdemeanors, unauthorized water removal, and civil infractions. Local expenditures are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires that the required surety bond provided by the Treasurer and any Deputy Treasurer of the St. Mary's County Metropolitan Commission be in a form approved by the Maryland Insurance Administration and the County Attorney.

The bill alters criminal misdemeanor penalties and sets procedures for civil infraction citations where defendants elect to stand trial before the District Court, including trial scheduling and remission of collected fines, impacting court operations supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a three-year pilot program allowing the City of Gaithersburg and the City of Rockville to use stop sign monitoring systems in school zones, subject to local authorization, and impose a civil penalty of up to $40 on vehicle owners for violations.
qa_results.responsible_party: City of Gaithersburg, City of Rockville, District Court of Maryland, and the Maryland State Highway Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Motor vehicle owners and drivers traveling through school zones in Gaithersburg and Rockville, school pedestrians and students, and local law enforcement agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may increase minimally from FY 2027 through FY 2030 from fines on contested citations paid to the District Court, with no material impact on State expenditures. Local revenues and expenditures for Gaithersburg and Rockville will increase from FY 2027 through FY 2030 to install and administer systems, collect citation penalty revenues (capped at $40 per violation), and reinvest net proceeds into public/pedestrian safety; specific dollar amounts are indeterminate.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Under the statute amended by the bill, stop sign monitoring systems deployed on State highways located within school zones must be authorized by the State Highway Administration, and SHA is required to place prominent signs giving notice of monitoring systems on State highways.

The District Court of Maryland (supported by the AOC) is responsible for prescribing the uniform citation form, setting penalty prepayment amounts, adopting procedures for citation issuance and contested hearings, and processing contested violation cases and fine collections.

The MVA is responsible for enforcing vehicle registration holds or suspensions for individuals who fail to pay or contest stop sign monitoring citations, and for ensuring that these civil citations are not recorded as moving violations on driving records.

MDOT is the parent department overseeing both the State Highway Administration and the Motor Vehicle Administration, both of which have statutory roles in the authorization of placements on State highways, signage, and vehicle registration enforcement.

The bill mandates that the City of Gaithersburg and the City of Rockville submit a comprehensive evaluation report on the pilot program's costs, operations, citations, and safety effectiveness to the Governor by December 1, 2028.
Under the automated enforcement provisions governing the program, any net citation revenues exceeding statutory caps (10% of total municipal/county revenues) must be remitted to the Comptroller.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 604 proposes a constitutional amendment requiring the Governor to include appropriations in the annual State budget to fund all terms of memoranda of understanding (MOUs) reached through collective bargaining or binding arbitration for State employees, State institutions of higher education, and the Maryland Environmental Service. Contingent on voter approval, the bill also reforms statutory collective bargaining procedures by introducing binding arbitration for certain State employee impasses, establishing neutral arbitrator oversight, and expanding collective bargaining topics to include fringe and health benefits.
qa_results.stakeholders: State employees, exclusive employee representative unions, the Governor, Maryland Environmental Service, and State institutions of higher education
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Contingent on voter approval in November 2026, State expenditures (all funds) increase annually by at least $150,000 beginning in FY 2028 for arbitration services and additional labor relations/human resources personnel. Personnel and other operational expenditures may be affected, potentially significantly, beginning in FY 2029 depending on the outcomes of negotiated MOUs and binding arbitration awards. Local government finances and revenues are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill proposes an amendment to Article III, § 52 of the Maryland Constitution and statutory changes requiring the Governor to include appropriations in the annual budget bill necessary to fund all terms of collective bargaining memoranda of understanding or binding arbitration awards.

DBM is the State's central budget and personnel agency, responsible for conducting collective bargaining on behalf of the Governor. The bill substantially alters collective bargaining timelines, subjects negotiations to neutral arbitration, expands bargaining subjects to health and fringe benefits, and imposes direct personnel and operational costs on DBM.

MES is explicitly named throughout the bill and the proposed constitutional amendment as an entity whose collective bargaining agreements and arbitration awards must be funded in the Governor's budget, which the fiscal note indicates could impact MES's traditional nonbudgeted status.

PERB is the state agency responsible for overseeing and standardizing public sector collective bargaining and adjudicating unfair labor practice charges, which are expressly preserved and referenced under the bill's new arbitration framework.

USM and the Chancellor are explicitly designated in the bill and proposed constitutional amendment regarding collective bargaining representation, memoranda of understanding, and the requirement that the Governor include required appropriations in the annual budget.

Morgan State University's governing board is specifically designated in the bill as a bargaining party for its employees, and its employee memoranda of understanding are subject to the bill's budgetary inclusion requirements.

St. Mary's College of Maryland is specifically named as an employer entity whose governing board designates collective bargaining representatives and whose employee agreements are subject to the bill's provisions.

The bill proposes a constitutional amendment that must be submitted to the voters of Maryland for approval or rejection at the November 2026 general election, which SBE is responsible for administering.

The bill specifically references and maintains existing statutory impasse and arbitration provisions governing the uniformed fire employees of the BWI Airport Fire and Rescue Department, which is operated by MAA.

MDOT oversees the Maryland Aviation Administration (including the BWI Airport Fire and Rescue Department referenced in the bill) and employs state personnel subject to collective bargaining requirements.

The bill allows a neutral arbitrator to direct the production of revenue and expenditure estimates compiled by the Bureau of Revenue Estimates and the Board of Revenue Estimates, units associated with the Comptroller.

OAG serves as legal counsel to the State, the Governor, and state agencies in interpreting constitutional amendments, implementing collective bargaining law, and defending state actions in court proceedings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands eligibility for the residential property tax payment deferral program in Anne Arundel County to include permanently and totally disabled service members, including eligible members of reserve components, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), and the Public Health Service (PHS).
qa_results.stakeholders: Anne Arundel County homeowners who are permanently and totally disabled members of the uniformed services, reserve components, NOAA, or PHS, and Anne Arundel County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Effect: None. Local Effect: Potential minimal decrease in Anne Arundel County property tax revenues during any deferral period, depending on the number of new participants. Revenues will increase upon repayment when deferrals end, ownership transfers, or the eligible owner dies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill broadens property tax deferral eligibility criteria for disabled service members in Anne Arundel County to include reserve components and uniformed service members of NOAA and the Public Health Service. While the program is administered locally and has no direct state fiscal impact, it relates to the department's mission of advocating for and informing active-duty service members, veterans, and military families about housing benefits and tax relief.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 607 increases the statutory annual salaries of the Maryland Comptroller, State Treasurer, Attorney General, and Secretary of State starting with the four-year term of office beginning in January 2027, in accordance with the recommendations of the Governor's Salary Commission.
qa_results.stakeholders: Current and future holders of the offices of Maryland Comptroller, State Treasurer, Attorney General, and Secretary of State.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $10,800 in FY 2028, $21,500 in FY 2029, $32,300 in FY 2030, and $43,000 in FY 2031 to reflect salary increases and fringe benefits for the four constitutional officers. There is no effect in FY 2027, state revenues are unaffected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly sets and increases the statutory annual salary for the Comptroller of Maryland for the term beginning in January 2027.
The bill directly sets and increases the statutory annual salary for the State Treasurer for the term beginning in January 2027.
The bill directly sets and increases the statutory annual salary for the Attorney General for the term beginning in January 2027.
The bill directly sets and increases the statutory annual salary for the Secretary of State for the term beginning in January 2027.

DBM is responsible for state budget execution and personnel management, and it will be responsible for incorporating the mandated salary increases and fringe benefit expenditures into future state budgets.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The legislation directly enacts the statutory salary recommendations formulated and submitted by the Governor's Salary Commission.
The bill was introduced by request of the Governor's Salary Commission and adjusts salaries for key constitutional officers who serve alongside or within the executive branch.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Chief Judge of the Appellate Court of Maryland and administrative judges for the circuit courts or the District Court to receive an annual stipend in addition to their annual salaries, and increases the minimum compensation of the Chairman of the Workers' Compensation Commission to match the salary of the Chief Judge of the District Court.
qa_results.responsible_party: Workers' Compensation Commission and the Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: The Chief Judge of the Appellate Court of Maryland, administrative judges of the circuit courts and District Court, and the Chairman of the Workers' Compensation Commission.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures for the Workers' Compensation Commission increase by $22,300 annually starting in FY 2027 to raise the Chairman's salary to equal that of the Chief Judge of the District Court. The expenditure impact of annual stipends for administrative judges is accounted for under separate enacted legislation (Senate Joint Resolution 2 and House Joint Resolution 6 of 2026). There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the judicial branch by authorizing annual stipends for the Chief Judge of the Appellate Court of Maryland and judges serving as administrative judges in the circuit courts and the District Court, which are administered through the court system.

The bill directly alters the statutory compensation of the Chairman of the Workers' Compensation Commission to be at least equal to the salary of the Chief Judge of the District Court, resulting in an annual increase in special fund expenditures for the commission beginning in FY 2027.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires qualified organizations in St. Mary's County to obtain a gaming permit before operating a gaming device, and authorizes the County Commissioners of St. Mary's County to adopt regulations and appoint a designee to administer permit issuance.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Commissioners of St. Mary's County
qa_results.stakeholders: Qualified organizations operating gaming devices in St. Mary's County, including volunteer fire companies, religious, fraternal, civic, war veterans', and charitable organizations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact. St. Mary's County can administer permit issuance and enforcement using existing resources, and county revenues are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency serves as Maryland's primary regulatory body for gaming. While this bill establishes a local permit framework administered by St. Mary's County rather than the State, state-level statutory changes to gaming device regulations and charitable gaming operations fall within the agency's general policy area.

Under the governing subtitle in the Criminal Law Article for St. Mary's County gaming, State Police officers are authorized to inspect records of proceeds and expenditures maintained by qualified organizations operating gaming devices.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill defines 'living shorelines' in statute alongside nonstructural shoreline stabilization measures as preferred erosion control methods for waterfront properties. It alters the Maryland Department of the Environment's (MDE) waiver process for property owners seeking exemptions to install structural stabilization, requiring site visits upon request within 45 days, notice to local soil conservation districts, the creation and publication of a waiver evaluation scoring system, and stakeholder engagement on future process improvements.
qa_results.stakeholders: Waterfront property owners, licensed marine contractors, local soil conservation districts, and businesses or state/local agencies undertaking shoreline stabilization projects.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: MDE can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. Special fund revenues for the Wetlands and Waterways Program Fund may increase beginning in FY 2027 if definitions lead to more structural shoreline stabilization projects subject to permit application fees. State and local government expenditures for shoreline stabilization projects may increase due to potential project delays and cost increases. Workload and potential costs for local soil conservation districts may also increase; specific dollar amounts are undetermined.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary implementing agency responsible for adopting regulations, establishing and publishing a waiver evaluation scoring system, conducting requested site visits within 45 days, collaborating with stakeholders, and submitting a progress report to the General Assembly.

MDE must consult with DNR when adopting regulations for shoreline stabilization measures and waiver processes. Additionally, provisions governing erosion control in the Natural Resources Article under DNR are repealed and aligned with the Environment Article.

The bill requires MDE to provide local soil conservation districts—which operate under the purview and coordination of the Department of Agriculture—with written notice of waiver requests and an opportunity to submit recommendations.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 618 authorizes the use of electronic rental agreements for self-service storage facilities, prohibits occupants from using storage spaces beyond their rental term after receiving a notice of nonrenewal, and establishes required notice procedures and timelines before an operator may dispose of remaining personal property. Operators must grant occupants at least 30 days following a nonrenewal notice to vacate property and provide at least 10 days' notice of intent to dispose before disposing of any remaining items.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners and operators of self-service storage facilities and occupants renting storage units in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government finances and operations are not materially affected by the bill. The impact on small businesses is anticipated to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division enforces statutory protections under the Maryland Commercial Law Article. The bill amends provisions under the Maryland Self-Service Storage Act governing rental agreements, nonrenewal notices, and procedures for disposing of personal property.

qa_results.bill_summary: Enters Maryland into the Interstate Podiatric Medical Licensure Compact to establish an expedited licensure pathway for qualified podiatrists to practice across member states, creates the Interstate Podiatric Medical Licensure Compact Commission to oversee administration, and establishes procedures for background checks, license renewals, joint investigations, and interstate disciplinary actions. The Act is contingent on at least four other states enacting substantially similar legislation.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Podiatric Medical Examiners (within the Maryland Department of Health)
qa_results.stakeholders: Podiatrists seeking expedited multi-state licensure, patients receiving podiatric medical care, and the State Board of Podiatric Medical Examiners.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures and revenues for the State Board of Podiatric Medical Examiners (BPME) are expected to increase by an indeterminate amount upon joining the compact. Expenditures will rise due to potential annual assessments levied by the commission, participation in a coordinated information system, and processing licensure applications; revenues may increase through fees collected for issuing and renewing expedited licenses. Local operations and finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health oversees health occupation licensing boards, including the State Board of Podiatric Medical Examiners (BPME), which will implement the compact's licensing, verification, and disciplinary provisions. Furthermore, the bill explicitly directs MDH to notify the Department of Legislative Services once the contingent enactment threshold is met.

The bill enters Maryland into an interstate compact and establishes Maryland's representation and participation in the Interstate Podiatric Medical Licensure Compact Commission, which falls under interstate compact bodies and memberships in which the State participates.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the qualification requirements for an attorney appointed or retained as counsel to a local board of elections by requiring the individual to be a registered voter of the State of Maryland rather than a registered voter of the specific county.
qa_results.stakeholders: Local boards of elections and attorneys seeking appointment or retention as legal counsel for local boards of elections across Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal effect and does not materially affect local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Board of Elections is responsible for overseeing the activities of local boards of elections across the state and ensuring compliance with the Election Law Article. This bill expands the eligibility criteria for counsel appointed or retained by local boards of elections from county residents to any registered voter in Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 622 increases the maximum number of registered cannabis agents a micro dispensary can employ from 10 to 20, extends the authorization for certain licensed dispensaries to deliver medical cannabis until July 1, 2027, and renames the responsible vendor training program to the cannabis agent training program while updating its curriculum and shifting the training frequency requirement from annually to within 90 days of hire and at least once every two years thereafter.
qa_results.stakeholders: Cannabis business licensees (including micro dispensaries and converted medical cannabis dispensaries), registered cannabis agents and employees, cannabis agent training program providers, and medical cannabis patients.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Cannabis Administration can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. The bill does not materially affect State revenues and has no effect on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was introduced at the request of the Maryland Cannabis Administration (MCA) and directly alters its regulatory scope. MCA is tasked with adopting regulations for cannabis agent training programs, approving training curriculum applications, prioritizing existing responsible vendor programs, and overseeing micro dispensary employee caps and dispensary delivery authorizations.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill establishes the Purple Star Colleges Program, administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission, to designate and recognize higher education institutions and private career schools that provide comprehensive support services for military-connected students. To qualify, institutions must designate a uniformed services staff liaison, create an accessible military resources webpage, maintain a transition program, and provide staff professional development. The bill also updates the definition of a military-connected student under the Purple Star Schools Program.
qa_results.stakeholders: Military-connected college and secondary students (service members, veterans, spouses, and dependents), institutions of higher education, and private career schools.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $43,821 in FY 2027 and $46,400 in FY 2028 for the Maryland Higher Education Commission to hire a contractual half-time program manager to implement the program and adopt regulations. Public higher education institutions and local community colleges may incur voluntary, absorbable costs if they seek designation. MSDE can implement regulatory changes with existing resources. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is the primary implementing agency tasked with administering the newly established Purple Star Colleges Program, developing application criteria, adopting regulations, and reviewing college applications.
MHEC is directly charged with establishing, administering, and adopting regulations for the Purple Star Colleges Program, incurring direct fiscal impacts for implementation staffing.
The bill amends the statutory definition of 'military-connected student' under the Purple Star Schools Program, which is administered by the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE).
USM institutions may voluntarily apply for Purple Star College designation by meeting specified service, web resource, transition program, and staff liaison criteria.

As a public institution of higher education, Morgan State University is eligible to seek Purple Star College designation under the program by implementing qualifying services and support for military-connected students.
As a public institution of higher education, St. Mary's College of Maryland is eligible to apply for Purple Star College designation.
DVMF advocates for and supports veterans, service members, and military families, aligning with the bill's focus on military-connected students.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that MHEC consult with the Maryland College Collaboration for Student Veterans Commission when adopting regulations to implement the Purple Star Colleges Program.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Safe Staffing Act of 2026 requires licensed non-State hospitals in Maryland to comply with accreditation and CMS staffing standards, establish a clinical staffing committee composed of managers and employees, and implement an annual clinical staffing plan by July 1, 2028.
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed Maryland hospitals, hospital clinical staff, nurses, healthcare workers, and hospital patients
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect state or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends Title 19 of the Health - General Article to require licensed hospitals to comply with certain staffing standards, establish clinical staffing committees, and implement clinical staffing plans. The Maryland Department of Health is responsible for the licensing, oversight, and regulation of healthcare facilities under this title.

qa_results.bill_summary: Transfers the responsibility for collecting annual statutory contributions from animal research facilities for the Human-Relevant Research Fund from the Maryland Department of Health to the Maryland Department of Agriculture, which will distribute the proceeds to the Maryland Technology Development Corporation.
qa_results.stakeholders: Research facilities in Maryland that conduct animal testing and submit federal APHIS Form 7023 (including higher education institutions), researchers seeking grants or loans for non-animal testing alternatives, the Maryland Department of Agriculture, the Maryland Department of Health, and TEDCO.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State General Fund expenditures for the Maryland Department of Agriculture increase by $42,900 in FY 2027, rising to $54,200 by FY 2031, to fund a half-time administrative officer to track compliance and collect contributions. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Human-Relevant Research Fund administered by TEDCO continue and may increase due to improved collection rates. There is no material impact on the Maryland Department of Health, and local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 625 transfers the duty of collecting annual contributions from animal research facilities for the Human-Relevant Research Fund from the Department of Health to the Department of Agriculture, resulting in increased personnel and operating expenditures for the department.
The bill repeals the statutory provisions requiring the Maryland Department of Health to collect research facility contributions and enforce compliance, relieving the agency of this responsibility.

TEDCO administers the Human-Relevant Research Fund, which receives the contributions collected under this legislation to fund grants and loans for non-animal research alternatives; revenues and grant funding may increase with improved collection enforcement.

Several public senior institutions of higher education within the University System of Maryland are research facilities subject to annual reporting and contribution requirements, and they are also eligible recipients for research grants and loans from the fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission to include specific curriculum requirements for entrance-level and in-service police training regarding individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities, dementia, and autism, including techniques for locating wandering individuals, water searches, sensory-aware approaches, and reunification.
