qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Law enforcement recruits and officers, police training academies, and individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities, dementia, or autism and their families.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not anticipated to be materially affected. Local government expenditures may experience a potential minimal increase to the extent that local police training schools do not already conduct the specific training mandated by the bill. Local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC) is administratively housed within DPSCS. The bill directly alters MPTSC's statutory powers and duties under Public Safety Article § 3-207 to require specific autism, dementia, and intellectual/developmental disability curricula in entrance-level and in-service police training.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police operates training academies and must update its entrance-level and in-service training programs to include the required modules on dementia, autism, wandering/elopement, and sensory-aware approaches.
DNR operates the Maryland Natural Resources Police, a statewide law enforcement body whose officers must complete MPTSC-mandated entrance-level and in-service training courses.
MDTA maintains its own sworn police force that is subject to MPTSC training standards and will need to incorporate the new curriculum topics into its officer training programs.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 635 requires applicants seeking positions with direct contact with children in specified child care facilities to submit to a criminal history records check and requires the Maryland State Department of Education to establish a centralized unit by June 30, 2027, to process and manage these checks. The bill also repeals the cap on the number of Deputy State Superintendents of Schools that may be appointed, lowers the age threshold from three to two years old for children served by child care centers where probationary employment qualifications apply for first-time child care teachers, and directs the Department to review and report on the background check process by October 1, 2028.
qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants, employees, and volunteers seeking positions involving direct contact with children at child care facilities; operators of registered family child care homes and licensed child care centers; and preschool- and school-age children in child care settings.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are not affected, and it is anticipated that the Maryland State Department of Education can establish the centralized unit and implement the bill's provisions with existing resources, resulting in minimal fiscal impact. While additional Deputy State Superintendents may be appointed, any associated operational costs would depend on future administrative decisions. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary agency tasked with implementing the bill. It must establish a centralized unit by June 30, 2027, to process and manage criminal history records checks for child care facility personnel, alter probationary employment qualification rules for certain child care teachers, remove the cap on appointed Deputy State Superintendents, and conduct a comprehensive review of the background check process to report to the General Assembly by October 1, 2028.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly references and interacts with the Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository (CJIS-CR), which is housed within DPSCS, for the collection, dissemination, and interagency coordination of criminal history record information for child care workers.

DHS oversees child abuse and neglect clearances for child care center personnel under related Family Law provisions and will be involved in the interagency coordination and review of child care background check processes mandated by the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Vax Act requires the Maryland Secretary of Health to issue, publish, and distribute evidence-based recommendations for immunizations, screenings, and preventive services for infants, children, and adults based on guidance from authoritative medical organizations. It authorizes pharmacists to administer vaccines recommended by the Secretary to individuals at least seven years of age, updates health insurance mandates to require coverage of these recommended services without cost-sharing, and repeals obsolete statutory provisions regarding the pertussis vaccine.
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland health insurance policyholders and enrollees, pharmacists, healthcare providers, health insurance carriers, infants, children, and adults receiving vaccinations and preventive screenings.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration will experience a minimal increase in FY 2027 only from the $125 rate and form filing fee. Form reviews by the Maryland Insurance Administration and additional administrative duties for the Maryland Department of Health can be handled using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill places direct statutory responsibility on the Secretary of Health to establish, publish, and distribute state recommendations for immunizations, screenings, and preventive services, and alters statutory vaccination administration frameworks under health occupations.

The bill explicitly mandates that the Secretary of Health obtain an analysis from the Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC) meeting the requirements of § 15-1501 of the Insurance Article before adopting recommendations for certain preventive services.

The Maryland Insurance Administration and the Insurance Commissioner are tasked with enforcing mandated coverage requirements without cost-sharing based on the Secretary's recommendations, receiving the distributed recommendations, and reviewing affected carrier rate and form filings.
The bill is an Administration initiative submitted on request of the Governor, reflecting the administration's public health policy agenda.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Secretary of Health to take into consideration the applicable guidance of the Maryland Statewide Advisory Commission on Immunizations when developing recommendations.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 640 revises, consolidates, and repeals various statutory reporting requirements, boards, and commissions across Maryland state government to improve efficiency and eliminate obsolete or duplicative mandates. Among other changes, it repeals several advisory boards—including the Renewable Fuels Incentive Board, Criminal Justice Information Advisory Board, Partnership for Workforce Quality Advisory Board, Two-Generation Family Economic Security Commission, and Commission on Trauma-Informed Care—modifies the composition and terms of other state bodies, updates report deadlines and structures, and authorizes compensation for members of the Interagency Council on Homelessness who have lived experience with homelessness.
qa_results.stakeholders: State and local agencies, members of affected boards and advisory councils, and members of the Interagency Council on Homelessness who have lived experience with homelessness.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no direct fiscal effect on state or local finances, as its provisions are largely procedural in nature, eliminating or modifying reporting mandates and streamlining board operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM requested this departmental legislation as part of the state's Government Modernization Initiative to streamline government operations, eliminate obsolete task forces and commissions, and relieve unnecessary reporting mandates on state agencies.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly repeals, alters the membership of, or modifies statutory reporting obligations for numerous executive branch boards, commissions, task forces, and advisory councils across state government.

The bill repeals the Renewable Fuels Incentive Board and directly transfers the board's duties and renewable fuels credit certification processes to the Department of Agriculture. It also removes the Secretary of Agriculture from the Cannabis Public Health Advisory Council.

The bill repeals the Partnership for Workforce Quality Advisory Board under Commerce, alters terms and staggering for the Maryland Life Sciences Advisory Board, modifies the membership and reporting cycle for the Maryland Aerospace and Technology Commission, and removes Commerce representation from the Customer Council and Green Purchasing Committee.

The bill replaces specialized intervention services reporting with a mandate for MSDE to compile county-level grade 3 literacy proficiency data and report to state leadership, repeals suicide prevention program reporting, eliminates the obsolete 3-year GCEI update and reporting requirements, and removes MSDE from the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Committee.

The bill repeals several MDH reporting mandates (including hepatitis C and cancer registry reports), consolidates youth camp epinephrine reporting, partners MDH with DHS to compile and submit prekindergarten enrollment reports, alters the reporting deadline for health practitioner preceptor tax credits, and modifies health-related advisory council memberships.

The bill repeals the Two-Generation Family Economic Security Commission and the Commission on Trauma-Informed Care, repeals the multidisciplinary alternative response advisory council, alters the Maryland Commission on Caregiving membership, and directs local DSS offices to report prekindergarten notifications to DHS for joint reporting with MDH.

The bill designates the Secretary of Housing and Community Development (or designee) as the permanent chair of the Interagency Council on Homelessness, removes chair term limits, shifts annual reporting deadlines, and requires DHCD to administer a compensation policy for council members with lived experience of homelessness.

The bill repeals DNR's requirement to publish a website list of state park maintenance projects exceeding $25,000, repeals annual reporting on the nutria eradication plan, and alters membership seats on the Hart-Miller-Pleasure Island Citizens Oversight Committee.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals the Criminal Justice Information Advisory Board (allowing the Secretary to operate the Central Repository without its advice) and alters the composition of the Customer Council.

The bill repeals an annual reporting requirement regarding the Oil Contaminated Site Environmental Cleanup Fund and updates membership appointments for the Hart-Miller-Pleasure Island Citizens Oversight Committee.

GOPI houses and leads the Government Modernization Initiative (GMI), which coordinated across state departments to identify obsolete reporting requirements, boards, and commissions repealed or altered by this legislation.

The bill alters various gubernatorial appointment structures (such as staggered terms on the Life Sciences Advisory Board and membership on oversight bodies) and updates statutory report delivery requirements to the Governor.
The bill repeals the annual reporting requirement obligating the Maryland Department of Labor to report on voter registration activities and efficiency at one-stop career centers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill modifies the membership of the Justice Reinvestment Oversight Board housed within GOCPP by removing the Secretary of Health.
The bill adjusts the statutory membership composition of the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Committee housed within the Transportation Article.
The bill updates statutory references and clarifies MHCC's collaborative reporting duties regarding the Health Care Disparities Policy Report Card.
The bill adjusts the annual deadline by which MDH must submit tax credit certificate reports for health care preceptors to the Comptroller from January 31 to March 1.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the educational and experiential qualifications required to obtain a certified public accountant (CPA) license in Maryland. It establishes alternative pathways to licensure by allowing applicants with a bachelor's degree in accounting to qualify through two years (4,000 hours) of practical work experience, alongside options for master's degree holders or bachelor's degree holders with an additional 30 credit hours to qualify with one year (2,000 hours) of experience. It also extends the maximum period during which practical experience can be accrued from three to six years.
qa_results.stakeholders: Prospective certified public accountant (CPA) candidates, licensed CPAs, accounting firms, and employers of accountants in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Public Accountancy can implement the bill using existing resources. Special fund revenues may increase minimally to the extent that alternative pathways encourage additional individuals to seek licensure. There is no local government fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Public Accountancy is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing. The department is directly responsible for administering the revised CPA examination and licensure requirements established by the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Lowers the qualifying age from 65 to 60 for eligible energy customers to participate in the Office of Home Energy Programs' simplified annual uniform redetermination process for energy assistance program enrollment.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Human Services (Office of Home Energy Programs)
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income energy utility customers aged 60 to 64 who qualify for energy assistance programs (such as MEAP and EUSP), and local administering agencies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local administering agencies can handle administrative changes with existing budgeted resources. The bill does not add new funding; instead, expanding redetermination eligibility alters how existing funds are utilized. If additional households enroll, benefit amounts may be adjusted downward to accommodate more participants within available funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 648 is a departmental bill requested by the Department of Human Services (DHS). The Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP) is housed within DHS and is the primary entity responsible for implementing and managing the uniform redetermination process for energy assistance programs.

The bill expands streamlined energy assistance redetermination to individuals aged 60 and older, directly aligning with the Department of Aging's focus population and network of local services that support older adults.

MEA manages the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), which provides funding allocations for the Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP) administered under these provisions, and was consulted for the bill's fiscal analysis.
The PSC regulates the electric and gas utilities and oversees ratepayer surcharges that fund the Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP), and was consulted as an information source for the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill increases the maximum amount of Program Open Space funds that can be transferred to the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority Financing Fund from up to $6.0 million to up to $12.0 million annually. It also adjusts the limit on funds used for operating expenses to up to 7% or $600,000 (whichever is greater), removes statutory limits capping grant awards at 50% of project costs, and authorizes the Authority to set matching fund requirements and terms for grants and loans.
qa_results.stakeholders: Local governments, entities managing certified heritage areas, communities and tourists in heritage areas, and businesses involved in heritage preservation or State land acquisition.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no net effect on overall State finances, but it redirects up to $6.0 million annually beginning in FY 2027 from Program Open Space State land acquisition to the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority Financing Fund. Transferred funds will support two new staff positions costing $202,318 in FY 2027, rising to $207,002 by FY 2031. Local government revenues and expenditures may increase beginning in FY 2027 as local entities receive grants or loans with more flexible matching requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Heritage Areas Authority (MHAA) and the Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) are housed within the Department of Planning. The bill expands MHAA's grant and loan authority, modifies operating expense caps, and results in two additional personnel within the department to administer the expanded funding program.

The bill alters distributions from Program Open Space (POS), which is administered by DNR, by increasing the maximum transfer from the State's share of POS funds to the MHAA Financing Fund from $3.0 million to $9.0 million, redirecting up to $6.0 million away from State land acquisition.

The bill authorizes transfers of funds from Program Open Space to the MHAA Financing Fund through appropriations in the State budget or by budget amendment, impacting State fiscal planning and personnel allocations.
The State Treasurer is statutorily designated to invest and reinvest the Maryland Heritage Areas Authority Financing Fund and credit investment earnings to the fund.

The Commission receives recreation and open space funding jointly with DNR from the State share of Program Open Space under Section 5-903(a)(2)(i)1A, from which up to $6.0 million in additional funds may be transferred under the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill increases the per capita State formula aid and minimum funding allocation for the State Library Resource Center (the Central Library of the Enoch Pratt Free Library System) incrementally from $2.07 to $2.64 per State resident between fiscal years 2028 and 2032.
qa_results.stakeholders: State Library Resource Center, Enoch Pratt Free Library System, local public library systems, and Maryland library patrons
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $628,900 in FY 2028, $1,328,500 in FY 2029, $2,036,600 in FY 2030, and $2,817,200 in FY 2031 due to the mandated per capita funding increase. State revenues are unaffected. Local finances are not materially affected, although local libraries benefit from resource center services.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Library Agency is responsible for funding and coordinating the State Library Network. The bill alters the statutory per capita funding formula for the State Library Resource Center, which is a key component of the state library network administered and funded through the agency.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for developing the state budget and managing mandated appropriations. The bill establishes phased-in mandated increases in general fund expenditures for the State Library Resource Center starting in fiscal year 2028.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Governor to annually proclaim January as Muslim American Heritage Month and May as Jewish American Heritage Month to recognize the contributions of Muslim and Jewish Americans to the State, while urging educational and cultural organizations to observe these months with appropriate programs, ceremonies, and activities.
qa_results.stakeholders: Muslim Americans, Jewish Americans, and educational and cultural organizations in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is no State or local fiscal impact; commemorating Muslim American Heritage Month and Jewish American Heritage Month does not affect government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the Governor to annually issue proclamations declaring January as Muslim American Heritage Month and May as Jewish American Heritage Month, urging educational and cultural organizations to observe them.

GOCI houses and coordinates ethnic, cultural, and faith-based commissions and community outreach initiatives that align with and support the observance of heritage and cultural months across the state.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of the Environment to submit reports to the General Assembly every six months on legally valid changes in federal environmental policy, including changes affecting greenhouse gas emissions standards, stationary sources, motor vehicles, federally delegated authority, and nuclear power, as well as the State's response to those changes.
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Department of the Environment, Maryland General Assembly, regulated environmental and energy industries, and the public.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of the Environment can fulfill the reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources. The bill has no effect on State revenues, local governments, or small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 663 specifically mandates that the Maryland Department of the Environment track legally valid changes in federal environmental policy—including greenhouse gas standards, stationary source rules, federally delegated authority, and nuclear power—and submit biannual reports to the General Assembly outlining those changes and the State's response.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the quota on alcoholic beverages licenses issued by the Board of License Commissioners for Cecil County so that it applies specifically to Class A licenses. Under the bill, the board may not issue more than one Class A license for every 2,000 registered voters (or major fraction) in the county, may not issue fewer than two Class A licenses per election district, and excludes all other license classes from the aggregate quota calculation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Cecil County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Class A alcoholic beverages license holders and applicants, local alcohol retailers, and residents of Cecil County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect Cecil County finances or operations. Small business effect: Minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates aspects of the alcohol industry in the state. While this bill specifically alters local Class A license quotas administered by the Cecil County Board of License Commissioners and has no direct state fiscal impact, it relates to the state's overall statutory framework governing alcoholic beverages.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits an individual in St. Mary's County from standing in a roadway, shoulder, median divider, or intersection designated as inherently dangerous by the county or a municipality in consultation with the State Highway Administration. Law enforcement officers may only issue citations if compliant warning signs are properly posted.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Highway Administration (Maryland Department of Transportation)
qa_results.stakeholders: Pedestrians, motorists, local law enforcement, and residents of St. Mary's County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances, as the State Highway Administration can handle consultation and approval requirements with existing resources. St. Mary's County operations and finances are also not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires St. Mary's County and municipal corporations to consult with the State Highway Administration (SHA) to determine if a State roadway is inherently dangerous, requires signage to comply with SHA standards, and mandates SHA approval prior to installing signs on State highways.

As the parent department of the State Highway Administration, MDOT oversees the state transportation network, manages traffic control device standards, and provided input on the bill's operational and fiscal impact.

MSP troopers enforce Maryland traffic and pedestrian laws on state roadways in St. Mary's County and are directly restricted from issuing citations under this statute unless the required warning signage is properly installed.
The Administrative Office of the Courts oversees the court operations that handle traffic citations and adjudicate misdemeanor or infraction violations under the Transportation Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires the Governor to include a mandatory appropriation of at least $2.0 million annually in the State budget for the Office of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman in the Maryland Department of Aging, funded from remittances paid by Medicaid managed care organizations (MCOs) that fail to meet medical loss ratio standards, supplemented by general funds if remittances fall short. The funding is intended to supplement, not supplant, existing appropriations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging (Office of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman) and the Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents of long-term care facilities (such as nursing homes and assisted living facilities), local Area Agencies on Aging, long-term care ombudsmen, and Medicaid managed care organizations (MCOs)
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $2.0 million annually beginning in FY 2028, either to meet the mandated appropriation if remittance funds fall short or to backfill Medicaid funds redirected to the ombudsman program. Total special fund expenditures have a net $0 impact, as up to $2.0 million is transferred from the Maryland Department of Health to the Maryland Department of Aging. State revenues are unaffected. Locally, revenues and expenditures for Area Agencies on Aging (AAAs) may increase as additional ombudsman funding is distributed.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly benefits the Department of Aging by establishing a statutory mandated appropriation of at least $2.0 million annually for the operations of its Office of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman, funded through MCO remittances or general funds.

The mandated appropriation is sourced from medical loss ratio (MLR) remittances paid by Medicaid managed care organizations to MDH, diverting up to $2.0 million in special funds that would otherwise support Medicaid expenditures and necessitating general fund backfill.

The bill places a direct statutory requirement on the Governor to include a mandated appropriation of at least $2.0 million for the Office of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman in the annual State budget bill.

As the agency responsible for preparing the Governor's annual budget and managing State expenditures, DBM must implement and account for this newly established mandated appropriation and any necessary general fund backfills.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the eligibility criteria for pediatric cancer research grants awarded from the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund, limiting eligible recipients to nonprofit hospitals, educational institutions, and other nonprofit organizations, thereby excluding individual physicians, laboratories, and persons.
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonprofit hospitals, educational institutions, nonprofit research organizations, pediatric cancer patients, and previously eligible individual physicians and commercial laboratories.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local effect: None. The bill's alterations to grant recipient eligibility are technical in nature and do not directly affect state or local government revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health and the Secretary of Health administer the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund, adopt regulations for the grant program, and distribute the research grants impacted by the bill's eligibility changes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Pediatric Cancer Research Commission is charged under Title 20 with establishing criteria, guidelines, and oversight for the award of research grants funded by the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Provides civil immunity to registered reduction operators, licensed funeral establishments, and crematory permit holders who transfer, as well as veterans service organizations that receive, unclaimed hydrolyzed or soil remains of a veteran or an eligible dependent for final disposition, provided they act in good faith.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor (Office of Cemetery Oversight) and Maryland Department of Health (State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors)
qa_results.stakeholders: Veterans and their eligible dependents, registered reduction operators, licensed funeral establishments, crematory permit holders, and veterans service organizations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected, and there is no local government fiscal impact. The impact on small businesses is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill concerns the transfer and disposition of unclaimed remains of veterans and eligible dependents to veterans service organizations, which directly interacts with the department's oversight of veterans' cemeteries and the statutory process where unclaimed remains are transferred to DVMF for final disposition.

The Maryland Department of Health houses the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors, which licenses funeral establishments and regulates reduction facilities and the disposition of human remains governed by the cross-referenced statutes.

The Department of Labor regulates crematory permit holders and registered reduction operators through the Office of Cemetery Oversight, whose licensees and registrants are granted civil immunity protections under the bill.

The bill amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article to provide statutory civil immunity to registered reduction operators and veterans service organizations, which impacts civil tort claims adjudicated in the Maryland court system.

qa_results.bill_summary: Clarifies and expands membership in the Correctional Officers' Retirement System (CORS) to include Maryland Department of Health employees serving as CAMH Specialist I - CI and CAMH Specialist II - CI at seven specified state facilities, establishing CORS membership as a condition of employment and providing mechanisms for transferring previous service credit.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System and Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Department of Health employees serving in CAMH Specialist I - CI and CAMH Specialist II - CI positions at specified facilities (approximately 12 positions).
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to have no discernible or material effect on State pension liabilities or contribution rates due to the small number of positions affected (approximately 12). There is no effect on State revenues and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System, including the Correctional Officers' Retirement System (CORS) and Employees' Pension System (EPS). The agency is directly responsible for implementing the membership changes, administering service credit transfers, processing member elections, and calculating benefit adjustments mandated by the bill.

The bill directly affects Maryland Department of Health personnel by moving qualifying employees (CAMH Specialist I - CI and CAMH Specialist II - CI) across seven MDH facilities into the Correctional Officers' Retirement System as a condition of employment.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames the Children's Cabinet Fund to the Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund and establishes mandated appropriations for grants to eligible Local Management Boards from fiscal year 2028 through 2031.
qa_results.stakeholders: Local management boards (LMBs), local governments, and Maryland children, youth, and families receiving interagency community services and prevention programs.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $500,000 in FY 2031 to satisfy a mandated appropriation to the Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund, following required appropriations from FY 2028 to FY 2030 that must at least equal the FY 2027 funding level ($22.3 million). Local revenues and expenditures increase by $500,000 in FY 2031 from additional grant funding awarded to local management boards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office for Children acts as the fiscal agent for the Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund (CCIF), staffs the Children's Cabinet, and administers the grant funds provided to local management boards.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for preparing and executing the annual state budget, which will need to incorporate the bill's mandated funding levels and $500,000 increase for the fund in fiscal year 2031.
The bill places a statutory mandate on the Governor to include specific funding levels for the Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2028 through 2031.

The bill updates statutory provisions in the Education Article that require the Maryland State Department of Education to collaborate with the fiscal agent of the newly renamed Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund on rate-setting processes.
The bill makes conforming name changes in the Health - General Article regarding the Children's Cabinet Interagency Fund and funding pools for services to children with disabilities.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill increases the maximum fine or penalty Baltimore City is authorized to establish for violations of its ordinances, rules, or regulations from $1,000 to $5,000.
qa_results.responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals, businesses, and property owners in Baltimore City who are subject to city ordinances, rules, or regulations and associated enforcement citations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected. Baltimore City revenues may increase beginning in fiscal year 2027 to the extent that higher fines or penalties are imposed and collected for civil or criminal violations. Baltimore City expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the maximum fines Baltimore City can establish for criminal and civil ordinance violations, which may be adjudicated in state courts (such as the District Court of Maryland in Baltimore City). The Administrative Office of the Courts was consulted for fiscal impact analysis, though the overall operational and fiscal effect on the court system is minimal.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes in Anne Arundel County a Class GC (golf course) alcoholic beverages license for courses with at least nine holes, as well as sports activity venue licenses (beer and wine, or beer, wine, and liquor) for commercial recreational facilities offering activities such as bowling, simulators, pickleball, or indoor training centers, authorizing on-premises sales and consumption without requiring a separate Sunday permit.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Anne Arundel County golf course operators, commercial sports and recreational facility owners (such as bowling alleys, pickleball facilities, and simulator venues), facility patrons aged 21 and older, and the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Anne Arundel County local revenues will increase beginning in FY 2027 depending on the number of licenses issued, based on annual fees of $1,200 for a Class GC license, $1,200 for a sports activity venue beer, wine, and liquor license, and $740 for a sports activity venue beer and wine license. County expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new retail alcoholic beverages licenses in Anne Arundel County. While the licenses are administered and issued locally by the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, the Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcoholic beverages industry and collects state sales taxes.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill modifies requirements concerning health insurance provider panels and contracts between insurance carriers and health systems. It expands notice and continuity-of-care requirements to include behavioral health providers, alters how carriers report impending material network changes to the Insurance Commissioner, mandates advance notice and a 90-day contract adherence period when carriers and health systems terminate or fail to renew contracts, and creates a 90-day special enrollment period in the individual market for patients whose regular providers are terminated from a network.
qa_results.stakeholders: Health insurance enrollees and patients, health insurance carriers, health systems and hospitals, and health care practitioners (including primary care and behavioral health providers).
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operational impacts on the Maryland Insurance Administration and the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange are minimal and can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. While the Insurance Commissioner is authorized to assess fines of $5,000 per day for failing to timely file access plan updates, the penalty provision is not expected to materially impact State revenues. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was requested as a departmental bill by the Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA). It requires carriers to notify the Insurance Commissioner of impending provider terminations and access plan updates, authorizes the Commissioner to assess daily fines for late filings, requires MIA to receive consumer complaints, and directs the Commissioner to develop a uniform form for transitional care requests.

The bill establishes a new 90-day special enrollment period in the Individual Exchange (Maryland Health Connection) for individuals whose treating provider is terminated from their health plan's provider panel.

The bill amends the Health - General Article (§ 19–310.7) to mandate that health systems comply with contract termination notification and continuation requirements, impacting licensed health facilities and systems under MDH's purview.

DBM was consulted as an information source for the bill due to its responsibility for managing state employee health benefits and policies, which interact with health carrier network rules and requirements.

qa_results.bill_summary: Transfers the regulatory authority over crematories and reduction facilities from the Office of Cemetery Oversight to the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors. It also alters board governance provisions concerning member removal and quorum, increases civil penalty limits for violations, mandates the employment of at least two inspectors by the board, and establishes a stakeholder workgroup to review laws and regulations.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors
qa_results.stakeholders: Crematory operators, reduction facility operators, morticians, funeral directors, cemetery operators, and consumers using crematory and reduction services in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2027, State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors special fund expenditures increase by at least $101,200 (and between $90,600 and $103,500 annually through FY 2031) to fund an additional full-time inspector position. Board special fund revenues increase by an indeterminate amount from transferred registration and permit fees. Office of Cemetery Oversight special fund revenues decrease by approximately $6,000 biannually. General fund revenues may minimally increase from higher civil penalty maximums. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors is housed within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill directly impacts the department by transferring full regulatory oversight of crematories and reduction facilities to the Board, altering Board quorum and member removal rules, increasing penalties, and requiring the Board to employ an additional inspector.

The Office of Cemetery Oversight is an agency within the Maryland Department of Labor. The bill strips OCO of regulatory authority over crematories and reduction facilities, alters the composition of its Advisory Council on Cemetery Operations, and decreases OCO special fund revenues.
The bill amends the statutory criteria under which the Governor may remove appointed members of the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors.

The bill repeals Section 5-803 of the Business Regulation Article concerning reporting and transferring unclaimed cremated remains and soil remains of veterans to the Department of Veterans and Military Families, consolidating those procedures under Health Occupations law.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 711 enhances data privacy protections for Maryland residents by prohibiting data controllers from knowingly selling consumer personal data to government entities that have engaged in or supported civil immigration enforcement within the prior six months without a valid court warrant. The bill also broadens Public Information Act restrictions by requiring record custodians to take reasonable steps to prevent the disclosure of personal information and photographs for immigration enforcement, expands similar restrictions and warrant requirements to law enforcement message switching systems, and broadens governmental protection policies to encompass all sensitive data rather than just geolocation data.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, Department of State Police, Motor Vehicle Administration, and the Office of the Attorney General (Division of Consumer Protection)
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland consumers and residents (particularly immigrant populations), data controllers and processors, public record custodians, the state Judiciary, and law enforcement agencies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are not directly affected. State general fund expenditures may increase significantly for the Judiciary to implement staffing and programming changes necessary to screen public record requests and determine search intent at courthouse kiosks; most other State agencies can handle the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. Local government expenditures may also increase significantly for certain local custodians due to heightened scrutiny of Public Information Act requests, though specific dollar estimates are unavailable. Local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends provisions governing the disclosure of MVA public records (§ 4-320 and § 4-320.1), requiring MVA to restrict access to personal information and photographs for immigration enforcement without a warrant, submit detailed annual reports to the General Assembly, and promulgate implementing regulations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is specifically mandated under § 3-529 to adopt regulations governing access to message switching systems and law enforcement databases, and under § 4-320.1 to adopt regulations and submit annual reports to the General Assembly regarding immigration-related record requests.

The Department of State Police is explicitly required by § 4-320.1 to adopt regulations and procedures restricting record and facial recognition access for immigration enforcement, submit annual reports to the General Assembly, and comply with restrictions on law enforcement databases and message switching systems.

The fiscal note specifically highlights that the Judiciary / Administrative Office of the Courts may face a significant operational and fiscal impact to adjust procedures, courthouse kiosk access, and screening processes to determine whether individuals seeking public records are doing so for immigration enforcement.

Under § 10-1702 of the State Government Article, all Maryland governmental entities must develop and publish procedures preventing the sale and redisclosure of personal records and sensitive data in direct consultation with DoIT.

The bill amends the Maryland Online Data Privacy Act, which is enforced by the Consumer Protection Division of the OAG. The bill explicitly authorizes the Division to publish educational materials on civil immigration enforcement and impacts public record access guidance administered by OAG.
MDOT is the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration, which is directly tasked with major regulatory, operational, and reporting mandates under the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes qualifying charitable or civic organizations affiliated with a professional National Football League (NFL) team playing in Baltimore City to conduct raffles during home games, subject to geofencing, age-verification, and timing restrictions, and extends the statutory authorization for raffles conducted by organizations affiliated with a Major League Baseball (MLB) team.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City government / Baltimore City Police Department
qa_results.stakeholders: Charitable organizations affiliated with professional NFL and MLB teams in Baltimore City (such as the Ravens and Orioles), game attendees purchasing raffle tickets, and local civic or charitable programs receiving proceeds.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected; potential minor substitution effects on State lottery revenues are negligible. Local finances for Baltimore City are not materially affected, as the Baltimore City Police Department can issue permits using existing resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency regulates commercial gaming and state lottery operations in Maryland. While the bill specifically authorizes charitable raffles administered at the local level in Baltimore City, the fiscal analysis assesses potential substitution effects on state lottery revenues and consulted the agency during review.

The bill authorizes in-person and electronic raffles at professional baseball and football games and defines specific geofenced geographic boundaries around Oriole Park at Camden Yards and M&T Bank Stadium, facilities owned, operated, and maintained by the Maryland Stadium Authority.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 718 establishes a State policy that email systems and resources for State and public higher education employees are intended to support State business and cannot serve as a public forum. It requires State agencies and public higher education institutions to incorporate provisions into their information technology policies and plans that protect email services from spam and non-business use, including automatic spam filtering, while permitting incidental personal use that has a de minimis impact.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Information Technology and governing boards of public institutions of higher education
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland State employees, public higher education employees, State agencies, and public institutions of higher education
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not anticipated to be materially affected because the bill generally codifies existing practice. Local government operations and finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DoIT is the primary implementing agency responsible for setting state IT policies, reviewing and approving IT standards and plans submitted by state agencies and public institutions of higher education, and incorporating them into the statewide IT master plan.

As a public higher education system specifically brought under the IT plan requirements of § 3.5-305, USM's governing board is required to develop and submit IT policies, standards, and plans regarding employee email systems and anti-spam filtering to the Secretary of DoIT.

As an independent public institution of higher education subject to § 3.5-305 under the bill, Morgan State University's governing board must develop and submit IT policies, standards, and plans regarding email systems and spam filtering to the Secretary of DoIT.

As an independent public institution of higher education subject to § 3.5-305 under the bill, the college's governing board must develop and submit IT policies, standards, and plans regarding email systems and spam filtering to the Secretary of DoIT.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill repeals the June 30, 2030 termination date for awarding initial scholarships under the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship program, allowing eligible veterans, active service members, and their dependents to continue receiving new and renewed scholarship awards indefinitely.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission (Office of Student Financial Assistance)
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland resident veterans, active-duty service members, activated reservists who served in the Afghanistan or Iraq conflicts, and their eligible spouses and children pursuing undergraduate higher education.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $750,000 annually beginning in FY 2031 to maintain the scholarship program beyond its original sunset date. There is no effect on state revenues and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC directly administers the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship and its dedicated special fund. The bill repeals the June 30, 2030 termination date, allowing the commission to continue awarding initial scholarships indefinitely.

As the primary state entity overseeing postsecondary financial aid and administering the Douglas J. J. Peters scholarship program and fund, the commission is directly responsible for implementing the permanent continuation of awards under this bill.

The department is tasked with advocating for Maryland veterans, active-duty service members, and their families to secure state education benefits. The permanent continuation of this scholarship directly affects the veteran population and families the agency supports.

The maximum annual scholarship award is statutorily calculated based on the highest resident undergraduate tuition, fees, and room and board across USM institutions, and many scholarship recipients enroll at USM campuses.

By statute, the State Treasurer holds the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship Fund separately, and the bill ensures the fund continues operating beyond FY 2030.

The Comptroller is statutorily required to account for the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship Fund, which will remain active beyond 2030 under this legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Uniformed Services Spouses Act extends various educational, scholarship, and employment benefits to spouses of active-duty service members and veterans, and broadens the definition of eligible veterans from those with an honorable discharge to those with an other than dishonorable discharge, including members of the Commissioned Corps of the Public Health Service and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. Key provisions include granting course priority registration at public higher education institutions, expanding community college veteran resource center support to spouses, allowing spouses to use senatorial and Delegate scholarships out of state, and expanding hiring preferences and state personnel selection test credits.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission, public institutions of higher education, and the Department of Budget and Management
qa_results.stakeholders: Active-duty service members, veterans (including those with other than dishonorable discharges and members of the PHS and NOAA Commissioned Corps), and military/veteran spouses.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not materially affected, and revenues remain unchanged. Requirements can be absorbed using existing budgeted resources. Minor administrative updates to the Department of Budget and Management's JobAps system, training guides, and community college/university policies are expected to be minimal. The bill does not change the total authorized scholarship funding amounts awarded by legislators.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM serves as the state's central personnel agency. The bill expands the definition of eligible veterans who receive selection test credits within the State Personnel Management System, requiring DBM to update its JobAps application system, policy guides, and personnel training materials.

MHEC oversees statewide higher education policies and coordinates state financial aid. The bill amends eligibility criteria for Senatorial and Delegate scholarships to allow active service members' spouses to use awards at out-of-state institutions and maintain domicile eligibility.

USM comprises public institutions of higher education that are directly mandated by the bill to grant priority course registration to eligible service members' spouses and adopt policies to implement the requirement.

As an independent public institution of higher education, Morgan State University must implement priority course registration for eligible service members and their spouses and establish complying institutional policies.
As an independent public higher education institution, St. Mary's College must adopt policies and grant priority course registration to eligible service members and eligible spouses.

The bill amends the Labor and Employment Article (§ 3-714) regarding permissible hiring and promotion preferences granted by private employers, counties, and municipalities to veterans and military spouses.

The department is the principal state agency advocating for and assisting veterans, active-duty service members, and their families. The bill directly expands state benefits, higher education access, campus resources, and employment preferences for service members and their spouses.

The bill's purpose paragraph references hiring preferences under the Public Service Commission (and the Commission is listed as an information source in the fiscal note), although the operative statutory section amended in the Public Utilities Article applies to WSSC.

MDOT operates its own human resources and personnel management structure and was consulted as an information source regarding the application of veteran and spousal hiring preferences and selection test credits.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the membership eligibility criteria for a Class C (veterans' organization) alcoholic beverages license in Anne Arundel County by allowing organizations composed of members who served in any branch of the uniformed services (including the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the Public Health Service) to qualify, and repealing the requirement that members must have served during wartime.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Veterans' organizations and clubs in Anne Arundel County, as well as veterans and service members of the uniformed services, including the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the Public Health Service.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal effect. It does not materially affect Anne Arundel County finances or operations, with only a minimal potential effect on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill broadens the membership eligibility criteria for veterans' organizations qualifying for a Class C alcoholic beverages license by expanding eligibility from wartime armed forces members to members of all uniformed services (including NOAA and the Public Health Service), which aligns with the agency's mission to advocate for and support veterans and service members.

The Comptroller has broad authority over the regulation and taxation of the alcoholic beverages industry in Maryland, though local retail Class C licenses are directly administered and issued by the local Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Franchise Reform Act modifies the Maryland Franchise Registration and Disclosure Law by extending the period within which the Securities Commissioner may take enforcement actions from three to five years, altering the statute of limitations for civil liability claims, and guaranteeing franchisees the right to freely associate and join franchisee trade associations without franchisor interference. It also establishes the Maryland Franchise Disclosure Document Renewal Fast-Track Review Pilot Program to expedite registration renewal reviews and mandates an evaluation report to legislative committees by September 30, 2031.
qa_results.responsible_party: Securities Commissioner in the Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Franchisees, franchisors, subfranchisors, prospective franchise buyers, and the Office of the Attorney General.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $305,518 in FY 2027 (reflecting three new positions: one assistant Attorney General, one administrator, and one examiner, along with start-up and operating costs), growing to $413,400 by FY 2031. Additional costs may be incurred for tracking technology. The Securities Act Registration Fund may potentially mitigate general fund impacts. Revenues are not materially affected, and local finances and operations experience no material impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Franchise Registration and Disclosure Law is administered and enforced by the Securities Commissioner within the Office of the Attorney General (OAG). The bill extends the Commissioner's enforcement timeline, establishes the Franchise Disclosure Document Renewal Fast-Track Review Pilot Program under OAG, requires OAG to adopt regulations and submit a study by 2031, and results in a direct fiscal impact of over $300,000 annually for additional OAG personnel.

The bill creates a private right of action for franchisees to seek injunctive relief, damages, and attorney's fees in circuit court for violations of franchisee association rights, alters civil liability filing deadlines, and authorizes enforcement actions brought by the Securities Commissioner in circuit court.

qa_results.bill_summary: Legalizes the 2025 Edition of the Baltimore County Code of Public Local Laws and its supplements containing General Assembly enactments, establishing the code as evidence of the law in Maryland courts and for public officials.
qa_results.stakeholders: Baltimore County residents, local government officials, courts, and legal professionals relying on the Baltimore County Code of Public Local Laws
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal effect. Baltimore County can likely handle publication costs with existing budgeted resources, and county revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill provides that the 2025 Edition of the Baltimore County Code of Public Local Laws and any supplement shall be recognized in all Maryland state courts as evidence of the public local laws enacted by the General Assembly.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the deadline from December 31, 2025, to December 31, 2030, for community solar energy generating systems to receive Public Service Commission approval to qualify agrivoltaics land for an agricultural use property tax assessment. It also creates a preconstruction determination process administered by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation and authorizes an application fee to offset administrative costs.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Community solar project operators and developers, agricultural landowners, and local taxing jurisdictions.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Annuity Bond Fund revenues and local property tax revenues may experience a potential decrease beginning in FY 2027, depending on the number of new community solar facilities placed in service. Specific revenue estimates are indeterminate. Administrative expenditures for the State Department of Assessments and Taxation are expected to be fully offset by application fee revenues authorized by the bill.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly alters the statutory deadline by which community solar energy generating systems must be approved by the Public Service Commission (extending it from December 31, 2025, to December 31, 2030) for the underlying land to be eligible for agricultural use tax assessments.

The bill establishes preconstruction qualification determinations, rescission rules, and agricultural use assessment standards for community solar agrivoltaic sites; adverse determinations or valuation disputes issued by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation may be appealed to the local Property Tax Assessment Appeals Boards.

As the highest administrative review body for real property tax classification and assessment disputes, the Maryland Tax Court has jurisdiction to hear appeals resulting from determinations and valuations of land under the agrivoltaics agricultural use assessment.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 735 delays the implementation of the Maryland Earned Income Tax Credit Assistance Program for Low-Income Families by five years, shifting its start to tax year 2030 and extending its termination date to December 31, 2035. It also directs the Comptroller's Office to study outreach methods to increase claims of the State earned income tax credit and requires the Department of Service and Civic Innovation to study how Maryland Corps participants can assist low-income residents in accessing tax credits and public assistance, with both reports due by December 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller's Office and the Department of Service and Civic Innovation
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income Maryland residents eligible for the Earned Income Tax Credit, Maryland Corps participants, and state and local tax authorities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund and local income tax revenue reductions associated with increased claims under the Earned Income Tax Credit Assistance Program are delayed until tax year 2030. The Comptroller's Office and the Department of Service and Civic Innovation can conduct the required studies and submit reports using existing budgeted resources. No specific dollar estimates are provided.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller's Office is the primary administering agency of the Maryland Earned Income Tax Credit Assistance Program, whose full implementation and annual reporting requirements are delayed by five years under the bill. In addition, the Comptroller is mandated to conduct an extensive study on taxpayer outreach strategies and submit a report by December 1, 2026.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Department of Service and Civic Innovation to conduct a study and submit a report by December 1, 2026, examining how Maryland Corps participants could assist low-income Marylanders in claiming the EITC and accessing other public benefits.

The Governor's Office receives required reporting on the effectiveness and operational statistics of the Earned Income Tax Credit Assistance Program, the schedule for which is adjusted and extended under the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Transfer-on-Death Deed Act, allowing real property owners to transfer property to one or more designated beneficiaries upon their death without going through probate, while providing procedures for the creation, recordation, and revocation of transfer-on-death deeds and exempting qualifying deeds from recordation and transfer taxes.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (Clerks of the Circuit Court) and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland real property owners, designated beneficiaries, estate planners, and heirs.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $15,700 (or $15,696) in FY 2027 only for one-time Judiciary computer programming costs. General fund revenues may decrease minimally starting in FY 2027 due to reduced probate fees and inheritance taxes collected by registers of wills, while special fund revenues for the Circuit Court Real Property Records Improvement Fund may increase from land record surcharges. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends recording procedures administered by the clerks of the circuit courts for transfer-on-death deeds, instruments of revocation, and notices of death. It specifically references the intake sheet forms provided and managed by the Administrative Office of the Courts (AOC), and the fiscal note identifies one-time expenditures for Judiciary IT programming changes.

The bill allows real property to pass outside of probate via transfer-on-death deeds, which directly impacts the administration of decedents' estates overseen by the Registers of Wills and may reduce probate fees and inheritance tax collections.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $450,000 in the State budget for the Growing Family Child Care Opportunities Program for fiscal years 2028 through 2030.
qa_results.stakeholders: Family child care providers, local county governments, child care resource centers, and children and families needing child care services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Establishes a mandated appropriation of $450,000 annually for fiscal years 2028 through 2030 for the Growing Family Child Care Opportunities Program, to be funded with federal funds if authorized or general funds. The Department of Legislative Services projects no net change in State expenditures under the assumption that level funding would have occurred even without the mandate based on historical funding patterns. Local governments and partnering child care resource centers are guaranteed access to grant funding in fiscal 2028 through 2030.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Growing Family Child Care Opportunities Program is established within and administered by the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), which awards grants and oversees program reporting.
The bill explicitly mandates that the Governor include a $450,000 appropriation for the program in the annual state budget bill for fiscal years 2028 through 2030.

As the principal agency responsible for developing the state budget and managing fiscal planning, DBM must incorporate the bill's mandated annual appropriation of $450,000 into the budget for fiscal years 2028 through 2030.

qa_results.bill_summary: Mandates membership in the Correctional Officers' Retirement System (CORS) for local detention center officers in Dorchester County if the county elects to participate in CORS, transferring past eligibility and creditable service from the Employees' Pension System and exempting the officers from certain member contribution catch-up requirements.
qa_results.stakeholders: Dorchester County detention center officers (approximately 37 individuals) and the Dorchester County government.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Effect: None. Local Effect: If Dorchester County chooses to participate in CORS, its pension liabilities increase by an estimated $842,322 (based on a June 30, 2025 actuarial analysis). Starting as early as FY 2028, Dorchester County's net annual employer contributions are estimated to increase by $36,748 (an initial increase of $147,756 minus a $111,008 annual new entrant liability credit over 25 years). Local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System, including the Employees' Pension System (EPS) and the Correctional Officers' Retirement System (CORS). The bill governs the transfer of Dorchester County detention center officers and their service credits from EPS to CORS if Dorchester County elects to participate.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits the Maryland Department of Health from imposing cost sharing (copayments, coinsurance, or deductibles) for services provided under the Collaborative Care Model (CoCM) to Medicaid recipients, requires commercial health insurers and HMOs to cover CoCM services, and requires the Maryland Health Care Commission to study the impact of eliminating cost sharing for CoCM services in commercial insurance.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health, Maryland Health Care Commission, and Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Medicaid recipients, individuals covered by commercial health insurance plans seeking integrated primary and behavioral health care, primary care and behavioral health providers, and health insurance carriers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration will see a minimal increase in FY 2027 from $125 rate and form filing fees. The Maryland Health Care Commission can complete the required study using existing budgeted resources. There is no immediate fiscal impact on Medicaid or the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 746 explicitly amends the Health - General Article to prohibit the Maryland Department of Health from imposing copayment, coinsurance, or deductible requirements for services provided under the Collaborative Care Model to Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) recipients.

The bill explicitly mandates that the Maryland Health Care Commission conduct a study on the impact of eliminating health insurance cost-sharing for Collaborative Care Model services across private carriers and report its findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by December 1, 2026.

The bill establishes coverage mandates for Collaborative Care Model services under the Insurance Article for commercial insurers, nonprofit health plans, and HMOs, requiring the Maryland Insurance Administration to review rate and form filings and collect associated filing fees.

The Department of Budget and Management administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. Although evaluated in the fiscal note, the bill has no fiscal impact on the State plan because it already reimburses for Collaborative Care Model services.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the membership of the Oversight Committee on Quality of Care in Nursing Homes and Assisted Living Facilities by removing members from specified legislative committees and organizations, adding a representative from LeadingAge Maryland, and adjusting representation guidelines for the assisted living industry.
qa_results.responsible_party: Oversight Committee on Quality of Care in Nursing Homes and Assisted Living Facilities
qa_results.stakeholders: Oversight Committee members, Maryland General Assembly, nursing home and assisted living facility operators, long-term care advocacy organizations (including LeadingAge Maryland, Health Facilities Association of Maryland, and Voices for Quality Care), and facility residents.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact. The changes are technical in nature and do not directly affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the statute governing the Oversight Committee on Quality of Care in Nursing Homes and Assisted Living Facilities, codified under the Health - General Article. The Department of Health regulates these facilities, provided information for the fiscal note, and has multiple statutory seats on the committee, including the Secretary of Health, the Director of the Office of Health Care Quality, and the Deputy Secretary for Behavioral Health.

The Secretary of Aging and the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman (which is housed within the Department of Aging) are statutory members of the Oversight Committee on Quality of Care in Nursing Homes and Assisted Living Facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the membership structure and composition of the Oversight Committee on Quality of Care in Nursing Homes and Assisted Living Facilities.
The Secretary of Disabilities, or the Secretary's designee, is a designated statutory member of the oversight committee whose composition is modified by the bill.
The Secretary of Human Services, or the Secretary's designee, is a designated statutory member of the oversight committee whose composition is modified by the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill modifies the early childhood educator career ladder for eligible private prekindergarten providers by removing fixed statutory deadlines and establishing relative, ongoing timeframes and new pathways for assistant teachers and lead teachers to meet educational and experiential qualification requirements.
qa_results.stakeholders: Eligible private prekindergarten providers, early childhood educators, assistant teachers, lead teachers, and private childcare small businesses.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are unaffected. The bill alters qualification deadlines and pathways without modifying funding formulas or imposing new mandates on local school systems. Oversight of the career ladder will continue to be handled by the Maryland State Department of Education using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is the primary regulatory agency responsible for overseeing early childhood education programs and establishing the career ladder qualifications, standards, and credential pathways for educators employed by eligible private prekindergarten providers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits an individual from using force, threat of force, or physical obstruction to interfere with or physically injure another person who is lawfully exercising or attempting to exercise their First Amendment right of religious freedom at a place of religious worship, establishing misdemeanor penalties of up to 90 days imprisonment and/or a maximum fine of $1,000.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary, State's Attorneys, and state and local law enforcement agencies
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals attending or exercising religious freedom at places of religious worship, religious congregations and organizations, and individuals subject to criminal penalties for obstruction or interference.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new misdemeanor criminal offense for obstructing or interfering with the exercise of religious beliefs at places of worship, which will be filed and adjudicated within the District Court and Circuit Courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a misdemeanor offense punishable by up to 90 days imprisonment and potential probation, which falls under the purview of local detention centers, state pretrial detention in Baltimore City, and the Division of Parole and Probation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Because the new misdemeanor carries a penalty of incarceration of up to 90 days, indigent individuals charged under this statute are entitled to representation by the Office of the Public Defender.

As the primary state law enforcement agency enforcing criminal laws across Maryland, MSP officers are authorized to investigate and enforce this new prohibition against physical obstruction and interference at places of worship.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the misdemeanor crime of gift card forgery for intentionally altering or tampering with a gift card or its packaging to defraud another, and defines the valuation method of gift cards for criminal theft prosecutions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Consumers who purchase or receive gift cards, retail merchants, and individuals accused of gift card theft or tampering
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations. Any impact on small businesses is projected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new misdemeanor offense of gift card forgery and establishes statutory valuation methods for gift cards in theft cases, affecting court filings, caseloads, and judicial proceedings.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new criminal misdemeanor punishable by up to 18 months of imprisonment and sets valuation metrics that could affect theft penalties, impacting caseloads and legal defense representation for indigent individuals.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
