agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill introduces an incarceration penalty of up to 18 months for gift card forgery and impacts general theft penalties, which may result in individuals being sentenced to correctional facilities or placed under probation supervision.

As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is responsible for investigating criminal violations, including retail fraud, tampering, and theft offenses involving gift cards.

The Office of the Attorney General oversees consumer protection issues relating to fraudulent retail practices and gift card tampering, as well as handling appellate criminal matters resulting from convictions.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill enhances homeowner protections in property tax sales by requiring local governments to withhold dwellings from tax sale if the homeowner has a documented terminal illness or medical hardship, expanding Homeowner Protection Program (HPP) eligibility by raising the maximum assessed home value from $300,000 to $450,000, giving priority HPP enrollment to those with terminal illnesses or medical hardships, and allowing homeowners to designate a family member or representative to work with the State Tax Sale Ombudsman.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) and the State Tax Sale Ombudsman
qa_results.stakeholders: Homeowners facing delinquent property taxes (particularly those with terminal illness or medical hardship and those owning homes assessed between $300,000 and $450,000), designated family representatives, county tax collectors, and tax sale investors.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances will see no change in mandated appropriations for the Homeowner Protection Program (HPP); however, expanding eligibility may increase special fund expenditures from the Homeowner Protection Fund beginning in FY 2027 as appropriated funds are more fully utilized, alongside increased special fund revenues in future years from repayments. Local government tax revenues may experience minor delays or reductions beginning in FY 2027 as eligible properties are withheld from tax sales, though impacts may be minimal if homeowners enroll in HPP and liens are paid by the State.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 753 requires the State Department of Assessments and Taxation and the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to consult with the Maryland Department of Health to define 'terminal illness' and 'medical hardship' by regulation for the purposes of withholding qualifying homeowners' dwellings from tax sales.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands the permitted hours of sale for Class B beer, wine, and liquor (golf course) licenses in Wicomico County, allowing license holders to begin selling alcoholic beverages at 7:00 a.m. rather than 10:00 a.m. Monday through Sunday.
qa_results.responsible_party: Wicomico County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Holders of Class B beer, wine, and liquor golf course licenses in Wicomico County and golf course patrons.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: Wicomico County revenues are not affected, and any additional enforcement activities can be handled with existing county resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry. Although the bill specifically alters the hours of sale for local Class B golf course alcoholic beverages licenses administered by the Wicomico County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, it pertains to the broader regulation and taxation of alcoholic beverages in Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a provisional license to practice bachelor social work or master social work for initial applicants who have satisfied all education and experience requirements except passing the required examination. The provisional license is nonrenewable, valid for 12 to 24 months, requires practice under a board-approved supervisor, and terminates upon expiration or upon obtaining a full license after passing the examination.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Social Work Examiners (within the Maryland Department of Health)
qa_results.stakeholders: Initial applicants for bachelor and master social work licenses in Maryland, supervising social workers, and recipients of social work services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures for the State Board of Social Work Examiners increase by $64,900 in FY 2027 to hire one administrator to process and monitor provisional licenses, rising to $85,400 by FY 2031. Board special fund revenues increase by an indeterminate amount starting in FY 2027 from reasonable license fees established by the board to cover administrative costs. There is no local government fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the State Board of Social Work Examiners, which operates within the Maryland Department of Health, with creating, issuing, regulating, and reporting on provisional social work licenses, resulting in operational requirements and a direct fiscal impact for staffing and administration.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires Maryland health occupations boards to allow applicants seeking license or certificate renewal to receive continuing education credits for completing an approved human trafficking awareness training program. The training program must be free of charge, at least one hour in duration, and approved by the Maryland Department of Health in collaboration with a local university and relevant stakeholders. Additionally, health occupations boards must conduct outreach and adopt regulations to carry out the law.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and health occupations boards
qa_results.stakeholders: Regulated health care practitioners, health occupations boards, higher education institutions with relevant programs, and survivors of human trafficking
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not materially affected, as the Maryland Department of Health and health occupations boards can approve the training program, promulgate regulations, and conduct outreach using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary implementing agency tasked with approving the human trafficking awareness training program in collaboration with stakeholders, and its constituent health occupations boards are required to adopt regulations and conduct outreach to allow continuing education credits.

The bill requires MDH to collaborate with a local university to approve the training program, specifically citing the University of Maryland SAFE Center for Human Trafficking Survivors as an illustrative institution.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires MDH to consult with the Maryland Human Trafficking Task Force when approving the human trafficking awareness training program.

Morgan State University qualifies as a local university with relevant public health and social work programs eligible to collaborate on the training program, and was consulted as an information source for the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to conduct an independent cost-driven rate-setting study for community-based behavioral health services by June 30, 2028. It also establishes the Workgroup on Behavioral Health Rate Methodology Modernization within the Maryland Health Care Commission to develop transparent, cost-based reimbursement methodologies for certified community behavioral health clinics, outpatient mental health centers, and independent outpatient providers, and assigns related interim and annual reporting requirements to the Commission.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and Maryland Health Care Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Community-based behavioral health service providers (including certified community behavioral health clinics, outpatient mental health centers, and independent outpatient providers), direct care clinicians and staff, and patients receiving community behavioral health care.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $391,974 in FY 2027 ($181,699 general funds for MDH and $210,275 special funds for MHCC) and $356,100 in FY 2028 ($158,500 general funds for MDH and $197,600 special funds for MHCC) for contractual staff, operating expenses, and contractual services to conduct the rate study and support the workgroup. MHCC may incur indeterminate ongoing special fund costs in out-years for annual reporting. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH, including its Behavioral Health Administration and Medical Care Programs Administration, is directly responsible for conducting the rate-setting study, overseeing provider cost reporting, designating a technical liaison, and developing and implementing the resulting payment system. The department also incurs general fund expenditures for contractual personnel to complete this work.

MHCC houses and provides primary staff support for the newly created Workgroup on Behavioral Health Rate Methodology Modernization, assists MDH with the rate-setting study, collects provider data, and is tasked with ongoing annual reporting requirements, resulting in dedicated special fund expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Workgroup on Behavioral Health Rate Methodology Modernization as a temporary advisory body to evaluate cost drivers and develop transparent, cost-based reimbursement methodologies before terminating in 2028.
The Governor's Office receives interim and final study reports from both the Workgroup and the Maryland Health Care Commission regarding behavioral health delivery and rate modernizations.

qa_results.bill_summary: The NyKayla Strawder Memorial Act requires a law enforcement officer to forward a complaint to the Department of Juvenile Services if a child under the age of 13 is alleged to have committed an act resulting in the death of a victim, and mandates that an intake officer file a petition alleging the child is a child in need of supervision (CINS).
qa_results.stakeholders: Children under the age of 13 alleged to have committed acts resulting in death, their families, law enforcement officers, victims' families, and the juvenile justice system.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that DJS intake officers must file a petition alleging that a child is in need of supervision (CINS) if a complaint is filed alleging that a child under 13 committed an act resulting in the death of a victim, and requires law enforcement to forward such complaints to DJS.

Mandatory filing of Child in Need of Supervision petitions brings these cases before the juvenile court division of the Maryland Judicial Branch, impacting court dockets and operations supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

The bill statutorily requires law enforcement officers, which includes Maryland State Police troopers investigating fatal incidents involving minors under 13, to forward complaints directly to the Department of Juvenile Services.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender provides representation to indigent juveniles involved in court proceedings, which can include youth subject to juvenile petitions under Courts and Judicial Proceedings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires Washington County and municipalities within the county to grant a 100% property tax credit against county and municipal real property taxes for property owned by Platoon 22, Incorporated and used to provide housing to veterans.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governing body of Washington County and governing bodies of municipal corporations within Washington County (including the City of Hagerstown)
qa_results.stakeholders: Platoon 22, Incorporated, military veterans receiving housing, Washington County, and the City of Hagerstown
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Beginning in fiscal year 2027, local property tax revenues decrease by approximately $4,000 annually for Washington County and approximately $5,000 annually for the City of Hagerstown. Local expenditures are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates a local property tax credit for real property owned by Platoon 22, Inc. that is used to provide housing to veterans. While there is no direct state fiscal impact, the bill directly concerns veteran housing and support services, which aligns with the department's mission to support veterans and coordinate veteran housing initiatives.

The board has jurisdiction over administrative appeals involving property valuations, tax exemptions, and local property tax credits following initial assessments, making it potentially relevant if disputes arise concerning the eligibility or application of this mandatory credit.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date from June 30, 2027, to June 30, 2030, for provisions authorizing aquaculture leaseholders to place shellfish, bags, nets, and structures on submerged aquatic vegetation with prior written approval from the Department of Natural Resources.
qa_results.stakeholders: Aquaculture leaseholders and small businesses engaged in shellfish aquaculture
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State finances and has no local effect. Small businesses engaged in shellfish aquaculture may experience a meaningful positive economic benefit from the continuation of the authorization.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly extends the Department of Natural Resources' authority and regulatory framework regarding aquaculture leases and the placement of shellfish, bags, nets, and structures on submerged aquatic vegetation through June 30, 2030.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes current and vested former members of the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS) who are or were assigned as helicopter pilots in a State law enforcement aviation unit to receive up to five years of military service credit even if they receive credit for that military service from another retirement system, while prohibiting individuals from receiving service credit under this provision more than once.
qa_results.stakeholders: Members and vested former members of the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System who serve or served as helicopter pilots in State law enforcement aviation units with prior military service.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Because the bill is anticipated to apply to only a small number of individuals, there is no discernible effect on State pension liabilities, contribution rates, or expenditures. There is no effect on State revenues and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency directly administers the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS) and the State Retirement and Pension System, and will be responsible for reviewing applications and granting the military service credit to eligible helicopter pilots.

The Maryland State Police operates the State's law enforcement Aviation Command, whose sworn helicopter pilots are members of LEOPS and the intended beneficiaries of this pension service credit exception.
As the State's central personnel and budget agency, DBM oversees state employee benefits, retirement policies, and state employer contributions to the pension systems.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of Commerce to allow eligible fund managers under the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Business Account (SMWOBA) to receive and retain a loan management fee ranging from 1.5% to 3% of the total loan principal, and authorizes the department to set an annual cap on cumulative management fees.
qa_results.stakeholders: Eligible fund managers (including local economic development corporations and private investment entities) and small, minority, and women-owned businesses in Maryland seeking capital.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State funding for SMWOBA is not affected; the Department of Commerce can implement the bill with existing resources, though general fund expenditures could rise if additional oversight is required. At the local level, local economic development entities serving as fund managers may receive additional fee revenue (illustratively up to $600,000 diverted from SMWOBA based on $20.0 million in annual program funding), which reduces the overall amount directly available for loans and grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Commerce administers the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Business Account (SMWOBA) and is directly authorized by the bill to allow eligible fund managers to receive and retain a loan management fee (between 1.5% and 3.0% of loan principal) and to establish an annual cap on cumulative fees.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Aging Resilience Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund administered by the Maryland Department of Aging to support the department's mission, including partnership development and agency programs, services, and activities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging (Secretary of Aging)
qa_results.stakeholders: Older Maryland adults (seniors), caregivers, families of seniors, and local Area Agencies on Aging (AAAs)
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues and expenditures increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in fiscal year 2027 from investment earnings, collected fees, and philanthropic or other accepted contributions. The Department of Aging can administer the fund with existing budgeted resources. Local Area Agencies on Aging revenues and expenditures may also increase if funds become available.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Aging Resilience Fund to support the Department of Aging's mission, designates the Secretary of Aging as the administrator of the fund, and requires the Department to submit an annual report on the fund's finances to the General Assembly.
The bill requires the State Treasurer to hold the Aging Resilience Fund separately and invest its moneys in the same manner as other State moneys.
The bill requires the Comptroller to account for the newly established Aging Resilience Fund.

DBM oversees the state budget execution and fiscal operations; the bill specifies that expenditures from the fund must be in accordance with the State budget and limits mid-year appropriation reductions.
The bill explicitly restricts the Governor's statutory authority to reduce appropriations for the Aging Resilience Fund in the State budget once approved by the General Assembly.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Building Homes Act authorizes Baltimore City and county or municipal governing bodies to grant an optional local property tax credit for affordable dwellings financed through a mortgage or deed of trust from a nonprofit entity. To qualify, the dwelling must have a legally binding covenant of at least 20 years enforcing income and equity or appreciation restrictions. The credit covers up to the difference between the property tax on the full assessed value and the tax on the portion of the value the homeowner pays via their first mortgage.
qa_results.responsible_party: The Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City, and county and municipal governing bodies
qa_results.stakeholders: Homeowners of qualifying affordable housing, nonprofit housing organizations and mortgage providers (such as Habitat for Humanity), and local governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Local property tax revenues may decrease beginning in FY 2027 to the extent that local jurisdictions elect to grant the tax credit; the exact revenue reduction cannot be reliably estimated because it depends on local adoption, dwelling values, and participation rates. Local expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes an optional local property tax credit for affordable dwellings subject to nonprofit mortgages and long-term affordability covenants. While the credit is administered and enacted at the county and municipal levels, it directly aligns with DHCD's core mission to promote and preserve affordable homeownership opportunities across Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill specifies three public service intern fellowships within the Walter Sondheim Jr. Public Service Internship Scholarship Program, increases the maximum scholarship award amount from $5,000 to $6,000, and mandates that beginning in fiscal year 2028, the Governor must appropriate at least 125% of the fiscal year 2026 appropriation for the program.
qa_results.responsible_party: The Shriver Center at the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC)
qa_results.stakeholders: College and graduate students pursuing public service internships in Maryland, public and nonprofit sector employers, and the University of Maryland, Baltimore County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $87,500 annually beginning in FY 2028 to fulfill a mandated minimum appropriation of $437,500 (125% of the estimated $350,000 FY 2026 appropriation). Raising the maximum scholarship cap from $5,000 to $6,000 does not affect total program expenditures, though it may reduce the total number of scholarships awarded. No direct local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Walter Sondheim Jr. Public Service Internship Scholarship Program is administered by the Shriver Center at the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC), a member institution of the University System of Maryland. The bill directly mandates increased State budget funding for UMBC to support specific fellowship programs beginning in fiscal year 2028.

The bill mandates an appropriation in the annual State budget beginning in fiscal year 2028 equal to at least 125% of the fiscal year 2026 appropriation, which directly impacts the Department of Budget and Management's role in executive budget preparation and fiscal planning.
The bill establishes a statutory requirement mandating that the Governor include a specific minimum appropriation for the program and UMBC within the annual budget bill starting in fiscal year 2028.

The scholarship program is codified under Title 18 (Student Financial Assistance) of the Education Article, which falls under the broader regulatory purview of the Maryland Higher Education Commission, although daily administration of this specific program is handled by UMBC.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the State Department of Assessments and Taxation, in coordination with several state and legal entities, to conduct a study evaluating the use of blockchain technology for securely recording and verifying real property leases and titles, and assessing its potential use by law enforcement and courts to resolve property disputes involving squatting.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Property owners, tenants and lessees, law enforcement agencies, state courts, legal aid organizations, and individuals involved in real property disputes or squatting
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected; any potential minimal costs associated with conducting the study and participating in the workgroup can be absorbed within existing resources. Local government operations and finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Office of the Attorney General to coordinate with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation and other entities to conduct the study on blockchain-based real property title and lease recordation and report the results.

The Maryland State Police is specifically mandated to coordinate with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to evaluate blockchain technology, particularly regarding its potential use by law enforcement to resolve real property disputes involving squatting.

As the administrative head of the Maryland Judiciary, the Administrative Office of the Courts is directly affected because the bill requires coordination with the Maryland Judiciary to conduct the study and assess the use of blockchain in resolving court disputes involving squatting and title recordation.
The bill requires the findings and recommendations of the blockchain real property study to be reported directly to the Governor on or before December 31, 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Department of Aging to award grants to nonprofit organizations and area agencies on aging to foster social connections for individuals in aging-in-place programs through events and gatherings at multigenerational third places, including covering operational, administrative, and lease/rental costs for senior villages to access these community spaces.
qa_results.stakeholders: Seniors and individuals participating in aging-in-place programs, senior villages, nonprofit organizations, and area agencies on aging.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not significantly impacted because the bill primarily broadens the allowable uses of existing grant funds, and the Maryland Department of Aging can manage any administrative adjustments with existing resources. Local governments operating area agencies on aging may receive grants for the expanded purposes, resulting in a corresponding increase in local revenues and expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly authorizes and tasks the Maryland Department of Aging with administering grants to nonprofit organizations and area agencies on aging for aging-in-place programs at multigenerational third places and setting related application and disbursal regulations.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 816 authorizes the Executive Director of the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund (MAIF) to establish an auto insurance affordability program limiting maximum premium rates for eligible private passenger policyholders with household incomes at or below 250% of the federal poverty level, subject to review and approval by the Maryland Insurance Administration. The bill also reduces the cap on MAIF's private passenger auto assessment allocation percentage from 3% to 1% on other motor vehicle insurers.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund (MAIF) and the Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA)
qa_results.stakeholders: MAIF policyholders (particularly low-income drivers with household income up to 250% of the federal poverty level), private passenger motor vehicle insurers in Maryland, and standard market auto policyholders.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no material impact on State or local government operations or finances. MAIF revenues will likely decrease in FY 2028 and FY 2029 compared to current law, as MAIF can continue offering discounted premiums to certain low-income policyholders rather than raising them to fully adequate rates as ordered by MIA. Lowering the assessment allocation cap from 3% to 1% is not expected to affect MAIF revenues, and MAIF expenditures are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends provisions governing the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund (MAIF), authorizing its Executive Director to establish an affordability program that caps premiums for qualifying lower-income drivers and reducing the statutory assessment allocation percentage cap for the private passenger auto division from 3% to 1%.

The Maryland Insurance Administration and the Insurance Commissioner are tasked with the regulatory oversight, review, and approval of MAIF's proposed affordability program and premium rates, and have the authority to require modifications if statutory criteria are not met.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the maximum annual salary of circuit court clerks and registers of wills from $146,500 to the salary of a State employee at Grade 26, Step 20 of the Maryland Standard and Bargaining Salary Scale, effective at the beginning of the next term of office, and repeals an obsolete minimum salary provision for the register of wills in Baltimore City.
qa_results.stakeholders: Clerks of the circuit courts, registers of wills, and the Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by $403,800 in FY 2027 and $692,300 annually thereafter due to salary increases for circuit court clerks. General fund revenues decrease by $386,300 in FY 2027 and $662,100 annually thereafter due to salary increases for registers of wills reducing excess fees remitted to the State. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the maximum annual salary that may be set for registers of wills across Maryland and repeals an obsolete minimum annual salary provision for the Register of Wills for Baltimore City.
The bill alters the maximum annual salary for the clerks of the circuit courts, resulting in a significant general fund expenditure impact on the Judiciary budget to fund the salary increases.

The Board of Public Works is the entity statutorily tasked with determining and setting the specific annual salaries of circuit court clerks and registers of wills within the new maximum cap established by the bill.

The bill involves the Comptroller in administering deficiencies in office expenses and salaries for registers of wills, requiring written authorization for fund transfers from remitted taxes or excess fees.
The bill pegs the maximum salary limits for clerks and registers of wills to Grade 26, Step 20 of the State Standard and Bargaining Salary Scale, which is administered and maintained by DBM.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 828 allows the Governor to appoint an employee of a local county board of education as a regular member of the Maryland State Board of Education, permitting up to two board members (including the teacher member) to be local board employees at any given time. It establishes that a county board employee member cannot be a county superintendent, may participate in executive sessions, and faces specific voting restrictions regarding personnel disciplinary or dismissal appeals. It also specifies that when a board member is legally prohibited from voting on a matter, an affirmative vote of a majority of the members eligible to vote is required for action.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor of Maryland and Maryland State Board of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland State Board of Education, county board of education employees, public school staff, and the Maryland Department of Education
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is procedural in nature and does not directly affect State or local government finances, revenues, or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the membership criteria, voting restrictions, and quorum rules of the Maryland State Board of Education, which oversees the Department of Education.

The Governor is responsible for appointing members to the State Board of Education with the advice and consent of the Senate, and the bill expands the statutory eligibility criteria to permit an additional employee of a county board of education to be appointed.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and managing appointments to state boards, including the State Board of Education under the bill's updated membership parameters.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 829 requires applicants for a State for-hire driver's license or a local taxicab driver's license to submit documentation verifying completion of an approved human trafficking awareness training program. It also prohibits transportation network companies from permitting transportation network operators to provide prearranged rides unless they complete human trafficking awareness training within 30 days of their first ride. Additionally, the bill protects licensed taxicab drivers, for-hire drivers, and transportation network operators from civil or criminal liability when reporting or responding in good faith to suspected incidents of human trafficking.
qa_results.stakeholders: For-hire drivers, taxicab drivers, transportation network companies (TNCs), transportation network operators (rideshare drivers), license applicants, and victims of human trafficking.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures for the Public Service Commission increase by $10,000 in FY 2027 only for one-time modifications to its online licensing application software. Special fund revenues increase correspondingly by $10,000 in FY 2027 through assessments on regulated public service companies. Local governments can handle administrative requirements using existing resources with no effect on local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary implementing regulatory agency for the bill, tasked with verifying human trafficking awareness training documentation for for-hire driver's license applicants and incurring a fiscal cost of $10,000 in FY 2027 to update its licensing software.

The bill provides civil and criminal immunity to for-hire drivers and transportation network operators who report or respond in good faith to suspected human trafficking, which impacts judicial proceedings and case adjudications.
The Office of the People's Counsel monitors and advocates regarding regulated utility services and proceedings before the Public Service Commission, and was consulted on the fiscal and policy note.

qa_results.bill_summary: Reestablishes the Commission to Advance Lithium-Ion Battery Safety in Maryland with expanded membership and an updated mandate to study lithium-ion battery safety, recycling, fire prevention, and transportation risks, requiring an interim report by December 1, 2026, and a final report by December 1, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the State Fire Marshal
qa_results.stakeholders: First responders, firefighters, battery manufacturers, battery recycling and solid waste facilities, electric utilities, freight and shipping industries, the Port of Baltimore, insurance providers, and Maryland residents.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $70,700 in FY 2027 and $30,100 in FY 2028 for the Office of the State Fire Marshal to hire one temporary contractual management associate to provide staff support and complete reports. Commission member expense reimbursements are minimal and absorbable. There is no effect on revenues and no material fiscal impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the State Fire Marshal (OSFM), a division of the Department of State Police, is required to staff the commission, and the State Fire Marshal or a designee serves as a member. The bill has a direct fiscal impact on the agency, requiring $70,700 in FY 2027 and $30,100 in FY 2028 for contractual staffing.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill reestablishes the Commission to Advance Lithium-Ion Battery Safety in Maryland as a temporary advisory body with an altered membership and expanded study mandate through June 30, 2028.

The Secretary of the Environment appoints two commission members (one representing the department and one representing the Land and Materials Administration). The commission is tasked with studying battery recycling, storage, disposal, and impacts on solid waste facilities.

The Director of the MEA appoints three commission members (one MEA representative, one lithium-ion battery manufacturer representative, and one vehicle propulsion battery manufacturer representative), and the commission evaluates clean energy and storage applications.

The Secretary of Transportation appoints representatives from the Maryland Port Administration and ocean freight shipping industry. Additionally, the commission is tasked with evaluating battery risks on roads, rail, and tunnels across Maryland.
The commission includes a designated representative of the Maryland Port Administration, and the commission is specifically mandated to study battery risks at the Port of Baltimore.

The Maryland Insurance Commissioner appoints two commission members representing the property casualty and commercial insurance industries. The commission must evaluate the impacts of battery risks on insurance providers and coverage availability.
The Chair of the Public Service Commission appoints a commission member, and the commission examines battery fire prevention and safety in utility applications and grid-scale storage.
The Secretary of Natural Resources appoints a representative from the department's Power Plant Research Program to serve on the commission.
The commission must submit a final report detailing its findings and recommendations to the Governor by December 1, 2027.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes licensed pharmacists to enter into prescriber-pharmacist agreements to treat opioid use disorder using controlled dangerous substances (CDS) drug therapy, provided they register with the federal Drug Enforcement Administration and the Maryland Office of Controlled Substances Administration, complete required training, and query the Prescription Drug Monitoring Program before initiating or modifying therapy. The bill also includes licensed certified midwives as authorized prescribers permitted to enter into therapy management contracts and repeals the requirement that prescribers submit agreement copies to their respective health occupations licensing boards.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health (including the State Board of Pharmacy and the Office of Controlled Substances Administration)
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed pharmacists, authorized prescribers (licensed physicians, podiatrists, certified advanced practice nurses, and certified midwives), and individuals receiving treatment for opioid use disorder.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $58,635 in FY 2027 to hire one part-time (0.5 FTE) administrative specialist to process CDS registration applications and cover a one-time $1,750 software database update; ongoing annual expenditures range from $49,000 to $56,400 through FY 2031. State general fund revenues increase by approximately $72,000 in FY 2027 from initial CDS three-year registration fees ($120 per applicant), with projected annual revenues of $7,200 in FY 2028 and FY 2029, $79,200 in FY 2030 (reflecting renewals), and $14,400 in FY 2031. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 838 directly affects health occupation regulatory boards within MDH (including the State Board of Pharmacy and the Board of Nursing), regulates the Prescription Drug Monitoring Program (PDMP), and results in a direct fiscal impact of general fund expenditures for personnel and software updates, as well as revenue from registration fees.

The bill explicitly requires pharmacists seeking to treat opioid use disorder with controlled dangerous substances (CDS) under a prescriber-pharmacist agreement to individually register with the Office of Controlled Substances Administration (OCSA). OCSA will process the new registrations, collect fees, update its online database, and hire additional staff as detailed in the fiscal note.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires the Board of Community College Trustees for Frederick County to include an opportunity for public comment at each meeting, record each meeting via audio or video, post recordings online free of charge within two business days when practicable, and maintain recordings and minutes in perpetuity. It also requires board members to undergo training on board governance, structure, responsibilities, and roles at least once every two years.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Community College Trustees for Frederick County
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the Frederick Community College Board of Trustees, Frederick Community College staff and students, and members of the public in Frederick County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Frederick Community College expenditures may increase minimally to record, post, and permanently store board meeting recordings, though training and initial web postings can be managed within existing resources. Frederick County government revenues and expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's central regulatory and coordinating agency for postsecondary education, MHEC oversees statewide policies and standards for Maryland's higher education institutions, including community colleges like Frederick Community College. While the bill directly imposes requirements on the local board, MHEC was consulted as an information source regarding community college governance.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City and governing bodies of counties and municipal corporations to grant an optional local property tax credit on the dwelling house of a surviving spouse of a military service member who is ineligible for the existing statewide property tax exemption.
qa_results.responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City and the governing bodies of Maryland counties and municipal corporations
qa_results.stakeholders: Surviving spouses of military service members and disabled veterans who are ineligible for the existing property tax exemption, as well as county and municipal governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Local property tax revenues will decrease beginning in FY 2027 to the extent local governments enact the credit. The exact local revenue loss is indeterminate and will depend on which jurisdictions grant the credit, local property tax rates, and property values. Local expenditures are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes local property tax credits for surviving spouses of deceased military service members who are ineligible for the existing statewide exemption. As the principal agency providing advocacy, support, and resource navigation for military families and veterans' surviving spouses, the department is directly concerned with policies affecting benefits and housing affordability for this population.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands eligibility for two Maryland higher education financial assistance programs. First, it extends eligibility for the Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship to Delmar, Maryland residents who graduate from Delmar High School in Delaware. Second, it expands and renames the Fallen Transportation Workers Scholarship Program to the Fallen and Surviving Transportation Workers Scholarship Program, extending eligibility to surviving transportation workers of catastrophic accidents (causing at least $100 million in facility damages) and expanding eligible family members of fallen and surviving workers to include unmarried partners, their children, and siblings under certain conditions. Additionally, it allows scholarship awards under this program to cover the total cost of attendance.
qa_results.stakeholders: Delmar, Maryland residents graduating from Delmar High School; surviving and fallen Maryland transportation workers and their eligible family members (spouses, unmarried partners, children, stepchildren, and siblings); and Maryland institutions of postsecondary education.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures and special fund revenues and expenditures increase beginning as early as fiscal 2027 (more likely fiscal 2028) due to expanded eligibility and authorizing awards for the total cost of attendance under the Fallen and Surviving Transportation Workers Scholarship Program; exact amounts are indeterminate due to an unknown number of eligible recipients. The expansion of the Community College Promise Scholarship does not increase overall state funding mandates, though it may alter waitlists. Local community colleges can implement application updates using existing resources with no effect on local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is the primary regulatory and administering agency for State student financial assistance programs, including the Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship and the Fallen and Surviving Transportation Workers Scholarship Program and its associated special fund.

As the primary state entity overseeing postsecondary student financial aid, the Commission is tasked with administering the Fallen and Surviving Transportation Workers Scholarship Program and managing the allocation of funds to postsecondary institutions.

MDOT is explicitly tasked under § 18–4003(e) with providing the Commission, to the extent practicable, with the names and contact information of the families of fallen and surviving transportation workers after qualifying accidents.
The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold and invest the Fallen and Surviving Transportation Workers Scholarship Fund and receive deposits of gifts or grants for the program.
The Comptroller is designated in statute to account for the Fallen and Surviving Transportation Workers Scholarship Fund.

USM institutions determine eligibility and award funds for enrolled scholarship recipients, and the maximum award amount under the Fallen and Surviving Transportation Workers Scholarship is statutorily benchmarked to full-time undergraduate tuition and fees across USM institutions.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill exempts property owned by the City of Hagerstown and used primarily for public social, recreational, and entertainment purposes from state, county, and municipal property taxes. It also retroactively applies this property tax exemption, as well as an existing exemption for the Hagerstown Multi-Use Sports and Events Facility, Inc., back to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2023 (fiscal 2024), requiring the State, Washington County, and the City of Hagerstown to refund any excess property taxes collected.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: City of Hagerstown, Hagerstown Multi-Use Sports and Events Facility, Inc., Washington County, and local taxpayers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Annuity Bond Fund (ABF) revenues decrease by approximately $80,300 in FY 2027 due to retroactive refunds for the Hagerstown Multi-Use Sports and Events Facility, plus an ongoing annual reduction of $22,300 starting in FY 2027 from the City of Hagerstown property exemption. Washington County and City of Hagerstown local property tax revenues decrease by approximately $1.3 million in FY 2027 for retroactive refunds ($575,700 county and $718,300 municipal), with an additional ongoing annual reduction of $160,000 beginning in FY 2027. State and local expenditures are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the State pay refunds for excess property taxes paid due to the retroactive exemption, which directly impacts the Comptroller's role as the state's principal tax administrator and payer of state disbursements and refunds.
The bill reduces State property tax revenues that flow directly into the Annuity Bond Fund (ABF), which is managed to service the State's general obligation bonds overseen by the State Treasurer.

The reduction in Annuity Bond Fund revenue impacts debt service calculations for State general obligation bonds, which can affect the State property tax rate annually set by the Board of Public Works.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the State Fire Prevention Commission to update the State Fire Prevention Code to incorporate specific sections of the NFPA 101 Life Safety Code, allowing valet trash and recyclable materials awaiting scheduled collection to be placed in corridors and exits of apartment buildings under specified safety standards.
qa_results.stakeholders: Apartment residents, apartment building owners and property managers, and valet trash and recycling collection services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The State Fire Prevention Commission can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources, and state revenues are not affected. The bill is not expected to materially affect local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Fire Prevention Commission and the Office of the State Fire Marshal are established within the Department of State Police. The bill directly mandates the Commission to adopt regulations amending the State Fire Prevention Code to incorporate specific NFPA 101 standards regarding valet trash collection.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly orders the State Fire Prevention Commission, a statutory state regulatory commission, to adopt specific regulations regarding trash and recyclable materials placement in corridors and exits under the Life Safety Code.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill exempts certain vulnerable groups—including children who are homeless, siblings of enrolled children, and families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance, TANF, or Supplemental Security Income—from any enrollment freeze in the Child Care Scholarship Program. It also requires the Maryland State Department of Education to establish a prioritized waitlist during enrollment freezes, develop a new program application capturing child care employment details, and review job training eligibility methodology.
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income families seeking child care assistance, homeless children, siblings of participating children, recipients of TCA, TANF, or SSI, child care facility employees, and child care providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $350,000 in FY 2027 for IT modifications to the Child Care Scholarship tracking system and web portals. Costs for waitlist exemptions are expected to be offset by savings or copayment adjustments under contingent companion legislation (HB 1321). No impact on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the Child Care Scholarship Program. The bill requires MSDE to establish and manage a waitlist during an enrollment freeze with specific priority tiers, exempt certain low-income and vulnerable populations from the freeze, develop a new program application, and conduct a review of job training eligibility criteria.

The bill explicitly exempts recipients of Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) and the federal Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) program—both administered by DHS—from any enrollment freeze in the Child Care Scholarship Program, necessitating data sharing and verification coordination between MSDE and DHS.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires a home builder holding a property open to the public to conspicuously display an unobstructed notice informing prospective buyers that the sales representative's duty of loyalty is only to the home builder and that buyers have the right to independent representation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Home Builder Registration Unit in the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Home builders, registered sales representatives, and prospective new home buyers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local government finances or operations. Small business impact is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends Title 4.5 of the Business Regulation Article, which governs home builder registration. The Home Builder Registration Unit is housed within the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General, making OAG the primary regulatory and enforcement body for these consumer disclosure requirements.

The Maryland Department of Labor oversees the licensing and regulation of real estate professions (including sales agents and brokers) through the Maryland Real Estate Commission and was consulted as an information source regarding sales representative disclosures and real estate representation rules.
The Administrative Office of the Courts was consulted for fiscal analysis regarding potential civil disputes or enforcement actions arising from non-compliance with statutory disclosure mandates.

qa_results.bill_summary: Clarifies that the Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council is a tax-exempt body politic and corporate, in addition to being an instrumentality of the State.
qa_results.stakeholders: The Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council, Centers for Independent Living, and Maryland residents with disabilities who receive independent living services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state or local fiscal impact. The bill's clarification of legal status is technical in nature and does not directly affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill clarifies the legal and tax-exempt corporate status of the Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council (MSILC), which works with Centers for Independent Living to develop and implement the State Plan for Independent Living for individuals with disabilities, directly aligning with the Department of Disabilities' mission to coordinate community living and services for Maryland residents with disabilities.

MSDE oversees the Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS), which partners with the Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council in submitting, monitoring, and evaluating the State Plan for Independent Living under the federal Rehabilitation Act.

As the state's principal tax collector and administrator of state tax laws, the Comptroller has an interest in statutory provisions clarifying the tax-exempt status of state instrumentalities and bodies politic.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands eligibility for the Maryland Police Officers and Probation Agents Scholarship Program to include correctional officers and individuals enrolled in certificate programs, renaming the initiative the Maryland Police Officers, Probation Agents, and Correctional Officers Scholarship Program.
qa_results.stakeholders: Current and prospective correctional officers, police officers, probation agents, and Maryland public colleges and universities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $20,000 in FY 2027 for one-time system enhancements to the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS). Expanding scholarship eligibility does not require additional spending because awards can be made within existing appropriations or applicants can be placed on a waiting list. State revenues and local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the scholarship program through its Office of Student Financial Assistance, updating eligibility guidelines, publicizing the program, and making technical updates to the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS).

MHEC is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the scholarship program through its Office of Student Financial Assistance, updating eligibility guidelines, and making necessary enhancements to MDCAPS.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS employs state correctional officers and probation agents. The expansion of this scholarship program to include correctional officers directly supports DPSCS workforce development, recruitment, and staff retention.
State police officers are eligible participants in this scholarship program, and the bill expands eligible educational tracks to include certificate programs that further their careers.
USM institutions are eligible public senior higher education institutions where scholarship recipients can enroll in degree and certificate programs funded by the scholarship.
Morgan State University is a public senior higher education institution eligible to enroll recipients who utilize these scholarship funds for degree or certificate programs.
Saint Mary's College of Maryland is an eligible public four-year higher education institution where recipients may apply their scholarship funding.
DJS operates juvenile detention and supervision facilities and was consulted as a stakeholder regarding correctional workforce classifications and scholarship eligibility.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Nonpublic Special Education School Renovation Program, administered by the Interagency Commission on School Construction, to provide grants to eligible nonpublic special education schools for facility renovations, health and safety improvements, infrastructure modernization, technology upgrades, residential cottage upgrades, and necessary new construction.
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonpublic special education schools, residential treatment centers, and students with disabilities placed in nonpublic educational programs.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $145,200 in FY 2027 to hire two full-time administrative and engineering staff (one at IAC and one at MSDE) to establish and manage the program, increasing to $285,300 by FY 2031. The bill states legislative intent for an annual capital budget appropriation of at least $5.0 million beginning in FY 2028; this does not alter total State capital expenditures, but may reduce or delay other capital projects or increase PAYGO general fund expenditures if PAYGO funds are utilized. There is no effect on revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Nonpublic Special Education School Renovation Program within the Interagency Commission on School Construction (IAC), requiring IAC to administer the grant program, evaluate applications, award funding, and adopt implementing regulations.

The program provides grants tied to MSDE-approved educational programs and standards, and the fiscal note allocates a new full-time school facilities engineer position to MSDE to establish technical criteria and assist with application evaluations.
The bill expresses the intent of the General Assembly that the Governor include an appropriation of at least $5.0 million for the program in the annual capital budget bill.
DBM oversees the state budget planning and execution process, which includes coordinating the annual capital budget recommendations to address the legislative funding intent.
DGS provides review for school construction designs and public facilities documents, though the fiscal note anticipates minimal additional impact on the agency.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 855 extends the allowable display window for candidate and proposition signs in common ownership communities (condominiums, homeowners associations, and cooperative housing corporations). It allows these communities to restrict sign displays to a time period of no less than 45 days prior to the start of early voting (or 45 days prior to the election or vote if no early voting takes place) through 7 days after the election or vote.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents, property owners, and governing boards of common ownership communities (condominiums, homeowners associations, and cooperative housing corporations), as well as political candidates and campaign organizations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no effect on State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General (specifically the Consumer Protection Division) handles inquiries and disputes related to common ownership communities (HOAs, condominiums, and cooperative housing corporations). While the bill does not have a fiscal impact, it amends statutory governance rules under the Corporations and Associations Article and Real Property Article that fall within consumer protection purview.

The Administrative Office of the Courts provides administrative support to the state courts, which may hear civil actions or covenant enforcement disputes involving homeowners, condominium owners, and common ownership community associations regarding the allowable sign display timeframe.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) to register every local school system in Maryland as an associate member of a national membership organization providing access to the Educator Identification Clearinghouse and pay all related fees and dues. Local school systems must use the clearinghouse to screen individuals offered employment for licensed educator positions on or after August 1, 2026, and ensure those individuals apply for and obtain required licenses before interacting with children.
qa_results.stakeholders: Educator applicants and newly hired teachers requiring licenses, local school systems, and Maryland public school students.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2027, State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $28,596 (approximately $28,600) annually for MSDE to pay membership dues and subscription fees for all 24 local school systems. State revenues are unaffected. Local school system expenditures decrease minimally (up to $2,400 per district) for school systems that currently pay for clearinghouse membership independently; other local school systems can perform the required screenings using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) to register all 24 local school systems as associate members of a national membership organization providing access to the Educator Identification Clearinghouse and to pay all associated membership dues and subscription fees, resulting in an annual general fund expenditure increase of approximately $28,600.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Information Technology to publish the Statewide Information Technology Master Plan on its website and submit it to the General Assembly within one year after the Governor's inauguration in each term. It establishes notification requirements if the plan is delayed and mandates an annual briefing to the General Assembly on the plan's implementation, material changes, and deployment across the Executive Branch.
qa_results.stakeholders: Executive Branch state agencies, the Governor, the Maryland General Assembly, and the public.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Information Technology can handle the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. The bill has no effect on state revenues and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 861 directly tasks the Department of Information Technology and the Secretary with publishing the Statewide Information Technology Master Plan within one year of each gubernatorial inauguration, submitting it to the General Assembly, issuing notifications if delayed, and providing an annual briefing on plan implementation and deployment.
The bill establishes the deadline for the IT Master Plan based on the Governor's inauguration date for each term and requires written notification to the Governor if the deadline cannot be met.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits a freight railroad train operating in Maryland on a rail corridor shared with high-speed passenger or commuter trains from operating without a crew of at least two individuals, excluding hostler or yard service. Imposes civil penalties of up to $10,000 for a first willful violation and up to $25,000 for repeat violations within three years, contingent on the enactment of similar legislation in New York, Pennsylvania, and Virginia.
qa_results.stakeholders: Freight railroad companies (including CSX), freight train crews and rail labor unions, MARC commuter rail operations, and passengers on rail corridors shared with freight trains.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Under current federal regulations requiring two-person crews, the bill has no material fiscal effect on state or local finances or operations, and MD Labor can absorb enforcement with existing resources. However, if federal two-person crew rules are invalidated or repealed, an existing track access agreement between MTA and CSX could trigger up to $6.0 million annually in State Transportation Trust Fund expenditures to reimburse CSX labor costs. Minimal general fund revenue may result from civil penalties.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Labor and Employment Article under the Railroad Safety and Health Program, authorizing the Commissioner of Labor and Industry within the Department of Labor to enforce the two-person crew requirement and assess civil penalties of up to $25,000 for willful violations. Additionally, the department is specifically tasked with monitoring and notifying the Department of Legislative Services when the multi-state enactment contingency is met.

Under an existing track access agreement with freight operator CSX for the MARC commuter rail lines, MTA could be required to reimburse CSX up to $6.0 million annually for incremental labor costs if state law mandates crew sizes and federal requirements are struck down or repealed.

As the parent department overseeing the Maryland Transit Administration (MTA), MDOT could face a fiscal impact of up to $6.0 million from the State Transportation Trust Fund to cover potential CSX freight railroad staffing reimbursements under the MTA track access agreement.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Maryland Workforce Apprenticeship Utilization Act requires contractors and subcontractors on covered public works projects subject to prevailing wage laws to use qualifying apprentices or journeyworkers for a specified percentage of total labor hours (initially 20% beginning January 1, 2027) or make payments to the State Apprenticeship Training Fund or a qualified apprenticeship program. The bill expands apprenticeship requirements to the University System of Maryland and Baltimore City Community College, alters reporting and auditing requirements, and adjusts authorized uses of the State Apprenticeship Training Fund.
qa_results.stakeholders: Contractors and subcontractors on public works contracts, apprentices, journeyworkers, apprenticeship training programs, public four-year universities, and Baltimore City Community College.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues for the State Apprenticeship Training Fund will increase beginning in FY 2027 as contractors make payments in lieu of meeting apprentice participation thresholds, though a reliable estimate is not feasible. General fund revenues may increase minimally from civil penalties. State and local procurement costs may increase if contractor competition decreases due to workforce requirements, or conversely decrease if apprentice labor offsets higher-wage journeyworkers. State agencies can implement and monitor the provisions using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MD Labor is the primary implementing and enforcing agency under the bill. The Secretary of Labor is required to establish apprenticeship utilization percentages, administer and distribute the State Apprenticeship Training Fund, audit participating programs, receive contractor reports, and enforce penalties for violations.

The bill explicitly amends State Finance and Procurement law to subject the University System of Maryland to Title 17, Subtitle 6 apprenticeship utilization requirements for public works procurement contracts.
The bill specifically subjects Morgan State University public works procurements to Title 17, Subtitle 6 apprenticeship utilization mandates.
The bill applies Title 17, Subtitle 6 apprenticeship requirements on public works contracts directly to Saint Mary's College of Maryland as a covered public institution under § 11-203.

As the State's primary public works and capital facilities construction agency, DGS must ensure that covered state construction contracts and contractors comply with the expanded apprentice utilization standards and reporting mandates.
MDOT administers extensive transportation infrastructure public works projects that are subject to prevailing wage and the bill's new apprenticeship utilization percentage mandates.
BPW reviews and approves major public works contracts and oversees the procurement policies of public universities, which are newly brought under the apprenticeship requirements.
Statutorily mandated under § 17-602(d) to account for the State Apprenticeship Training Fund.
Statutorily mandated under § 17-602(d) to hold the State Apprenticeship Training Fund separately.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Identified in the fiscal note as a state agency that procures and manages public work construction and facility maintenance projects subject to prevailing wage and apprentice utilization rules.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Maintains statutory jurisdiction over procurement disputes and contract claims for public works contracts awarded by state entities, including public universities affected by the amended provisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill extends the termination date of the Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing from June 30, 2026, to December 31, 2028, and extends the deadline for the workgroup to submit its final report of findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly to December 1, 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing and the Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
qa_results.stakeholders: Deaf, deafblind, and hard of hearing individuals in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not affect state revenues, and state expenditures can be handled using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing (ODHH) serves as the primary staffing and coordinating agency for the Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing, whose reporting deadline and termination date are extended by this bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly extends the operations, reporting deadline, and statutory termination date of the Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing.
ODHH operates within the Governor's Office, and the workgroup is statutorily required to submit its findings and recommendations to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires a county or municipality to provide notice to the Maryland Department of the Environment within 10 business days after accepting a permit application for a new building that has a proposed gross floor area of 35,000 square feet or more (excluding parking garage area). The notice must include the address, permit application number, total square footage, building type, planned energy sources, and owner contact information.
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners and developers of new buildings with 35,000 square feet or more of gross floor area, local government permitting agencies (counties and municipalities), and the Maryland Department of the Environment.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland Department of the Environment can receive the required permit notices with existing resources, and local governments can issue the required notices using existing resources. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 870 adds § 2-1603 to the Environment Article, requiring local jurisdictions to provide formal notice to the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) within 10 business days of accepting permit applications for new buildings of 35,000 square feet or larger, including details on energy sources, square footage, and building ownership.

The introduced bill originally placed new regulatory requirements on the Maryland Department of Labor to adopt energy conservation standards under the Maryland Building Performance Standards; however, these provisions were stricken by amendment, leaving the department with minimal to no direct operational responsibilities under the final bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires mandatory membership in the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS) for permanent full-time police officers of the Seat Pleasant Police Department if the department becomes a participating governmental unit, and grants eligible members service credit for prior employment with the department.
qa_results.stakeholders: Permanent full-time local law enforcement officers of the Seat Pleasant Police Department and the City of Seat Pleasant.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. For the City of Seat Pleasant, assuming it joins LEOPS, pension liabilities increase by $2,104,315 for 25 law enforcement officers. Beginning as early as fiscal 2028, net employer contributions are estimated to increase by $541,380 annually (reflecting $680,330 in initial contributions offset by a $138,950 annual new entrant liability credit for 25 years). There is no discernible impact on local revenues or other participating governmental units.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS), including the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS). The bill mandates LEOPS membership and calculates prior service credit for officers of the Seat Pleasant Police Department if the municipality participates as a participating governmental unit (PGU).

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners from three to five members, requiring the Governor to appoint members from a list recommended by the county's General Assembly delegations. It establishes that no more than three members may belong to the same political party and no more than two members may reside in the same legislative district. Additionally, it requires the Board to adopt and publish a written policy on conflicts of interest and member recusal.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners and the Governor of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Anne Arundel County alcoholic beverage licensees and businesses, Anne Arundel County residents, prospective board members, and Anne Arundel County government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected. Anne Arundel County expenditures increase by $39,995 annually beginning in FY 2027 to cover salaries ($15,000 each), fringe benefits, and incidental expenses for the two additional board members. County revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the Governor's statutory appointment responsibilities by expanding the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners from three to five members and requiring the Governor to make appointments from lists submitted by the county's legislative delegations.

As the unit within the Executive Department responsible for vetting, managing, and processing gubernatorial appointments to state and local boards and commissions, the Office of Appointments will administer the recruitment and appointment process for the expanded board seats.

The bill mandates that the Board adopt and publish a written policy related to conflicts of interest and recusal, an area aligned with the State Ethics Commission's broader oversight and guidance on public ethics and conflict-of-interest standards.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the workers' compensation occupational disease presumption for heart disease and hypertension to Carroll County correctional deputies who suffer from partial/total disability or death, subject to medical examination and reporting requirements. It also classifies these deputies as public safety employees, entitling them to enhanced permanent partial disability benefits for awards under 75 weeks.
qa_results.stakeholders: Carroll County correctional deputies and the Carroll County government/Sheriff's Office.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are unaffected. Carroll County expenditures will increase beginning in FY 2027 due to higher workers' compensation costs from the occupational disease presumption and enhanced permanent partial disability benefits (which can add up to $18,944 per claim for awards under 75 weeks). The total expenditure increase cannot be reliably estimated as claim volume is indeterminate.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Workers' Compensation Commission administers the state's workers' compensation law and adjudicates disputed claims. The bill alters statutory compensability presumptions and enhances permanent partial disability benefit rates for Carroll County correctional deputies, which the Commission must apply when resolving claims.

The Subsequent Injury Fund reviews and investigates workers' compensation claims involving pre-existing health conditions. Because the bill establishes specific requirements regarding pre-existing heart disease and hypertension disclosure and liability thresholds, the Fund may be involved in claims with prior disabling conditions.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill permanently establishes the State's Consumer Health Information Hub by repealing its June 30, 2026 termination date, while also eliminating the Governor's requirement to include an annual $350,000 mandated appropriation for the Hub, directing it instead to carry out its duties to the extent funding is available.
qa_results.responsible_party: University of Maryland Herschel S. Horowitz Center for Health Literacy (State's Consumer Health Information Hub)
