qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland consumers, public health and health care professionals, community-based organizations, and State and local government agencies using or providing plain-language health and benefits information.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill repeals the annual $350,000 mandated appropriation and the June 30, 2026 sunset date for the Hub, specifying that duties be carried out to the extent funding is available. The Department of Legislative Services indicates no direct material impact on State or local finances or operations, as the fiscal 2027 budget did not include funding for the Hub due to its scheduled termination under prior law.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State's Consumer Health Information Hub is housed at the Herschel S. Horowitz Center for Health Literacy at the University of Maryland, an institution within the University System of Maryland. The bill repeals the hub's termination date and eliminates its $350,000 mandated annual appropriation.
DBM is responsible for drafting the state budget and supervising budget execution; the bill repeals a statutory mandated annual appropriation of $350,000 for the Consumer Health Information Hub.
The bill repeals the requirement that the Governor include an annual $350,000 appropriation for the Consumer Health Information Hub in the state budget bill.
MDH collaborates directly with the Consumer Health Information Hub on public health communication, health literacy initiatives, and the evaluation of public health media campaigns.
The statute specifically tasks the Hub with supporting public reporting of vital public health information, including health care quality reports issued by the Maryland Health Care Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the governing body of Wicomico County or any municipality within the county to grant an optional property tax credit for real property owned by Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services, Inc. that is intended for development, rehabilitation, and transfer to a private owner, excluding administrative or warehouse properties.
qa_results.responsible_party: Wicomico County Government and municipal governing bodies within Wicomico County
qa_results.stakeholders: Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services, Inc., prospective homebuyers of rehabilitated properties, and local governments in Wicomico County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Local property tax revenues for Wicomico County and municipalities will decrease by a minimal amount beginning in FY 2027 to the extent the credit is enacted. As a reference, Salisbury Neighborhood Housing Services paid $3,611 in total property taxes on 14 parcels in FY 2026. Local expenditures are not directly affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Maryland Transit and Housing Opportunity Act promotes transit-oriented development by allowing eligible rail transit-served areas to be designated as enterprise zones and requiring the Maryland Economic Development Corporation to prioritize redeveloping transit-adjacent state, city, or WMATA-owned land under the Strategic Infrastructure Revolving Loan Program. It also restricts local jurisdictions from imposing minimum off-street parking mandates within a quarter-mile of frequent rail transit stations without an approved parking study, prohibits certain local land use restrictions on state-owned transit land, requires local zoning to permit mixed-use development within a half-mile of rail stations, and delays the collection of local development impact fees and excise taxes until construction completion and occupancy permit issuance.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation, Maryland Economic Development Corporation, and Maryland Department of Commerce
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial and residential developers, property owners, transit commuters, local governments, and small businesses located near rail transit stations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures will increase by an indeterminate amount in future years to reimburse local governments for 50% of the enterprise zone property tax credits claimed in newly designated TOD zones. General fund, Transportation Trust Fund, and Higher Education Investment Fund revenues will decrease in future years as businesses claim enterprise zone income and corporate tax credits. Local property tax revenues will decrease commensurately due to the property tax credit. Local revenues from development impact fees and excise taxes will also be delayed from the start of development until project completion and occupancy, though specific statewide dollar estimates are indeterminate.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is directly tasked with reviewing and concurring with local jurisdictions' adequate parking studies within 45 days, approving transit-oriented development plans on state-owned transportation land contiguous to rail transit stations, and managing transit-oriented development policies. In addition, leases of MDOT property in enterprise zones receive specific exemptions under the bill.

The bill explicitly amends MEDCO's statute under the Strategic Infrastructure Revolving Loan Program, requiring MEDCO to prioritize projects that redevelop government-owned land contiguous to rail transit stations.

Commerce administers Maryland's Enterprise Zone program. The bill establishes that qualifying transit-oriented developments are automatically designated or eligible to be designated as enterprise zones outside of the statutory limit on annual designations by the Secretary of Commerce.

The Comptroller administers state income tax filings and tax credits; designating additional areas as enterprise zones reduces state income and corporate tax revenues through enterprise zone income tax credits.

MDP guides statewide land use planning and coordinates the Sustainable Growth Subcabinet, which designates TODs and is designated under the bill to receive formal written opt-out elections from local governments regarding enterprise zone status.
This is an Administration bill advancing the Governor's strategic priorities regarding housing production, transit-oriented development, and executive initiatives on state-owned land.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 895, the Protection From Predatory Pricing Act, prohibits food retailers (operating establishments of at least 15,000 square feet) and third-party delivery service providers from using dynamic pricing or personal data to set higher prices on tax-exempt food for specific consumers. It also prohibits using protected class data to offer, advertise, or sell consumer goods or services if doing so denies or withholds advantages or accommodations accorded to others. Violations are designated as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, subject to enforcement by the Consumer Protection Division following a 45-day notice-and-cure period, without providing a private right of action.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
qa_results.stakeholders: Food retailers with establishments of at least 15,000 square feet, third-party food delivery service providers, merchants, and Maryland grocery consumers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase at least minimally beginning in FY 2027 for the Office of the Attorney General (OAG) to obtain contractual training and technical expertise to enforce the bill's provisions. While OAG estimated personnel costs of approximately $325,000 annually for two positions, the Department of Legislative Services determined that initial staffing needs are unclear and costs will initially be minimal. State revenues and local government finances are not expected to be materially impacted by existing penalty provisions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division is the primary enforcement agency for the bill, tasked with issuing notices of violation, administering the 45-day right-to-cure process, and prosecuting unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, incurring fiscal expenditures for specialized staff and technical expertise.
This is an Administration bill proposed by request of the Governor to advance executive policy priorities protecting consumers against predatory pricing and algorithmic price discrimination.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the National Guard State Active Duty Mobilization Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund administered by the Office of the Adjutant General in the Military Department to cover costs for personnel and equipment during State active duty mobilizations ordered by the Governor.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Adjutant General within the Military Department
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the Maryland National Guard, the Military Department, and Maryland residents affected by emergencies requiring National Guard response.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures that would occur anyway are accelerated to capitalize the fund, likely with at least $1.0 million in FY 2027, resulting in a corresponding increase in special fund revenues. Special fund expenditures will increase starting in FY 2027 depending on mobilizations. General fund expenditures will also accelerate as needed for ongoing replenishments. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the National Guard State Active Duty Mobilization Fund within the Office of the Adjutant General and designates the Adjutant General as the administrator of the fund.
The fund is specifically created to cover personnel and equipment expenses supporting Maryland National Guard operations and deployments during State active duty mobilizations.
The statute explicitly requires the State Treasurer to hold the newly established fund separately and invest its moneys in the same manner as other state funds.
The statute explicitly requires the Comptroller of Maryland to account for the newly established special fund.
The fund pays for State active duty mobilizations ordered by the Governor in the role of commander-in-chief during state emergencies and crises.
The fund relies on state budget appropriations, budget amendments, and ongoing replenishment to capitalize and maintain operational effectiveness, involving DBM's budget supervision.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Delivering Economic Competitiveness and Advancing Development Efforts (DECADE) Act reorganizes and expands several Maryland economic development financing and incentive programs. Among its provisions, it redesignates the Economic Development Opportunities Program Account as the Strategic Closing Fund under the Department of Commerce; consolidates MSBDFA financing programs under a single fund and reallocates $5.0 million in video lottery terminal revenues to it; transfers the Regional Institution Strategic Enterprise (RISE) Zone and Build Our Future Grant programs to the Maryland Economic Development Corporation (MEDCO); extends multiple tax credits (including Job Creation, Research and Development, and Employer Security Clearance Costs); and exempts certain intercompany IT and digital goods transactions between affiliated entities from the state sales and use tax.
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland businesses (particularly small, minority-, and women-owned enterprises), technology and research and development firms, film production entities, defense and security contractors, higher education institutions, and local governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: In FY 2027, State general fund and special fund revenues decrease by $35.5 million and $1.8 million, respectively (net reduction of $37.3 million), due to sales and use tax exemptions on affiliated group IT services and digital goods. From FY 2028 to FY 2031, total net negative State fiscal impacts range between $71.8 million and $79.5 million annually due to ongoing sales tax revenue losses, extensions of the Job Creation and R&D tax credits, and increased general fund expenditures to support the Build Our Future Grant Program and backfill Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund revenues. Local governments experience minor reductions in highway user revenues and potential impacts on local property tax revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Primary implementing agency for the DECADE Act. The bill restructures, renames, and enhances numerous Commerce-administered economic development funds and tax credits, including establishing the Strategic Closing Fund, establishing the Maryland Small Business Development Financing Fund, modifying the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Businesses Account, and altering multiple tax credit programs (Job Creation, R&D, Film Production, and SCIF). It also transfers the RISE Zone and Build Our Future Grant programs to MEDCO.

MEDCO is the direct recipient of programs transferred from Commerce under the bill, specifically assuming full administrative and grant-making authority over the Regional Institution Strategic Enterprise (RISE) Zone Program and the Build Our Future Grant Program, as well as managing their associated funds and concierges.

Administers significant tax provisions altered by the bill, including a major sales and use tax exemption for certain related-party information technology services and digital products resulting in substantial general and special fund revenue reductions. The Comptroller also accounts for newly structured special funds, administers income tax credits, and is mandated to report on tracking R&D tax credit carryforwards.

Required by statute under the bill to hold, invest, and reinvest moneys and credit earnings for several special nonlapsing funds, including the Strategic Closing Fund, the Maryland Small Business Development Financing Fund, the Regional Institution Strategic Enterprise Zone Fund, and the Build Our Future Grant Fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Responsible for the regulation and oversight of video lottery terminal (VLT) proceeds, which the bill reallocates by mandating that $5,000,000 of proceeds be distributed to the Maryland Small Business Development Financing Fund, with the remainder distributed to the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Businesses Account.

Oversees the State budget, state revenues, and the State Reserve Fund, which includes the renamed Strategic Closing Fund (formerly the Economic Development Opportunities Program Account). DBM manages budget amendments and fiscal allocations impacted by the bill.

Incurs a notable fiscal impact because extensions and modifications to corporate income tax credits (Job Creation, R&D, SCIF, and Film Production) directly reduce corporate income tax distributions to the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) and local highway user revenue capital grants.

The bill impacts TEDCO by redirecting recoveries of investments and grant repayments previously funded by transfers from MSBDFA funds into the Enterprise Fund (including investments in MMG Ventures LLP) into the newly created Maryland Small Business Development Financing Fund, and interfaces with RISE zone programs.

HB 898 is an Administration priority bill ('DECADE Act') requiring executive budget appropriations for the Strategic Closing Fund, processing transfers via budget amendment subject to LPC review, and receiving mandated periodic reports on economic development programs.

USM institutions serve as eligible 'qualified institutions' partnering in RISE zones and are eligible recipients of grants under the Build Our Future Grant Program (capped at up to 50% of annual fund appropriations). Additionally, Higher Education Investment Fund revenues are impacted by corporate tax credit provisions.

As a public university, Morgan State qualifies as an eligible institution under the RISE Zone Program and is eligible to apply for and receive infrastructure grants under the Build Our Future Grant Program.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill prohibits agents of private home detention monitoring agencies, courthouse employees, and correctional facility employees from soliciting business, enticing individuals to use a specific agency, or distributing, displaying, or wearing advertising materials on the grounds of a courthouse or correctional facility. Violators face misdemeanor penalties, including fines up to $2,500 for a first offense and up to $5,000 for subsequent offenses, alongside mandatory license suspensions and referrals to the state for licensed entities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Private home detention monitoring agencies and their agents, courthouse staff, correctional facility staff, and individuals involved in pretrial or post-conviction proceedings requiring home detention monitoring.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services can implement the bill with existing resources. The misdemeanor penalty provisions are not anticipated to have a meaningful effect on State general fund revenues or local revenues, and local expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is the regulatory body that licenses private home detention monitoring agencies (PHDMAs), operates State correctional facilities, and is explicitly designated in the bill to receive referrals of convicted licensees for appropriate licensing or disciplinary action.
The bill was requested by the Maryland Judicial Conference and directly regulates conduct occurring on courthouse grounds and applies prohibitions specifically to courthouse employees.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits law enforcement agencies from assigning law enforcement officers to non-administrative duties unless issued compliant protective body armor. Requires body armor to conform to National Institute of Justice standards and be replaced before manufacturer expiration dates, establishing reporting procedures to the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission and penalizing noncompliant agencies through withheld grant funds from the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission and the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
qa_results.stakeholders: Law enforcement agencies, Maryland law enforcement officers, Maryland Department of Health Secured Transportation and Investigation Unit officers, and the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $55,300 in FY 2027 for the Maryland Department of Health to purchase 45 protective body armor vests for its Secured Transportation and Investigation Unit. Future replacements will increase expenditures after the initial five-year period. Other State and local law enforcement agencies can implement the requirements with existing budgeted resources. Noncompliant agencies risk having certain State grant funds withheld by the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly tasks GOCPP with receiving noncompliance notifications from the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission, withholding grant funds from noncompliant law enforcement agencies, and barring grant disbursements under specified conditions.

MDH is directly fiscally impacted by the bill, requiring an estimated $55,300 general fund expenditure in FY 2027 to purchase 45 sets of protective body armor for officers in its Secured Transportation and Investigation Unit (STIU).

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS administratively houses the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC), which is mandated to receive notices of expired body armor from law enforcement agencies and notify GOCPP. DPSCS's Division of Parole and Probation is also associated with state body armor programs.
As the primary state law enforcement agency, MSP is directly subject to the bill's requirements regarding officer body armor standards, replacement schedules, and reporting obligations.
DNR operates the Maryland Natural Resources Police and is subject to the bill's body armor standards, equipment replacement timeline, and reporting mandates.
MDTA maintains its own dedicated, sworn police force and is subject to the bill's body armor standards and replacement requirements.
MDOT oversees modal administrations with law enforcement units (such as MTA and MDTA police) that must comply with the protective body armor and replacement standards.
The Comptroller employs sworn enforcement officers who fall under law enforcement agency definitions and are subject to the bill's body armor requirements.
USM institutions employ campus police forces that are classified as law enforcement agencies and must comply with the body armor requirements and replacement schedules.
Morgan State University operates its own campus police department and must ensure its officers are outfitted with protective body armor compliant with the bill's standards.
The Department of Labor was surveyed regarding its regulatory and enforcement personnel to ensure compliance with the bill's law enforcement officer standards.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a licensee at Laurel Park to conduct live racing of Arabian breed horses under specified conditions, including limits on the number of races, separate purse funding, and approval by the State Racing Commission.
qa_results.stakeholders: Laurel Park licensees, Arabian breed horse owners, trainers, jockeys, and racing patrons.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no direct effect on State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor oversees the State Racing Commission, which regulates horse racing in Maryland and must review and approve the live racing of Arabian breed horses authorized under this bill at Laurel Park.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the membership of the Worcester County Board of License Commissioners from three to five members appointed by the Governor with Senate advice and consent, establishes staggered four-year terms, and sets initial terms for the two new members beginning July 1, 2026.
qa_results.stakeholders: Worcester County Board of License Commissioners, board appointees, and Worcester County alcoholic beverage licensees and residents.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Worcester County expenditures increase by $4,200 annually beginning in fiscal year 2027 to cover the $2,100 annual salaries for the two new board members. Worcester County revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 914 requires the Governor to appoint two additional members to the Worcester County Board of License Commissioners, expanding the board from three to five members.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments to local boards and commissions, including the newly created seats on the Worcester County Board of License Commissioners.
The Secretary of State serves as the depository for statements of charges and findings should the Governor remove any member of the board from office.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Practical Applications of Real Estate Appraisal (PAREA) Grant Program within the Maryland Higher Education Commission to award grants to minorities living in historically redlined neighborhoods and underrepresented communities who are pursuing PAREA, aiming to diversify the appraisal profession and help close appraisal gaps.
qa_results.stakeholders: Minorities residing in historically redlined neighborhoods and underrepresented communities who are pursuing real estate appraisal careers via PAREA, as well as property owners and communities affected by appraisal gaps.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase beginning in FY 2027. One-time IT programming costs for grant administration are estimated at $50,000 in FY 2027. Grant expenditures depend on appropriations and program parameters; illustratively, funding 10 participants annually would cost approximately $88,000 per year (for course costs and licensing/registry fees), bringing estimated FY 2027 general fund expenditures to $138,000. Maryland Department of Labor special fund revenues may increase minimally beginning in FY 2028 from licensing fees ($250 per licensee). There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly establishes the Practical Applications of Real Estate Appraisal (PAREA) Grant Program within MHEC and requires MHEC to administer the program, resulting in operational and grant expenditure impacts.
MHEC is tasked with establishing, implementing, and administering the PAREA Grant Program to provide grants to prospective real estate appraisers.

The Maryland Department of Labor houses the State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors, which oversees PAREA approval and appraiser licensing, and may see a minimal increase in special fund licensing revenues.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 925 establishes restrictions and monitoring requirements on the land application of sewage sludge containing per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS). Beginning October 1, 2028, it prohibits applying sewage sludge with 50 parts per billion (ppb) or more of regulated PFAS to agricultural or marginal land, and limits application for sludge between 25 and 50 ppb subject to commingling limits, source tracking studies, and mitigation plans. It also authorizes pretreatment standards, monitoring protocols, and fee structures for industrial users discharging PFAS.
qa_results.stakeholders: Sewage sludge generators, publicly owned treatment works and wastewater treatment plant operators, industrial wastewater dischargers, farmers and agricultural landowners, and utility ratepayers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $248,100 in FY 2027, increasing to $331,800 by FY 2031 for the Maryland Department of the Environment to hire three staff members for regulatory oversight, technical assistance, and monitoring. Expenditures may partially be offset if permit fees are raised under the Clean Water Fund. Local government expenditures could increase significantly starting in FY 2029 for wastewater treatment plants with PFAS levels exceeding 25 ppb (such as WSSC, which estimates annual sludge management cost increases of $4.1 million to $8.2 million and potential capital upgrade costs of up to $200 million). Local jurisdictions and pretreatment authorities may offset costs through new or increased fees and rates on industrial dischargers.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) is the primary regulatory agency responsible for administering and enforcing the bill, including establishing monitoring protocols for PFAS in sewage sludge, reviewing and approving mitigation plans, developing pretreatment standards and industrial user controls, and issuing guidance and regulations.

MES is explicitly defined by statute as a sewage sludge generator and operates approximately 90 wastewater treatment plants across Maryland. The bill impacts MES's testing protocols and operational sludge management, potentially increasing its nonbudgeted expenditures and fee revenues.

Under Maryland law cited in the bill, MDE may not adopt regulations concerning the land application of sewage sludge without the approval of the Department of Agriculture, which also sets nutrient requirement recommendations for agricultural land application.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the County Commissioners of Carroll County to borrow up to $27 million through the issuance and sale of general obligation bonds to finance the acquisition, construction, improvement, or development of various public facilities, including public works, schools, water and sewer infrastructure, and agricultural land preservation, as well as to fund loans to volunteer fire departments for emergency-related equipment and facilities.
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents, taxpayers, students, and volunteer fire departments in Carroll County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: Carroll County revenues increase by up to $27.0 million from bond proceeds, while county debt service expenditures increase by an estimated $2.0 million annually over a 20-year maturity period based on a 3.96% interest rate.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly exempts the bonds, refunding bonds, interest, and derived income from all State and local taxation, which falls under the tax administration and revenue enforcement purview of the Comptroller of Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Carroll County Office of Permits and Inspections to deny the issuance or renewal of a commercial license or permit if the applicant has unpaid personal property taxes, unless the applicant provides evidence that the tax amount is being disputed, and allows issuance or renewal upon proof of payment.
qa_results.responsible_party: Carroll County Office of Permits and Inspections
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial license and permit applicants and businesses in Carroll County with unpaid personal property taxes, as well as Carroll County government.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no State fiscal effect and does not materially affect Carroll County operations or finances. The small business effect is minimal.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill modifies the sales and use tax provisions concerning multiple points of use (MPU) certificates for digital codes, digital products, and taxable data and IT services. It establishes an authorization process through the Comptroller for buyers to issue MPU certificates valid for at least two years, sets rules for certificate generation, renewal, and revocation, relieves vendors from collecting sales and use tax when presented with a valid certificate, and establishes verification and notification requirements.
qa_results.stakeholders: Buyers and vendors of digital codes, digital products, and taxable IT and data services in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $183,400 in FY 2027 (including $75,000 for one-time computer programming and ongoing costs for two financial compliance auditors), rising to $207,000 by FY 2031. General fund revenues may experience an indeterminate decrease due to reduced tax compliance capacity and risk of fraudulent MPU certificates. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary agency responsible for administering the state's sales and use tax laws. Under HB 933, the Comptroller must review, authorize, renew, deny, and revoke buyers' authority to issue multiple points of use (MPU) certificates, manage notifications to vendors, and provide the online application system for certificate generation. The bill has an explicit fiscal impact on the agency, requiring $183,400 in FY 2027 for two financial compliance auditors and computer programming updates.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the membership of the Washington County Salary Study Commission by replacing the representative from the Cumberland Valley Associated Builders and Contractors, Inc. with a representative from the Washington County Home Builders Association, Inc.
qa_results.stakeholders: Washington County Home Builders Association, Inc., Cumberland Valley Associated Builders and Contractors, Inc., Washington County Salary Study Commission, and Washington County government officials
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not affect State operations or finances and does not materially affect Washington County operations or finances.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires Montgomery County Public Schools (MCPS) to track and publish data on food procured for school meals from certified local farms and certified Chesapeake invasive species providers during the 2026–2027 school year. Using that baseline, MCPS must set procurement target increases for specified school years through the 2036–2037 school year and establish a plan to meet those targets in coordination with the Montgomery County Office of Food Systems Resilience and public input.
qa_results.responsible_party: Montgomery County Public Schools (in coordination with the Montgomery County Office of Food Systems Resilience)
qa_results.stakeholders: Montgomery County Public Schools, MCPS students and families, Maryland certified local farms, and certified Chesapeake invasive species seafood dealers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. MCPS local expenditures will increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in fiscal 2027 due to one-time information technology costs for purchase tracking and ongoing personnel costs for a full-time coordinator. MCPS food expenditures will also likely increase to the extent that certified local and invasive species food products cost more than noncertified alternatives.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill relies on certification standards established under the Certified Local Farm and Fish Program and intersects with the Jane Lawton Farm-to-School Program, both of which are administered by the Maryland Department of Agriculture.

The bill amends the Education Article to impose local food procurement tracking and target-setting mandates on a local school system (Montgomery County Public Schools), which operates under the broader oversight of the Maryland State Department of Education.

The bill references statutory definitions of certified Chesapeake invasive species providers who must be licensed seafood dealers under the Natural Resources Article overseen by the Department of Natural Resources.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill extends the timeframe to complete and file a certificate of birth—and for attending medical providers to submit required birth and medical information—from 5 calendar days to 12 calendar days after birth. Additionally, it permits filing within 10 days if a parent notifies the individual responsible for filing on a form provided by the Secretary of Health no later than 5 days after the birth occurs.
qa_results.stakeholders: Parents of newborn children, healthcare institutions, attending physicians, nurse midwives, physician assistants, nurse practitioners, and other clinicians responsible for filing birth certificates.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state or local fiscal impact; the changes are procedural in nature and do not directly affect governmental revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH), through the Secretary of Health and the Vital Statistics Administration, is responsible for vital records, including establishing the forms and receiving the filing of birth certificates altered by this bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) to notify and consult with the relevant local health department within 24 hours of initiating an investigation into a nursing home complaint alleging actual harm or immediate jeopardy. Additionally, it establishes the Health Care Quality Improvement Initiative and a temporary task force staffed by MDH to evaluate and recommend improvements to the safety, quality of care, workforce retention, and oversight of nursing homes and assisted living programs.
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents and families of individuals in nursing homes and assisted living facilities, facility staff and healthcare workers, long-term care operators, and local health departments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no significant fiscal impact on the State or local governments. Both the Maryland Department of Health and local health departments can handle the coordination, notification, and task force staffing requirements using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill. It must notify and coordinate with local health departments when initiating nursing home investigations, provide staff support for the new Health Care Quality Improvement Initiative task force, designate the task force chair, and have multiple departmental leaders (including the Secretary, Deputy Secretaries, and the Executive Director of the Office of Health Care Quality) serve on the task force.

The Executive Director of MHCC is designated as a member of the task force, and the task force is explicitly required to collaborate with MHCC regarding the use and sharing of available data and expertise for oversight, monitoring, and transparency of nursing homes and assisted living programs.

The Secretary of Aging is a statutorily appointed member of the task force established to evaluate quality of care, oversight, and affordability in nursing homes and assisted living facilities, which align directly with the department's core advocacy for older adults.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a temporary task force to carry out the Health Care Quality Improvement Initiative through June 30, 2029, charged with studying care quality, workforce issues, and oversight in nursing homes and assisted living programs.
The Secretary of Human Services is designated as a statutory member of the task force established to carry out the Health Care Quality Improvement Initiative.
The Attorney General (or their designee) is designated as a member of the task force established to evaluate nursing home and assisted living facility quality and oversight.
The task force is required to submit preliminary and final findings and recommendations to the Governor by December 1, 2027, and December 1, 2028, respectively.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the Invasive Blue Catfish Pilot Program from June 30, 2026, through June 30, 2030, adds the Blue Catfish Gill Net Program to the pilot program, and modifies annual reporting requirements to the General Assembly.
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial and for-hire fishers harvesting blue catfish, seafood small businesses, and the Invasive Catfish Advisory Committee.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected, as the Department of Natural Resources can implement the pilot program extensions and modifications with existing budgeted resources, and revenues are unaffected. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) with implementing and extending the Invasive Blue Catfish Pilot Program through 2030, adding the Blue Catfish Gill Net Program, and submitting annual reports to legislative committees.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifies that the Invasive Blue Catfish Pilot Program must be established and carried out by DNR in coordination with the Invasive Catfish Advisory Committee.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the requirement that printed deeds or other real property instruments offered for recordation include specific margin sizes, and requires circuit court clerks to date each change or correction made to information in the general alphabetical index on the specific horizontal line where the change is made.
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals and entities recording real estate instruments, title companies, property owners, and circuit court land record offices.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the procedural and formatting requirements for recording deeds and requires clerks of the circuit courts—supported administratively and operationally by the Administrative Office of the Courts—to date changes or corrections in the general alphabetical index of land records.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Governor, subject to approval by the Board of Public Works, to transfer funds from the Revenue Stabilization Account (Rainy Day Fund) to the State Disaster Recovery Fund, provided the transfer does not reduce the Rainy Day Fund balance below 5% of estimated General Fund revenues for that fiscal year.
qa_results.responsible_party: The Governor and the Board of Public Works
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland local governments, state agencies, and communities impacted by natural disasters or emergencies that do not receive federal disaster declarations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is authorizing in nature and has no direct fiscal impact on state or local finances. If a transfer occurs, special fund revenues for the State Disaster Recovery Fund will increase, while the Rainy Day Fund may experience minimal interest revenue losses. If the Rainy Day Fund balance drops below 7.5% of general fund revenues following a transfer, general fund expenditures would increase in subsequent years by at least $50.0 million annually until restored. Local governments may benefit from additional disaster relief aid.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly authorizes the Governor to transfer funds from the Revenue Stabilization Account to the State Disaster Recovery Fund, subject to approval by the Board of Public Works.
The bill explicitly requires the approval of the Board of Public Works before the Governor may transfer funds from the Revenue Stabilization Account to the State Disaster Recovery Fund.

The Maryland Department of Emergency Management administers the State Disaster Recovery Fund, which directly receives the transferred funds to support disaster recovery efforts and potential administrative staffing.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for state budget oversight, fiscal planning, and managing reserve accounts such as the Revenue Stabilization Account and Catastrophic Event Account.
The Comptroller serves as a member of the Board of Public Works, which must approve fund transfers under the bill, and acts as the state's chief financial officer overseeing state accounting.
The State Treasurer sits on the Board of Public Works, which is required to approve the transfers, and serves as custodian of state funds, overseeing deposits, fund balances, and investments.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to conduct a study on buildings in Maryland that are more than 40 years old and contain condominiums—including examining unit counts, owner demographics, and reserve study and funding data—and report findings to the General Assembly by December 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Condominium unit owners and condominium governing bodies in buildings that are more than 40 years old.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $75,000 in FY 2027 only for contractual services to conduct the required study. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Department of Housing and Community Development to conduct a study on Maryland condominium buildings that are more than 40 years old and report its findings to the General Assembly by December 1, 2026, resulting in an estimated fiscal impact of $75,000 for contractual services in FY 2027.

The Secretary of State is responsible for the registration and oversight of condominiums in Maryland, making the study of condominium buildings and reserve funds relevant to its regulatory purview and records.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 957 requires each local school system in Maryland to designate a cybersecurity point of contact, comply with the State minimum cybersecurity standards established by the Department of Information Technology (DoIT) beginning in 2027, conduct biennial cybersecurity maturity assessments, and certify compliance every two years. It also tasks DoIT's Office of Security Management with annually reviewing and updating the cybersecurity standards and advising local school systems upon request on compliance, maturity assessments, and remediation efforts.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Information Technology (specifically the Office of Security Management) and local school systems
qa_results.stakeholders: Local school systems, county boards of education, public school students and staff, and local school system information technology personnel
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations can handle the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources, with no effect on State revenues. Local school system expenditures increase beginning in fiscal 2027 to meet minimum cybersecurity standards, conduct biennial assessments, and implement remediation (for example, Prince George's County Public Schools estimates upgrades exceeding $2.0 million). Local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Department of Information Technology and its Office of Security Management with establishing, annually reviewing, and updating the State minimum cybersecurity standards. Additionally, DoIT is required to receive compliance certifications and point-of-contact notifications from local school systems and to provide advisory support regarding cybersecurity assessments and remediation.

The bill amends the Education Article to mandate that all local school systems comply with state cybersecurity standards, designate points of contact, and perform biennial maturity assessments, which directly impacts the operations and administration of the public school systems overseen by MSDE.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the restrictions on granting letters of administration in probate to noncitizens, allowing an individual who is not a U.S. citizen or permanent resident to serve as a personal representative of a decedent's estate if the individual is domiciled in the United States and is the decedent's spouse, ancestor, descendant, or sibling.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Registers of Wills and Orphans' Courts
qa_results.stakeholders: Noncitizens and non-permanent residents domiciled in the United States who are close relatives (spouses, ancestors, descendants, or siblings) of a decedent, as well as probate courts and estate beneficiaries.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Department of Legislative Services, the bill does not directly affect State finances and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 963 directly alters the statutory criteria under which the Register of Wills may grant letters of administration to noncitizen personal representatives during estate probate proceedings.

The Administrative Office of the Courts provides administrative and legal support to the judicial branch, including the Orphans' Courts which adjudicate probate matters and issue letters of administration in judicial probate.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires owners or operators of retail electric vehicle charging equipment to display contact information for the responsible local party and mandates that retail electricity sold as vehicle fuel be measured and billed strictly in kilowatt-hours dispensed during the charging session. It also permits charging operators to assess separate itemized service fees based on time or fixed amounts.
qa_results.stakeholders: Electric vehicle drivers, electric vehicle charging station owners and operators, and retail electricity sellers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill codifies existing regulatory standards and practices in part and is not expected to have a direct, material fiscal impact on State or local government revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends Title 11 (Weights and Measures) of the Agriculture Article. The Department of Agriculture's Weights and Measures Program is the primary regulatory authority responsible for inspecting, testing, and certifying commercial weighing and measuring devices, including EV charging equipment.

The Public Service Commission regulates electric companies and retail electricity markets across the state. The statutory standards established for the retail dispensing and per-kilowatt-hour pricing of electricity as vehicle fuel intersect with utility and energy resale regulatory oversight.

The Maryland Energy Administration coordinates state clean transportation and electric vehicle infrastructure policies and programs, which are directly informed by retail EV charging and measurement standards.

The Department of General Services manages state-owned facilities, vehicle fleets, and sustainability initiatives, which include state-owned or operated EV charging stations that may dispense vehicle fuel.

The Comptroller regulates motor fuel and sales taxes in the state; while provisions directing the Comptroller to set minimum prices were amended out, the office provided input regarding retail vehicle fuel regulation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Fair and Agricultural Education Promise Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund administered by the Comptroller to support agricultural education. The bill requires a $200,000 annual general fund appropriation to provide annual grants of $100,000 each to the Maryland Agricultural Education Foundation and the Maryland FFA Association, while repealing an existing $75,000 annual distribution from the State horse racing special fund to the foundation.
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Agricultural Education Foundation, Maryland FFA Association, agricultural students and educators, and horse racing special fund grantees.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2028, general fund expenditures increase by $200,000 annually to fund the mandated appropriation, with corresponding increases in special fund revenues and expenditures. Horse racing special fund revenues effectively increase by $75,000 annually beginning in FY 2027 due to the repeal of a mandated distribution, resulting in a net State fiscal impact of +$75,000 in FY 2027 and -$125,000 annually in FY 2028 through FY 2031. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly designates the Comptroller as the administrator of the Maryland Fair and Agricultural Education Promise Fund, tasking the office with accounting for the fund and disbursing the annual mandated grants to the Maryland Agricultural Education Foundation and the Maryland FFA Association.
The bill requires the State Treasurer to hold the newly established fund separately, manage its investments, and exempt its interest earnings from accruing to the General Fund.

The fund is codified under the Agriculture Article to promote statewide agricultural education and fairs, impacting key agricultural youth and educational programs central to the department's core mission.
The bill establishes a statutory mandate requiring the Governor to include an appropriation of $200,000 to the fund in the annual State budget bill.
As the agency responsible for preparing and executing the annual State budget, DBM must accommodate and track the mandated $200,000 general fund appropriation to the new special fund.

The bill modifies the allocation of the horse racing Special Fund under the Business Regulation Article (which falls under the Maryland Racing Commission within MD Labor) by eliminating the $75,000 statutory grant to the Maryland Agricultural Education Foundation.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 975 prohibits licensed massage therapists, registered massage practitioners, and third parties acting on their behalf from advertising massage therapy services that state, imply, or suggest sexual, escort, or prostitution services are available, or placing ads on websites known for advertising such services. The bill requires advertisements to include the practitioner's licensed full name and license or registration number, sets daily violation penalties for noncompliant online ads, requires existing noncompliant billboards or signs to be removed by May 1, 2027, and directs the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners to adopt regulations defining prohibited content and reporting procedures.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed massage therapists, registered massage practitioners, massage therapy businesses, and consumers of massage therapy services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not significantly impacted; the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners can adopt the required regulations using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local government fiscal impact. Small business impacts are minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly regulates the practice and advertising standards of massage therapy under the Health Occupations Article, requiring the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners (housed within the Maryland Department of Health) to adopt regulations, define prohibited content, and handle reporting of violations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes Kanaiyah's Law, requiring the Department of Human Services to establish and maintain a Guardianship Assistance Program providing monetary and medical assistance to eligible guardians of minor children, and creates the State Foster Youth Ombudsman within the department to investigate complaints, advocate for youth in out-of-home care, and provide legal expertise on child welfare matters.
qa_results.stakeholders: Foster youth and children in out-of-home placement, legal guardians, relative caregivers, adoptive parents, and local departments of social services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $37,500 in FY 2028 and $50,000 annually thereafter, assuming DHS repurposes an existing vacant position at a higher grade for the ombudsman (or by $120,000 in FY 2028 and at least $154,000 annually if a new position must be created). State revenues and local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 980 directly tasks the Secretary of Human Services and the Department of Human Services (DHS) with establishing and maintaining the Guardianship Assistance Program, adopting implementing regulations, and housing the newly created State Foster Youth Ombudsman.

The bill creates the State Foster Youth Ombudsman position within the State Personnel Management System, requiring DBM oversight regarding personnel classification, position repurposing (PIN allocation), and ongoing state budget appropriations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the hours of sale for Class HC (health club) 6-day and 7-day beer and wine license holders in Harford County, allowing them to sell beer and wine for on-premises consumption until 11:00 p.m. instead of 9:00 p.m.
qa_results.responsible_party: Harford County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Class HC (health club) beer and wine license holders in Harford County and their members or patrons.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact and does not materially affect Harford County finances or operations. Any impact on small businesses is anticipated to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is responsible for regulating the alcohol industry and collecting state sales and excise taxes on alcoholic beverages. While this legislation specifically alters the local hours of sale for Class HC beer and wine licenses administered by the Harford County Board of License Commissioners, it touches upon the regulation of alcoholic beverages in the state.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Don't You Worry (Wurie) Act requires sellers of travel services and independent agents to annually submit proof of at least $1,000,000 in professional liability and errors and omissions insurance to the Maryland Department of Labor and pay an annual filing fee. The bill also establishes the Sellers of Travel Services Registration Fund to administer and enforce these regulations.
qa_results.stakeholders: Sellers of travel services, independent travel agents, and consumers purchasing travel services in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues increase by at least $99,000 in FY 2027 and approximately $111,400 annually thereafter from annual filing fees ($300 initial fee). State expenditures increase by $106,513 in FY 2027 ($101,000 special funds and $5,513 general funds) to hire one executive director and cover start-up costs, with ongoing special fund expenditures ranging between $95,400 and $109,000 in future years. General fund revenues increase minimally from interest earnings. There is no material local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MD Labor is the primary implementing agency responsible for regulating sellers of travel services and independent agents, collecting annual filings and insurance verifications, setting fees, enforcing compliance, and administering the newly established Sellers of Travel Services Registration Fund.

The bill statutorily requires the Department of Labor to pay all collected registration and filing fees to the Comptroller, who is directed to distribute those revenues into the Sellers of Travel Services Registration Fund.

The bill provides that the newly created special fund is subject to audit under State Government Article § 2-1220, and the fiscal note identifies that OLA will incorporate the fund into its regular periodic audits of MD Labor.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 996 updates several provisions governing Maryland corporations and partnerships. It requires the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) to notify filers of rejected charter documents and retroactively accept corrected filings submitted within 30 days. It also permits boards of registered open-end investment companies to act without a meeting via majority consent under certain conditions, clarifies corporate actions that can be taken under bankruptcy court orders without stockholder approval, repeals misdemeanor criminal fines for officers and agents of unregistered foreign corporations, and clarifies rules governing limited partnership agreements and amendments.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Corporations, foreign corporations doing business in Maryland, corporate officers and directors, open-end investment companies, limited partnerships and partners, bankruptcy trustees, and business filers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: SDAT can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State revenues, and it does not affect local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends provisions governing when a foreign corporation may maintain a lawsuit in Maryland State courts and repeals a misdemeanor penalty for officers and agents transacting business for an unregistered foreign corporation. The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the State's judicial branch and was consulted as an information source for the bill's fiscal note.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to issue a Class 7 micro-brewery license to certain Class B-D-7 license holders in the 46th district, establish a standard memorandum of understanding (MOU) template for license applicants and neighborhood associations, approve specified license transfers and extensions, and grant a seven-day sales privilege to certain Class D licensees upon payment of a one-time fee. It also temporarily permits a licensed premises on West Pratt Street to allow consumption of donated alcohol during nonprofit rental events and requires the board to adopt tiered penalties for violations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license holders and applicants in Baltimore City (specifically in the 40th and 46th districts), local neighborhood associations, and nonprofit organizations holding events at licensed venues.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no State fiscal impact. Baltimore City finances and operations are not expected to be materially affected; however, the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners receives a one-time fee of $15,000 from each Class D licensee granted a 7-day sales privilege, which must be used for MOU enforcement.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill regulates alcoholic beverage licenses, brewery permissions, and tax-remitted alcohol donations in Baltimore City. The Comptroller serves as the state's principal tax collector and oversees alcohol industry taxation and regulation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes holders of a Class 9 limited distillery license to manufacture, rectify, or bottle more than one brand of alcoholic beverage and allows them to produce up to 31,000 gallons per calendar year for another brand or entity.
qa_results.stakeholders: Class 9 limited distillery license holders, other distillery businesses contracting production, and consumers of craft distilled spirits
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. It is projected to have a meaningful positive impact on small business Class 9 distilleries by enabling revenue growth through contract distilling and multibrand retail sales.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends provisions regarding Class 9 limited distillery licenses, authorizing license holders to produce multiple brands and manufacture up to 31,000 gallons of product for other entities. According to the agency summary, the Comptroller regulates the alcohol industry and is responsible for administering and collecting state taxes, including excise and sales taxes related to alcoholic beverage production and retail sales.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 1001 grants the State Administrator of Elections, Deputy State Administrator, and local election directors the authority to keep the peace and order arrests at polling places, requiring on-duty police officers to obey their orders. The bill also updates rules regarding challengers, watchers, and canvass observers by extending accredited challenger and watcher access to early voting centers, prohibiting challengers and watchers from physically handling voting equipment, requiring copies of accreditation certificates to be submitted in advance to local election boards, and updating who may designate challengers, watchers, and observers (including political committees and independent expenditure entities).
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections (including the State Administrator and Deputy State Administrator) and local boards of elections (including local election directors)
qa_results.stakeholders: Registered Maryland voters, election judges and election staff, candidates, political parties, political committees, independent political expenditure filers, accredited and nonaccredited election challengers and watchers, canvass observers, and law enforcement officers assigned to polling places.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill has no State fiscal impact and is not expected to directly affect local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Election Law Article to grant specific peace-keeping, operational, and arrest-ordering authority to the State Administrator, Deputy State Administrator, and local election directors at polling places, early voting centers, and counting centers. The State Board of Elections oversees election administration and is tasked with prescribing required forms for accredited challengers and watchers.

The bill requires police officers on duty at polling places to obey orders from the State Administrator, Deputy State Administrator, or local election directors to keep the peace and execute arrests, providing statutory protection as if executing a valid arrest warrant.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits nursing facilities from involuntarily transferring or discharging a resident to temporary housing such as a hotel or shelter, and requires confirmation of acceptance from the receiving facility before any transfer occurs. It also establishes new notice and timeline requirements for involuntary discharges and transfers, regulates appeal procedures, and expands the requirements of post-discharge care plans.
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents of nursing facilities and comprehensive/extended care facilities, their families and representatives, and nursing facility operators and staff.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operational requirements can be handled with existing budgeted resources, with no impact on state revenues. There is no local government fiscal impact, and the impact on small business nursing facilities is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary regulatory and implementing agency for nursing facilities. The bill requires the Department to update the standardized notice form for involuntary transfers or discharges, receive copies of all such notices, and adopt regulations governing safe and sustainable post-discharge environments.

The Department of Aging oversees the statewide Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program, which advocates for facility residents. The bill requires nursing facilities to provide the Ombudsman with written notice of any proposed involuntary transfer or discharge and mandate inclusion of the Ombudsman's contact details on resident notices.

The Office of Administrative Hearings employs the Administrative Law Judges who conduct hearings and issue orders regarding contested involuntary nursing home transfers and discharges, and the bill directly modifies statutory procedures and timelines linked to these proceedings.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Vulnerable Adult Banking Protection Act authorizes fiduciary institutions to delay or deny disbursements from the accounts of eligible adults (individuals at least 65 years old or vulnerable adults) if financial exploitation is reasonably suspected. It requires institutions to notify authorized parties, Adult Protective Services, law enforcement, or State's Attorneys; permits notification of trusted contacts; mandates disclosure of relevant financial records; and provides immunity from civil and administrative liability for institutions acting in good faith.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Human Services (Adult Protective Services Program), local law enforcement agencies, and State's Attorneys
qa_results.stakeholders: Eligible adults (seniors aged 65 and older and vulnerable adults), fiduciary institutions (banks, credit unions, and savings institutions), trusted contacts and family members, and adult protective services and law enforcement personnel.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances. Local social service agencies and law enforcement agencies can handle the bill's requirements with existing resources, and local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly involves the Adult Protective Services (APS) program operated through local departments of social services under the Department of Human Services, requiring fiduciary institutions to report suspected financial exploitation, share financial records, and coordinate delays or extensions of account disbursements with APS.

The bill amends the Financial Institutions Article regarding fiduciary institutions, which are regulated and supervised by the Commissioner of Financial Regulation within the Maryland Department of Labor.
The bill authorizes courts of competent jurisdiction to issue orders extending or terminating disbursement delays requested in response to suspected financial exploitation of vulnerable adults.

The bill requires fiduciary institutions to notify law enforcement agencies—which include state police—when delaying disbursements due to suspected exploitation, and authorizes law enforcement to receive financial records and petition for disbursement delay extensions.

The bill addresses the financial exploitation of adults aged 65 and older, aligning closely with the Department of Aging's mission to protect the rights and welfare of older adults, although operational enforcement is directed to Adult Protective Services and law enforcement.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Maryland counties and municipalities, individually or jointly, to establish multidisciplinary and multiagency local suicide fatality review teams. The bill outlines team membership, operational requirements, coordination with state and child fatality review entities, access to records, confidentiality protections, and exceptions to the Open Meetings Act, with the goal of identifying risk factors and developing recommendations to prevent suicide deaths.
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals at risk of suicide and their families, local health departments, county and municipal governments, healthcare and behavioral health providers, emergency medical services, local law enforcement, and public school systems.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not expected to be materially affected, as the Maryland Department of Health is assumed to absorb implementation and regulatory oversight within existing budgeted resources (though indeterminate costs could arise if vendor contracts are needed for secure data sharing). Local health department and municipal expenditures may increase indeterminately beginning in FY 2027 for jurisdictions opting to establish review teams, with estimated costs ranging from $30,000 to $50,000 per local team. Local and state revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH oversees public health programs, houses the State Suicide Fatality Review Committee, maintains vital records and medical examiner investigative data subject to review, and is explicitly authorized under § 5-1110 to adopt regulations governing local suicide fatality review teams.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the State Suicide Fatality Review Committee with establishing operating protocols, data collection standards, and guidance for local teams, as well as receiving their reports and recommendations.

Directors of local departments of social services (which are administered by DHS) are designated members of local teams, and local teams are authorized to request and review confidential social services records.
Local suicide fatality review team membership includes county superintendents of schools, who lead the local school systems under MSDE's policy and oversight umbrella.
The bill allows a State law enforcement officer to serve as a member of a local review team and authorizes teams to request police investigative data for reviews.

qa_results.bill_summary: Known as Ralph's Act, this bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to provide an expedited Medicaid eligibility determination for developmental disabilities services—specifically within 60 business days—for qualifying individuals who received home- and community-based waiver services in another state for at least 10 years and relocated to Maryland to live with an immediate family member following the death or incapacitation of their caretaker. Eligible individuals are placed in the crisis resolution category and granted access to waiver services through the appropriate reserve category.
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals with developmental disabilities relocating to Maryland after the death or incapacitation of their caretaker, their resident family caregivers, and individuals currently on Maryland's Developmental Disabilities Administration service waitlists.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations will be impacted, but the Department of Legislative Services estimates the Maryland Department of Health can likely handle the limited number of expedited determinations using existing resources, though redirection of resources could cause processing delays for other applications. If expedited determinations spur higher application volumes requiring additional staff, expenditures could increase by approximately $80,000 annually, split equally between general and federal funds. Revenues and local government operations/finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH), primarily through its Developmental Disabilities Administration, is directly responsible for implementing the bill by establishing and administering expedited eligibility determinations and waiver placements for qualifying relocating individuals with developmental disabilities.

The Department of Disabilities coordinates and monitors services and policy across state agencies for Marylanders with disabilities, making the expansion and expediting of developmental disability waiver services relevant to its overarching mission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renders noncompete and conflict of interest clauses null and void for licensed architects if their employer had more than 30 employees (the majority working in Maryland) at the start of employment, but on the enforcement date no longer has its principal place of business in Maryland or no longer has the majority of its employees reporting to or working remotely from Maryland.
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed architects and employers of architects with more than 30 employees that relocate their workforce or principal place of business outside Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends § 3-716 of the Labor and Employment Article regarding noncompete and conflict of interest clauses, which falls under the regulatory domain of the Maryland Department of Labor. Additionally, the department houses occupational and professional licensing boards, including the State Board of Architects referenced via the Business Occupations and Professions Article.

The bill renders certain noncompete and conflict of interest contract provisions null and void as against public policy and establishes definitions around judicial enforcement actions, which directly guides the adjudication of contract and employment disputes in Maryland courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits the State or any unit of local government from approving the construction or operation of real property for use as a detention facility (including immigration detention facilities) by a private entity, bars private entities from operating or occupying such facilities, establishes civil penalties of up to $10,000 per day for violations, and authorizes the Attorney General to seek injunctive relief and civil enforcement.
qa_results.stakeholders: Private detention facility operators and contractors, individuals subject to civil or criminal involuntary confinement (including immigrant detainees), and local government zoning authorities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances, though civil penalty revenues of up to $10,000 per day could be collected if private entities violate its provisions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly designates the Office of the Attorney General as the enforcement authority empowered to bring civil actions against private entities for violations, seek injunctive relief, and report any court rulings that invalidate statutory provisions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state department overseeing correctional policies, detention standards, and correctional facilities under the Correctional Services Article, the agency is affected by the statewide statutory prohibition against private detention facilities.
State courts will adjudicate civil enforcement actions initiated under the bill, issue injunctive relief, and levy civil penalties of up to $10,000 per day against violators.

qa_results.bill_summary: This joint resolution adopts the salary recommendations of the Governor's Salary Commission for Maryland's Governor and Lieutenant Governor for the four-year term beginning January 20, 2027. It establishes the Governor's annual salary at $195,000 for the first year, $202,000 for the second and third years, and $210,000 for the fourth year; and sets the Lieutenant Governor's annual salary at $175,000 for the first year, $180,000 for the second and third years, and $185,000 for the fourth year.
qa_results.stakeholders: The Governor and Lieutenant Governor of Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures will increase for salaries and fringe benefits by $0 in FY 2027, $6,800 in FY 2028, $13,600 in FY 2029, $20,900 in FY 2030, and $28,300 in FY 2031. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The joint resolution directly establishes the salary schedule for the Governor of Maryland for the four-year term beginning January 20, 2027.
The joint resolution directly establishes the statutory salary schedule for the Lieutenant Governor of Maryland for the four-year term beginning January 20, 2027.

As the state's central budget and personnel agency, DBM oversees state salary administration and budget implementation; a copy of the adopted resolution is also specifically required to be forwarded to the Secretary of Budget and Management.
The State Treasurer serves as an ex officio member of the Governor's Salary Commission, which evaluated compensation and issued the recommendations adopted by this resolution.

qa_results.bill_summary: This joint resolution implements the recommendations of the Judicial Compensation Commission to increase the salaries of Maryland Judiciary judges by $5,900 annually across fiscal years 2027 through 2030 (a total increase of $23,600 per judge). It also establishes an annual $7,500 stipend during those fiscal years for the Chief Judge of the Appellate Court of Maryland and circuit court and District Court administrative judges.
