agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor regulates state-chartered financial institutions through the Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, which approves credit union mergers, consolidations, and waivers under the Financial Institutions Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Decreases the membership of the Board of Trustees of the Maryland School for the Deaf from 19 to 13 members and increases the minimum number of deaf members from 6 to 7, while establishing a phase-out process as current board members' terms expire.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor of Maryland and the Board of Trustees of the Maryland School for the Deaf
qa_results.stakeholders: Current and future members of the Maryland School for the Deaf Board of Trustees, the deaf and hard-of-hearing community, and students and staff of the Maryland School for the Deaf.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures for the Maryland School for the Deaf are expected to decrease minimally due to reduced meal costs for quarterly board meetings. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the size and composition of the Board of Trustees of the Maryland School for the Deaf, reducing membership from 19 to 13 and increasing the minimum number of deaf members from 6 to 7.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and recruiting candidates for state boards and commissions, and will be tasked with implementing the new composition requirements and phase-out schedule for the Board of Trustees.

The Governor appoints the members of the Maryland School for the Deaf Board of Trustees with the advice and consent of the Senate and is directed to prioritize appointing deaf members as seats expire.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a circuit court to authorize or direct transactions that grant access to financial records or establish eligibility for government assistance programs on behalf of a minor or disabled person without appointing a guardian.
qa_results.stakeholders: Minors, disabled individuals, and their families or caregivers seeking single-transaction court orders as an alternative to full guardianship
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends statutory procedures in circuit courts under § 13-204 of the Estates and Trusts Article, authorizing judges to permit transactions granting access to financial records and establishing eligibility for government assistance programs without appointing a guardian. The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the circuit courts in implementing court rules and statutory changes.

The bill allows circuit courts to authorize transactions specifically to establish eligibility for government assistance programs, notably Medical Assistance (Medicaid), which is administered by the Maryland Department of Health.

The bill impacts proceedings to establish eligibility for government assistance programs for minors and vulnerable individuals, programs which are largely overseen and administered at the state level by the Department of Human Services.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) to permit deer population reduction on contiguous properties of at least 10 acres with documented deer damage, modifies Sunday hunting hours in select counties, and permits Sunday bow hunting in Baltimore City. Additionally, from July 1, 2027, through June 30, 2030, it repeals county-specific Sunday hunting statutes and requires DNR to adopt regulations governing Sunday hunting across game bird and mammal seasons while establishing procedures for counties to request regulatory changes and requiring annual reports on deer management and safety.
qa_results.stakeholders: Hunters, private property owners, farmers, outdoor recreationists, and county governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local government finances; the Department of Natural Resources can implement its requirements using existing resources. There is a potential meaningful positive economic impact on small businesses such as hunting outfitters, farms experiencing less crop damage, and auto repair shops.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources (DNR) is the primary implementing agency for the bill. DNR is authorized to permit deer population reductions on properties with documented damage, regulate Sunday hunting hours and seasons across Maryland counties, map applicable permit areas, adopt comprehensive Sunday hunting regulations starting July 1, 2027, and submit annual reports on hunting safety and stakeholder interests to the General Assembly.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of the Environment, in consultation with the Maryland Department of Agriculture, to define "agritourism" in its stormwater management regulations and consider tailored best management practices, including standard plans for temporary parking and the use of cropland, meadows, and pastures for runoff treatment. Additionally, requires Montgomery County and the Montgomery Soil Conservation District to review the county's agritourism stormwater review and approval process and report their findings by December 31, 2026.
qa_results.stakeholders: Farms and agricultural operators engaged in agritourism, Montgomery County government, and local soil conservation districts.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government changes can be handled using existing budgeted resources with no impact on state or local revenues. Agricultural small businesses that conduct agritourism activities may benefit from more tailored stormwater management practices.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary regulatory agency tasked with adopting stormwater management regulations that define 'agritourism' and incorporate best management practices for agritourism stormwater management, as well as consulting on Montgomery County's plan review process.
MDA must be consulted by MDE to establish the regulatory definition of 'agritourism' for stormwater management criteria.
The Governor's Office is a designated recipient of the report on the agritourism stormwater management review required to be submitted by December 31, 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands eligibility for the Maryland Graduate and Professional Scholarship Program to include Maryland residents attending the University of Maryland Eastern Shore enrolled in Master of Medical Science in Physician Assistant Studies, Doctor of Pharmacy, Doctor of Physical Therapy, or Doctor of Veterinary Medicine degree programs.
qa_results.stakeholders: Graduate students attending the University of Maryland Eastern Shore in eligible degree programs, as well as students and higher education institutions currently participating in the Maryland Graduate and Professional Scholarship Program.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No net impact on State expenditures or revenues. Program funding is set in the annual State budget ($1.2 million in the fiscal 2027 budget as introduced). Adding UMES reallocates existing scholarship funding among eligible institutions based on State resident enrollment. The Maryland Higher Education Commission can implement the changes with existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC establishes and administers the Maryland Graduate and Professional Scholarship Program, calculates allocations to participating institutions based on resident enrollment, and sets guidelines and regulations for implementation.
The Commission is the primary administering body responsible for establishing program guidelines, adopting regulations, and allocating scholarship grant funds among eligible institutions.

The bill expands scholarship eligibility specifically to students enrolled in four professional and graduate degree programs at the University of Maryland Eastern Shore (UMES), a member institution of the University System of Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires public senior higher education institutions and community colleges in Maryland to provide access to all methods of over-the-counter contraception on campus and annually report on this access to the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC). In turn, MHEC is required to compile and submit an annual report summarizing this information to the General Assembly.
qa_results.stakeholders: Students attending Maryland public four-year higher education institutions and community colleges, as well as institutional staff and health centers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local community college higher education expenditures and revenues are anticipated to increase, at least minimally, to expand over-the-counter contraception offerings to include all methods (e.g., purchasing products, installing vending machines, staffing), which may be offset by student fee revenues. Most four-year institutions, MHEC, and Baltimore City Community College are expected to handle annual reporting requirements using existing resources, though some institutions may incur administrative costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is directly responsible for administering the reporting process, providing the reporting form to public senior higher education institutions and community colleges, collecting their annual contraception access reports, and compiling and submitting an annual report to the General Assembly.

Constituent institutions of the University System of Maryland are defined as public senior higher education institutions under the bill and are required to annually report to MHEC regarding on-campus over-the-counter contraception access, methods provided, amounts distributed, and student consultation.

Morgan State University is explicitly designated as a public senior higher education institution subject to the bill's annual reporting requirements regarding campus over-the-counter contraception provision and student engagement.

St. Mary's College of Maryland is explicitly designated as a public senior higher education institution subject to the bill's annual reporting requirements on over-the-counter contraception access and student consultation.

The Maryland Department of Health is authorized under the amended statute to provide assistance to community colleges upon request in developing contraception access plans and collaborating with organizations experienced in vending machine contraception delivery.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Maryland Transit Administration Reform Act repeals the Baltimore Regional Transit Commission and establishes two new oversight bodies within the Maryland Transit Administration: the Board of Directors for Baltimore Core Transit Service and the Commuter Services Advisory Board. The bill establishes staffing requirements for these boards, tasks the Maryland Transportation Commission with determining qualifications and compensation for up to 12 MTA management positions, and directs the Maryland Department of Transportation to contract with the Baltimore Metropolitan Council to study the creation of a statewide rail authority.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Transit Administration and Maryland Department of Transportation
qa_results.stakeholders: Baltimore-area transit riders, commuter bus and MARC train commuters, Maryland Transit Administration management and frontline employees, and local jurisdictions in the Baltimore region
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) net expenditures increase by $319,456 in FY 2027, accounting for five new staff positions ($548,752), operating costs ($45,704), and a rail authority technical study contract ($100,000), partially offset by $375,000 in savings from repealing the Baltimore Regional Transit Commission. Net expenditures increase between $210,500 and $310,100 annually from FY 2028 through FY 2031, reflecting full ongoing staff costs offset by $500,000 in annual BRTC savings. TTF expenditures may increase further by up to several hundred thousand dollars annually based on compensation adjustments made by the Maryland Transportation Commission for up to 12 MTA management positions. State revenues and local government finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill fundamentally restructures governance within the Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) by repealing the Baltimore Regional Transit Commission, establishing the Board of Directors for Baltimore Core Transit Service and the Commuter Services Advisory Board, setting minimum staffing allocations, and adjusting management personnel compensation structures.

MTA is a modal administration within MDOT; MDOT is required to provide staff for the newly created boards, the Secretary of Transportation serves on the boards, and MDOT must contract with the Baltimore Metropolitan Council to conduct a technical study on establishing a rail authority.

The Secretary of Budget and Management is statutorily tasked with reviewing and evaluating proposed salary adjustments for up to 12 MTA management personnel positions to assess whether adjustments pose an adverse impact on special fund expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals the Baltimore Regional Transit Commission and creates two new permanent advisory/governing bodies: the Board of Directors for Baltimore Core Transit Service and the Commuter Services Advisory Board.
The Governor is responsible for appointing members and designating the chairs of both the Board of Directors for Baltimore Core Transit Service and the Commuter Services Advisory Board.

Assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments for the newly established Board of Directors for Baltimore Core Transit Service and the Commuter Services Advisory Board.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires health care facilities that perform surgical procedures to adopt and implement policies by January 1, 2028, mandating the use of a smoke evacuation system during any surgical procedure that may generate surgical smoke.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health (Office of Health Care Quality)
qa_results.stakeholders: Hospitals, ambulatory surgical facilities, freestanding medical facilities, and surgical personnel such as surgeons, nurses, anesthesiologists, surgical technologists, and patients.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Office of Health Care Quality can monitor and enforce compliance with existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1087 amends the Health - General Article to require licensed health care facilities that perform surgical procedures to implement smoke evacuation policies. The Maryland Department of Health, through its Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ), regulates and inspects these health care facilities and will be responsible for ensuring compliance with the bill's requirements.

qa_results.bill_summary: Senate Bill 741 expands the definition of 'virtual currency kiosk operator' to include persons who install or operate software enabling stand-alone automated devices to provide virtual currency services in Maryland, subjecting them to existing state registration and regulatory requirements. It also clarifies that kiosks cannot provide the same services as automated teller machines (ATMs) and excludes standard cash transactions linked to deposit, credit, or convenience accounts from the definition of virtual currency services.
qa_results.responsible_party: Commissioner of Financial Regulation (Maryland Department of Labor)
qa_results.stakeholders: Virtual currency kiosk operators, software installers and operators for virtual currency kiosks, small businesses operating kiosks, and consumers utilizing virtual currency services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances, and has no local fiscal impact. Small businesses operating virtual currency kiosks may experience a potential meaningful impact through compliance and registration expenses for software installers and operators.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor houses the Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, which licenses, registers, and regulates financial institutions and virtual currency kiosk operators in the State. The bill directly alters regulatory definitions and requirements enforced by the Commissioner.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Commerce to develop and maintain the Maryland Local Sourcing Portal, a searchable online database designed to connect Maryland businesses with local suppliers of tariff-impacted goods and other inventory, and to submit an annual report to the General Assembly on its use and effectiveness.
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland businesses, local suppliers and sources of goods, and small businesses seeking domestic or alternative sources for tariff-impacted inventory.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $142,900 in FY 2027, reflecting the cost of one contractual data analyst and $75,000 in IT portal development expenses, followed by ongoing operating and IT maintenance costs of $91,800 in FY 2028, $95,100 in FY 2029, $98,500 in FY 2030, and $102,100 in FY 2031. There is no effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 757 directly tasks the Department of Commerce with developing, maintaining, and annually reporting on the Maryland Local Sourcing Portal, including incurring technology startup and contractual staffing costs.
The bill explicitly authorizes the Department of Commerce to coordinate with DoIT to leverage existing digital infrastructure and minimize costs associated with portal development and maintenance.
The bill authorizes the Department of Commerce to coordinate with the Office of the Comptroller to identify potential local Maryland business sources for inclusion in the sourcing portal.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the University System of Maryland to issue up to $50.0 million in academic facilities bonds to finance specific capital improvements at Towson University, the University of Maryland, College Park, and the Rita Colwell Center, as well as systemwide facility renewal projects.
qa_results.stakeholders: Students, faculty, staff, and visitors across University System of Maryland institutions and campuses
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues and expenditures from bond proceeds increase by $50.0 million in FY 2027. Higher education expenditures increase by an estimated $4.2 million annually beginning in FY 2028 for 20 years to pay debt service on the revenue bonds. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 769 is a departmental bill requested by the University System of Maryland (USM) that authorizes the system to issue up to $50 million in academic revenue bonds to finance capital and facilities renewal projects across USM institutions, with USM responsible for the debt service.

qa_results.bill_summary: Senate Bill 775 establishes standards for gun buyback programs in Maryland. It requires federal firearms licensees and law enforcement agencies that operate gun buyback programs to completely destroy surrendered firearms and all attached components to render them permanently inoperable and unrepairable, unless a firearm is determined to be stolen or evidence of a crime. Law enforcement agencies must check the National Crime Information Center database to verify whether surrendered firearms are lost, stolen, or tied to a crime prior to destruction. The bill also establishes fines up to $10,000 per violation and mandates the revocation of a dealer's license for noncompliant licensed firearms dealers.
qa_results.stakeholders: Federal firearms licensees, licensed firearms dealers, state and local law enforcement agencies, and individuals participating in gun buyback programs.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal and Policy Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. The bill establishes potential misdemeanor criminal fines and civil penalties of up to $10,000 per violation, but overall fiscal impacts remain minimal or negligible.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Secretary of State Police to revoke a firearms dealer's license if the licensee violates the gun buyback provisions. In addition, the Department of State Police regulates firearms dealers and, as a statewide law enforcement agency, is subject to the firearm check and destruction requirements when participating in or operating gun buyback programs.

The bill establishes a new misdemeanor offense subject to a fine up to $10,000 for operating an unauthorized gun buyback program, which impacts District and Circuit Court caseloads and judicial administration.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new misdemeanor criminal offense for operating a gun buyback program contrary to statutory requirements, potentially requiring legal defense services from OPD for qualifying indigent defendants.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals a statutory exemption that previously exempted individuals or entities acquiring or assigned certain mortgages, mortgage loans, or installment loans from consumer credit licensing requirements under Title 11 of the Financial Institutions Article, correcting a provision erroneously enacted in 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor (Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation)
qa_results.stakeholders: Entities and individuals that acquire or are assigned mortgages, mortgage loans, or installment loans, as well as consumer credit borrowers in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances and has no local effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor, through the Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, oversees the licensing and regulation of financial institutions, mortgage lenders, and consumer credit providers under Title 11 of the Financial Institutions Article. This bill repeals an exemption from these licensing requirements.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires Maryland hospitals to adopt a policy establishing protocols for responding to immigration enforcement actions at the facility, consistent with guidance issued by the Attorney General. Hospitals must make the policy accessible to all staff and provide annual training to ensure staff understanding.
qa_results.stakeholders: Hospital patients, hospital staff and healthcare workers, hospital administration, and immigration enforcement personnel
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires Maryland hospitals to adopt immigration enforcement policies consistent with the guidance developed and issued by the Attorney General under § 6-111 of the State Government Article.
The bill amends the Health - General Article to mandate operating protocols and staff training requirements for hospitals licensed and regulated within the state under MDH's regulatory purview.
The bill originally tasked the Commission with developing and publishing a model policy for hospitals, but this mandate was subsequently stricken by committee amendment.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes an individual who enrolls themselves or a dependent in health insurance during a special enrollment period for pregnancy to choose whether coverage begins on the first day of the month pregnancy was confirmed or the first day of the month following plan selection, and requires the carrier to select one of those options if the individual does not choose.
qa_results.stakeholders: Pregnant individuals and their dependents enrolling in health insurance, and health insurance carriers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration will increase minimally in FY 2027 from the $125 rate and form filing fee. Review of filings and operational adjustments for the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange can be handled with existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on local finances or the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 794 alters coverage effective date options for individuals enrolling during the special enrollment period for pregnancy within the Individual Exchange, requiring minor operational and IT adjustments to the Maryland Health Connection enrollment platform.

As the primary regulator of health insurance policies and carriers in Maryland, MIA will review updated plan form filings to ensure compliance with the altered pregnancy special enrollment period effective date provisions, collecting associated filing fees.

qa_results.bill_summary: Senate Bill 814 voids residential property service agreements entered into before June 1, 2023, if the service provider has forfeited the right to do business in the State and is defunct and not in good standing with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation on or after June 1, 2026. Such agreements cannot exceed two years, run with the land, create a lien or encumbrance, or be assigned without consent. It also authorizes an individual with an interest in property subject to such a lien to file an action in circuit court to declare the agreement void and seek compensatory damages, attorney's fees, and court costs.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (Circuit Courts) and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential property owners encumbered by service agreements and defunct residential service providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a statutory cause of action allowing persons with an interest in residential property subject to an invalid service agreement lien to file an action in the circuit courts for declaratory relief, damages, and attorney's fees.

The Maryland Department of Labor oversees the licensing and regulation of real estate professionals and home improvement contractors who execute residential service agreements, and was consulted for the bill's fiscal analysis.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters notice requirements for judicial in rem tax foreclosures on certain vacant and abandoned properties by requiring counties and municipal corporations to serve the complaint on each interested party in accordance with the Maryland Rules, rather than mailing notice and a copy by first-class and certified mail within five days of filing.
qa_results.responsible_party: County and municipal governments and the Circuit Courts of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Interested parties of vacant, unsafe, or abandoned properties subject to tax foreclosure (including property owners, mortgagees, and lienholders) and local governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State finances and is not anticipated to materially affect local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the service and notice requirements for judicial in rem tax foreclosures filed in county circuit courts by requiring service in accordance with the Maryland Rules. As the administrative support agency for the Maryland Judicial Branch, the Administrative Office of the Courts supports circuit court operations and procedures.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Annual Corrective Bill corrects various technical errors, grammatical omissions, outdated terminology, and obsolete cross-references across multiple articles of the Annotated Code of Maryland and the Public Local Laws of Somerset County, without making substantive changes to the law.
qa_results.stakeholders: State and local government entities, the court system, legal professionals, and members of the public utilizing the Annotated Code of Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: None. The bill is purely technical in nature and has no effect on State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill makes technical corrections to the Human Services Article by explicitly adding statutory definitions designating the Department of Disabilities and the Secretary of Disabilities for the Ethan Saylor Alliance and the Assistive Technology Services Fund.

The bill corrects multiple cross-references, obsolete terms, and grammatical errors throughout the Education Article, including provisions related to school funding formulas, Blueprint for Maryland's Future estimates, teacher mentoring guidelines, and special education.

The bill corrects technical errors and obsolete accounts within the Transportation Article, including Transportation Trust Fund accounts, bond authorizations for zero-emission buses, and vehicle titling language.
The bill updates language regarding managed aquifer recharge permits and corrects the statutory name of a legislative committee receiving annual reports on on-site sewage disposal funding.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill makes technical and obsolete language corrections in the Correctional Services Article (including removing obsolete references to the death penalty) and corrects misnomers regarding the Division of Correction.

The bill corrects statutory cross-references in the State Finance and Procurement Article regarding nonvisual access standards for IT procurements and cybersecurity incident reporting under the State Chief Information Security Officer.

The bill corrects internal cross-references in the State Personnel and Pensions Article concerning termination of external investment managers and notifications regarding reemployed correctional officer retirees.

The bill corrects technical references in the Health - General Article, including updating terminology to 'substance use disorder', correcting references to the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, and removing obsolete cross-references.
The bill makes technical and grammatical corrections in the Labor and Employment Article concerning gross misconduct in unemployment insurance, apprenticeship grants, and internal fund references.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill updates an obsolete statutory agency name reference in the Health - General Article to reflect the agency's current title.
The bill amends language in the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article regarding the payment of contested automated camera enforcement citations to the District Court.
The bill corrects subsection numbering and references in the Education Article governing the Safe Schools Fund and training provided by the Center.
The bill removes redundant references to the Secretary of Budget and Management in capital project planning sections of the State Finance and Procurement Article.
The agency is referenced in technical amendments in the Health - General Article related to multi-agency coordination on reducing firearm violence.

qa_results.bill_summary: Senate Bill 865 extends the termination date of the Workgroup on the Affordability of Private Passenger Automobile Insurance to June 30, 2027, and alters its membership and responsibilities. The workgroup is tasked with developing data-driven, concrete legislative recommendations through recorded voting to reduce automobile insurance premiums—specifically evaluating territorial rating and other rating factors contributing to disparate impacts—and submitting an updated report by January 1, 2027.
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland motorists and private passenger automobile insurance policyholders, automobile insurance companies, insurance producers, and consumer advocacy organizations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are not affected. The Maryland Insurance Administration can likely handle the bill's requirements with existing budgeted resources; however, special fund expenditures could increase minimally if additional analyses require expanding an existing actuarial consulting contract. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration is the primary implementing agency for the bill; the Maryland Insurance Commissioner chairs the workgroup, MIA provides staff and administrative support, and MIA is directly responsible for overseeing the study and submitting the report.

The Executive Director of the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund (or their designee) is statutorily designated as a member of the workgroup studying private passenger automobile insurance affordability.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill extends the termination date, expands the duties, and alters the composition of the Workgroup on the Affordability of Private Passenger Automobile Insurance, a temporary advisory body established by statute.
The workgroup is required to submit its updated findings and concrete legislative recommendations directly to the Governor by January 1, 2027.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Workforce Launch Pilot Program within the Department of Commerce to recruit out-of-state businesses in strategic industries to Maryland by providing customized, no-cost workforce training. The Department must partner with up to two community colleges to deliver the training, establish job-creation and salary metrics for participating businesses, and require reimbursement if the performance metrics are not met.
qa_results.stakeholders: Out-of-state businesses seeking to establish operations in Maryland, Maryland workers receiving customized job training, and up to two partner Maryland community colleges (including potentially Baltimore City Community College).
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $1,000,000 in FY 2027 (effectuating a contingent budget appropriation) and by an assumed $1,000,000 in FY 2028 to support training grants and one contractual staff position, followed by $42,600 in FY 2029 for staffing to complete the final report. Local community college (and/or Baltimore City Community College) revenues and expenditures increase to match grant funds received for training costs. Indeterminate revenues could be recovered if participating businesses fail to meet performance metrics.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes and requires the Department of Commerce to administer the Maryland Workforce Launch Pilot Program, partner with community colleges, distribute training funds, monitor performance metrics, and submit an evaluation report.
The Department of Commerce is required to submit a report on the effectiveness of the pilot program and recommendations for statewide expansion to the Governor by December 31, 2028.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the use of stop sign monitoring systems in school zones located in the 41st Legislative District of Baltimore City under an existing pilot program. The bill subjects recorded violators to civil penalties up to $40 and requires 50% of the fines collected to be distributed to the local management board for Baltimore City to fund youth programming and services in the 41st Legislative District.
qa_results.stakeholders: Motorists driving through school zones in the 41st Legislative District in Baltimore City, as well as youth residing in or attending school in that district.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $5,938 in FY 2027 for one-time Judiciary computer programming costs, while State general fund revenues may increase minimally through FY 2030 from contested citations paid in District Court. Baltimore City revenues and expenditures will increase beginning in FY 2027 through FY 2030 depending on system implementation, installation/administrative costs, fine collections, and subsequent spending on youth programming and public safety.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Judiciary/Administrative Office of the Courts handles contested citations through the District Court and incurs estimated one-time programming expenditures of approximately $5,938 in FY 2027 to implement the automated citation tracking updates.

Under the statute governing the pilot program, the State Highway Administration is responsible for authorizing stop sign monitoring systems on State highways in school zones and prominently placing signs providing notice of their use.

As the parent department of the State Highway Administration, the Department of Transportation oversees the state roadways and signage requirements implicated by expanding the automated stop sign enforcement program.
Under statutory automated enforcement provisions referenced in the fiscal analysis, any local jurisdiction net fine revenues exceeding statutory thresholds must be remitted to the Comptroller.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to reimburse applied behavior analysis (ABA) services delivered by behavior technicians to Medicaid recipients with autism spectrum disorder. It prohibits the Department from requiring certification as an immediate condition of reimbursement, though it permits requiring technicians to obtain and maintain certification within 150 days of beginning service delivery.
qa_results.stakeholders: Behavior technicians, healthcare providers offering applied behavior analysis (ABA) therapy, and Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) recipients diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State administrative oversight expenditures can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources of the Maryland Department of Health, with minimal impact split evenly between general and federal funds. Revenues are not materially affected, and there is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 898 directly requires the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) to provide reimbursement for applied behavior analysis services under the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), establishes credentialing and certification timelines for behavior technicians, and mandates that MDH adopt implementing regulations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Advanced Manufacturing Grant Program and an accompanying special fund within the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO) to award grants to companies specializing in regenerative medicine and advanced manufacturing for facilities, infrastructure improvements, and equipment.
qa_results.stakeholders: Companies and small businesses specializing in regenerative medicine and advanced manufacturing in Maryland, along with vendors supplying equipment, facilities, or services to them.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues and expenditures increase by $5.0 million in FY 2027 to capitalize the grant program, with General Fund expenditures increasing by approximately $800,000 in FY 2027 for administrative expenses (including two staff). Starting in FY 2028, PAYGO General Fund expenditures increase by $5.0 million annually to capitalize the fund, yielding matching special fund revenues and expenditures (which will absorb ongoing administrative expenses). There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: TEDCO is the primary agency responsible for establishing, administering, and adopting regulations for the Maryland Advanced Manufacturing Grant Program and managing the associated special fund.
The bill mandates that the State Treasurer hold and invest the monies in the newly created Maryland Advanced Manufacturing Grant Program Fund, ensuring interest earnings are credited to the fund.
The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller to account for the newly established Maryland Advanced Manufacturing Grant Program Fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that TEDCO consult with the Maryland Stem Cell Research Commission on all program criteria, procedures, and regulations relating to regenerative medicine.
According to the fiscal note, DGS holds $3.0 million in budgeted PAYGO general funds that are designated to be transferred to TEDCO to capitalize the new grant fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a temporary related event promoter's permit in Baltimore City for events associated with the Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity, Inc. 2027 Conclave, establishing application procedures, fees, requirements, and penalties for unauthorized promotion or operation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City
qa_results.stakeholders: Event promoters, Baltimore City alcoholic beverages license holders, State caterer license holders, and attendees of events associated with the 2027 Kappa Alpha Psi Conclave.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Baltimore City revenues may increase minimally in FY 2027 and FY 2028 from $50 application fees and permit fees of either $500 (under 300 person capacity) or $1,500 (300 or more person capacity), as well as potential penalty fines ranging from $1,000 to $3,000. Monitoring and enforcement can be handled with existing city resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill regulates alcoholic beverages sales, event promoter permits, and requirements for State caterer's license holders in Baltimore City. Based on the agency summary, the Comptroller regulates the alcohol industry, making the subject matter of the bill relevant to the agency's work, though primary local administration lies with the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners and enforcement on State caterers is directed to the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment to allow the chair of the Commission on Judicial Disabilities to recall a former member to serve as a temporary substitute member, or request the Governor to appoint a temporary substitute member or extend a current member's term, in instances of recusal, disqualification, or term expiration without a replacement. The bill also withdraws and repeals previously enacted constitutional amendments from 2025.
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the Commission on Judicial Disabilities, Maryland state judges, Maryland Bar attorneys, and Maryland voters
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: If approved by voters in the November 2026 election, the Commission on Judicial Disabilities will experience operational efficiencies. There is no material impact on State finances or operations, and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly authorizes the Governor, upon request of the Commission on Judicial Disabilities chair, to appoint temporary substitute members to the Commission or extend the term of current members until replacements are appointed.

As the executive office assisting the Governor with vetting and processing state board and commission appointments, it would support the Governor in handling temporary substitute appointments and term extensions for the Commission on Judicial Disabilities.

Provides central administrative and operational support to Maryland's judiciary. The bill directly impacts the operations and temporary membership of the Commission on Judicial Disabilities, which investigates state judges and reports to the Supreme Court of Maryland.

The bill proposes a constitutional amendment that must be prepared and placed on the ballot for statewide voter approval at the November 2026 general election, a process administered by the Board of Elections.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Maryland Fair Chance Housing Act regulates the use of criminal history records checks in residential leasing for landlords managing or owning five or more rental units. It restricts landlords from inquiring into or considering a prospective tenant's criminal history prior to extending a conditional rental offer, with exceptions for specific violent and sex offenses. The bill establishes procedures and individualized assessment criteria for withdrawing conditional offers, prohibits discriminatory housing advertisements, provides civil immunity to landlords who rent to individuals with criminal histories, and imposes a civil penalty of up to $500 per violation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development (Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs)
qa_results.stakeholders: Prospective residential tenants (specifically individuals with criminal records) and landlords or property managers owning or managing five or more residential rental units in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill, including its penalty provisions of up to $500 per violation, is not anticipated to have a material impact on State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD), specifically its Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs, with adopting regulations to implement the subtitle and developing and publishing a model notice document for landlords on its website.

The bill requires the model disclosure to notify prospective tenants of their right to file a complaint under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act (§ 13-401 of the Commercial Law Article), which is enforced by the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General.
The Maryland court system may receive and adjudicate landlord-tenant disputes and civil penalty actions resulting from alleged violations of the fair chance housing provisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands assignment of benefits provisions in health insurance to dentists and establishes parallel rules for dental plan organizations, prohibiting them from barring an assignment of benefits to a dentist or refusing direct reimbursement to nonpreferred dentists, provided required pre-treatment disclosures and forms are completed.
qa_results.stakeholders: Dentists (especially nonpreferred dental providers), dental patients (insureds and dental plan enrollees), health insurers, and dental plan organizations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration will see a minimal increase in FY 2027 from $125 rate and form filing fees. MIA can handle any additional workload using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates insurers and dental plan organizations subject to the bill. Additionally, the Insurance Commissioner is required to develop disclosure forms to document the assignment of benefits, and the agency will experience a minimal increase in special fund revenues from policy form filings.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the application and credentialing process for health care providers seeking to join an insurance carrier's provider panel, shortening timeframes for carriers to notify providers regarding application status and decisions. It repeals a carrier's authority to charge credentialing application fees, requires dedicated direct phone and email customer service for credentialing inquiries, mandates using the online credentialing system as the primary source for updating provider directories, and modifies standards for designating uniform credentialing forms and multi-carrier online provider directory systems.
qa_results.stakeholders: Health care providers, commercial health insurance carriers and dental plans, credentialing intermediaries, and insured patients/enrollees.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operational impacts on the Maryland Insurance Administration can be handled with existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government operations and finances are not affected. Small business effects are minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIA and the Insurance Commissioner are the primary regulatory authorities responsible for implementing the bill, which includes adopting regulations for carrier provider directories and online credentialing systems, reviewing reports from credentialing vendors, and reporting findings to the General Assembly.

The bill references health care providers with immunity under the Maryland Tort Claims Act (which is administered by the Treasurer's Office via the State Insurance Trust Fund) for provider panel reimbursement purposes, and the Treasurer's Office was consulted on the legislation, though it faces no direct administrative responsibilities or fiscal impact.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires certain health insurance policies, contracts, and certificates that reimburse for services within the scope of practice of a licensed graduate professional counselor, licensed master social worker, or licensed psychologist to also reimburse for covered services rendered by graduate-level counseling, social work, or psychology clinical interns. To be eligible for reimbursement, services must be provided at an outpatient health care facility under the direct supervision of an appropriate licensed supervisor and billed by that supervisor.
qa_results.stakeholders: Insured individuals receiving behavioral health services, graduate-level clinical interns in counseling, social work, and psychology, supervising licensed mental health providers, outpatient behavioral health facilities, and health insurance carriers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration will see a minimal increase in FY 2027 only from $125 rate and form filing fees. Any operational workload increases for the agency can be handled within existing budgeted resources. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates health insurance policies and carriers in the state. The bill establishes mandated health insurance reimbursement requirements for services provided by graduate-level clinical interns, requiring MIA to review policy form filings and collect related form filing fees.

The Maryland Department of Health oversees the health occupations licensing boards—including the State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists, the Board of Social Work Examiners, and the Board of Examiners of Psychologists—whose supervisory standards and COMAR regulations govern the interns and supervisors specified in the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the governing body of Calvert County to establish a property tax credit on real property formerly used solely as a tobacco barn, provided the property is subject to a tobacco buyout agreement or qualifies for an agricultural use assessment and is used for an approved agricultural activity.
qa_results.stakeholders: Calvert County agricultural landowners and property owners who own former tobacco barns.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are unaffected. Calvert County property tax revenues will decrease beginning in fiscal year 2027 to the extent that the county chooses to enact and grant the tax credit; the exact amount is indeterminate as the county does not maintain an inventory of eligible properties. County expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board hears appeals and resolves disputes regarding property valuations, agricultural use assessments, and eligibility for property tax credits following initial determinations by the local supervisor of assessments.

The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest administrative body hearing appeals from decisions of local taxing authorities and the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board concerning property tax assessments, exemptions, and credits.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the tax collector for each county to include a website address or quick-response (QR) code in the written materials sent with each property tax bill, directing taxpayers to a county webpage that lists available property tax credits and provides instructions on how to apply.
qa_results.responsible_party: County tax collectors and county governments
qa_results.stakeholders: County property taxpayers and county tax collection agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. County expenditures are not expected to be significantly impacted by including a website link or QR code with tax bills, and county revenues are not directly affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill makes it a misdemeanor to recklessly or willfully and maliciously deface, damage, or destroy telecommunications infrastructure, subject to up to six months imprisonment and/or a fine up to $500. It also expands the statutory definition of junk or scrap metal to include specified telecommunications equipment and infrastructure, prohibiting junk dealers and scrap metal processors from purchasing such equipment unless the seller provides documentation demonstrating lawful authority to sell it.
qa_results.responsible_party: State and local law enforcement agencies, the Maryland Department of Labor, and the Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Telecommunications companies, junk dealers, scrap metal processors, consumers, and individuals selling scrap metal
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. Any potential impact on small businesses is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new criminal misdemeanor offense for defacing, damaging, or destroying telecommunications infrastructure, which directly impacts District Court and circuit court case processing and judicial operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new misdemeanor offense punishable by up to six months of imprisonment, requiring legal representation by public defenders for indigent defendants charged under the statute.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The creation of a misdemeanor punishable by incarceration for up to six months may impact community supervision, parole, probation caseloads, and detention operations overseen by the department.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is responsible for investigating malicious destruction of property, enforcing criminal laws concerning infrastructure damage, and monitoring compliance with scrap metal regulations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a Class C per diem municipal to-go beer, wine, and liquor license and a temporary to-go event permit in Worcester County. The Worcester County Board of License Commissioners is authorized to issue the license to the Town of Berlin, Pocomoke City, and the Town of Snow Hill for up to seven consecutive days, allowing alcoholic beverages to enter designated special event areas. The board may also issue temporary to-go event permits to eligible Class B and Class D license holders located within or adjacent to the event area, allowing them to sell alcoholic beverages in approved to-go cups.
qa_results.responsible_party: Worcester County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Worcester County local governments (specifically the Town of Berlin, Pocomoke City, and the Town of Snow Hill), Class B and Class D alcoholic beverages license holders within or adjacent to designated special event areas, and event patrons.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: Worcester County revenues will increase beginning in FY 2027 from license fees ($45 per day) and temporary to-go permit fees ($20 per day), although the exact amount cannot be reliably estimated because the number of licenses and permits issued is unknown. Worcester County can handle the administration and enforcement using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is responsible for regulating Maryland's alcohol industry and collecting state sales and excise taxes on alcoholic beverages. Although this legislation is local to Worcester County and administered directly by the Worcester County Board of License Commissioners with no direct state fiscal impact, it relates to the regulation and retail sale of alcoholic beverages.

qa_results.bill_summary: Mandates that local detention center officers in Allegany County become members of the Correctional Officers' Retirement System (CORS) rather than the Employees' Pension System if Allegany County elects to participate in CORS, while granting transferred service credit without requiring officers to pay past contribution rate differences.
qa_results.stakeholders: Allegany County detention center officers (approximately 73 officers) and the Allegany County government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: If Allegany County elects to participate in CORS, its pension liabilities will increase by approximately $2.4 million ($2,396,120). Net annual employer pension contributions are projected to increase by $164,546 beginning in FY 2028, reflecting a $311,155 annual gross increase offset by an annual new entrant liability credit of $146,609 for 25 years. Local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System, including the Correctional Officers' Retirement System (CORS) and the Employees' Pension System (EPS). The bill directly impacts the agency's administration of member transfers, service credit calculations, and asset/liability adjustments for Allegany County detention center officers joining CORS.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 1109 enacts the Public Health Reform Act, which establishes the Maryland Medical Reserve Corps within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) to replace the Maryland Responds Health Reserve Corps; creates the Public Health Workforce Development Fund administered by the Maryland Community Health Resources Commission; modifies the membership, staffing, leadership, and duties of the Commission on Public Health while extending its termination date to June 30, 2028; requires the Department of Legislative Services to establish a process assessing health equity impacts of legislation; and enacts administrative reforms regarding local health departments, hospital board participation, and county health officer contract approvals.
qa_results.stakeholders: State and local public health departments, county health officers, public health workers, medical volunteers, and Maryland residents.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures (general or special funds) increase by an indeterminate amount beginning as early as FY 2027 to capitalize the Public Health Workforce Development Fund; special fund revenues and expenditures increase accordingly. Expenditures also increase minimally in FY 2027 and FY 2028 to fund staffing for the two-year extension of the Commission on Public Health. Most other agency provisions can be absorbed with existing resources, though evaluating health equity impacts for legislation could require significant general fund expenditures if staff additions are needed. Local health departments could see increased revenues if awarded funding from the Public Health Workforce Development Fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary implementing agency for several provisions in the bill, including organizing the Maryland Medical Reserve Corps, establishing coordination mechanisms with county health officers, providing quarterly updates on the implementation of recommendations to the Commission on Public Health, convening a recruitment and classification workgroup, and co-administering fund transfers from the Population Health Improvement Fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill substantially alters the governance, membership, duties, annual reporting requirements, and workgroups of the Commission on Public Health, extends its termination date by two years to June 30, 2028, and alters the composition of the Maryland Corps Program Advisory Board.

The Secretary of Budget and Management (or designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the Commission on Public Health, and DBM is required to participate in an MDH-convened workgroup evaluating local health department recruiting and classification processes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DSCI oversees the Maryland Corps Program, and the bill amends the statute governing the Maryland Corps Program Advisory Board by expanding its gubernatorial appointees to include a county health officer.

The bill explicitly authorizes HSCRC, jointly with MDH, to transfer funds from the Population Health Improvement Fund to the newly established Public Health Workforce Development Fund in alignment with the federal AHEAD Model agreement.
The Secretary of Information Technology (or designee) is added as a member of the Commission on Public Health.

The Governor is tasked with appointing an additional health officer member to the Maryland Corps Program Advisory Board, up to two public members to the Commission on Public Health, and receives annual reports regarding the implementation of public health recommendations.

The bill creates the Public Health Workforce Development Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund and requires the State Treasurer to hold and invest the money of the fund, with interest credited back to the fund.
The Comptroller is required by statute to account for the newly established Public Health Workforce Development Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters notice requirements for judicial in rem tax foreclosure actions on vacant and abandoned properties by requiring a county or municipality to serve the complaint on each interested party in accordance with the Maryland Rules, rather than sending notice and a copy by first-class and certified mail within five days of filing.
qa_results.responsible_party: County and municipal governments and the Circuit Courts
qa_results.stakeholders: Interested parties (property owners, mortgagees, and lienholders) of vacant and abandoned properties subject to tax foreclosure, as well as local government taxing authorities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State finances and is not anticipated to materially affect local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters procedural requirements for judicial in rem tax foreclosure complaints filed in county circuit courts by replacing statutory mailing requirements with service in accordance with the Maryland Rules, directly impacting circuit court filing and service procedures administered by the judicial branch.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires health care providers managing pregnancy or postpartum care to conduct screenings for perinatal behavioral health conditions at well visits within the child's first year; requires health insurance carriers and Medicaid to cover these screenings; tasks the Maryland Department of Health with identifying screening tools, developing training programs, and disseminating information; provides standing referrals for behavioral health services; and requires the Maryland Health Care Commission to study coverage impacts by December 1, 2026.
qa_results.stakeholders: Pregnant and postpartum individuals, infants, health care providers, hospitals, health insurance carriers, and Medicaid enrollees.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration in FY 2027 only from $125 rate and form filing fees. MDH, Medicaid, health occupations boards, and MHCC can implement requirements using existing budgeted resources. There is no fiscal impact on the State plan and no likely increase in local government health care expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH), including Medicaid and health occupations boards, is tasked with identifying screening tools, assisting providers with referral resources, developing training programs for perinatal behavioral health conditions, providing written information to WIC agencies, and covering perinatal behavioral health screenings under Medicaid.

The bill mandates that the Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC) conduct a comprehensive analysis and report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2026, on the impact of perinatal behavioral health screening coverage and cost-sharing prohibitions.

The Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) regulates commercial health insurers that must comply with the new coverage mandate and standing referral requirements, and anticipates a minimal increase in special fund revenues from rate and form filing fees.

Under the amendment adding § 10–758 of the Tax – General Article, the Comptroller is responsible for administering and processing the new refundable State income tax credit of $1,000 for parents of stillborn children.
DBM oversees the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which was analyzed for coverage alignment regarding perinatal behavioral health condition screenings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes members of the U.S. Foreign Service and their spouses who relocate to Maryland under an assignment or detail to practice their profession in the State under an out-of-state occupational or professional license for the duration of the assignment, provided they meet specific criteria and good standing requirements.
qa_results.responsible_party: State occupational and professional licensing authorities (including the Maryland Department of Labor, Maryland Department of Health, Maryland Department of Agriculture, and Maryland State Department of Education)
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the U.S. Foreign Service and their spouses holding out-of-state professional licenses who relocate to Maryland on assignment or detail, as well as businesses and clients utilizing their professional services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: In FY 2027, State general fund expenditures increase by up to $30,000 for the Maryland State Department of Education and special fund expenditures increase by at least $15,000 for the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners to update licensing software. General and special fund revenues decrease indeterminately beginning in FY 2027 due to foregone licensing fees (including up to $3,000 annually for veterinary licenses). Local government operations and finances are not significantly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends numerous occupational and professional licensing statutes administered by the Department of Labor and its regulatory boards, including accountants, architects, barbers, cosmetologists, electricians, stationary engineers, foresters, interior designers, landscape architects, pilots, plumbers, engineers, land surveyors, real estate professionals, tax preparers, contractors, HVACR technicians, locksmiths, and financial service entities.

The bill significantly impacts health occupations boards housed within MDH by allowing eligible Foreign Service members and spouses to practice in Maryland under out-of-state credentials across disciplines such as medicine, nursing, dentistry, pharmacy, physical therapy, psychology, social work, counseling, and others.

The bill directly amends licensing requirements under the Agriculture Article for veterinarians, pest control applicators/consultants, nutrient management planners, fertilizer applicators, and milk testers/calibrators. The State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners anticipates a direct fiscal impact requiring a $15,000 IT system update.

The bill modifies educator certification requirements for teachers and school counselors. MSDE anticipates a general fund expenditure increase of up to $30,000 in FY 2027 to update its teacher licensure platform to accommodate this alternate authorization pathway.

The bill modifies licensing and certification mandates administered by MDE and its affiliated licensing boards, including on-site wastewater professionals, waterworks and waste systems operators, well drillers, marine contractors, surface miners, radiation machine inspectors, and scrap tire handlers.

The bill impacts licensing and certification authorities administered by the Secretary of State Police and MSP units, including private detectives, security guards, security system technicians, and vehicle inspection mechanics under the Automotive Safety Enforcement Division (waiving examination requirements).

The bill amends the Transportation Article to allow eligible individuals to practice or do business under out-of-state credentials without obtaining separate MVA licenses for vehicle salesmen, automotive dismantlers and recyclers, title service agents, drivers' schools, and driving instructors.

The bill amends the Insurance Article regarding licensing exceptions for insurance producers, insurance advisers, bail bondsmen, public adjusters, and motor club service providers who are Foreign Service members or spouses.

The bill modifies licensing requirements overseen by the Commission, allowing eligible individuals to act as energy salespersons, energy vendors, and master plumber/gasfitters in the State under out-of-state licenses.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends provisions governing licensing for video lottery terminal/table games employees, operators, manufacturers, and sports wagering personnel to exempt eligible Foreign Service members and spouses from state-specific licensure.

Clerks of the circuit courts issue several local business licenses (peddlers, junk dealers, scrap metal processors, traders, exhibitors, and promoters) affected by the bill's portability provisions, which will impact local licensing administration and fee revenue.

The bill modifies Labor and Employment Article provisions regarding registration qualifications and administrative supervision for rehabilitation counselors and vocational evaluators practicing before or registered with the Commission.
MDOT is the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration, which administers the commercial and business licenses amended under Title 15 of the Transportation Article.
The bill creates licensing exemptions for eligible Foreign Service members and spouses who hold out-of-state credentials to practice as taxidermists or licensed tree experts under DNR's jurisdiction.

The bill amends licensing requirements for transient vendors licensed by the State Comptroller under Business Regulation § 17-20A-02 and cross-references tax/fee collection provisions administered by the agency.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill modifies Education Article § 13-516, which governs the licensure and certification of emergency medical services (EMS) providers overseen by the EMS Board and MIEMSS.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends Business Occupations and Professions § 20-301 to allow eligible out-of-state licensees to operate private home detention monitoring agencies licensed by the Secretary of Public Safety and Correctional Services.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes licensed pharmacists to order certain vaccines (including influenza, COVID-19, or public health emergency vaccines) for individuals at least three years old without requiring the pharmacist to administer the vaccination. It also establishes requirements for ordering vaccinations for administration by adult caregivers to minors under 18 and mandates reporting of ordered vaccines to the ImmuNet Program.
qa_results.stakeholders: Pharmacists, adult caregivers, and vaccine recipients ages 3 and older.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact because the changes are technical in nature and do not directly affect governmental finances. Small business impacts on pharmacies are expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health houses the State Board of Pharmacy, the State Board of Physicians, and the State Board of Nursing, and oversees the state's immunization registry (ImmuNet). The bill amends the Health Occupations Article to regulate pharmacist vaccination ordering protocols, reporting requirements to ImmuNet, and Board regulations.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 1137 requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to conduct a study on residential-in-commercial-zone (RICZ) laws—statewide legislation allowing multifamily residential or mixed-use developments as permitted uses in commercially zoned areas. The department must assess the impacts on communities, infrastructure, economic development, and housing production, and submit findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Local governments, residential and mixed-use property developers, commercial property owners, and residents in urban, suburban, and rural communities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $75,000 in FY 2027 only for the Department of Housing and Community Development to procure contractual services to assist with conducting the study and preparing the required report. State revenues and local government finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1137 directly tasks the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) with conducting a comprehensive study on residential-in-commercial-zone (RICZ) laws, assessing impacts on infrastructure, housing production, and economic development, and reporting recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2026. The bill also has a direct fiscal impact of $75,000 on DHCD in FY 2027 for contractual services.

As the state's principal agency for land use planning, growth policy, and local zoning technical guidance, the Department of Planning has subject matter interest and expertise directly relevant to the study of commercial-to-residential land use and was consulted in the development of the bill's fiscal analysis.
The bill requires DHCD to report its final study findings and statutory recommendations on residential-in-commercial-zone laws to the Governor on or before December 1, 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: Clarifies the Consumer Price Index calculation used to determine cost-of-living adjustments for retirees of the State Retirement and Pension System by establishing that the missing October 2025 index value—omitted due to a federal government shutdown—is calculated as the average of the September 2025 and November 2025 values for adjustments effective July 1, 2026, and July 1, 2027.
qa_results.stakeholders: Retirees and beneficiaries of the State Retirement and Pension System
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is anticipated to have no discernible effect on State or local pension liabilities or employer contribution rates, and has no effect on revenues. While the methodology slightly increases the calculated COLA rate for calendar year 2025 by 0.067 percentage points relative to an 11-month average, statutory COLA caps limit the impact on post-2011 service credit, and any nominal liability changes are amortized over 10 to 15 years and largely offset in subsequent years.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the calculation of the Consumer Price Index used to determine cost-of-living adjustments (COLAs) for retirees of the State Retirement and Pension System, which is administered and operated by the Maryland State Retirement Agency.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 1139 makes administrative, procedural, and clarifying changes to the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS). Among other provisions, it alters certain local employer payment due dates, establishes a 7.75% annual interest penalty on delinquent pension payments owed by county governments, requires participating governmental units (PGUs) to make enrollment available to all eligible employees, clarifies default enrollment procedures when employee election documentation is not submitted, and updates immediate vesting provisions.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Retirement and Pension System (Board of Trustees and State Retirement Agency) and the Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Eligible local and county governments, participating governmental units (PGUs), local employees, law enforcement officers, detention center officers, firefighters, emergency medical technicians, and the State Retirement and Pension System.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Effect: None; the bill is clarifying and procedural in nature and does not directly affect governmental finances. Local Effect: Local government expenditures increase to the extent that a county fails to make timely payments required under current law to the SRPS, subjecting it to a 7.75% annual interest penalty withheld by the Comptroller. No effect on local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1139 directly amends the administration of the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS) by clarifying participation requirements, election procedures, affidavits, service credit rules for participating governmental units, and payment deadlines and interest rates for delinquent employer contributions.

The bill explicitly tasks the State Comptroller with intercepting and withholding delinquent payments owed by county governments or local employers to the SRPS Board of Trustees, including newly clarified 7.75% annual interest penalties, via setoff against funds due to those local entities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
