agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals the statutory provision under State Personnel and Pensions § 29-304 that previously granted immediate retirement vesting rights to the Special Secretary of the Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs upon taking office.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force to Modernize County and Municipal Revenue Structures to study, evaluate, and make recommendations on the revenue structures, sources, and taxing authority of Maryland's county and municipal governments.
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland county and municipal governments, local officials, and Maryland taxpayers and residents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not significantly affected, as the Department of Legislative Services can likely handle staffing and administrative duties with existing budgeted resources; however, additional general fund expenditures could be needed if contractual staff or consultants are required. Expense reimbursements for task force members are minimal and absorbable. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland, or the Comptroller's designee, is designated as a statutory member of the newly created Task Force to Modernize County and Municipal Revenue Structures.
The Secretary of Budget and Management, or the Secretary's designee, is designated as a statutory member of the Task Force to Modernize County and Municipal Revenue Structures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a temporary task force—the Task Force to Modernize County and Municipal Revenue Structures—to conduct a comprehensive study and report recommendations on local government revenue structures.
The Task Force is required to submit a report detailing its findings and recommendations to the Governor on or before December 1, 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 1148 establishes the Legacy Protection Program within the State Department of Assessments and Taxation, administered by the State Tax Sale Ombudsman, to help heirs who inherit residential property clear titles, avoid tax sales, and stay in their homes. It provides grants for legal services, probate fees, and inheritance taxes, creates the Legacy Protection Fund financed by state and county contributions, and allows eligible heirs who are not yet record title holders to qualify for homeowners' and homestead property tax credits for up to three years.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Tax Sale Ombudsman within the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
qa_results.stakeholders: Heirs and legatees of deceased homeowners, estates and personal representatives of deceased homeowners, legal services organizations assisting with probate, and county governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2028, State general fund expenditures increase by $250,000 annually due to a mandated appropriation, and special fund revenues and expenditures increase by $750,000 annually to finance the Legacy Protection Program ($250,000 from the State and $500,000 paid collectively by counties). County expenditures collectively increase by $500,000 annually starting in FY 2028. Additionally, beginning in FY 2027, State and local property tax revenues may experience an indeterminate decrease, and State general fund expenditures for the homeowners' property tax credit may increase due to the expansion of tax credits to eligible heirs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to collaborate with the Registers of Wills to develop a step-by-step guide to probating an estate and becoming the record title holder of a dwelling. Additionally, the program provides grants to heirs to cover probate fees and inheritance taxes collected by the Registers of Wills.
The bill establishes the Legacy Protection Fund and statutorily requires the State Treasurer to hold the fund separately and invest its moneys in the same manner as other State funds.
The bill requires the Comptroller to account for the newly established Legacy Protection Fund and exempts the fund from standard net interest transfers to the General Fund.
The bill establishes a statutory mandate requiring the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $250,000 in the State budget bill for the Legacy Protection Fund beginning in fiscal year 2028.
As the agency responsible for state budget preparation and execution, DBM must implement the bill's annual mandated general fund appropriation of $250,000 for the Legacy Protection Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Comptroller to settle a claim of the State that is in arrears against a business entity that has permanently ceased operations, regardless of how long the claim has been in arrears, eliminating the standard two-year waiting period for those businesses.
qa_results.stakeholders: Business entities that have permanently ceased operations and owe claims or taxes in arrears to the State.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State tax revenues (general funds and special funds) are estimated to increase, potentially by $250,000 annually beginning in FY 2027, as claims are settled sooner. General fund expenditures for the Comptroller's Office increase by $74,124 in FY 2027 (and $98,500 by FY 2031) to hire one revenue administrator to handle settlement claims. Local income tax and local highway user revenues may also increase by an indeterminate amount annually beginning in FY 2027.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the primary implementing agency responsible for examining and settling claims of the State that are in arrears. The bill directly impacts the Comptroller's Offer in Compromise Program by eliminating the two-year waiting period for businesses that have permanently ceased operations, requiring an additional revenue administrator position to process the anticipated increase in settlements.
The State Treasurer's Office serves as the custodian of State funds and receives the settled sums paid into the State Treasury upon discharge of the claims.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of State Police to study and make recommendations regarding the employment, commissioning, training, jurisdiction, and regulatory oversight of special police officers, and to submit a report of its findings to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 1, 2026.
qa_results.stakeholders: Special police officers, public and private employers of special police officers (including county and municipal governments, educational institutions, and businesses), security training academies, and law enforcement agencies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures can be handled using existing budgeted resources, and state revenues are not affected. Local government finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Department of State Police conduct a comprehensive study on the employment, commissioning, training, jurisdiction, and regulatory oversight of special police officers, and submit a final report to the Governor and General Assembly.
The bill explicitly requires the Department of State Police to consult with a representative of the Office of the Secretary of State in conducting the required study.

The final study findings and policy recommendations regarding special police officers must be formally submitted to the Governor by December 1, 2026, and the Governor oversees executive appointments and commissions of special police officers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Calvert County to enter into long-term procurement contracts of up to 20 years for infrastructure or asset management programs for assets with a life cycle of at least 15 years, such as water towers, flow meters, and other water and sewer assets.
qa_results.responsible_party: Calvert County Board of County Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Calvert County government, local taxpayers, utility customers, and contractors providing infrastructure and asset management services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no State fiscal effect. It does not materially affect Calvert County government finances, though it may result in operational efficiencies for the county.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the death and burial benefits under the Calvert County Length of Service Award Program (LOSAP) for eligible volunteer fire, rescue, and emergency medical services personnel, raising the maximum benefit for volunteers with 25 years of certified service from $10,000 to $14,000, and increasing the per-year-of-service benefit from $336 to $560 for certain volunteers who reach age 70 without completing 25 years of service.
qa_results.stakeholders: Calvert County volunteer fire, rescue, and emergency medical services members and their surviving beneficiaries.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are unaffected. Calvert County expenditures may increase by approximately $16,000 annually beginning in FY 2027 based on an average rate of four deaths per year among qualified volunteers. County revenues are not affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Updates an obsolete statutory reference in the Public Local Laws of Calvert County from Calvert Memorial Hospital to CalvertHealth Medical Center, Inc., and its successors regarding the County Commissioners' authority to appropriate funds to the medical center.
qa_results.stakeholders: CalvertHealth Medical Center and residents of Calvert County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact. It is purely procedural in nature and does not affect Calvert County finances.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 1164 directs the Public Service Commission (PSC) to study the feasibility of requiring water companies, sewage disposal companies, and combined water and sewage disposal companies to adopt limited-income mechanisms to help eligible low-income customers afford service, requiring a report to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2026. Effective July 1, 2027, it authorizes the PSC to require these companies to implement such limited-income mechanisms.
qa_results.stakeholders: Privately owned water and sewage disposal companies, eligible limited-income customers of these companies, and other ratepayers (including nonlimited-income residential customers, small businesses, and local governments) who could see rate adjustments to fund assistance programs.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill can be implemented by the Public Service Commission using existing budgeted resources, with no effect on State revenues and no material impact on State expenditures. Local government revenues are unaffected; however, local governments and small businesses operating as customers of affected water or sewage companies could experience rate increases as early as fiscal 2028 to fund adopted limited-income mechanisms.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1164 directly tasks the Public Service Commission with studying the feasibility of requiring water and sewage disposal companies to adopt limited-income mechanisms, submitting a report by December 1, 2026, and authorizing the Commission to require and regulate such mechanisms beginning July 1, 2027.

The Office of the People's Counsel represents residential utility consumers before the Public Service Commission in rate and tariff matters, including proceedings involving private water utilities and limited-income affordability programs.

The Department of Human Services oversees the Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP), which is tasked under Section 4-309 with certifying participant eligibility if an approved limited-income mechanism requires income qualification verification.
The bill requires the Public Service Commission to report its feasibility findings on limited-income mechanisms directly to the Governor on or before December 1, 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires registered apprenticeship programs utilized by contractors on certain State procurements, prevailing wage public work contracts, and capital construction projects to maintain a completion rate of at least 25% if the program has graduated at least one apprenticeship cohort, as verified by the Maryland Department of Labor. It also modifies covered procurement requirements so that contractors must utilize a registered apprenticeship or eligible internship program for contracts valued at $1 million or more.
qa_results.stakeholders: State and local contractors and subcontractors, registered apprenticeship program sponsors, apprentices, and public contracting agencies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues for the State Apprenticeship Training Fund may increase beginning in FY 2027 to the extent contractors opt to pay into the fund rather than using an apprenticeship program, though a reliable estimate is not feasible. State and local procurement costs could potentially increase if reduced eligible apprenticeship programs limit bidder competition, though compliance payment alternatives may mitigate this effect. State agencies and local governments can implement the requirements with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MD Labor is the primary implementing agency responsible for verifying that apprenticeship programs meet the required 25% completion rate, overseeing registered apprenticeship programs, and administering the State Apprenticeship Training Fund.
Houses the Chief Procurement Officer, who is tasked with adopting regulations and establishing the criteria for 'covered procurements' subject to the apprenticeship requirements.
The Secretary of Information Technology must be consulted by the Chief Procurement Officer when establishing criteria and regulations for IT contracts subject to Title 3.5.
Statutorily responsible for accounting for the State Apprenticeship Training Fund, which receives contractor payments and penalty revenues affected by the bill.
Statutorily responsible for holding the State Apprenticeship Training Fund separately as a nonlapsing special fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the voting authority of the student member of the Howard County Board of Education to include decisions regarding geographical attendance areas, school construction and property acquisition or disposition, donations, condemnation, school consolidation and student transportation, budgetary matters, and student suspensions and expulsions.
qa_results.stakeholders: Howard County Board of Education members, the student board member, and students and staff of the Howard County Public School System.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state or local fiscal impact. The bill's provisions are procedural in nature and do not directly affect Howard County school finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees the state's public education system, comprising the 24 local school systems. While the bill specifically alters the voting rights of the student member on the Howard County Board of Education with no state fiscal impact, MSDE maintains overall policy and administrative oversight of public education governance across Maryland school districts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters provisions governing the Board of Directors of the Howard County Economic Development Authority by decreasing required board meetings from monthly to once every other month, repealing the designation of an ex officio nonvoting representative from the Mid-Maryland Private Industry Council, and changing the title of the Executive Director from Chief Administrative Officer to Chief Executive Officer.
qa_results.stakeholders: Board members and Executive Director of the Howard County Economic Development Authority, Howard County Government, and the Mid-Maryland Private Industry Council.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact and does not materially affect Howard County operations or finances. There is also no small business effect.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Howard County Executive, when submitting the annual budget to the Howard County Council, and the County Council, in its approved budget for the Howard County Board of Education, to state in writing the percentage of county general fund revenue (excluding one-time expenses) allocated to the school board operating budget and public school system operating costs, including pensions, benefits, debt service, safety, and transportation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Howard County Executive and Howard County Council
qa_results.stakeholders: Howard County Public School System, Howard County Board of Education, county officials, and Howard County taxpayers and residents.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: Howard County can implement the reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources, with no effect on revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends reporting requirements under Section 5-102 of the Education Article for Howard County's annual school operating budget. As approved local school budgets must be submitted to the State Superintendent of Schools, who heads the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), MSDE receives these updated reporting submissions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires a municipality seeking to annex land located in a different legislative district than the municipality to provide written notice via email and the U.S. Postal Service to the members of the General Assembly representing the affected legislative districts after introducing an annexation resolution.
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland municipalities, members of the General Assembly representing affected districts, and property owners in areas proposed for municipal annexation.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Planning provides data analysis, policy guidance, and technical assistance regarding local government land use, comprehensive planning, and municipal boundary changes such as annexations.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires the State Board of Architects to deny, suspend, revoke, or reprimand an architect's license or permit under specified disciplinary grounds, including fraudulent misrepresentation of holding a license or permit. It mandates that the Board notify county code officials when a license is suspended or revoked, requires local code officials to verify an architect's credentials before processing building permits, and authorizes the Board to create an electronic portal for anonymous reporting of suspected violations.
qa_results.stakeholders: Architects, applicants for architectural licenses and permits, county building code officials, and individuals reporting violations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Architects and local code officials can implement the requirements using existing resources. Special fund expenditures may increase minimally if the Board chooses to establish the optional anonymous reporting portal, but these expenditures are discretionary. State and local revenues are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Architects is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing. The bill directly impacts the Board's regulatory and disciplinary authority, notification requirements to local code officials, and options for complaint portals.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 1181 reforms the process for placing children in out-of-home care under Voluntary Placement Agreements (VPAs), specifically for children with developmental disabilities or mental illnesses requiring treatment. The bill establishes strict timelines for local departments of social services to assess requests and determine eligibility, clarifies that parents retain legal and educational decision-making rights without surrendering custody, and states that families need not exhaust all home- and community-based services before seeking out-of-home placement. It restricts referrals to child support enforcement for families entering VPAs, renders pre-existing child support arrears owed to the State under VPAs uncollectable, and mandates training, data collection, and reporting by the Department of Human Services and the Maryland Department of Health.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Human Services (Social Services Administration and Child Support Administration) and the Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Children with developmental disabilities, mental illnesses, or behavioral health needs; parents and legal guardians seeking residential or out-of-home care; local departments of social services; and behavioral health care providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $94,709 in FY 2027 (reflecting a 90-day start-up delay) and rise to $127,700 by FY 2031 for the Department of Human Services to hire one program manager for compliance, training, and reporting. Child Support Foster Care Offset special fund revenues may decrease indeterminately due to limits on child support collections. In addition, if child support provisions conflict with federal Title IV-E rules, federal funding ($751,912 in 2025) could be jeopardized. At the local level, Montgomery County expenditures increase by approximately $162,000 annually for two social workers and system upgrades.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Human Services (including the Social Services Administration and Child Support Administration) is the primary implementing agency. The bill sets strict assessment timelines for local departments, alters child support referral and enforcement rules for voluntary placement agreements, mandates staff training, requires data collection and publishing, and requires a joint report with the Department of Health.

The Maryland Department of Health is required to consult on annual training for local department staff, interfaces through local behavioral health authorities for psychiatric residential treatment referrals, and is required to jointly prepare and submit a major report on voluntary placement agreements and hospital overstays with the Department of Human Services.

The bill impacts judicial proceedings by requiring court findings for children in voluntary placements extending beyond 180 days, restricting court orders for child support under voluntary placements, and requiring the Child Support Enforcement Administration to file motions in court to modify existing child support orders.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes employees of the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission (WSSC) who are suspended for disciplinary purposes to appeal the suspension to the Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH), requiring OAH to dispose of the case or conduct a hearing and issue a final decision.
qa_results.stakeholders: Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission employees facing disciplinary suspensions
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local revenues are unaffected. Both the Office of Administrative Hearings and the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission can implement the bill's provisions using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 1185 directly expands the statutory duties of the Office of Administrative Hearings by requiring it to dispose of cases or conduct hearings and issue final decisions regarding appeals of disciplinary suspensions of Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission employees.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 1186 alters insurance and liability requirements for peer-to-peer (P2P) car sharing programs in Maryland. It repeals provisions making P2P program insurance automatically primary, permits required liability coverage to be maintained by the shared vehicle driver, exempts the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund (MAIF) from covering shared vehicles that are not replacement vehicles, allows auto insurers to cancel or exclude coverage for personal policies of vehicles used in car sharing, clarifies when P2P programs must provide primary coverage for third-party claims, authorizes programs to transfer liability and charge drivers for tolls and traffic citations incurred during sharing periods, and excludes P2P programs from being defined as owners for red light camera citations.
qa_results.stakeholders: Peer-to-peer car sharing platforms, shared vehicle owners, shared vehicle drivers, motor vehicle liability insurers, and the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration will increase minimally in FY 2027 from rate and form filing fees; enforcement can be handled with existing budgeted resources. Operations and finances of the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund are not materially affected. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill significantly amends the Insurance Article regarding motor vehicle liability insurance requirements, priority of coverage, and permitted policy exclusions for peer-to-peer car sharing programs, generating rate and form filings that MIA must review and regulate.

The bill explicitly amends statutory provisions concerning MAIF, stating that MAIF is not required to provide coverage to a shared vehicle driver for the use of a shared vehicle that is not a replacement vehicle, and clarifying MAIF's right to exclude coverage during the car sharing period.

The bill amends several sections of the Transportation Article regarding peer-to-peer car sharing requirements, mandatory security, fees/tolls, and vehicle owner definitions under traffic monitoring laws.

As the MDOT administration responsible for mandatory motor vehicle liability security (§ 17-103) and vehicle registration laws, MVA is affected by changes to required vehicle insurance standards and liability allocations.

The bill authorizes peer-to-peer car sharing programs to transfer monetary liability and charge drivers for any tolls incurred while the vehicle was in their possession, impacting toll violation and collection administration.

The bill excludes peer-to-peer car sharing programs from the definition of 'owner' for citations recorded by traffic control signal monitoring systems, which are adjudicated within the state court system.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 1192 expands the membership of the State Board of Sign Language Interpreters from 7 to 11 members, alters quorum and removal provisions, and extends key regulatory deadlines. It delays the requirement for the Board to publish licensing standards to July 1, 2027, and extends the deadline for sign language interpreters to obtain a license to January 1, 2028 (or July 1, 2028, for those working in educational settings). Additionally, it adds educational settings as a potential specialty area, requires a stakeholder report before specialty regulations are promulgated, adjusts application documentation and out-of-state waiver requirements, and mandates that public entities provide reasonable accommodations supporting deaf and hard of hearing individuals' format preferences for interpreting.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Sign Language Interpreters (within the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing)
qa_results.stakeholders: Sign language interpreters, deaf, deafblind, and hard of hearing individuals, interpreter agencies, and public/private entities utilizing sign language interpreters in legal, medical, or educational settings.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues from licensing fees ($150 initial fee) are delayed until FY 2028, as are any minimal general fund revenues from penalty provisions. Approximately 400 new licenses are projected initially in FY 2028, followed by roughly 200 annually. Special fund expenditures are not affected, and the Board and participating agencies can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Houses the State Board of Sign Language Interpreters, establishes the board nomination process, provides staff support for the specialist area report, and includes interpreter licensing statistics in its annual report.
The Secretary of Disabilities (or designee) is designated as an ex officio nonvoting member of the board, and the department must be consulted regarding the specialist area report.
The Secretary of Labor (or designee) is designated as an ex officio nonvoting member of the State Board of Sign Language Interpreters.
The Governor appoints all 11 members of the board, receives the annual report and specialist area report, and is granted explicit authority to remove members for excessive unexcused absences.
MSDE is a designated statutory consultee for the board's report on specialty areas, specifically concerning sign language interpreter standards in educational settings.
The Maryland Department of Health must be consulted by the board when completing the report evaluating interpreter specialist areas in medical and behavioral health settings.
The Maryland Judiciary must be consulted by the board regarding specialty area licensure and interpreter standards in legal settings.
Assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing appointments for the expanded 11-member board based on nominations from ODHH.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts retirees of the Correctional Officers' Retirement System from a retirement allowance earnings offset if they are reemployed as a bailiff in a Maryland State court.
qa_results.stakeholders: Retirees of the Correctional Officers' Retirement System who are reemployed as bailiffs in Maryland State courts.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill likely has no discernible or material effect on State or local pension liabilities or employer contribution rates because it applies to a limited number of individuals, and foregone offsets are not accounted for in calculating system liabilities. There is no effect on State or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the Correctional Officers' Retirement System (CORS) and the State Retirement and Pension System. It is directly responsible for administering the earnings offset rules, processing employer notifications, and adjusting retiree allowances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS employs the correctional officers who retire under CORS. In addition, the bill specifically mandates that the Commissioner of Correction, Commissioner of Pretrial Detention and Services, and Director of the Patuxent Institution include rehired retirees under the new bailiff exemption in their annual reporting to the Joint Committee on Pensions.

The Administrative Office of the Courts provides administrative, operational, and personnel support to Maryland's State courts, which employ bailiffs who will benefit from the reemployment earnings offset exemption.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of the Environment to develop an action plan for the enforcement of secondary maximum contaminant levels to address water discoloration, taste, and odor in community and nontransient, noncommunity water systems, consult with stakeholders, and report findings and recommendations to the General Assembly.
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners, operators, and residents of community water systems and nontransient, noncommunity water systems; community and nonprofit organizations representing affected residents; and the Maryland Rural Water Association.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of the Environment can develop the action plan, consult with stakeholders, and report findings to the General Assembly using existing budgeted resources. The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances or operations, as it requires the development of a plan rather than its implementation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) with developing an action plan for the enforcement of standards for secondary maximum contaminant levels (SMCLs) at community and nontransient, noncommunity water systems, consulting with relevant stakeholders, and reporting findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by December 1, 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: Adds a substitute member to the Garrett County Board of License Commissioners; creates a Special Event Permit for Class 3 and Class 4 wineries allowing on-premises consumption at private events; sets operational and staffing requirements for caterers and license holders exercising catering options; authorizes catering off-premises anywhere in the county; and requires alcoholic beverage license applicants to disclose citizenship or lawful immigration status.
qa_results.responsible_party: Garrett County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverage licensees (wineries, caterers, restaurants, hotels, resorts) and license applicants in Garrett County, catered event hosts and patrons, and the Garrett County Board of License Commissioners.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Garrett County expenditures increase by $3,000 annually beginning in FY 2027 to pay the salary of the new substitute board member. Garrett County revenues increase beginning in FY 2027 by an indeterminate amount from Special Event Permit fees ($1,750 annual permit fee plus an initial $1,750 issuing fee).

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Governor to appoint a new substitute member to the Board of License Commissioners for Garrett County, subject to legislative confirmation.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments to state and local boards, including the newly created substitute member seat on the Garrett County Board of License Commissioners.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes all Maryland counties, rather than only select specified jurisdictions, to honor certificates of guarantee issued by nonprofit contractor associations or their subsidiaries to fulfill county bond requirements, while clarifying that counties are not mandated to accept them.
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland county governments, construction contractors, and nonprofit contractor associations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected, as the Maryland Insurance Administration can enforce requirements within existing budgeted resources. Local fiscal impact is expected to be minimal because counties are permitted, but not required, to honor certificates of guarantee.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends Section 1-203 of the Insurance Article regarding certificates of guarantee for county bond requirements. The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates insurance practices in the state and can enforce the bill's provisions with existing budgeted resources.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Safe and Healthy Homes for All Act requires the Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs within the Department of Housing and Community Development, in collaboration with the Attorney General, to develop a comprehensive plan to identify severe health and safety risk multi-unit rental properties (properties with 50 or more units), expand office capacity, and implement effective interventions against negligent landlords. The department must publicly post the identified properties on its website and submit the plan, recommendations, and a follow-up report to the Governor and General Assembly.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development, Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs
qa_results.stakeholders: Renters and tenants living in multi-unit rental properties with 50 or more units, landlords and property owners of large residential rental properties, tenant advocacy organizations, and local housing agencies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $248,500 in FY 2027 for two contractual positions (a program manager and community assistant) and one-time contracting services ($100,000), followed by an increase of $84,700 in FY 2028 for ongoing costs until the bill's termination on December 31, 2027. State revenues are unaffected, and local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD and its Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs (OTLA) are the primary entities tasked with developing the plan to identify severe health and safety risk properties, publishing the list on its website, submitting reports and recommendations, and incurs direct fiscal expenditures.
The bill explicitly mandates that the Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs develop the plan and interventions in collaboration with the Attorney General.
DHCD is required to submit the plan, recommended statutory changes, and final report directly to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the University System of Maryland to conduct a study evaluating the relationship between climate change, homeowner's insurance availability and pricing, and emergency disaster preparedness, and to submit a report with recommendations to the General Assembly by July 1, 2027.
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland homeowners, residential property insurance policyholders, insurance companies and agents, and state and local emergency management agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund (Strategic Energy Investment Fund) expenditures increase by $100,000 in FY 2027 to fund the study. Higher education expenditures could increase by up to an additional $200,000 to cover total study costs (estimated at $200,000 to $300,000), which would be offset by general funds or higher education revenues. Local governments and other participating state agencies can coordinate using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: USM is the primary implementing agency directed by the bill to conduct a comprehensive study evaluating the relationship between climate change, homeowner's insurance availability and cost, and emergency preparedness, and submit findings to the General Assembly by July 1, 2027.

MDEM is statutorily mandated to coordinate with and oversee USM's study, which directly evaluates emergency management funding, FEMA capabilities, and modifications to the State Disaster Recovery Fund administered by MDEM.

MIA is required to coordinate with and oversee the study, which focuses heavily on homeowner's insurance pricing, private flood insurance markets, and potential modifications to the Insurance Article.

MDE is designated to coordinate with and provide oversight for the study, which intersects directly with the department's responsibilities for flood hazard management and state climate resilience policies.
DNR is statutorily designated to participate in the coordination and oversight of the study examining climate change impacts and resilience measures.
MEA administers the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), from which the bill authorizes and expends up to $100,000 to fund USM's study.

qa_results.bill_summary: The Jillian and Lindsay Wiener Short-Term Rental Safety Act establishes fire safety standards for short-term rental units rented for under 30 consecutive days. It requires hosts to post evacuation diagrams and emergency phone numbers, provide working fire extinguishers, and install interconnected smoke and carbon monoxide alarms. Booking services must notify hosts of these rules and verify compliance documentation. Additionally, by July 1, 2028, counties and Baltimore City (unless short-term rentals are banned) must establish annual inspection requirements and report compliance to the State Fire Marshal, who must report to the General Assembly.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the State Fire Marshal
qa_results.stakeholders: Short-term rental hosts, booking services/platforms, short-term rental guests, third-party fire safety inspectors, and county and Baltimore City inspection agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not expected to be materially affected as the Office of the State Fire Marshal can implement the requirements with existing resources. Local government expenditures increase to conduct annual inspections and hire inspection personnel (e.g., Montgomery County estimates $152,460 and Harford County estimates $200,000 in fiscal 2027), though these costs may be offset by local inspection fees authorized under the bill.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the State Fire Marshal (OSFM) and the State Fire Prevention Commission operate within the Maryland Department of State Police. The bill tasks the State Fire Marshal with establishing qualifications, certifications, and licensing standards for third-party inspectors, approving alternative smoke alarm standards, collecting annual inspection compliance reports from local jurisdictions, and submitting a final report to the General Assembly.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the annual salary of the Prince George's County State's Attorney from $199,000 to $250,000, taking effect at the beginning of the next term of office.
qa_results.stakeholders: Prince George's County State's Attorney and Prince George's County government/taxpayers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected. Prince George's County local expenditures increase by $40,371 in FY 2027 (reflecting the term starting in December 2026) and by $69,207 annually thereafter to account for the salary increase and fringe benefits. Revenues are not affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission's (WSSC) procurement programs by replacing its local small business enterprise program with a broader business participation program. It expands eligibility to include local businesses, small businesses, Maryland-based businesses, and veteran- and disabled veteran-owned businesses, giving preference to local and local small businesses. It also permits vendor reciprocity and self-certification, repeals the statutory name of the Office of Supplier Diversity and Inclusion to allow WSSC to rename it by regulation, and authorizes WSSC to adopt regulations encouraging workforce engagement and local economic benefits.
qa_results.stakeholders: Local businesses in Montgomery and Prince George's counties, Maryland-based businesses, small businesses, veteran- and disabled veteran-owned businesses, and contractors bidding on WSSC contracts.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Effect: None. Local Effect: None. According to the fiscal note, the bill's changes are procedural in nature and do not directly affect state or local government revenues or expenditures.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Baltimore City Board of Estimates to enter into payment in lieu of taxes (PILOT) agreements to provide full or partial real property tax exemptions for qualifying newly constructed or rehabilitated commercial and multifamily residential economic development projects in Baltimore City's Downtown RISE District.
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial and multifamily residential real estate developers, property owners in Baltimore City's Downtown RISE District, and Baltimore City government and residents.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect is none. Baltimore City property tax revenues may decrease beginning in FY 2027 depending on the number and assessed value of participating economic development projects; this decrease will be partially mitigated by payments negotiated under the PILOT agreements. Potential job creation may also increase local income tax revenues. Specific dollar estimates are not provided.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Critical Infrastructure Protection Branch within the Maryland Coordination and Analysis Center, led by an appointed Chief Critical Infrastructure Officer, to evaluate threats, conduct voluntary cyber and physical assessments, and prioritize critical infrastructure assets. The bill also requires the Maryland Department of Emergency Management to coordinate consequence management efforts following attacks, and requires the Department of Information Technology to provide cybersecurity standards and allow critical infrastructure owners and operators to join the Maryland Information Sharing and Analysis Center.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Coordination and Analysis Center (MCAC), Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM), and Department of Information Technology (DoIT)
qa_results.stakeholders: Public and private owners and operators of critical infrastructure (including hospitals and health care facilities), State and local emergency management agencies, and Maryland residents dependent on critical infrastructure systems.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact because it generally codifies an existing branch within MCAC, and MDEM and DoIT can implement their required duties using existing resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no anticipated material fiscal impact on local governments or small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill statutorily requires the Department of Emergency Management, in consultation with the Maryland Coordination and Analysis Center, to coordinate consequence management efforts and respond to cascading impacts of an attack on the State's critical infrastructure.

The bill mandates the Department of Information Technology (and its Office of Security Management) to coordinate on threat determinations, allow critical infrastructure owners/operators to join the Maryland Information Sharing and Analysis Center, provide cybersecurity reporting standards, and direct critical infrastructure cybersecurity efforts across State government.

The Maryland Coordination and Analysis Center (MCAC), which houses the newly established Critical Infrastructure Protection Branch and whose Executive Director must appoint the Chief Critical Infrastructure Officer, is operated within the Department of State Police.

The bill specifies that the Chief Critical Infrastructure Officer must coordinate with and advise the Director of the Governor's Office of Homeland Security on critical infrastructure security issues.
The bill specifically requires the Critical Infrastructure Protection Branch to coordinate with the Public Service Commission to determine threat levels to the State's critical infrastructure.
The bill explicitly requires the Chief Critical Infrastructure Officer to coordinate with the National Guard regarding critical infrastructure security efforts.
The bill requires the Chief Critical Infrastructure Officer to advise the Governor on critical infrastructure security issues and aligns with executive homeland security priorities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts certain personal property used in manufacturing from municipal corporation personal property taxes in Prince George's County for businesses that hold an alcoholic beverages manufacturer's license and employ 50 or fewer workers.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Small alcoholic beverage manufacturers with 50 or fewer employees in Prince George's County (specifically one brewery in Riverdale Park) and municipal corporations in Prince George's County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. At the local level, property tax revenues for the Town of Riverdale Park decrease by approximately $12,500 annually beginning in fiscal year 2027 due to the exemption of personal property for a local brewery assessed at $626,240. Local expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a specific personal property tax exemption for qualifying small alcohol manufacturing businesses in Prince George's County. The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board handles administrative appeals concerning personal property valuations and tax exemptions.
The Maryland Tax Court is the highest level of administrative review for tax disputes, including appeals of decisions concerning personal property assessments and exemptions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the definition of an extraordinary development district under tax increment financing law to include sites for immersive entertainment venues (privately owned venues with at least 3,000 seats and development costs of at least $500 million). Authorizes Prince George's County or its revenue authority to use bond proceeds for the acquisition, construction, or rehabilitation of such venues, allows the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission to pledge certain property taxes to secure county bonds, establishes that exterior displays are not considered signs under local zoning, and authorizes the Secretary of Transportation to grant related regulatory waivers.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prince George's County Government, Prince George's County Revenue Authority, and the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Prince George's County taxpayers and local government, the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission, private commercial developers of entertainment venues, and regional tourism and hospitality industries.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected. Prince George's County revenues and expenditures increase beginning as early as FY 2026 from bond issuances, tax increment financing, and debt service payments. A portion of property tax revenues collected by the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission may be redirected into the county's special fund to secure county-issued bonds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds § 8-706 to the Transportation Article, granting the Secretary of Transportation specific statutory authority to issue waivers or exceptions for outdoor advertising and signage provisions that require State approval for immersive entertainment venues.

Title 8 of the Transportation Article governs state highways, including outdoor advertising and roadside signage regulations under Subtitle 7, which the State Highway Administration administers and oversees.

The bill modifies the Economic Development Article regarding tax increment financing districts and immersive entertainment venues to bolster tourism and economic development, and the department was consulted in the development of the fiscal note.
The bill amends provisions in the Land Use Article regarding tax increment financing districts and zoning compliance, and the department was consulted as an information source for the fiscal note.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Workgroup for an Inclusive State Workplace to study and recommend ways to expand part-time State employment opportunities for individuals facing barriers under traditional full-time employment structures. The workgroup must submit a final report by September 15, 2027, and the Department of Budget and Management must develop and distribute guidance to State agencies based on these recommendations by December 31, 2027.
qa_results.stakeholders: State agencies, current and prospective State employees, and individuals seeking part-time employment with benefits (such as caregivers, individuals with disabilities, and older adults)
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not materially affected, as the Department of Budget and Management can staff the workgroup and issue agency guidance with existing budgeted resources, and any member expense reimbursements are minimal and absorbable. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM is the lead agency responsible for staffing the Workgroup for an Inclusive State Workplace. The Secretary serves as a member, and DBM is tasked with developing and issuing guidance to all State agencies on expanding part-time employment opportunities based on the Workgroup's findings.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill statutorily creates a temporary advisory body, the Workgroup for an Inclusive State Workplace, to study and issue recommendations on expanding inclusive part-time employment opportunities in State government.

The Secretary of Transportation (or designee) is designated as a member of the Workgroup, and the Workgroup is specifically directed to examine and outline steps to encourage the expansion of part-time employment within the Department of Transportation.

The Chancellor (or designee) is designated as a member of the Workgroup, and the Workgroup is explicitly tasked with outlining steps to encourage the expansion of part-time employment within the University System of Maryland.
The Secretary of Disabilities (or designee) serves on the Workgroup, which focuses on identifying and removing barriers to State employment for individuals with disabilities.

The Secretary of Aging (or designee) is a designated member of the Workgroup, which is tasked with studying inclusive employment pathways for older adults challenged by traditional full-time structures.
The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) serves as a designated member of the Workgroup.
The Secretary of Health (or designee) serves as a designated member of the Workgroup.
The Secretary of Information Technology (or designee) serves as a designated member of the Workgroup.
The Comptroller (or designee) serves as a designated member of the Workgroup.

The Governor is responsible for designating the chair of the Workgroup and appointing stakeholder members, including union, caregiving, disability, healthcare, older adult, and labor economics representatives.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and processing candidates for appointment to the newly established Workgroup.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits credentialing entities for certified recovery residences from allowing residences to refuse services to individuals receiving medication-assisted treatment (MAT) for opioid use disorder, or requiring an individual to stop or modify their MAT regimen as a condition of receiving services.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health's Behavioral Health Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals receiving medication-assisted treatment (MAT) for opioid use disorder and operators of certified recovery residences in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Behavioral Health Administration already maintains nondiscrimination policies, so codifying this practice does not affect revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH), specifically through its Behavioral Health Administration (BHA), approves the credentialing entity that establishes certification requirements, monitors, and certifies recovery residences across the state. This bill sets mandatory statutory requirements for those credentialing standards regarding medication-assisted treatment (MAT).

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development to study housing availability and affordability in Montgomery County, identify development prospects and regulatory impacts, and issue interim reports in 2027 and 2028 followed by a final report in 2029.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Montgomery County residents, renters and prospective homebuyers, housing developers, and Montgomery County government agencies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $50,000 annually in FY 2027 through FY 2029 (totaling $150,000) for the Department of Housing and Community Development to hire an outside consultant to conduct the required study and analysis. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) is the primary implementing agency tasked with conducting the study on housing availability and affordability in Montgomery County, issuing interim and final reports, and conferring with local agencies, resulting in an estimated general fund expenditure increase of $50,000 annually from FY 2027 through FY 2029.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes land use and zoning requirements for the Patuxent Research Refuge and the Beltsville Agricultural Research Center by requiring local zoning authorities to designate and maintain federally owned portions of these properties in open space, reserved open space, or resource conservation zoning classifications, and prohibiting commercial, industrial, or residential uses if transferred or encumbered. It also prohibits converting central natural areas to agricultural, active recreational, forestry, or plant-harvesting uses, and mandates a public hearing and state environmental agency consultation before any development is approved.
qa_results.responsible_party: Local zoning authorities (including the Anne Arundel County Council and the Maryland-Washington Regional District Councils), in consultation with the Maryland Department of Natural Resources and the Maryland Department of the Environment.
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents, property developers, and local communities in Anne Arundel and Prince George's counties, as well as conservationists and visitors of the Patuxent Research Refuge and Beltsville Agricultural Research Center.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances, according to the Department of Legislative Services.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that local zoning authorities must consult with the Department of Natural Resources prior to making a final decision approving any proposed development on land within the Patuxent Research Refuge or the Beltsville Agricultural Research Center to ensure it will not substantially impact a central natural area.

The bill explicitly requires local zoning authorities to consult with the Maryland Department of the Environment before approving any development on Patuxent Research Refuge or Beltsville Agricultural Research Center land, confirming the proposed development will not have a substantial impact on central natural areas.

The Department of Planning serves as the state's principal agency for comprehensive land use planning policy and resource preservation, and it provided information on the bill's land use and zoning mandates.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Neighborhood Social Connection and Development Program within the West North Avenue Development Authority (WNADA) to provide technical support and award grants to community organizations for initiatives that foster social connection and community development along the West North Avenue Corridor in Baltimore City. It also expands the purpose of the Continuing the CORE Partnership Fund within the Department of Housing and Community Development to assist WNADA in removing blighted property.
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents, community development corporations, neighborhood associations, nonprofit organizations, and volunteer groups within the West North Avenue Corridor in Baltimore City.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures in total are likely unaffected, though WNADA may redirect up to $150,000 annually in existing funds from other priorities to award grants under the program. Expanding the purpose of the Continuing the CORE Partnership Fund to include WNADA blight removal projects has no effect on overall State finances. State revenues and Baltimore City finances and operations are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Housing and Community Development Article regarding the Continuing the CORE Partnership Fund, expanding the fund's purpose to assist the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD), in conjunction with the West North Avenue Development Authority, in removing blighted property in Baltimore City.

The Maryland Stadium Authority is a statutory partner with DHCD under the Continuing the CORE Partnership Fund for blighted property removal in Baltimore City, a section amended by the bill to include the West North Avenue Development Authority.
The bill requires the West North Avenue Development Authority to submit an annual report to the Governor detailing its comprehensive grant-awarding activities under the new program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the criteria that regulations governing the application process for the Catalytic Revitalization Project Tax Credit must emphasize to include applications that promote workforce housing, in addition to affordable housing.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Developers and sponsors of catalytic revitalization projects, households eligible for workforce housing, and communities where revitalization projects are located.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Overall State and local revenues and expenditures are not affected. The bill may alter the allocation of existing tax credit awards among qualifying projects with varying timelines and costs. The Department of Housing and Community Development can update relevant regulations using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Housing and Community Development administers the Catalytic Revitalization Project Tax Credit program and is required to adopt updated regulations establishing an application process that emphasizes applications promoting workforce housing.

The bill requires the Secretary of Housing and Community Development to consult with the Department of Commerce when adopting regulations governing the application process and standards for the tax credit.
The Comptroller administers the State income tax system through which taxpayers claim the Catalytic Revitalization Project Tax Credit against their tax liability.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 1280 requires the University of Maryland, College Park, with assistance from the Department of Human Services and in consultation with the Office of the Comptroller, to study and make recommendations on the feasibility of establishing and operating the Supporting Our Caregiver Infrastructure Program. The proposed program would provide universal monthly payments/stipends to caregivers for each qualified dependent in their care. A final report of findings and recommendations must be submitted to the General Assembly by July 1, 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: University of Maryland, College Park (with assistance from the Department of Human Services)
qa_results.stakeholders: Caregivers caring for qualified family members (individuals age 60 and older, individuals with Alzheimer's disease, and children or adults with developmental or functional disabilities) and dependent care recipients.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: University System of Maryland higher education expenditures increase by $490,000 in FY 2027 only for the University of Maryland, College Park to conduct the study and complete the report. The Department of Human Services and the Office of the Comptroller can perform their required advisory and support roles with existing resources. There is no effect on State revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the University of Maryland, College Park (a constituent institution of USM) lead and conduct the feasibility study and report on the Supporting Our Caregiver Infrastructure Program, resulting in an estimated higher education expenditure increase of $490,000 in FY 2027.

The bill requires the Department of Human Services to directly assist UMCP by identifying federal, State, and local funding sources, determining administrative and operating costs, and consulting with partner agencies.
The bill requires UMCP to consult with the Office of the Comptroller to examine the economic impacts of the program, including effects on state and local economies and enhanced tax revenues.
The bill explicitly mandates that the Department of Human Services consult with the Maryland Department of Aging in conducting the caregiver program feasibility study.
The bill explicitly requires the Department of Human Services to consult with the Maryland Department of Health as part of the feasibility study.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes residential service agencies (RSAs) providing private duty nursing services to hire licensed nurses who do not meet clinical experience requirements, provided the RSA implements an approved training program, assigns clinical supervision and preceptors, and conducts regular competency evaluations approved by the Maryland Department of Health.
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential service agencies (RSAs), licensed nurses providing private duty nursing, and patients receiving home health care services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $204,857 in FY 2027, comprising $99,736 in general fund expenditures for the Office of Health Care Quality and $105,121 in Medicaid expenditures (50% general funds, 50% federal funds) to hire two new staff members. Federal fund revenues increase by $52,560 in FY 2027 from Medicaid matching funds. Future years reflect ongoing salary and operational costs. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH), specifically through its Office of Health Care Quality and Medicaid administration, is the primary regulatory agency tasked with implementing the bill. MDH must adopt regulations, review and approve residential service agency training programs and competency evaluations, conduct provider audits, and investigate complaints, resulting in direct fiscal and operational impacts including the need for additional staff.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands the existing barbershop and beauty salon alcoholic beverages license in Anne Arundel County to include liquor, permitting license holders to provide customers with up to 1.7 ounces of liquor for on-premises consumption during a visit.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Barbershop and beauty salon owners, employees, and customers in Anne Arundel County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact and is not anticipated to materially affect Anne Arundel County revenues or expenditures. The annual license fee remains unchanged at $100.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is responsible for alcohol tax collection and general regulation of the alcoholic beverages industry in Maryland. While local licensing and enforcement in Anne Arundel County are handled by the local board of license commissioners, the expansion of permitted alcoholic beverage offerings (to include liquor) touches on the broader regulatory framework for alcohol.

The Department of Labor oversees occupational licensing boards, including the State Board of Barbers and the State Board of Cosmetologists, which issue the underlying barbershop and beauty salon permits referenced as prerequisites for this alcoholic beverages license.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 1300 renames the African American Heritage Preservation Program to be the Speaker Adrienne A. Jones African American Heritage Preservation Program, modifies the statutory duties and focus areas of the Maryland Commission for Women, and reclassifies the Commission's executive director position from a special appointment to the skilled service under the State Personnel Management System.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Human Services and the Maryland Commission for Women
qa_results.stakeholders: Women in Maryland, women's advocacy and community organizations, state personnel within the Maryland Commission for Women, and applicants or beneficiaries of the African American Heritage Preservation Program.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State fiscal impact is negligible; any cost associated with the Department of Human Services reclassifying the executive director position into the skilled service is minimal, and the Maryland Commission for Women can implement the altered duties using existing budgeted resources. Renaming the preservation program has no financial impact. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Commission for Women is housed within the Department of Human Services. The bill removes the Secretary of Human Services' direct appointment power for the commission's executive director, shifts the position to skilled service, and substantially revises the statutory duties of the commission.

The Maryland Historical Trust, which is housed within the Department of Planning, administers the African American Heritage Preservation Program under State Finance and Procurement Article § 5A-330, which the bill officially renames.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the statutory duties, powers, and governance structure of the Maryland Commission for Women, an executive advisory body.
The bill amends the Housing and Community Development Article (§ 6-212) to update statutory references to the renamed program within the Sustainable Communities funding priority provisions.

DBM administers the State Personnel Management System (SPMS), and the bill specifies that the executive director of the Commission for Women is not a special appointee and must be placed in the skilled service within SPMS.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) to annually include college enrollment and six-year graduation rates of foster youth in its child welfare reporting, along with comparison data for students not in the welfare system where appropriate. It also requires MSDE, in collaboration with the Department of Human Services (DHS), to submit a report by December 1, 2026, outlining recommendations, service gaps, and best practices to improve educational and career outcomes for children and foster youth in the State child welfare system.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education (in cooperation with the Department of Human Services)
qa_results.stakeholders: Children and foster youth in the Maryland child welfare system, foster students, and public education administrators.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local fiscal impact is none. The Maryland State Department of Education and the Department of Human Services can meet the reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary agency tasked with expanding its annual reporting on children and foster youth in the child welfare system to include college enrollment and six-year graduation data, alongside comparison data. MSDE is also required to lead the development of a comprehensive report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2026, on improving educational outcomes for students in foster care.

DHS oversees the State's child welfare and foster care systems. The bill requires MSDE to report child welfare educational outcomes to DHS annually and requires DHS to cooperate with MSDE in developing and submitting the study on improving educational outcomes for foster youth.

The MLDS Center maintains the longitudinal data linking public K-12 student records with postsecondary enrollment and completion data, which is necessary to track and report on college enrollment and six-year graduation rates for foster youth.

MHEC coordinates postsecondary education data and administers state financial aid programs (including tuition waivers for foster youth); it serves as a key data contributor regarding postsecondary enrollment and degree attainment.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the Child Care Scholarship (CCS) Program by repealing the presumptive eligibility process and authorizing the Maryland State Department of Education to establish a sliding fee copayment scale for families with household income above the federal poverty line (capped at 7% of income). It exempts families at or below the federal poverty line and recipients of certain public assistance programs from copays. Additionally, during an enrollment freeze, the Department must identify, inform, and assist eligible applicants in accessing publicly funded prekindergarten, Head Start, or Early Head Start programs.
qa_results.stakeholders: Low- and moderate-income families seeking or receiving child care assistance, children eligible for child care subsidies or prekindergarten, and participating child care providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $749,700 in FY 2027 to cover 1.0 new program manager position and $650,000 in one-time programming changes, with ongoing annual personnel and operating costs ranging from $118,200 in FY 2028 to $134,800 in FY 2031. Implementing sliding-scale copays and repealing presumptive eligibility are expected to offset scholarship costs, allowing over 1,000 additional children to be served without expanding total program grant spending. State revenues and local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the Child Care Scholarship (CCS) Program administered by the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE). It authorizes MSDE to establish a sliding fee copayment scale, eliminates copayments for households at or below the federal poverty level, repeals presumptive eligibility provisions, sets requirements to assist waitlisted applicants with Pre-K and Head Start enrollment, and requires reporting to the General Assembly, incurring direct fiscal and operational impacts on the department.
Under the statute governing the Child Care Scholarship Program, the Comptroller is responsible for issuing payments to child care providers within five days of receiving notice from MSDE.

qa_results.bill_summary: Decreases the archery hunting safety zone in Baltimore City (except in Legislative District 43A) from 150 yards to 50 yards from a dwelling house, residence, church, or other building or camp occupied by humans.
qa_results.stakeholders: Archery hunters, private property owners, and residents in Baltimore City (excluding Legislative District 43A)
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Natural Resources Article to decrease the archery hunting safety zone in Baltimore City (with an exception for Legislative District 43A) from 150 yards to 50 yards. The Department of Natural Resources regulates hunting seasons and safety regulations and enforces wildlife and hunting laws through the Natural Resources Police.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 1326 authorizes the Department of Human Services to disclose reports or records of child abuse or neglect, following a finalized finding of indicated abuse or neglect, to certain child care center administrators, youth sports program personnel, and organizations responsible for supervising or caring for children to determine an individual's suitability for employment or voluntary service.
qa_results.stakeholders: Minors participating in sports or child care, administrators and coaches of youth sports programs, child care centers, child-supervising organizations, and individuals applying for employment or volunteer roles with these entities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Department of Legislative Services, the Department of Human Services can implement the bill using existing resources, with no effect on revenues. While DHS estimated an annual expenditure increase of approximately $567,000 for additional staff, DLS determined additional positions are not necessary. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends provisions governing the Department of Human Services (DHS) by expanding its authority to disclose reports and records of indicated child abuse or neglect to certain child care, youth sports, and child supervision entities for employment and volunteer suitability determinations.

The bill references child care centers, letters of compliance, and nonpublic schools regulated or registered under the State Department of Education, which also provided information for the fiscal analysis.
The bill updates a statutory reference removing the Juvenile Justice Monitoring Unit from the Office of the Attorney General to reflect its transfer to the Office of the Correctional Ombudsman.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the application cycle for the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit Program to allow homeowners to apply on a year-round basis by extending the application deadline from October 1 to February 14 of the taxable year.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Eligible Maryland homeowners applying for the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit, as well as local governments that offer supplemental property tax credits.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $168,200 annually beginning in FY 2028 to fund additional property tax credits, though the actual increase could be higher depending on late applicants. State revenues are unaffected. Local governments providing a supplement to the State credit may see an indeterminate decrease in local property tax revenues to the extent more homeowners qualify.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill increases State general fund expenditures by an estimated $168,200 annually beginning in FY 2028 to fund additional homeowners' property tax credits resulting from the expanded year-round application window, impacting DBM's oversight of the State budget and expenditure planning.

PTAAB is responsible for hearing administrative appeals concerning property tax credits and exemptions determined by SDAT; altering application deadlines and eligibility procedures for the homeowners' property tax credit directly affects the timing and nature of potential appeals.

The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest administrative appellate body for disputes concerning state property tax credits and appeals arising from decisions of the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board.
