agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and fiscal planning. The bill establishes an indefinite, mandated general fund appropriation of $10 million annually beginning in FY 2029.
The bill statutorily requires the Governor to include an ongoing appropriation of $10 million in the annual state budget bill for the medical center beyond FY 2028.
The bill amends the Health - General Article concerning state funding to support critical healthcare services, clinical programs, and regional health delivery at the medical center.
USM was an information source for the fiscal analysis due to the close academic and clinical relationship between the University of Maryland Medical System and USM institutions.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 1554 requires the Office of the Comptroller, in consultation with the Public Service Commission and PJM Interconnection, to study and report to the General Assembly on exempting electricity used for agricultural purposes from the State sales and use tax, including an estimate of the exemption's fiscal impact.
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland farmers and agricultural producers, electric companies, and the Office of the Comptroller.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Comptroller's Office may increase in FY 2027 to conduct the required study. State revenues are not affected. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1554 explicitly directs the Office of the Comptroller to lead, prepare, and submit the required study and report regarding sales and use tax exemptions on electricity for agricultural purposes, and the office may incur fiscal expenditures to conduct the study.

The bill explicitly mandates that the Comptroller conduct the study in consultation with the Public Service Commission, which regulates the electric companies that supply power and hold customer billing and usage data.

The study directly evaluates tax relief intended to lower operating costs for agricultural activities (livestock, poultry, soil irrigation, and crop handling), aligning with the Department's mission to support the economic viability of Maryland farming and agribusiness.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill establishes a Real Estate Advisory Committee within the Department of General Services (DGS) to advise DGS, the Board of Public Works (BPW), and the General Assembly on commercial real estate trends and asset management best practices. It also applies requirements for BPW review and reporting to the Legislative Policy Committee for high-value property acquisitions and long-term, high-cost leases, and establishes community engagement conditions for the disposition of a specific Baltimore City parcel.
qa_results.stakeholders: State agencies acquiring or leasing commercial real estate, commercial property owners and lessors doing business with the State, and Baltimore City residents in the Guilford Avenue area affected by property disposition.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $90,008 in FY 2027, rising to $121,000 by FY 2031, to hire one administrative staff member within the Department of General Services to prepare required submissions for the Legislative Policy Committee and staff the advisory committee. There is no effect on State revenues and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes the Real Estate Advisory Committee within DGS, requiring the Department to provide staff, have the Secretary designate the chair and appoint members, and manage additional reporting, justification, and cost-benefit analysis requirements for significant real estate acquisitions and leases, resulting in a general fund expenditure increase of approximately $90,000 for a new position.

The bill requires the new Real Estate Advisory Committee to advise BPW and report to it annually. It also modifies BPW approval requirements for real property acquisitions and high-value leases by mandating specific justifications and analyses be submitted to the Legislative Policy Committee.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new permanent advisory body within the executive branch—the Real Estate Advisory Committee—to advise state leadership on commercial real estate trends and state asset management best practices.

As an agency that manages state-owned property and leases, MDOT is identified in the fiscal note as responsible for producing and disseminating required justifications and analyses for qualifying real estate transactions to the Legislative Policy Committee.

As an entity managing significant state property and leases, USM is identified in the fiscal note as responsible for compiling and submitting required justifications and cost-benefit analyses for qualifying acquisitions and leases.
The Governor is a statutory recipient of the Real Estate Advisory Committee's annual report of findings and recommendations regarding state real estate asset management.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill prohibits the Department of Human Services' out-of-home placement program from placing children in unlicensed settings, including hotels, motels, homeless shelters, office buildings, and pediatric hospital overstay settings. It establishes a Child and Youth Placement Review Panel and a Senior Advisor for Children and Families within the Governor's Office for Children, requires Rapid Response Placement Teams to address pediatric hospital overstays within 48 to 72 hours, and establishes the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care for Children, Youth, and Families.
qa_results.stakeholders: Children and youth in out-of-home placements, pediatric hospital overstay patients, foster care providers, hospitals, and child welfare agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures for the Governor's Office for Children increase by $204,600 in FY 2027 to hire one contractual Senior Advisor and one permanent policy advisor, with costs ranging between $121,000 and $252,300 in subsequent fiscal years. The Maryland Department of Health and the Department of Human Services can absorb duties with existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Child and Youth Placement Review Panel and the Senior Advisor for Children and Families within GOC, tasks GOC with staffing both the Review Panel and the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care for Children, Youth, and Families, and incurs operational and staffing expenditures.

DHS is prohibited from placing children in unlicensed settings under its out-of-home placement program, employs a pediatric overstay coordinator with expanded reporting duties, is authorized to execute emergency procurements for placements, serves on the Review Panel and Advisory Council, and must submit a progress report to the General Assembly.

MDH employs a pediatric overstay coordinator with expanded data collection and reporting duties, designates the reporting system for hospitals notifying coordinators of overstay patients, serves on the Review Panel and Advisory Council, and jointly submits a required report with DHS.

The Secretary of Juvenile Services is designated as a member of both the Child and Youth Placement Review Panel and the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care for Children, Youth, and Families, and DJS residential programs are potential placement referral options.

The State Superintendent of Schools is designated as a member of the Child and Youth Placement Review Panel and the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care for Children, Youth, and Families; the bill also monitors emergency petitions executed in schools.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally establishes two new executive bodies: the Child and Youth Placement Review Panel and the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care for Children, Youth, and Families (along with Rapid Response Placement Teams).
The Secretary of Disabilities is designated as an ex officio member of the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care for Children, Youth, and Families.
The Maryland Insurance Commissioner is designated as an ex officio member of the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care for Children, Youth, and Families.
The Executive Director of the Maryland Health Care Commission is designated as an ex officio member of the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care for Children, Youth, and Families.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Defender is designated as an ex officio member of the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care for Children, Youth, and Families.

The Governor appoints the Senior Advisor for Children and Families and several appointed stakeholder members of the Review Panel and Advisory Council, and receives annual reports from the Advisory Council.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to examine health insurance carriers showing a pattern of adverse decisions or grievances regarding emergency department services and to require independent reviews at carrier expense. It requires the Commissioner's annual appeals report to include post-acute care data, and directs the Maryland Health Care Commission, in conjunction with the Health Services Cost Review Commission, to conduct studies by January 1, 2027, quantifying hospital and post-acute bed capacity and evaluating options to facilitate transitions from acute to post-acute care.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Commissioner (Maryland Insurance Administration), Maryland Health Care Commission, and Health Services Cost Review Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, private review agents, patients receiving emergency and post-acute care, hospitals, and post-acute care facilities (such as skilled nursing and inpatient rehabilitation facilities).
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) special fund revenues may increase minimally to recoup the costs of any examinations, which are billed to carriers. Any additional workload for MIA, the Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC), and the Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC) can be handled using existing budgeted resources. Local effect: None.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to examine carriers regarding emergency department claims/authorizations and mandates the inclusion of post-acute services data in the annual appeals and grievances report.

The bill directly tasks the Commission with conducting two studies by January 1, 2027: one quantifying bed capacity in hospitals and post-acute care settings, and another analyzing options to facilitate transitions from acute to post-acute care settings.

The bill requires the Commission, in conjunction with the Maryland Health Care Commission, to conduct the studies on hospital/post-acute bed capacity and transitions of care, and report findings to the Governor and General Assembly.
The Maryland Health Care Commission is an independent agency housed within MDH, and the Secretary of Health provides information regarding HMO appeals and grievances referenced in the bill analysis.
The Governor is a mandated recipient of the reports and recommendations on bed capacity and acute-to-post-acute care transitions by January 1, 2027.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill reauthorizes and extends the termination date for Maryland's Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) Program and related requirements across state procurement, cannabis licensing, public-private partnerships, offshore wind projects, video lottery terminals, and sports wagering by five years, to July 1, 2031. It adopts updated legislative findings based on the 2025 disparity study, establishes quarterly reporting requirements for state procurement units, updates annual reporting deadlines, expands the definition of small business to include certain joint ventures, and requires the Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs to establish a small business certification review process.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs (within the Maryland Department of Social and Economic Mobility)
qa_results.stakeholders: Minority-, women-, and veteran-owned businesses; small businesses and qualifying joint ventures; state prime contractors; state procurement agencies; and licensees/developers in cannabis, sports wagering, video lottery, and offshore wind projects.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local fiscal impact is none. State agencies can implement the bill's additional reporting requirements and procedural updates using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the responsibilities and authority of the Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs, including establishing a small business certification review process, setting procurement reporting timelines, establishing MBE plans across multiple industries, and reporting to the General Assembly and Board of Public Works.

The Board of Public Works receives required annual procurement and waiver reports, must approve reporting formats and debarment regulations, designates the MBE certification agency, and cannot approve public-private partnership agreements until MBE participation goals are established.

The Office of State Procurement within DGS is tasked with jointly adopting regulations establishing criteria for contractor debarment, assisting with procedures for procurement exemptions, and collaborating on the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation.

The Office of the Attorney General is required to consult on the constitutional review and evaluation of disparity studies, consult on MBE plans for cannabis, offshore wind, P3s, and sports wagering, co-adopt debarment criteria, and handle contractor debarment referrals.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission is responsible for ensuring that video lottery terminal licensees and sports wagering licensees comply with State MBE program requirements as a condition of licensing.

The Administration and its Office of Social Equity must consult on disparity studies, evaluate constitutional compliance, and establish MBE participation plans and goals for cannabis licensees through July 1, 2031.

The Commission oversees offshore wind renewable energy credit (OREC) applications, where approved applicants must comply with the MBE program and submit semi-annual progress reports on MBE goal implementation through July 1, 2031.

MDOT is consulted by the Special Secretary regarding policies and guidelines for capital project MBE subgoals, has historic and regulatory ties as the State's designated MBE certification agency, and serves on the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation.
The Secretary of Labor (or designee) is newly added by the bill as a statutory member of the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the membership, meeting requirements, and responsibilities of the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation.

The State Retirement and Pension System is required under uncodified language amended by the bill to provide information necessary to assess the need for remedial measures to assist minority- and women-owned businesses in brokerage and investment management services.

The Governor receives annual reports and recommendations from the Governor's Subcabinet on Socioeconomic Procurement Participation and oversees the executive subcabinet and coordinating offices implementing the legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters provisions concerning horse racing facilities, the Prince George's County Blue Line Corridor (BLC), and the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) grant program. It designates the Maryland Stadium Authority (MSA) as the successor to the Maryland Thoroughbred Racetrack Operating Authority for Pimlico redevelopment and racing operations, clarifies the operating role of the Maryland Jockey Club, and reinstates community profit-sharing. It also increases bond authorization and expands allowable facilities for the Prince George's County Blue Line Corridor, and restructures the BRT grant program specifically to fund projects in Montgomery and Howard counties.
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland horse racing industry and backstretch workers, transit users and local governments in Montgomery and Howard counties, residents and businesses along the Prince George's County Blue Line Corridor, and the Pimlico surrounding community.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2027, State general fund revenues decrease by $14.0 million annually due to increased distributions from the State Lottery Fund to the Racing and Community Development Financing Fund (by $12.0 million) and the BLC Facility Fund (by $2.0 million), with corresponding increases in nonbudgeted revenues and expenditures. General fund expenditures increase by a one-time mandated appropriation of $5.0 million in FY 2028 for backstretch housing at Laurel Park. Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by $2.0 million annually beginning in FY 2028 for the BRT Fund, and Purse Dedication Account expenditures increase by $2.0 million annually beginning in FY 2028 for training facility debt service. Maximum bond issuance for the BLC is increased from $400.0 million to $425.0 million. Locally, Montgomery County receives $27.0 million annually and Howard County receives $2.0 million annually in BRT grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSA is the primary implementing agency for the bill, which was introduced by request as a departmental bill for the Authority. The legislation designates MSA as the successor to MTROA/MEDCO for racing facilities, alters long-term agreements for Pimlico Race Course, increases bond authorization for the Prince George's County Blue Line Corridor to $425 million, and repeals the authority to establish affiliated foundations.

The bill relieves MEDCO of operational responsibilities for the Pimlico Race Course project by transferring those rights and assets to the Maryland Stadium Authority, while directing $2,000,000 annually from the Purse Dedication Account to MEDCO for debt service on a thoroughbred training facility site.

MDOT administers the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) Fund and grant program altered by the bill. The bill mandates MDOT to enter into multi-year grant agreements exclusively with Montgomery and Howard counties and increases mandated Transportation Trust Fund appropriations to the BRT Fund by $2 million annually beginning in FY 2028.

The Comptroller is statutorily directed to execute revised monthly distributions from the State Lottery Fund to the Racing and Community Development Financing Fund ($29 million) and the Blue Line Corridor Facility Fund ($29 million), as well as distribute specific allocations from the Purse Dedication Account.

The bill directly mandates that 10% of the annual net income of the thoroughbred racetrack operator at the reconstructed Pimlico facility be distributed to the Pimlico Community Development Authority as local impact grants for community development activities.

The State Racing Commission is housed within the Department of Labor and is directly affected by provisions governing the issuance of mile track licenses, awarding of racing days to the Maryland Jockey Club or successor entities, and oversight of the Purse Dedication Account.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters mandated statutory distributions from the State Lottery Fund for racing and Blue Line Corridor debt service, impacting the agency's lottery bond coverage ratios and net proceeds returned to the General Fund.

The Board of Public Works oversees and approves MSA bond issuances up to statutory caps and must be formally notified at least 180 days in advance if thoroughbred racing becomes commercially unviable or unlawful.

The Treasurer invests money in the Purse Dedication Account and monitors State debt affordability and bond rating implications related to State Lottery Fund coverage ratios and county-issued BRT debt backed by state revenue.
The bill grants MSA the authority to delegate the adjudication of contested disputes concerning alternative use plans for the Pimlico racing facility site to the Office of Administrative Hearings.

The bill establishes statutory mandates requiring the Governor to include specific appropriations in the annual state budget bill, including $5 million in FY 2028 for Laurel Park backstretch housing and increased funding for the Bus Rapid Transit Fund.

DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and fiscal planning, which are impacted by the bill's new mandated general fund and special fund appropriations and the $14 million annual reduction in general fund lottery revenues.

The bill repeals Section 10-612 of the Economic Development Article, eliminating statutory provisions that required the State Ethics Commission to review conflict of interest policies and receive notices regarding MSA personnel serving on affiliated foundation boards.

qa_results.bill_summary: The COMPASS Act modifies Maryland's public school educational accountability program and composite scoring framework. Among other changes, it increases the maximum allowable weight of academic indicators from 65% to 70%, caps the weight of any single academic proficiency indicator at 20%, prohibits using teacher evaluations in accountability measures, adds school staffing and well-rounded curriculum progress to allowable school quality indicators, and requires annual reporting through 2031 on excluded indicators and correlations with student poverty.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education and the Maryland State Board of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland public school students, educators, public elementary and secondary schools, and local school systems
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no direct effect on State revenues or expenditures. Potential administrative expenses for the Maryland State Department of Education to modify the accountability system or prepare required annual reports are minimal and absorbable within existing resources. Local school system finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was introduced on behalf of the Department of Education (MSDE) and directly governs the State's public school educational accountability system and composite scoring parameters, requiring MSDE to administer the indicators and submit annual reports on accountability outcomes to the State Board of Education and the General Assembly.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill alters the definition of 'slot machine' to increase the number of bingo cards a handheld device may allow a user to play at the same time from 54 to 100. It also specifies that electronic instant bingo machines are not required to print a paper ticket for each play unless the player elects to do so, and requires the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency to hire an independent vendor to conduct a study and report on the potential expansion of electronic instant bingo machines, historical horse racing machines, and video lottery terminals by December 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: Electronic instant bingo players, commercial bingo operators and licensed charitable organizations, satellite simulcast facility operators, and gaming industry labor unions.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by up to $100,000 in FY 2027 only for the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency to retain a third-party consultant to conduct the mandated reports. State revenues and local finances in Anne Arundel and Calvert counties are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1587 directly tasks the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission with adopting regulations for electronic instant bingo machines and requires the agency to hire an independent third-party vendor to conduct a comprehensive study and report on the potential expansion of gaming machines, resulting in an estimated expenditure of up to $100,000 in FY 2027.

The bill requires the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency to submit a detailed report and policy evaluation to the Governor by December 1, 2026, regarding potential expansions of electronic instant bingo, historical horse racing, and video lottery terminals.

qa_results.bill_summary: House Bill 1598 authorizes standardbred racing licensees to receive capital construction grants from the Racetrack Facility Renewal Account (RFRA) without being required to expend matching funds, provided they complete the capital construction plan and conduct live racing in Maryland for at least 10 years following completion. The bill establishes grant recapture mechanisms if these conditions are unmet, and alters the distribution of unencumbered RFRA balances to 75% between Rosecroft Raceway and Ocean Downs Race Course if either facility permanently ceases live racing operations.
qa_results.stakeholders: Standardbred horse racing licensees, operators, owners, and trainers (specifically associated with Rosecroft Raceway and Ocean Downs Race Course), as well as racetrack facility employees.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, there is no state or local fiscal impact. The bill alters eligibility and matching fund requirements to access Racetrack Facility Renewal Account (RFRA) funds, but it does not change the overall funding levels, revenues, or distributions of the account.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Racing Commission, which administers the Racetrack Facility Renewal Account, approves capital construction plans, monitors compliance, adopts implementing regulations, and recaptures grant funds, is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. The bill also references racing licensees applying to the Secretary of Labor for reimbursement of certain expenditures.

The bill requires racing licensees to submit capital improvement plans to the Department of General Services (DGS) and requires the State Racing Commission to consult with DGS to monitor the implementation of approved capital construction plans and certify their completion in writing.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Chesapeake Bay Enhancement Program within the Department of Natural Resources to fund oyster propagation and replenishment projects mitigating transportation project impacts, and creates the Maryland Seafood Industry Financial Assistance Fund administered by MARBIDCO to provide loans and financial assistance to commercial watermen and seafood small businesses. Additionally, it prohibits license transfers for tidal fish licensees who are delinquent on MARBIDCO loans until compliance is restored.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources and Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial watermen, seafood industry small businesses, oyster harvesters, and tidal fish license holders.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $2.0 million in FY 2027 due to a contingent appropriation capitalizing the Maryland Seafood Industry Financial Assistance Fund. Nonbudgeted revenues increase by $2.0 million and nonbudgeted expenditures increase by $2.7 million in FY 2027 to provide loans and cover administrative costs, utilizing the appropriation and $675,000 transferred from other loan programs (to be repaid by June 30, 2028). Subsequent nonbudgeted revenues and expenditures will vary with loan repayments and reissuances. The statutory codification of the Chesapeake Bay Enhancement Program reflects an existing interagency agreement and has no independent net state fiscal effect. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 1599 establishes the Chesapeake Bay Enhancement Program within the Department of Natural Resources to fund oyster propagation and replenishment projects. It also prohibits DNR from approving transfers of tidal fish licenses or authorizations for borrowers who are delinquent on MARBIDCO loans.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Maryland Seafood Industry Financial Assistance Fund under MARBIDCO's administration to provide loans and financial support to commercial watermen and seafood small businesses, authorizes fund transfers from existing loan programs, and directs MARBIDCO to notify DNR regarding delinquent borrowers.

The bill mandates an annual appropriation of $2,000,000 from MDOT's Transportation Trust Fund to support the Chesapeake Bay Enhancement Program, codifying a long-standing interagency agreement to mitigate the environmental impacts of transportation and channel projects.

The Chesapeake Bay Enhancement Program specifically mitigates the impacts on the oyster population caused by transportation, dredging, and infrastructure projects that maintain or expand the Helen Delich Bentley Port of Baltimore, which MPA manages.
The bill mandates that the Governor include a $2,000,000 appropriation from the Transportation Trust Fund in the annual State budget bill starting in fiscal year 2028 and each year thereafter.

DBM oversees the state budget planning and execution, which includes administering the mandated Transportation Trust Fund appropriation and the contingent fiscal 2027 general fund appropriation of $2.0 million.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to issue Class B beer, wine, and liquor licenses for restaurants at specific locations in the 40th alcoholic beverages district subject to memorandums of understanding and seating waivers, allows member-only sales requirements to be waived for a Class C license on Eutaw Place, and alters boundaries governing restricted alcohol sales hours in a specified area of the district.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Restaurant operators, alcohol license applicants and holders, local patrons, and neighborhood associations (such as Bolton Hill, Hollins Roundhouse, and Mount Vernon–Belvedere) within Baltimore City's 40th legislative district.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact and does not materially affect Baltimore City finances or operations. Any impact on small businesses is minimal.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the eligibility criteria for a local-option property tax credit on the dwelling houses of certain disabled veterans and surviving spouses by raising the federal adjusted gross income limits to $150,000 for individual tax returns and $300,000 for joint returns (up from $100,000), and authorizes local governing bodies to adopt additional eligibility criteria based on income and disability rating.
qa_results.responsible_party: Local governing bodies of Maryland counties, municipalities, and Baltimore City
qa_results.stakeholders: Disabled veterans with service-connected disabilities of at least 50%, surviving spouses of disabled veterans, and county and municipal governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Local property tax revenues may decrease beginning in FY 2027 to the extent local jurisdictions offer the optional credit and higher income thresholds expand eligibility; the exact revenue reduction depends on local adoption, qualifying veteran populations, assessed home values, and local tax rates. Local expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Veterans and Military Families is responsible for advocating for and assisting Maryland veterans and their families in obtaining state and local benefits and services. This bill directly expands income eligibility thresholds for local property tax credits available to disabled veterans and their surviving spouses.

The Comptroller serves as the state's principal tax administrator and was consulted on the legislation. Although the property tax credit is enacted and granted at the local level, eligibility is directly linked to the veteran's federal adjusted gross income as reported for income tax purposes.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a mutual insurance holding company that directly or indirectly owns 100% of the capital stock of a reorganized stock insurer to convert its holding company system into a mutual insurer. The bill establishes requirements for adopting and approving a plan of conversion, including member and board approval, review by the Maryland Insurance Commissioner, and dissolution of the holding company.
qa_results.stakeholders: Mutual insurance holding companies, reorganized stock insurers, and their policyholders and members.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: There is no net fiscal impact on State finances or local governments. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Maryland Insurance Administration may increase correspondingly if the Commissioner retains an outside expert to review a conversion plan, as those costs are fully reimbursed by the applicant company; however, the exact amount cannot be reliably estimated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1616 establishes procedures for mutual insurance holding companies to convert to mutual insurers, requiring the submission and approval of conversion plans by the Maryland Insurance Commissioner, who heads the Maryland Insurance Administration. The agency is responsible for reviewing plans, holding potential hearings, adopting regulations, and potentially hiring outside experts to assist in evaluations.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill updates the Public Local Laws of Montgomery County regarding the Village of Drummond special taxing district by establishing the Village Council as its governing body. It outlines the Council's structure, duties, and meeting requirements, alters the eligible uses of special tax levy revenues, details an annual budget and appropriations process, raises competitive bidding thresholds to $15,000 with specified exceptions, and defines the Council's authority over public ways and officer appointments.
qa_results.responsible_party: Village Council of the Village of Drummond
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents and property owners in the Village of Drummond special taxing district in Montgomery County, as well as village officers and employees.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected. Local finances and operations are also not materially affected; the Village of Drummond anticipates paying between $1,000 and $5,000 each for surety bonds for two individuals, which will not significantly impact village finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill provides that any party affected by a final decision of the Village Council regarding special assessments for public way improvements may appeal the decision within 10 days to the Circuit Court for Montgomery County, which falls under the administration and operational support of the Administrative Office of the Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the annual compensation for both the Sheriff and the State's Attorney of Howard County, establishing statutory salaries of $220,601 in calendar year 2027, $227,230 in 2028, $234,079 in 2029, and $241,149 in 2030 and each subsequent year, taking effect at the start of the next terms of office.
qa_results.stakeholders: The Howard County Sheriff, the Howard County State's Attorney, and Howard County taxpayers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected. Howard County expenditures increase by approximately $48,000 in FY 2027, $96,000 in FY 2028, and at least $104,000 annually thereafter to fund the salary increases. County revenues are not affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Modifies prior authorizations of State debt in capital budgets from 2017 through 2025 by altering authorized project uses and scopes, changing grantee names, extending project termination deadlines, and eliminating certain matching fund requirements.
qa_results.stakeholders: Recipients of state capital grants, including local governments, educational institutions, nonprofit organizations, cultural institutions, and community health centers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill alters the terms, purposes, and deadlines for previously authorized State debt grants and does not materially affect State finances. Local fiscal impact is limited to instances where a local government is a grant recipient receiving extended timeframes, modified project scopes, or removed matching fund requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Board of Public Works oversees and approves capital grant disbursements, certifications of matching funds, and contract requirements associated with State Debt authorizations altered by this bill.
The Department of General Services administers and manages the execution of capital grant agreements and legislative bond initiatives modified by the bill.
The Department of Budget and Management oversees the state's capital budget process, monitors capital spending, and manages authorizations of state debt.
The bill explicitly removes the requirement that the Park Heights Renaissance grant recipient consult with the Department of Housing and Community Development regarding community investments.

qa_results.bill_summary: Proposes a constitutional amendment to specify that Maryland constitutional redistricting standards apply exclusively to state legislative districts for the Senate and House of Delegates, and that no provision in the Maryland Constitution (including the Declaration of Rights) provides criteria for congressional districts. The amendment also authorizes the General Assembly to grant original jurisdiction to the Supreme Court of Maryland to review congressional redistricting plans, and establishes specific language to place the question on the November 2026 general election ballot.
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland voters, candidates for congressional and state legislative office, the Maryland General Assembly, and the Supreme Court of Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The proposed constitutional amendment is not anticipated to materially affect State operations or finances, and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that a proposed constitutional amendment with specific ballot question language be submitted to Maryland voters at the November 2026 general election, which the State Board of Elections must administer and place on ballots statewide.

The bill authorizes the General Assembly to grant original jurisdiction to the Supreme Court of Maryland to review congressional districting plans and clarifies constitutional districting standards, directly impacting judicial review proceedings.

The Secretary of State oversees the certification and publication requirements for statewide ballot questions and serves as the keeper of the state's official records, including enacted constitutional amendments.
The Maryland Department of Planning maintains the official geographic information, demographic data, and mapping of the State's legislative and congressional election districts.

Pursuant to Article XIV of the Maryland Constitution and the bill text, election returns regarding the adoption or rejection of constitutional amendments are made to the Governor for formal proclamation.

qa_results.bill_summary: This emergency legislation withdraws and repeals duplicate provisions proposing a constitutional amendment regarding collective bargaining and binding arbitration for State employees from Chapter 156 of 2026. This technical correction ensures that identical language already enacted in Chapter 155 of 2026 remains on the ballot without appearing twice on the November 2026 general election ballot.
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland voters, State election administrators, and Maryland State employees eligible for collective bargaining.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact. It is purely technical in nature and avoids duplicative constitutional amendment language on the November 2026 general election ballot without altering governmental revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 2101 directly impacts the administration of the November 2026 general election ballot by withdrawing and repealing duplicate constitutional amendment language enacted under Chapter 156, ensuring that the proposed amendment on state employee collective bargaining appears on the ballot only once under Chapter 155.

DBM serves as the state's central personnel agency and oversees collective bargaining negotiations for state employees. While this emergency legislation is a technical measure to clean up ballot duplication, it directly concerns the enactment contingency of the Arbitration Reform for State Employees Act.

PERB administers collective bargaining for state executive branch employees. Although this bill is purely a technical correction regarding ballot questions, it relates directly to the underlying constitutional amendment governing binding arbitration and collective bargaining dispute resolution for state employees.

qa_results.bill_summary: Senate Bill 1 requires the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission to establish uniform statewide policies prohibiting law enforcement officers from wearing face coverings on duty (with limited health, safety, and undercover exceptions) and requiring officers to wear visible identification on outer clothing and verbally disclose their identity upon request. It preempts local policies and establishes that violations are civil offenses subject to a fine of up to $1,500 and constitute police misconduct.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland state and local law enforcement officers and agencies, the District Court of Maryland, and members of the public interacting with law enforcement.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may increase minimally from civil penalties (fines up to $1,500) collected through District Court adjudications. The Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission can implement the uniform policies using existing resources. State and local expenditures may experience minimal increases to the extent agencies must modify officer uniforms, equipment, or training programs to comply with the identification standards.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC), which is housed within DPSCS, develop uniform statewide policies regarding face coverings and identification requirements for all law enforcement officers in the State.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, MSP's sworn troopers are directly subject to the prohibition on face coverings, the requirements for displaying and disclosing identification, new uniform standards, and the authority/procedure for issuing citations.
The District Court is required to prescribe the uniform citation form, establish a fine prepayment schedule, docket and schedule trials, and adjudicate civil citations issued under the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP administers the Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund (CICF), which is designated under the bill to receive payments and fees resulting from District Court proceedings against defendants found guilty of violations.

DGS oversees the Maryland Capitol Police, whose sworn officers must adhere to the new uniform identification requirements and face covering restrictions, potentially incurring minimal costs for uniform modifications.
DNR employs the Natural Resources Police, whose officers are directly subject to the identification and face covering prohibitions and may need uniform modifications and training updates.
MDOT oversees modal administrations employing sworn law enforcement officers that are directly subject to the bill's uniform, training, and identification mandates.
MDTA employs a dedicated police force that must comply with the face covering ban, wear required outermost identification, and update officer training and uniforms accordingly.
MTA employs a sworn transit police force whose officers must comply with the uniform face covering and identification standards established under the bill.
The Comptroller employs sworn law enforcement agents in its Field Enforcement Division who are subject to the bill's operational, identification, and face covering requirements.
USM institutions employ sworn campus police forces that must adhere to MPTSC's uniform policies regarding identification and face covering prohibitions.
Morgan State University operates its own independent university police department, whose sworn officers must comply with the bill's uniform identification and face covering rules.
St. Mary's College of Maryland employs public safety and campus law enforcement personnel who are subject to statewide law enforcement standards and uniform policies.

qa_results.bill_summary: Provides collective bargaining rights to eligible nontenure track instructional faculty at University System of Maryland institutions, Morgan State University, and St. Mary's College of Maryland, and establishes a separate collective bargaining unit for them while excluding faculty at fully online institutions or whose positions are fully funded by grants, contracts, or clinical revenues.
qa_results.stakeholders: Eligible nontenure track faculty, higher education administrators, and staff at the University System of Maryland, Morgan State University, and St. Mary's College of Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures for USM institutions, MSU, and SMCM will increase minimally to reimburse the Public Employee Relations Board (PERB) for collective bargaining expenses, with a corresponding minimal increase in PERB reimbursable revenues and expenditures. Institutional administrative, legal, and personnel costs may increase—potentially significantly—depending on the outcomes of unionization elections and collective bargaining negotiations. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill extends collective bargaining rights and establishes a separate collective bargaining unit for nontenure track faculty at University System of Maryland constituent institutions, resulting in direct operational and potential personnel fiscal impacts.

The bill extends collective bargaining rights and creates a separate bargaining unit for eligible nontenure track faculty at Morgan State University, creating direct administrative and personnel impacts.

The bill extends collective bargaining rights and establishes a bargaining unit for eligible nontenure track faculty at St. Mary's College of Maryland, directly affecting its employment policies and expenditures.

The Public Employee Relations Board (PERB) is responsible for administering union representation elections, certifying exclusive representatives, resolving disputes, and investigating unfair labor practices for the newly eligible bargaining units.

The fiscal note identifies an operational impact on the Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH) to train administrative law judges on the new provisions and handle any resulting increase in grievance or dispute proceedings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands identity fraud statutes by prohibiting the unauthorized use of an individual's personal identifying information to cause harm, and criminalizing the use of artificial intelligence or deepfake representations to impersonate others, cause harm, or create and distribute false records. The bill establishes misdemeanor and felony penalties for violations and creates a civil cause of action allowing victims to seek injunctions and other appropriate relief.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police, Office of the Attorney General, and local State's Attorneys
qa_results.stakeholders: Victims of identity fraud and deepfake impersonation, individuals accused of identity fraud, law enforcement agencies, the Judiciary, and the Office of the Public Defender
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations. While it creates new criminal offenses and authorizes civil causes of action, the fiscal note assumes it will apply to a relatively small number of cases, and any impact on the Judiciary or Office of the Public Defender can be handled with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill maintains and applies provisions under the identity fraud statute granting the Department of State Police statewide investigative and enforcement authority, as well as the authority to adopt regulations governing multi-jurisdictional investigations by other police forces.

Under the statute amended by the bill, the Attorney General has concurrent authority with State's Attorneys to investigate and prosecute criminal violations of the identity fraud and AI deepfake provisions, including using grand jury powers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new misdemeanor and felony offenses for identity fraud involving artificial intelligence and deepfake representations, potentially increasing caseloads and litigation for public defenders representing indigent defendants.

The bill creates a new private civil cause of action for victims of AI and deepfake identity fraud seeking injunctive and other relief, while expanding criminal penalties heard across District and Circuit Courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes new felony penalties of up to 5 and 10 years of imprisonment, which affects state correctional facilities and parole and probation supervision under DPSCS.

The statute explicitly authorizes Maryland Transportation Authority Police officers to investigate identity fraud violations across the state pursuant to regulations adopted by the Maryland State Police.
The statute explicitly authorizes Maryland Port Administration Police officers to investigate identity fraud violations statewide pursuant to regulations adopted by the Maryland State Police.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires landlords of residential rental apartment buildings with 10 or more units to provide air conditioning capable of maintaining temperatures at 80 degrees Fahrenheit or lower from June 1 through September 30 each year. The requirement applies beginning June 1, 2026, for new construction and units where air conditioning was previously provided or required by lease, and beginning October 1, 2026, for units undergoing substantial electrical or heating system renovations, with exemptions for certain historic and Baltimore City public housing properties.
qa_results.responsible_party: Landlords (with oversight by local code enforcement agencies and the Judiciary)
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential tenants and landlords of apartment buildings containing 10 or more dwelling units, as well as local housing authorities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected. Local government expenditures may increase, potentially significantly, for jurisdictions and local housing authorities (such as the Housing Authority of Baltimore City) that own or operate residential rental units undergoing covered new construction or renovations, as well as for increased local code enforcement. Local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary state department responsible for housing standards, affordable rental housing programs, and habitability policies, making statutory changes to residential rental property standards relevant to its work.
The Maryland Judiciary handles residential landlord-tenant actions, rent escrow cases, and lease enforcement claims that may arise under this new Real Property statutory requirement.
The OAG provides legal guidance and enforces consumer protection laws, including tenant rights and unfair or deceptive trade practices involving residential leases and landlord obligations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Limits the amount that an employer may deduct from an employee's earnings for child support under an earnings withholding order to no more than 35% of the obligor's disposable earnings if the obligor's individual income does not exceed 250% of the federal poverty guidelines for an individual, unless the obligor was found to be voluntarily impoverished. It also permits employees to administratively contest earnings withholdings exceeding this limit.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Human Services (Child Support Administration)
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income child support obligors, child support recipients/children, employers processing wage withholding orders, and the Department of Human Services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures for the Department of Human Services increase by $618,800 in FY 2029 ($210,400 general funds, $408,400 federal funds) for initial IT enhancements to the Child Support Management System, and by approximately $59,500 annually thereafter ($20,200 general funds, $39,300 federal funds). Federal matching revenues increase by $408,400 in FY 2029 and $39,300 annually thereafter. Local court operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Child Support Administration is a division of the Department of Human Services, which is responsible for administering child support services, investigating employee withholding contests, and modifying Child Support Management System programming.
The bill authorizes employees to appeal the Department of Human Services' decisions regarding earnings withholding contests to the Office of Administrative Hearings for administrative adjudication.
Earnings withholding orders originate from or interact with judicial child support orders and court contempt proceedings within the Maryland Judiciary.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel and representation to the Department of Human Services and may be involved in contested child support earnings withholding cases.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill establishes plain-language requirements for ballot questions and petition signature pages seeking to place questions on the ballot, prohibiting passive voice, legal jargon, and double negatives. It also adjusts deadlines for preparing and certifying ballot questions to July 1 before a general election, mandates a 15-day public comment period, and requires the State Board of Elections and local boards of elections to publicly post the full text of ballot questions and related links for at least 90 days before the general election.
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland voters, petition sponsors and circulators, the Secretary of State, county and municipal attorneys, and local boards of elections.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government finances are not materially affected. The State Board of Elections can implement the bill's guidelines, public comment, and website posting requirements using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SBE is the primary agency responsible for administering Maryland's elections. The bill requires SBE to develop plain-language guidelines and instructions for petitions, host a 15-day public comment period for proposed ballot questions, publish certified ballot questions and related legislation at least 90 days before the general election, and ensure ballot compliance with the new plain language standards.

The bill directly amends the statutory deadline and duties for the Secretary of State, requiring the office to prepare and certify statewide ballot questions and legislative referendum questions to SBE on or before July 1, review public comments received during the 15-day comment period, and submit the certified plain text of the question.

The OAG serves as chief legal counsel to the State Board of Elections and the Secretary of State, provides statutory review and approval of constitutional question summaries under Election Law Article § 7-105, and provides legal guidance and defense concerning compliance with statutory plain-language requirements and petition challenges.

Under § 7-103(c), Clerks of the Circuit Court (supported operationally and administratively by the AOC) serve as the statutory fallback authority required to draft and certify local or municipal ballot question information adhering to the new plain-language requirements if local attorneys fail to timely certify them.

qa_results.bill_summary: Designates the megalodon as the official State shark, names The Natural History Society of Maryland as the State natural sciences museum, and directs the Governor to annually proclaim October 1 as Purple Lights Night in support and honor of victims and survivors of domestic violence.
qa_results.stakeholders: Victims and survivors of domestic violence, The Natural History Society of Maryland, and the Maryland public
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Governor to annually proclaim October 1 as Purple Lights Night in Maryland to honor victims and survivors of domestic violence.

The Maryland State Archives maintains official state records and the Maryland Manual On-Line, which catalogues and documents official Maryland state symbols, designations, and legal commemorative days.

qa_results.bill_summary: The bill alters procedures and requirements regarding public school construction. Among other changes, it repeals the requirement for the Interagency Commission on School Construction (IAC) to approve 75% of preliminary school construction allocations by December 31, establishes an appeal process for the 90% round of recommendations, updates reporting dates and content requirements, modifies conditions under which the State Superintendent of Schools must approve school facility plans and change orders, and distinguishes between IAC's Maintenance Effectiveness Assessment and Statewide Facilities Assessment.
qa_results.responsible_party: Interagency Commission on School Construction (IAC) and the State Superintendent of Schools
qa_results.stakeholders: Local school systems, county boards of education, local governing bodies, and public school students and staff across Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is largely procedural in nature and does not have a direct fiscal impact on State or local governments. Administrative adjustments may allow the Interagency Commission on School Construction to more efficiently utilize available resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the administrative procedures, reporting timelines, appeals processes, approval thresholds, and assessment requirements (Statewide Facilities Assessment and Maintenance Effectiveness Assessment) for which the IAC is primarily responsible.

The bill modifies statutory criteria and monetary thresholds under which the State Superintendent of Schools must review and approve county board proposals for site acquisitions, facility additions, renovations, and construction change orders.

The bill updates statutory provisions governing DGS's role in reviewing design and construction documents for applicable school construction projects and systemic renovations, in coordination with the IAC.

The bill alters reporting deadlines and mandates submission of annual reports to the Governor concerning school maintenance effectiveness, statewide facilities assessments, and the use of solar and alternative energy systems in school construction.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Port Administration to provide written notice to the Anne Arundel County Delegation to the General Assembly whenever it submits a written request to Anne Arundel County for approval to acquire an interest in land or improvements on land within the county.
qa_results.stakeholders: Anne Arundel County Delegation to the General Assembly, Anne Arundel County local government, and the Maryland Port Administration
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: The Maryland Port Administration can handle the notification requirements using existing budgeted resources, and revenues are not affected. Local effect: Anne Arundel County finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Port Administration is the primary entity governed by this legislation, which establishes a statutory requirement for the agency to provide written notice to the Anne Arundel County Delegation before public hearings or written requests regarding land acquisitions in Anne Arundel County.

The Maryland Port Administration is a modal administration within the Maryland Department of Transportation, making the department directly responsible for overarching oversight of the administration's land acquisition procedures and legislative compliance.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the criminal offense of counterfeiting and possessing counterfeit private instruments to include leases of real property and rental agreements relating to real property. Counterfeiting such documents with intent to defraud is classified as a felony subject to up to 10 years imprisonment and/or a fine up to $1,000, while fraudulent possession is a misdemeanor punishable by up to 3 years imprisonment and/or a fine up to $1,000.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, Maryland Judiciary, and local law enforcement agencies
qa_results.stakeholders: Property owners, landlords, tenants, real estate professionals, victims of lease fraud, criminal defendants, and the state and local judicial and correctional systems
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in State general fund and local revenues resulting from monetary fines imposed in District Court and circuit courts. Minimal increase in State and local expenditures associated with incarceration costs for individuals convicted under the expanded penalty provisions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands felony and misdemeanor criminal penalties for counterfeiting or possessing counterfeit leases or rental agreements, which directly impacts the department through potential increases in incarceration and commitment costs in State correctional facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The creation of new criminal offenses and expansion of counterfeit document penalties can result in an increased caseload for public defenders representing indigent defendants charged under the bill.
The bill adds new categories of criminal counterfeiting offenses that will be adjudicated in the Maryland District Court and Circuit Courts supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill prohibits consumer loan lenders, commercial loan lenders, and earned wage access providers from soliciting or receiving tips or donations from consumers, requires them to prominently disclose this prohibition, and shortens the timeframe to return any received tip to within seven days. It also subjects earned wage access providers to existing consumer loan standards regarding false or deceptive advertising and protections against discrimination.
qa_results.responsible_party: Commissioner of Financial Regulation within the Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Consumers using earned wage access and loan services, earned wage access providers, and commercial and consumer loan lenders in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 94 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Department of Labor. The Office of Financial Regulation within the Department of Labor regulates consumer loans and earned wage access providers, and the Commissioner of Financial Regulation is charged with enforcing the bill's requirements and oversight provisions.

The bill explicitly references written opinions and joint form/procedure approvals by the Attorney General to establish safe harbor defenses against penalties (§ 12-1509), and the Consumer Protection Division oversees consumer protection enforcement related to lending practices.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the eligibility of the Maryland Police Officers and Probation Agents Scholarship Program and the Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program (LARP) to include correctional officers, subjecting them to the same service obligations and eligibility requirements as police officers and probation agents.
qa_results.stakeholders: Current and prospective Maryland correctional officers, students pursuing careers in corrections, and Maryland higher education institutions.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $20,000 in FY 2027 for one-time system enhancements to the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS). Program award spending is unaffected because additional recipients can be placed on existing waiting lists if current appropriations are insufficient. There is no local fiscal impact or effect on revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC (through its Office of Student Financial Assistance) is the primary state agency responsible for administering the Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program and Scholarship Program, both of which are expanded by the bill to include correctional officers, requiring $20,000 in MDCAPS system modifications.

MHEC (through its Office of Student Financial Assistance) is the primary state agency responsible for administering the Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program and Scholarship Program, both of which are expanded by the bill to include correctional officers, requiring $20,000 in MDCAPS system modifications.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is the principal employer of state correctional officers and probation agents who stand to benefit directly from the expanded higher education loan repayment and scholarship tuition assistance programs.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill establishes an enforcement process to bring motor vehicles owned by Maryland residents that are improperly registered out-of-state into compliance with Maryland vehicle registration laws. It authorizes the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) to issue warnings, assess civil fines ($7 per day up to 60 days), and refer persistent noncompliant owners to local county attorneys for civil in rem vehicle immobilization actions. The bill also authorizes MVA to enter into reciprocal agreements with other states for automated traffic enforcement, permits the repossession of out-of-state plates under specified conditions, creates a temporary excise tax exemption through December 31, 2026, for qualifying returning vehicles, and prohibits title service agents from marketing or selling out-of-state registrations to Maryland residents.
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland residents operating vehicles registered out of state, title service agents, drivers with unpaid automated traffic citations, and local law enforcement and county attorneys.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues increase significantly, estimated at approximately $15.4 million in FY 2027 ($13.8 million for the Transportation Trust Fund and $1.6 million for emergency medical and trauma special funds) and $6.2 million annually thereafter, based on an initial cohort of Maryland residents with vehicles registered in Virginia. TTF expenditures increase by $379,365 in FY 2027 and up to $481,697 in FY 2031 to hire five customer service agents and cover operating and mailing costs. Local government revenues increase through shared highway user revenues and the collection of outstanding automated enforcement citations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MVA is the primary implementing agency responsible for enforcing vehicle registration laws, issuing warnings and civil fines to noncompliant Maryland residents with out-of-state tags, suspending licenses of noncompliant title service agents, negotiating reciprocal automated enforcement agreements, and processing an influx of vehicle titling and registrations.

As the parent department of MVA, SHA, and MDTA, MDOT oversees the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), which will incur both operational expenditures for implementation and substantial revenue increases from vehicle registrations, titling fees, and fines.

MDTA operates automated enforcement systems and toll facilities across Maryland, and stands to recover significant nonbudgeted citation revenues through reciprocal automated enforcement agreements authorized under the bill.

SHA operates automated traffic and work zone speed monitoring systems and will potentially receive additional special fund citation revenues collected via the reciprocal enforcement agreements authorized by the bill.
The Maryland court system, supported by the AOC, handles the adjudication of contested automated citations and any civil in rem actions initiated against noncompliant vehicles.
MSP enforces vehicle registration and traffic safety laws on state highways and may be involved in identifying improper registrations or enforcing plate seizures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS is directly funded in part by the Maryland Emergency Medical System Operations Fund (MEMSOF), which receives dedicated statutory surcharges from the increase in Maryland vehicle registrations generated under the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland 3-1-1 Oversight Board within the Maryland Information Network to evaluate, develop, and expand nonemergency 3-1-1 systems across Maryland. The program pilots AI-powered chatbots and voicebots in select counties to handle nonemergency requests and route calls, with a comprehensive implementation plan to expand the program statewide by July 1, 2028, while also establishing the temporary 3-1-1 Technical Advisory Committee.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland 3-1-1 Oversight Board and Maryland Information Network (MDInfoNet)
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland residents seeking nonemergency services, county and municipal governments, 9-1-1 public safety answering points, and 2-1-1 and 9-8-8 call centers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $1.0 million annually beginning in FY 2027 to fund MDInfoNet personnel, vendor procurement for chatbots and voicebots, marketing, and oversight. Local government expenditures in jurisdictions with existing 3-1-1 systems may decrease if local service costs are reduced or absorbed into the state program. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DoIT has a designated representative on the newly established Maryland 3-1-1 Oversight Board, the Secretary of Information Technology appoints a GIS expert to the 3-1-1 Technical Advisory Committee, and the agency is centrally responsible for state IT and artificial intelligence policy.

MDEM and the Maryland 9-1-1 Board (which MDEM oversees) each have designated seats on the Maryland 3-1-1 Oversight Board. Additionally, the Secretary of Emergency Management appoints two 9-1-1 Public Safety Answering Point Directors to the 3-1-1 Technical Advisory Committee to ensure coordination and call routing between 3-1-1 and 9-1-1 systems.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates two new advisory and oversight bodies: the Maryland 3-1-1 Oversight Board and the temporary 3-1-1 Technical Advisory Committee.

The Department of Aging is statutorily designated a representative seat on the Maryland 3-1-1 Oversight Board to ensure nonemergency community information and referral systems meet the needs of older adults.
The Department of Disabilities is given a designated representative on the Maryland 3-1-1 Oversight Board to ensure 3-1-1 chatbots, voicebots, and services meet accessibility and equity standards.

The Governor is responsible for appointing the board chair and specialized technical experts to the Oversight Board and the Advisory Committee, and receives reports evaluating the program and presenting the statewide expansion plan.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting appointees for the newly established Maryland 3-1-1 Oversight Board and the 3-1-1 Technical Advisory Committee.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill prohibits the creation, use, or dissemination of deepfakes to produce materially false information related to elections with the intent to influence or impede voters, misrepresent election facts, or cause harm, punishable as a misdemeanor. It also directs the State Administrator of Elections to publicly correct election misinformation or disinformation, authorizes injunctive relief and subpoenas under federal law, and permits the State Board of Elections to file civil actions to recover costs and damages from responsible entities.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Elections and State Administrator of Elections
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland voters, candidates, political campaigns, political action committees, and individuals or organizations that create or disseminate election-related media and communications.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues (Fair Campaign Financing Fund) may increase beginning in FY 2027 from criminal penalties of up to $5,000 per violation. General fund revenues may also increase to the extent the State Board of Elections recovers damages and costs incurred to correct election misinformation or disinformation through civil actions. State expenditures and local government finances are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the State Administrator of Elections to communicate accurate information to correct election misinformation/disinformation, authorizes the State Administrator to issue subpoenas and seek court injunctions, and authorizes the State Board of Elections to file civil actions to recover costs and damages.

The Office of the State Prosecutor is responsible for investigating and prosecuting election law violations in Maryland, receives referrals of reported election misinformation/disinformation from the State Board, and would have jurisdiction over the new criminal deepfake offenses.

The State court system will handle petitions for injunctions, civil actions filed by the State Board of Elections for damages and costs, and criminal proceedings resulting from the new deepfake misdemeanor charges.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new misdemeanor offense carrying penalties of up to 5 years of imprisonment, potentially requiring legal defense representation for indigent defendants charged under the statute.

As chief legal counsel to state agencies including the State Board of Elections, the Attorney General's office would provide legal representation and advice regarding subpoenas, injunctions, and civil litigation authorized by the bill.
As the state's public television and broadcast entity (Maryland Public Television), it is subject to the specific broadcaster exemptions and requirements established under the deepfake provisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a temporary nonrefundable State income tax credit for tax years 2026 through 2028 for retired 9-1-1 specialists, equal to 4.75% of the first $15,000 of qualifying retirement income (capped at $700 per individual). It caps total statewide tax credit certificates at $250,000 annually, to be distributed pro rata if applications exceed the cap, and requires a report on program outcomes.
qa_results.stakeholders: Retired 9-1-1 specialists in Maryland receiving retirement income from an employee retirement system
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by up to $250,000 annually from FY 2027 through FY 2029 due to tax credits claimed. State general fund expenditures for the Maryland Department of Emergency Management increase by $41,506 in FY 2027, $43,400 in FY 2028, and $45,300 in FY 2029 to hire a part-time contractual tax specialist and cover administrative operating expenses. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Department of Emergency Management as the primary administering agency responsible for accepting tax credit applications, verifying eligibility, issuing certificates up to the $250,000 annual cap, calculating pro-rata amounts if needed, notifying the Comptroller, and submitting a report to the Governor and General Assembly.

As the State's tax administrator, the Comptroller receives notifications of approved credit recipients from the Department of Emergency Management, accepts certificates submitted by qualifying taxpayers, and incorporates the new credit onto State income tax forms.

The bill mandates that the Department of Emergency Management submit a report to the Governor by December 1, 2028, detailing program activity, tax credits issued, and the number of vested 9-1-1 specialists in the State.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill updates Maryland campaign finance laws concerning the oversight, management, and control of campaign funds.
