If the federal contingency is met (NLRA repeal or ceded jurisdiction), special fund revenues and expenditures for the Public Employee Relations Board (PERB) will increase significantly to manage private sector collective bargaining and unfair labor practice enforcement, funded in part by civil penalties of up to $1,000 per employee. Local circuit courts experience no material fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes the Commissioner of Labor and Industry within the Department of Labor to assess civil penalties for child labor violations and to adjust those penalties annually based on inflation. MD Labor is also specifically required to monitor federal actions regarding the National Labor Relations Act and notify the Department of Legislative Services if statutory contingencies are triggered.

The bill significantly expands the authority of the Public Employee Relations Board to cover private sector employees if federal contingencies occur, granting the Board jurisdiction over union elections, certifications of exclusive representatives, unfair labor practice adjudications, binding arbitration orders, and civil penalties.

As the State's central personnel agency overseeing State employee regulations and standards, DBM is impacted by the amendment to the State Personnel and Pensions Article prohibiting Executive Branch units from seeking waivers from any applicable provisions of the federal Fair Labor Standards Act.
The bill establishes that orders issued by the Public Employee Relations Board regarding private sector unfair labor practices are subject to judicial review by the Circuit Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands eligibility for tuition and mandatory fee exemptions at Maryland public institutions of higher education by lowering the age threshold from 13 to 8 for foster care recipients who resided in an out-of-home placement for at least one year before being placed into guardianship, adopted, or reunited with a parent.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission and Maryland public institutions of higher education
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals who were in foster care/out-of-home placement on or after their eighth birthday, their adoptive or guardianship families, and Maryland public colleges and universities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2027, State higher education tuition revenues decrease, potentially significantly, while expenditures increase by an indeterminate amount due to higher enrollments (average tuition and fees are $11,192 at four-year institutions and $3,314 at Baltimore City Community College). Local community college tuition revenues also decrease, potentially significantly (average tuition and fees are $5,004), while expenditures increase by an indeterminate amount.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the eligibility criteria for foster care tuition exemptions based on out-of-home placements administered by the Department of Human Services (DHS). DHS maintains placement records and verifies foster care status for youth exiting care through adoption, guardianship, or reunification.

MHEC is the state's coordinating board for postsecondary education and receives required annual reports from all public institutions of higher education regarding the foster care recipient tuition waivers granted and the forms used.
MHEC is responsible for statewide postsecondary education coordination and receives required annual reporting from public colleges and universities regarding foster youth tuition waivers.

USM constituent institutions are required to provide tuition and mandatory fee waivers to eligible foster care recipients, which will decrease tuition revenues and increase financial aid liaison and administrative responsibilities.
As an independent public four-year university, Morgan State University must grant tuition and mandatory fee waivers to newly eligible foster care recipients, resulting in forgone tuition revenue.
As a public four-year institution, St. Mary's College of Maryland is subject to the tuition exemption mandate for foster care recipients, leading to a potential reduction in tuition and fee revenues.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands the scope of Maryland's Reduction of Lead Risk in Housing law by altering the definition of 'rental dwelling unit' to include non-independent units that have access to (rather than exclusively containing) permanent living, sleeping, eating, cooking, and sanitation facilities, thereby covering rooming houses, single-room occupancy units, and shared-housing arrangements built before 1978.
qa_results.stakeholders: Landlords and owners of pre-1978 rooming houses and shared-housing rental units, tenants residing in these units, lead inspection and abatement contractors, and local housing authorities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Lead Poisoning Prevention Fund increase by an estimated $1,406,300 in FY 2027, FY 2029, and FY 2031 (and $281,300 in FY 2028 and FY 2030) due to biennial registration fees of $75 per unit. State special fund expenditures increase by $369,600 in FY 2027 for 3 permanent personnel, database upgrades, and operating expenses, with ongoing annual costs ranging from $255,000 to $291,400. Local government expenditures may increase for any locally owned or operated housing entities now subject to registration, lead-dust inspection, and potential remediation costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the definition of 'rental dwelling unit' under Maryland's Reduction of Lead Risk in Housing law, which is administered by the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE). MDE will register an estimated 37,500 additional units, requiring three new positions, a database upgrade, and managing significant increases in special fund revenues and expenditures.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Insurance Administration, in consultation with relevant stakeholders, to study the use, regulation, and taxation of captive insurance companies by entities in Maryland, protecting proprietary information provided by nonprofit hospitals and health systems, and reporting findings and recommendations by January 1, 2027.
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonprofit hospitals, health care systems, for-profit entities using captive insurance, captive insurance companies, and insurance regulators.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Insurance Administration can conduct the required study using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no material effect on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIA is the primary agency tasked with implementing the bill, which requires it to conduct a comprehensive study on the use, regulation, and taxation of captive insurance companies in the State and submit a report of its findings and recommendations.
The bill mandates that the Maryland Insurance Administration submit its findings and policy recommendations on captive insurers directly to the Governor on or before January 1, 2027.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill requires certain health insurers and health maintenance organizations to cover the evaluation and management of menopause and menopause-associated symptoms. It also requires health occupations boards to grant at least two hours of continuing education credits for each hour of training completed on menopause and associated symptoms, adds members to the State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness, and requires the Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Commission for Women to evaluate and report on access to care and policy initiatives related to menopause.
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals experiencing perimenopausal, menopausal, and postmenopausal conditions, licensed health care providers, and commercial health insurers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $100,300 in FY 2027 and $30,200 in FY 2028 for the Maryland Department of Health to hire contractual staff and vendors to meet reporting requirements. Special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration experience a minimal increase in FY 2027 from the $125 rate and form filing fees. There is no material impact on the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, but local government health care expenditures may increase for those purchasing fully insured plans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) to identify menopause training programs for health occupations licensees, evaluate and develop an action plan to increase care access through community health workers, and evaluate methods for expanding clinical education on menopause. MDH also incurs fiscal expenditures for contractual personnel and vendor costs to complete the required studies and reports.

The bill establishes a health insurance mandate requiring carriers to provide coverage for the evaluation and management of menopause and menopause-associated symptoms, which MIA regulates and oversees through rate and form filings.

DHS houses the Maryland Commission for Women, which is required under the bill to evaluate policy initiatives improving the health and economic security of individuals with perimenopausal, menopausal, and postmenopausal conditions and report recommendations to the General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the statutory membership of the State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness and imposes a formal policy evaluation and reporting requirement on the Maryland Commission for Women.

DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program and was evaluated in the fiscal note regarding the application of the menopause coverage mandate to state employee health plans.

qa_results.bill_summary: This bill expands the state bankruptcy exemption for owner-occupied residential real property to include residential real property of a settlor held in a revocable trust. It increases the exemption cap to $125,000 for an individual (capped at $125,000 in aggregate if claimed by multiple individuals in the same proceeding for the same property), provides for annual adjustments based on the Consumer Price Index beginning in fiscal year 2028, and repeals restrictions prohibiting repeat or joint claims within an eight-year period.
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland individual debtors filing for bankruptcy, homeowners and settlors holding residential property in revocable trusts, and creditors.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article regarding debtor exemptions from execution on judgments in bankruptcy proceedings. The Administrative Office of the Courts was consulted as an information source for the fiscal analysis, though federal bankruptcy courts primarily handle Title 11 proceedings and state court operations are not directly impacted.

qa_results.bill_summary: This emergency bill codifies statutory deadlines and requirements for the timely receipt and canvassing of absentee (mail-in) ballots. It requires the State Board of Elections and local boards to refer to Internet-delivered absentee ballots as 'print-at-home ballots' in public communications. Additionally, if federal law or a court imposes differing timeliness deadlines for absentee ballots with federal contests, the bill directs that nonfederal contests on timely ballots still be counted, mandates corresponding canvass regulations, and requires a voter outreach and education campaign.
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland registered voters (specifically absentee and mail-in voters) and local boards of elections
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: If federal absentee ballot timeliness requirements differ from State law, State general fund expenditures will increase by an indeterminate amount in FY 2026, at least $317,000 in FY 2027, and $182,000 in each future fiscal year with a general election. Local government expenditures would collectively increase by an indeterminate amount in FY 2026, at least $392,000 in FY 2027, and $182,000 in future general election years. Costs cover additional ballot scanners, statewide voter registration system modifications, and public outreach campaigns.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the administration of absentee ballots by the State Board of Elections (SBE). SBE is tasked with referring to Internet-delivered absentee ballots as 'print-at-home ballots,' adopting regulations for absentee ballot canvassing under federal preemption scenarios, conducting voter outreach and notifications, and updating ballot scanning equipment and the statewide voter registration system, which results in significant operational and general fund expenditure impacts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts the driver's seat of a school bus from the requirement to meet the school bus seat upholstery fire block test standards established by the National School Transportation Specifications and Procedures.
qa_results.stakeholders: Local school systems, school bus operators/drivers, and school bus manufacturers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected, as the Motor Vehicle Administration can update inspection procedures with existing resources. Local school system expenditures may experience a potential minimal reduction beginning in FY 2027 due to lower procurement costs for driver's seat upholstery. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts MVA's vehicle safety regulations and inspection procedures, as the statute mandates MVA to adopt regulations promoting fire safety standards for school buses and update its inspection criteria to exempt driver's seats.
MDOT is the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA), which regulates school vehicle safety standards and oversees school bus equipment specifications in Maryland.

The statute amended is within the Education Article and requires MVA to adopt school bus fire safety regulations with the advice of the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), which oversees student transportation policies and standards for local school systems.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Caroline County Board of License Commissioners to appoint an individual as inspector for the board, as an alternative to the county codes administrator serving in that role.
qa_results.responsible_party: Caroline County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Caroline County Board of License Commissioners, the Caroline County codes administrator, appointed alcoholic beverage inspectors, and local alcoholic beverage licensees.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal effect and does not materially affect Caroline County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry. While this legislation specifically affects local administration and personnel for the Caroline County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, it relates generally to local enforcement of alcoholic beverages laws.
